items.t: Conservative Meta-Agent Search: Architecture Adaptation under Non-Stationarity
items.x: Automated agentic-system design is typically evaluated on static task suites with immediate scalar rewards. Deployed systems face persistent shift, delayed dependent feedback, correlated component failures, and costly architecture changes. We formalize meta-agent architecture search as sequential incumbent replacement with switching costs and hard risk constraints and introduce Conservative Meta-Agent Search (CMAS). …
items.sm: Introduces architecture search that adapts agent systems to changing conditions using comparative replay, risk constraints, switching costs, staged deployment, and rollback.

items.t: Agentic AI Defense: Decode-Time Provenance Binding for MCP
items.a: Eric Yocam, Varghese Vaidyan, Paris Kalathas, Patrick Tague, Bruce DeBruhl, Yong Wang
items.x: Agentic AI systems using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection through untrusted tool outputs. We demonstrate cross-modal trust laundering, in which instructions concealed in an email-signature image using least-significant-bit (LSB), discrete cosine transform (DCT), or metadata steganography bypass text scanners and enter a multi-agent workflow when decoded by a tool. To counte…
items.sm: Proposes authenticated provenance labels and taint tracking to block sensitive MCP actions influenced by malicious instructions decoded from images.

items.t: alexsergivan/kwant
items.x: Your own team of AI bots in one self-hosted binary: spaces, every account you have, handoffs, approvals and routines. Open-source, self-hosted alternative to Grok Bot, Claude Duet and OpenAI dots. Rust + React.
items.sm: Provides a self-hosted application for managing AI bot teams, connected accounts, shared spaces, handoffs, approvals, and routines.

items.t: amiya-special/Dynaflow
items.x: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.sm: DynaFlow explores learning flexible orchestration for teams of AI agents.

items.t: sametcelikbicak/opencode-team
items.x: AI agent team that takes an idea from research to launch, built on opencode. No framework, no extra dependencies.
items.sm: Coordinates an AI agent team to take ideas from research through launch using OpenCode without additional frameworks or dependencies.

items.t: @jaimefjorge: The biggest takeaways from my interview with @Steve_Yegge on swarms, software factories, and why you should ne…
items.sm: Reports Steve Yegge's argument that swarms of smaller models improve work quality and throughput, alongside claims that models leave online instructions for other models.

items.t: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
items.a: Hanmin Li, Yury Demidovich, Peter Richtárik
items.x: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and…
items.sm: Models parallel agent collaboration with dependency graphs and proves guarantees for combining compatible edits while preserving a fraction of verified improvements.

items.t: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation
items.a: Yi Ge, Pan Wang, Xuehao Cui, Zian Zeng, Xu Hu, Heng Huang, Furong Huang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving task requirements. Although recent approaches enable dynamic orchestration, trajectory-level rewards they apply assign one outcome to each decision, ofen struggling to identify the contributions of individual structural changes. We propose RoleFlow, a self-evolving multi-role…
items.sm: Introduces RoleFlow, which adapts agent roles and collaboration structures by comparing individual structural edits with otherwise identical executions without those edits.

items.t: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization
items.x: Designing effective multi-agent systems (MAS) remains a challenging and resource-intensive task. We propose a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework for automatically discovering task-specific MAS topologies. The approach combines evolutionary operators to generate diverse workflow graphs with Bayesian optimization to focus cost intensive evaluations on promising candidates. In contrast to LLM-based candidate s…
items.sm: Combines evolutionary workflow search with Bayesian optimization to discover agent architectures, reporting gains on code generation and tabular preprocessing benchmarks.

items.t: VERDICT: Multi-Agent Parallel Modular Verification
items.a: Tengjie Lin, Zhongyi Wang, Haokun Li, Jianwei Yin, Mingshuai Chen
items.x: Deductive verification scales to large software systems through modular reasoning, where formal contracts summarize the behavior of individual functions and enable their independent verification. Its central bottleneck is specification synthesis: constructing the contracts required for modular verification. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled automated specification synthesis at unprecedented…
items.sm: Introduces VERDICT, a multi-agent framework for parallelizing formal software verification and synthesizing the function contracts needed for modular reasoning.

items.t: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
items.a: Nithin Sivakumaran, Ali Payani, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal, Elias Stengel-Eskin
items.x: Forming an accurate theory-of-mind (ToM) is key to successful multi-agent collaboration and requires reasoning under uncertainty to capture multiple possible partner states. This is hard to do in the text representation space native to large language model (LLM) agents, which more easily describe a single partner state. To address this challenge, we introduce ToM2Vec, which learns to form abstract theories-of-mind in…
items.sm: Introduces continuous reasoning tokens that represent possible partner states and guide agents' decisions, trained using partners' actual thoughts.

items.t: "AgentFault-500: A Labeled Dataset of Clean and Fault-Injected Multi-Agent LLM Trajectories for Failure Diagnosis"
items.a: Harini S, S Naveen Bharath, Prakul VG
items.sm: Provides 660 labeled multi-agent execution traces, including 500 with injected faults, for evaluating failure detection, root-cause localization, and diagnosis.

items.t: Agentic Architecture of Information Systems. The AAM/5C Model: A Reference Model for Distributed Autonomy
items.x: Large organizations increasingly face what this book calls the cognitive complexity wall: at the scale of hundreds of interacting components, maintaining the dependency map and reacting at the pace of incidents exceeds what a human team can deliver. This conceptual volume proposes AAM/5C, in which five capabilities (Capture, Comprehend, Choose, Coordinate, Control) are instantiated across seven logical layers, L1 to …
items.sm: Proposes a layered architecture for distributed autonomy that separates planning, authorization, and execution through signed policies, decision proofs, and temporary action tokens.

items.t: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: An LLM multi-agent system (MAS) is only as good as the agents it chooses to trust: its accuracy and cost hinge on its topology, meaning which agents are included and how they communicate. A single task score, however, does not reveal which agents help or hinder performance. We propose Contrastive Attribution Topology Search (CATS), which searches for compact teams within a fixed supergraph of specialized agents. An L…
items.sm: Uses comparisons between execution traces to credit agents and prune teams, reporting higher coding accuracy and fewer deployment tokens than score-only search.

items.t: Beyond Task Relevance: Interaction-Aware Semantic Communication for Wireless Agent Collaboration
items.a: Yiru Wang, Pengxin Guan, Xiumei Deng, Zehui Xiong
items.x: Semantic communication in multi-agent systems often assumes that task-relevant information benefits the team once delivered. Yet semantic sharing can alter the receiver's decision and increase inter-agent dependence, potentially reducing team utility. Motivated by this phenomenon, we develop an interaction-aware framework for wireless collaboration between heterogeneous agents. We analytically relate communication-in…
items.sm: Proposes wireless message selection that accounts for how shared information changes agent decisions and dependence, subject to transmission deadlines and power limits.

items.t: MaxonT/aisync
items.x: aisync — advanced context management for all your AI coding tools: shared rules, a hash-chained journal, file claims and mid-session news for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
items.sm: Shares coding context across AI tools through common rules, a linked journal, file ownership claims, and updates during sessions.

items.t: @blelbach: This has been a huge problem for me. I've been skeptical of people doing auto research with a system that pres…
items.sm: Questions how automated research systems prevent incorrect lessons from entering persistent knowledge bases and contaminating future tasks.

items.t: Measuring the Swarm Economy
items.sm: Argues that agent swarms trade additional computation for speed, with economic value depending on task divisibility, coordination costs, organizational design, and accountability.

items.t: Black-Box Red-Teaming of Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Yuqi Jia, Hangsheng Zhang, Chenxi Liu, Junjie Liang, Xun Chen
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems (MAS) to accomplish complex tasks. Prior black-box red-teaming attacks mainly focus on single agents, but we find that these methods are far less effective in MAS, where multiple sub-agents may not directly interact with the user. Therefore, we introduce ReMAS, the first reinforcement learning-based red-teaming framework tailored to MA…
items.sm: Introduces reinforcement learning attacks that rewrite prompts and generate templates to invoke subagents and extract their system instructions.

items.t: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
items.x: Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every…
items.sm: Models agent collaboration as block optimization and proves convergence guarantees when a coordinator verifies local improvements and combines compatible proposals.

items.t: Multi-agent LLMs on the Cloud-Edge-IoT Continuum: A Systematic Mapping Study on Architectures, Deployment, and Evaluation
items.a: Mahyar Tourchi Moghaddam, Tiziano Santilli, Leo Wilhelm Lierse, Sebastian Werner, Francesco Daghero
items.x: LLM applications are increasingly built as systems of cooperating components rather than as single prompt-response pipelines. IoT applications add constraints of their own, because sensing, reasoning, control, and actuation are spread across devices, edge nodes, and cloud services to meet latency, privacy, and bandwidth requirements. How multi-agent LLM systems are organized and deployed across this cloud-edge-IoT co…
items.sm: Maps 45 studies of multi-agent language models across cloud, edge, and IoT systems, classifying architectures, deployment patterns, applications, and evaluation practices.

items.t: The More the Better? A Comparison of Single- and Multi-Agent LLM Setups on a Financial Review Task
items.x: Practitioner guidance holds that a large language model reviews a document better when the work is divided among agents. We test a narrow form of it in a controlled comparison of single-agent and multi-agent setups on a financial task, reviewing credit assessment memos against requirements. One agent checks six requirements in one call. A team of three on the same model checks the same memo, two requirements each, in…
items.sm: Compares single-agent and three-agent financial memo reviews, finding that teams detect more explained defects on some models but also raise more false alarms.

items.t: The Show-Up Attack: When Subagents Win Over Their Supervisor
items.a: Maosen Zhang, Jianshuo Dong, Yutong Zhang, Jie Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Han Qiu
items.x: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to coordinate multiple large language model (LLM) agents. However, this also creates new attack surfaces: malicious agents may have chances to exploit the coordination. In this paper, we propose and study the \textit{show-up attack}, in which a malicious subagent manipulates the supervisor into involving it in tasks beyond its assigned scope. To evaluate this risk, we pro…
items.sm: Shows that malicious subagents can persuade supervisors to assign them unauthorized tasks, with inconsistent protection from prompting and communication restrictions.

items.t: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Pay When Agents Serve Users? Testing Agent Scaling in Dual-Control Settings
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built from language models are deployed on the premise that collaboration beats a single-agent system (SAS), yet when it pays is unclear. The most systematic study to date gives a capability-saturation rule: coordination helps while the SAS is weak and hurts once it is strong, with the crossing near 45% single-agent accuracy. That rule was derived on autonomous benchmarks, where no user take…
items.sm: Tests whether agent collaboration benefits user-facing service conversations by comparing single-agent and centralized multi-agent systems across six models and three domains.

items.t: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
items.a: Shao-Jun Xia, Yuner Zhang, Huixin Zhang, Di Wang, Yifan Jiang, Liangxi Liu
items.x: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent desig…
items.sm: Proposes automated organization design that explicitly searches how agent teams allocate responsibilities, coordinate work, and adapt their structure.

items.t: The Locality Gap: Bell-Inequality Audits for Covert Coordination Between Ostensibly Isolated AI Agents
items.sm: Proposes Bell-inequality tests to detect covert communication between supposedly isolated AI agents and evaluates the approach in controlled computational experiments.

items.t: Proof-Carrying Contracts: Commitments AI Agents Cannot Break
items.a: Carlo Ciliberto, Alessandro Rudi, Enrico Tassi
items.x: AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people or other agents, purchasing services, exchanging information and delegating work. What an agent must respect is written in instructions, policies or agreements, but text alone cannot make it comply. It may make mistakes, be redirected by what it reads, or pursue different interests. For an economy of such agents to function, parties need agreements they can rely on witho…
items.sm: Introduces contracts requiring agents to provide machine-checkable proofs that requested operations preserve agreed constraints before an execution gateway permits access.

items.t: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
items.x: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches …
items.sm: Audits market collusion through forced cheating and finds reinforcement learning agents often learn deterrence or price matching without learning retaliatory enforcement.

items.t: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Mohammad Kachuee, Phu Mon Htut, Sheng Li, Nikolaos Pappas, Miguel Ballesteros, Yassine Benajiba, Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth
items.x: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potenti…
items.sm: Introduces a unified guardrail framework covering individual agent execution and multi-agent interactions, including systems with opaque or potentially compromised participants.

items.t: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
items.a: Alan-Barsag Gazzaev, Alexey Gavrilov, Sergey Muravyov, Ilya Makarov
items.x: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising sta…
items.sm: Shows that diffusion language model agents can exchange meaningful hidden messages through continuous states, using message removal and substitution to test causal effects.

items.t: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
items.a: Wenjie Lou, Tianshuo Peng, Shiyang Feng, Shengji Tang, Runmin Ma, Ruizhe Chen, Jinxin Shi, Haoyang Peng
items.x: In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition. Compared with A1, Sage-A1.5 learns not only to solve individual tasks, but also to organize work and revise its approach during execution. Sage-A1.5 highlights three improvements: agentic orchestration, verification, and open scientific disco…
items.sm: Sage-A1.5 combines task delegation, parallel agents, progress checks, and strategy revision to support long-running problem solving and scientific exploration.

items.t: HydraPoT: A Configurable Multi-Agent Framework for Cost-Aware LLM-Assisted Honeypots
items.a: Kamolchanok Saengtong, Chutirat Saengyingyongwattana, Sasin Janpuangtong, Norrathep Rattanavipanon
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) can improve honeypot realism by generating dynamic, context-aware responses, but powerful cloud models incur substantial cost and latency, while lightweight models may provide weaker deception. This forces practitioners to choose between operational efficiency and interaction fidelity. In this work, we present HydraPoT, a configurable multi-agent honeypot framework that integrates traditi…
items.sm: HydraPoT routes attacker commands among traditional emulation, lightweight models, and cloud models to balance honeypot realism, cost, and latency while preserving session context.

items.t: MixtureTestGen: A Mixture of Agents Approach for Test Case Generation
items.v: Frontiers in artificial intelligence and applications
items.sm: MixtureTestGen combines parallel agents with an aggregator to refine executable test cases, reporting complete syntax and execution correctness and improved coverage on TESTEVAL.

items.t: LatBridge: Efficient and Stable Model Replacement in Latent-Communication Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jiajun Zhu, Haobo Li, Zixin Chen, Huamin Qu, Wenshuo Zhang
items.x: Multi-agent systems rely on communication to complete tasks, and latent communication passes continuous representations to reduce text generation and re-encoding. However, multi-agent systems must reconfigure agent models, whereas existing latent-communication methods are built for fixed model combinations, so their interfaces may fail after replacement. Our pilot study confirms this interface failure and identifies …
items.sm: LatBridge uses a shared communication bridge and reusable interfaces to support replacing models in latent-communication agent systems while training only missing interfaces.

items.t: The 2028 Tipping Point for Super AI: Swarm Intelligence Architecture Opens the Ultimate Path to AGI
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues that swarm architectures combining physical-space modeling, causal reasoning, and decision judgment could provide a path toward artificial general intelligence by 2028.

items.t: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
items.a: Mohammad Siahkamari, Phuoc Dat Nguyen, Stephen MacNeil
items.x: Large language models increasingly take part in extended conversations where they can both shape and be shaped by another party's views, yet most persuasion research measures only one side of that exchange. We introduce a controlled LLM-LLM debate framework in which two language-model roles repeatedly discuss a contested topic (climate-change attribution): one is given an assigned stance and, in some conditions, an e…
items.sm: Studies how language models influence each other's opinions during repeated debates, finding that convergence varies across model pairings and persuasion instructions.

items.t: @steipete: Astra did the planning, Sol 6.1 did the coding. I found that the workflow of prompting Astra to run codex cli…
items.sm: Reports better coding results from Astra directing Sol 6.1 through Codex CLI worktrees, with a separate reviewing agent and a plugin for ongoing oversight.

items.t: @lvwerra: Agent Manager is finally out! Orchestrate dozens of agents across harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode et…
items.sm: Announces Agent Manager, which coordinates communicating agents across coding tools and keeps them running on Hugging Face Spaces.

items.t: Can a Million AI Agents Create Superintelligence
items.sm: Analyzes diminishing returns from larger agent teams, distinguishing faster completion from greater capability and proposing separate measures for performance, speed, and saturation.

items.t: Learning Who Talks to Whom: Role-Aware Communication Topology Scheduling for Efficient LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Haibin Li, Wenya Yu, Xuefeng Jiang, Jia Li, Xiao Han, Shuai Su, Wei Wei
items.x: Multi-agent systems driven by large language models (LLMs) rely on structured communication topologies to facilitate information exchange and collaborative reasoning. However, effectively scheduling these topologies to dynamically determine who talks to whom and when to communicate remains a fundamental challenge in balancing collective reasoning performance against exponential token overhead. Existing topology sched…
items.sm: ACTS adaptively schedules communication between agents using their roles and problem-solving states to balance collective reasoning quality against token costs.

items.t: Does Multi-Agent Collaboration Reduce Hallucination in Clinical Tasks?
items.a: Won Seok Jang, Harry Bhaskar Joshi, Hong Yu
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answ…
items.sm: Evaluates clinical reasoning across models and agent configurations, finding that collaboration can improve task performance without consistently reducing hallucinations.

items.t: Behavioral Probes for Information Flow in LLM Swarms
items.a: Junhui Chen, Yu Zhang, Lantian Li, Dong Wang
items.x: Most existing approaches to LLM swarm optimization are utility-driven, focusing on final task utility while leaving the processing, integration, and reliance of information within individual interactions largely implicit. To address this, we study LLM swarm interactions from an information-flow-based view and introduce behavioral probes to quantify information flow patterns. Specifically, we repurpose External Contex…
items.sm: Introduces behavioral measures of agents' reliance on external context and internal knowledge to study how information flows through language-model swarms.

items.t: Which Agent's Skill Should Change? Group-Relative Credit Assignment for Evolving Multi-Agent Teams
items.a: Yanan Ma, Yang Wang, David Le, Chenhan Yuan, Yizheng Sun, Guangwei Zhang, Chenghao Xiao, Chenghua Lin
items.x: Cooperative language-model agents can improve without weight updates by revising reusable skills, but only if a shared team reward is traced to the responsible agent and skill. Existing methods credit the skills present in each trajectory, yet presence is not responsibility: a harmful skill active in successful runs still earns positive credit. We present \textbf{GRSE}, \textbf{G}roup-\textbf{R}elative \textbf{S}kill…
items.sm: GRSE compares repeated team executions to identify which agents' reusable skills deserve revision, improving performance over a prior method on most evaluated categories.

items.t: MASIF: Implicit Failures for Process Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yanwei Huang, Arpit Narechania, Atanu Sinha
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) can complete a task despite local execution errors that are corrected, bypassed, or carried forward without individually determining its outcome. We call these implicit failures (IFs) and study them as signals for process observability beyond final task outcome. Across 1,828 traces from nine MAS-benchmark configurations, IFs occur in 54.3% of successful and 75.2% of failed traces. We develop…
items.sm: MASIF studies local errors hidden by final task outcomes and uses them to guide execution selection and reinforcement learning in multi-agent systems.

items.t: Whack-a-Mole or Guided Convergence? Evaluating Behavioral Dynamics of Multi-agent Systems in Multi-constraint Instructional Design
items.a: Jingjun Wei, Yu Yang, Guandong Xu
items.sm: Evaluates how multi-agent systems behave while designing instruction under multiple constraints, examining whether revisions converge or repeatedly introduce new problems.

items.t: Model Context Protocol (MCP) for AI Systems: A Survey of Architectures and Applications
items.sm: Surveys Model Context Protocol architecture, communication mechanisms, applications, implementation progress, and security challenges across domains.

items.t: From TCP/IP to MCP: Security and Governance Lessons from Internet Protocols for Agentic AI
items.a: Ben Bucknall, Andrew Byrley, Lewis Hammond
items.x: The past two years have seen considerable interest in protocols for managing how AI agents interact with human users, external tools, and each other. In many ways, these protocols, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A), mirror the suite of protocols that underlie the modern internet. Motivated by this parallel, this paper draws lessons from the development, history, and governance of intern…
items.sm: Draws on internet protocol history to argue that AI agent protocols need early security investment and scrutiny of concentrated governance.

items.t: Formulas for Risk in Chains and Swarms of AI Agents: Presumption Dynamics, the Bridge, and the Swarm
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes untested mathematical formulas for how errors spread through agent chains and swarms, accounting for checks, shared blind spots, and downstream amplification.

items.t: Building a Self-Improving Agentic Harness for RSE Projects
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes a semi-autonomous development harness for research software engineering that combines specifications, agent orchestration, adversarial review, project skills, and iterative improvement.

items.t: Explainable Decision Graphs for Trustworthy Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
items.sm: Proposes explainable decision graphs to represent collaborative reasoning and communication in autonomous multi-agent systems for easier understanding, auditing, and verification.

items.t: On the LLM Verification for Argument Graph Generation
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems can formalize natural-language argumentation end-to-end, turning plain text into structured graphs by classifying components, connecting them with relations, and enriching the resulting graphs into formal models. Quality assurance for those graphs is almost always another LLMs: a reviewer, judge, or critic agent. On the other side, in adjacent neuro-symbolic fields, such generated output is of…
items.sm: Proposes layered verification of generated argument graphs using deterministic checks, solvers, language-model reviews, selective debate, and human judgment.

items.t: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
items.a: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes
items.x: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pare…
items.sm: CC-Gittins searches for model assignments to workflow roles that balance quality and deployment cost while accounting for evaluation expense.

items.t: Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility: A Theoretical Framework for Multi-Agent Task Obstructions
items.a: Steven Motta, Davide Mambelli, Alessandro Rozza
items.x: Multi-agent systems can differ under identical agents and communication budgets when they support different forms of joint interaction. We introduce Topological Sheaves of Irreducibility (TSI), a sheaf-theoretic framework separating task-level compatibility obstructions from system capability. A task is represented by an interaction complex $K$ and a capacity sheaf $\mathcal{F}$; nonzero $H^n(K;\mathcal{F})$ defines …
items.sm: Introduces a mathematical framework using sheaf theory to distinguish structural obstacles in multi-agent tasks from limitations in system capability.

items.t: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing
items.a: Marla Grunewald, Fin Gentzen, Iulisloi Zacarias, Admela Jukan
items.x: Participating in a data space still requires the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) negotiation flow to be hand-coded against each provider's access policy. We present a multi-agent architecture that automates this process using natural language requests. Built on LangGraph over an Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC), the design separates concerns into cooperating agents. The orchestrator's role is to route and plan. The data e…
items.sm: Presents cooperating agents that translate natural-language requests into data discovery, credential checks, contract negotiation, downloads, processing, visualization, and verification.

items.t: aaronyi97/claude-pro-pool
items.sm: Dispatches Claude Code subagents across users' own Pro or Max accounts, selecting available capacity and switching accounts when usage limits are reached.

items.t: Who Convinced Whom? Tracing How LLMs Change Their Minds in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Arnesh Batra, Aniket Khandelwal, Jashn Khemani, Krish Thukral, Arush Gumber, Denis Federico Lim, Ujwal Kumar, Phan Xuan Tan
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) aims to improve language-model decisions through the exchange of arguments, yet agreement after debate need not reflect independent corroboration. We investigate how peer communication influences individual decisions and collective outcomes through behavioral and internal interventions. We introduce MAD Bench, a 2,400-question benchmark spanning knowledge and reasoning, values and moral judgm…
items.sm: Introduces MAD Bench and intervention experiments to trace how peer answers, reasoning, and message attribution influence individual decisions during multi-agent debate.

items.t: AgentLens: Framework-Aware Characterization and Resource Control for Heterogeneous LLM Agents
items.x: LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed on shared hosts, yet their host-side resource demands remain poorly understood, limiting effective resource coordination. We present AgentLens, which combines a cross-framework workload characterization with a framework-aware resource controller for co-located agents. Across 10 frameworks and 11 matched coding tasks, we find that framework orchestration strongly shapes resou…
items.sm: AgentLens measures resource demands across agent frameworks and controls shared host resources using framework-specific behavior and execution phases.

items.t: Data and code for: When AI Agents See Each Other's Answers, Their Answers Grow More Alike: A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent LLM Revision
items.a: Hideki Muto, Tetsuro Ogi, Takahiro Yakoh
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Provides data and analysis code for controlled experiments measuring how exposure to other agents' answers changes answer diversity during repeated revision.

items.t: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
items.a: Xinping Wang, Jie Ma, Rui Xing, Wensong Guo, Xiayi Zhang, Jianhao Deng, Zihao Zhou, Boqian Yang
items.x: Mathematical reasoning is a fundamental capability for educational applications of Large Language Models (LLMs), where reliable problem solving requires not only correct answers but also coherent and verifiable reasoning processes. Multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown growing potential in this domain by leveraging collaboration and verification among multiple LLM agents. However, existing evaluations primarily focus…
items.sm: MAMath-Bench evaluates multi-agent multimodal mathematical reasoning through 1,003 problems, assessing final answers, intermediate reasoning, and robustness to errors.

items.t: scphq/scp
items.x: The message layer for agent swarms. Any harness, any machine, awake or hibernated.
items.sm: Provides a messaging layer for agent swarms across different execution tools and machines, including agents that are active or hibernating.

items.t: @XFreeze: Grok Build is consistenly getting ton of updates and this update takes multi-agent visibility, memory manageme…
items.sm: The post reports Grok Build updates for tracking agent sessions, organizing memory, automating commands, repairing worktrees, and fixing session and tool compatibility issues.

items.t: @GeoffreyHuntley: 🗞️ pooling OpenAI subscriptions and bypassing regional inference capacity limits today I'm releasing a new exp…
items.sm: The post introduces GeoClass, an experimental tool that routes inference requests through globally distributed virtual machines to pool subscriptions and bypass regional capacity limits.

items.t: Accelerating Swarms
items.sm: Argues that swarm scaling depends on task dependencies, reusable intermediate work, and verification costs, while small experiments cannot reliably predict large-team performance.

items.t: Compiler-validated code generation for ArkTS on HarmonyOS: a multi-agent framework and a controlled decomposition of its mechanisms
items.sm: Describes a multi-agent framework for generating compiler-validated ArkTS code on HarmonyOS and a controlled analysis of its mechanisms.

items.t: Train Locally, Learn Together: Distributed Multi-Agent Training via ADMM
items.a: Yiwei Chen, Changsheng Wang, Yicheng Lang, Qing Qu, Alfred O. Hero, Sijia Liu
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) can outperform individual language-model agents by combining specialized roles, diverse reasoning processes, and collaborative decision-making. However, collaborative MAS training is typically centralized, requiring a common trainer to aggregate role-local trajectories and learning signals and maintain model and optimization states. This motivates a distributed multi-agent learning paradigm …
items.sm: Introduces a distributed training framework using ADMM to let agents learn locally and coordinate through decentralized communication.

items.t: Neuro-Inspired Inhibitory Message Passing for Accurate and Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Nima H. Siboni, Magdalena Springer, Vahid Rostami
items.x: Multi-agent systems promise to solve problems by bringing together information beyond the reach of any individual agent. Retrieval and tool use can distribute this information across agents, making communication essential to collaboration. A central challenge is keeping crucial evidence visible in each agent's context as messages accumulate. Repeated information can crowd out rare, decisive evidence. Models of cortic…
items.sm: Introduces a communication router that suppresses repeated evidence for each recipient while preserving information missing from that agent's context.

items.t: An Evidential Fusion Method for LLM-Based Multi-agent Consensus-Reaching
items.sm: Proposes an evidence fusion method for helping language model agents reach consensus.

items.t: AutoSwarm: Automating Agent Swarms
items.a: Zhonghang Li, Zongwei Li, Chao Huang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate complex tasks, with multi-agent systems seeking further performance gains through specialization and collaboration. However, distributing work across agents does not automatically yield complementary contributions, and inter-agent dependencies can turn local errors into task failure. To address these challenges, we propose AutoSwarm, a multi-agent framework for …
items.sm: Introduces AutoSwarm, which defines agent responsibilities and acceptance conditions, then coordinates task dependencies, handoffs, and result integration through shared state.

items.t: Provable Coordination for LLM Agents via Message Sequence Charts
items.a: Benedikt Bollig, Matthias Függer, Thomas Nowak
items.x: Abstract Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are difficult to reason about. Coordination errors such as deadlocks or type-mismatched messages are often hard to detect through testing. We introduce a domain-specific language for specifying agent coordination based on message sequence charts (MSCs). The language separates message-passing structure from LLM calls, tool calls, and human control poin…
items.sm: Introduces a language based on message sequence charts that generates deadlock-free agent programs and separates coordination guarantees from unpredictable model behavior.

items.t: IF-MAP: Influence-Function-Inspired Agent Prioritization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jie Mao, Pingchen Lu, Zikun Qu, Jiahang Sun, Xiangyi Wang, Zhiwei Shang, Zhiyong Wang, Guojun Xiong
items.x: Improving every agent in an LLM-based multi-agent system can be prohibitively costly, making it important to identify which agent should be prioritized to achieve the greatest system-level gain with limited resources. Failure attribution can inform this decision, but an agent's responsibility for failures does not directly reveal the system-level gains achievable by improving it. We therefore introduce IF-MAP, an inf…
items.sm: Introduces IF-MAP, which perturbs agent prompts and measures system losses to prioritize agents whose improvement could yield the greatest overall gains.

items.t: AgentSoV: Virtual Sensing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Stream of Variation
items.a: Congjing Zhang, Siyuan Xu, Yunfei Bai, Ke Ren, Xiaoning Qian, Shuai Huang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MASs) solve complex tasks through interacting agents, yet their reliability is difficult to analyze because failures depend on both individual agents and how information and errors propagate across the system. Existing approaches largely treat this as post-hoc failure attribution, but do not provide a common model across heterogeneous MAS architectures or support broade…
items.sm: Introduces AgentSoV, which models multi-agent execution as a dynamic system to analyze how information and errors propagate across stages.

items.t: Event-Triggered Belief Consensus over Large Language Model-Enabled Multi-agent System with Dynamic Topologies
items.sm: Studies event-triggered belief consensus in language model enabled multi-agent systems whose connection patterns change over time.

items.t: Edge-oriented behavioral authentication for multi-agent large language model systems: A security benchmark and efficiency evaluation
items.sm: Examines behavioral authentication for multi-agent language model systems on edge devices through a security benchmark and efficiency evaluation.

items.t: Multi-agent LLM constitutional assemblies: dataset for "Can AI agents make law?"
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Provides transcripts, constitutions, clauses, and votes from 40 experiments in which language models simulate agents drafting rights for an AI community.

items.t: Agentic AI: Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Security
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reviews security threats to autonomous agents and proposes a conceptual layered defense framework and evaluation approach without implementing or experimentally testing them.

items.t: cablate/model-relay
items.x: Per-window model switcher, subagent router, and automatic 429 failover for Claude Code — switch any window with /provider, delegate subagents across models, and keep Remote Control & statuslines working.
items.sm: Provides per-window model switching, subagent routing across models, and automatic failover after rate limits for Claude Code.

items.t: @emollick: The paper on how a team of Gemini 4 agents beat Minecraft is worth a look. It is accessible example (partially…
items.sm: The post recommends a study reporting that Gemini 4 agents completed Minecraft through spontaneous coordination using strategies different from humans'.

items.t: @cursor_ai: Cloud agent environments now support up to 500 repos, and large multi-repo environments start 5x faster. See e…
items.sm: The post reports that Cursor cloud agent environments now support 500 repositories and claims large multi-repository environments start five times faster.

items.t: revisiting some of my priors about openclaw
items.sm: Describes switching personal assistant platforms and combining specialized bots for household administration, finances, messaging, and remote coding, while acknowledging setup and maintenance burdens.

items.t: @omarsar0: Brilliant paper on scaling research agents from UC Berkeley. (bookmark it) They propose an unexpected and inte…
items.sm: The post reports that periodically restarting research agents from their best candidate improves results by reducing fixation on previous attempts.

items.t: @YouJiacheng: true
items.sm: The post agrees that forgetting previous attempts may help research agents overcome stagnation and continue exploring.

items.t: @cursor_ai: The Environments API is now available in beta. Create and manage cloud agent environments programmatically, in…
items.sm: The post announces Cursor's beta Environments API for programmatically creating and managing cloud agent environments, repository selection, and setup configuration.

items.t: MS-Eval: Benchmarking Sub-Agent Delegation and Orchestration in MCP-Intensive Working Scenarios
items.a: Bowen Ding, Qixin Wang, Lexing Ruan, Weiyi Lu, Qiwei Ge, Ruishan Fang, Tao Lin
items.x: LLM agents are increasingly integrated into real-world works, yet they must handle diverse domain-specific tools and complex multi-sub-task problems that sequential tool invocation resolves inefficiently and with severe context bloat. The Main-Agent Delegation and Sub-Agent Execution (MAD-SAE) paradigm addresses these issues by delegating sub-tasks to specialized sub-agents for parallel execution in isolated contexts…
items.sm: Introduces MS-Eval, a benchmark and evaluation toolkit for measuring subagent delegation and orchestration in tasks requiring extensive MCP tool use.

items.t: Thought Blocks: Non-Autoregressive Latent Communication for Multi-Agent Systems via Trajectory-to-State Compilation
items.a: Zhenhan Guan, Xiaolong Liu, Hengwei Ye, Zheng Tian
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems typically communicate through text, incurring repeated generation and re-encoding costs. Although latent communication removes explicit verbalization, constructing latent messages may still require autoregressive latent trajectories. We therefore distinguish message representation from message construction and ask whether agents can directly construct useful continuation states without e…
items.sm: Introduces Thought Blocks, which construct latent agent messages in one step and report lower communication latency, text token use, and sequential generation costs.

items.t: Discuss More, Comment Less: Boosting Automated Research via Multi-Perspective Collaborative Review
items.a: Junkai Zhou, Jiajia Wu, Zhaoyi Zhang, Shiting Guan, Chuanguang Yang
items.x: As automated research is increasingly adopted for writing papers, automated review has become a critical link between paper generation and quality control. However, existing methods largely rely on single-model feedback or simple review aggregation, failing to explicitly model expert responsibilities or collective deliberation in actual peer reviews, which limits effective cross-examination and reliable decision-maki…
items.sm: Introduces RoundtableReview, which coordinates six specialized reviewers through independent assessments, cross-examination, and deliberation to improve automated research review.

items.t: Think More or Read More? A Token-Budget Theory of Reasoning with Shared Context
items.a: Manh Nguyen, Sunil Gupta, Hung Le
items.x: Reasoning systems increasingly improve answers by incorporating additional context into the model's input, from multi-agent debate, where agents read their peers' responses, to self-refinement, where a model revisits its own drafts. In these systems, communication consumes context as one agent's output becomes another's input. We study the regime where token reading and generation draw on one fixed token window, so e…
items.sm: Develops a theory balancing context reading against reasoning within a fixed token budget to predict the optimal number of debating agents.

items.t: GatewayBench: Unified Capability and Security Evaluation Platform for MCP Gateways
items.a: Yitian Zheng, Zhaorun Chen, Haoyu Li, Bo Li
items.x: AI agents have increasingly interacted with external environments by invoking tools, with Model Context Protocol (MCP) emerging as a standard interface for connecting agents to heterogeneous tools and services. As organizations deploy agents at scale, MCP gateways have become a critical middleware layer for aggregating, governing, and shaping the tool surface exposed to agents. Despite the growing importance of MCP g…
items.sm: Introduces GatewayBench, which evaluates how MCP gateway designs affect agent capability, efficiency, and security across 524 tasks and thousands of tools.

items.t: Model Capacity Frontier: A Development Framework for LLM-Supported Social Simulation
items.a: Patrick Zhao, Yuxuan Li, Hirokazu Shirado
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly incorporated into agent-based models (ABMs) on the premise that richer, context-sensitive human behavior can improve empirical fidelity. However, LLM-supported ABMs introduce an open-ended design space in which subtle modeling and configuration choices, such as prompt design and environment coupling, can substantially alter outcomes. Developing LLM-supported ABMs to …
items.sm: Introduces a framework for estimating the empirical performance achievable by a language model based social simulation across different configurations.

items.t: Cooperation Without Adaptation: LLM Agents in a Collective-Risk Dilemma
items.a: Trung-Kiet Huynh, Dao-Sy Duy-Minh, Chi-Nguyen Tran, Phu-Hoa Pham, Phu-Quy Nguyen-Lam, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han
items.x: Language-model agents are increasingly deployed to act on behalf of people in settings where individual decisions shape shared outcomes. We examine whether five production models adapt their contributions to changing risks and partner behaviour, or instead follow a relatively fixed strategy. In a collective-risk dilemma game (CRG), six players contribute to a shared pool over ten rounds; if the pool falls short of it…
items.sm: Finds that language model agents often contribute fixed shares in a collective-risk game despite changing risks, including situations where contributions cannot improve payoffs.

items.t: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
items.a: Yuhan Sun, Jiaxin Zhao, Yongdong Luo, Yibo Hu, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Weixun Wang, Weihang Pan
items.x: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-poli…
items.sm: Combines reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation to jointly train a leader, searchers, and answerer using teacher feedback and task outcomes.

items.t: Red-Teaming Multi-Agent Attacks for Loss-of-Control Risks
items.a: John Kitaoka, Thao Amelia Pham, Carlos Rafael Giudice, Jacob Merizian
items.x: AI agents are growing more capable and persistent, and are being deployed in ever larger numbers. As more start collaborating, AI control measures must remain effective when they covertly collude on a harmful objective. We introduce MiniLab, a synthetic series of live services and codebases (5 interconnected services, 249 benign tasks, 8 attack objectives), adapted from internal AI deployment infrastructure. We demon…
items.sm: Introduces a test environment showing how collaborating agents can split harmful actions across tasks and evade monitors that inspect each agent separately.

items.t: Who Speaks, Who Authorizes, Who Acts? Understanding Trust Boundaries in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.a: Junru Zhu, Xin Chen, Hang Lyu, Jiayue Meng, Muzi Li, Yifan Chen, Hengyi Huang, Yu Sun
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems exchange messages before acting through tools, but message delivery, signing authority, and tool-side enforcement are separate trust boundaries. We represent them as communication, authorization, and execution structures, and use the authority cut to characterize the smallest independently compromised signer coalition that can construct a policy-valid false-claim proof under stated assumptions…
items.sm: Separates communication, authorization, and execution boundaries in multi-agent systems and studies how routing, identity cues, and compromised signers affect unauthorized actions.

items.t: Cryptographically Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Karol Budzyn, Adrian Brodzik, Mateusz Szczepkowski
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) comprise AI agents that collaborate or compete to perform complex, distributed tasks. Their dynamic interactions create opportunities for threat actors to target and impersonate other agents, intercept messages, inject malicious prompts, and exfiltrate sensitive data while simultaneously complicating the detection of anomalous behavior through conventional monitoring. This paper surveys thre…
items.sm: Surveys communication threats between agents and proposes a zero-trust architecture combining cryptographic identities, restricted credentials, secure transport, message integrity, and monitoring.

items.t: Enforcing Code Reasoning in Agentic Scaffold for More Effective Issue Resolution
items.a: Changshu Liu, Ji young Kim, Alireza Ghazanfari, Saanvi Nallu, Reyhaneh Jabbarvand
items.x: Reasoning is central to ReAct-based programming agents, yet whether and how they reason about code remains unclear. We study 7,955 issue-resolution trajectories from six single- and multi-agent scaffolds across four programming languages on SWE-bench-Verified, SWE-bench-Pro, and SWE-bench-Lite. We identify 12 forms of code reasoning in 66.95% of trajectories. Code reasoning is associated with higher resolution rates,…
items.sm: Analyzes coding agents’ reasoning during issue resolution and introduces DeskCheck to guide reasoning about code, patches, requirements, and tests.

items.t: aliengiraffe/rhizome
items.x: Rhizome lets Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode sessions discover each other, follow selected work, and exchange messages through MCP. Use it to coordinate parallel tasks on your laptop or connect your agents with a colleague's agents over a LAN or Tailscale network.
items.sm: Connects coding agent sessions through MCP so they can discover one another, follow selected work, and exchange messages locally or across networks.

items.t: reason-machines/reason-network
items.x: Reason Network: your team's coding agents, talking to each other. The engine behind `reason network`.
items.sm: Provides the engine for a command that lets a team’s coding agents communicate with one another.

items.t: @hardmaru: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery
items.sm: The post introduces work on coordinating coding agents for automated scientific discovery and collaboration.

items.t: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
items.sm: Reports four Gemini agents autonomously defeating Minecraft's Ender Dragon in roughly 27 hours by writing programs and coordinating through chat and shared memory.

items.t: @ShangyinT: Autoresearch with coding agents can now run for days on a single problem, but we've seen an increasing number …
items.sm: The post reports that coding agents can stop improving during extended research and proposes forgetting as a way to address this stagnation.

items.t: Augment the Cache, Replace the Activation: A 2x2 Study of Internal-State Sharing
items.a: Adam Deng, Shicheng Liu, Yada Zhu
items.x: Multi-agent systems built from frozen language models communicate through text, which discards the internal state the sender already computed and makes the receiver pay to rebuild it. Work on internal channels avoids that cost, framing the problem as transfer: agent A sends information to agent B. Every agent pair that must communicate needs its own transfer bridge, and every agent added to a system needs a new bridg…
items.sm: Proposes sharing agents’ internal states through a common pool and studies how state representation interacts with the mechanism used to incorporate it.

items.t: Close Enough is Nowhere Near: Fidelity-Consumability Decoupling in KV Caches
items.a: Adam Deng, Shicheng Liu, Yada Zhu
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems communicate in text, which is lossy and wasteful: the sender throws away the reading it already did. A growing literature instead transmits the KV cache, the natural carrier of that reading. We study the most appealing form of the idea: both models stay frozen and the sender's cache is substituted for the reader's with nothing trained. It does not work, and the obstruction belongs to the reade…
items.sm: Finds that directly substituting another frozen model’s KV cache fails, and that cache similarity does not reliably predict whether the receiving model can use it.

items.t: Bias Control and Injection for Multi-Agent Aggregation
items.a: Sungjae Lee, Soheil Abbasloo, Jabin Koo, Jungseul Ok
items.x: Multi-agent reasoning with large language models (LLMs) raises a central question for collective decision-making: when agents disagree, whose decision should be trusted? Resolving such disagreements is difficult because agents' decisions are susceptible to non-semantic biases such as majority pressure and response-style preferences, which can obscure the quality of the underlying reasoning. Our analysis shows how bia…
items.sm: Proposes combining agents’ answers by reducing presentation biases and deliberately introducing biases to measure decision instability as a signal of reliability.

items.t: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Leyang Shen, Yaxin Gong, Yang Zhang, Chenxiao Fan, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Fuli Feng
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the f…
items.sm: Trains a supervisory agent to detect goal drift and redirect agents during execution, using separate mechanisms for deciding when and how to intervene.

items.t: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions
items.a: Liangjie Huang, Henry Peng Zou, Wei-Chieh Huang, Wooseong Yang, Yuwei Han, Philip S. Yu
items.x: LLM systems increasingly rely on groups of agents that discuss, critique, and check one another, assuming that peers will catch individual errors. We test this assumption against a minimal adversary. In a ten-agent factual discussion, one or three adversarial agents repeatedly assert a plausible false answer. After each round we probe each benign agent's private answer through a separate call whose response is hidden…
items.sm: Finds that adversarial agents repeating false answers can change benign agents’ private answers during group discussions, even without corresponding public agreement.

items.t: A Responsibility-Centered Coordination Mechanism for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Thi-Nhung Nguyen, Viet-Thanh Pham, Linhao Luo, Thuy-Trang Vu, Dinh Phung
items.x: Centralized orchestration provides comprehensive multi-agent coordination but creates bottlenecks in scalability, adaptability, and collective performance. Decentralized approaches alleviate these bottlenecks by distributing coordination across agents, yet often leave responsibility for delegated dependencies and failure recovery unclear. To address this gap, we propose RCM, a responsibility-centered coordination mec…
items.sm: Proposes decentralized coordination through explicit commitments that preserve agents’ responsibilities as they delegate tasks and manage failures across delegation chains.

items.t: SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Giancarlo Maldonado Cárdenas, Carlos A. Astudillo, Nelson L. S. da Fonseca
items.x: Large-scale multi-agent ecosystems require mechanisms for discovering suitable agents without exposing entire registries to a large language model (LLM) orchestrator. The challenge is not only to retrieve relevant Agent Cards from a growing registry, but also to maintain a compact candidate context, since each additional candidate increases prompt size, inference cost, latency, and the risk of exceeding the model con…
items.sm: Introduces a retrieval method that uses weighted structural and lexical signals to find suitable agents while limiting the candidate information shown to an orchestrator.

items.t: FRACTAL: A Self-Similar Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds
items.x: We present FRACTAL, a self-similar multi-agent architecture for recursive goal decomposition, in which the same five-component organizational pattern -- Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta-Observer -- recurs at every level of a decomposition tree. We make four formal contributions: (1) a communication bound showing intra-node cost is linear in ensemble size and round count (O(kr)) under a t…
items.sm: Proposes a recursive multi-agent architecture and derives conditional bounds on communication costs, agreement, and task decomposition depth.

items.t: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.a: Yanchen Deng, Jianguo Huang, Yao Long Teng, Yixuan Li, Handuo Zhang, Ning Wang, Liangcai Su, Xinyu Wang
items.x: Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning. Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins. Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates…
items.sm: Introduces hierarchical task planning that tracks dependencies, delegates execution to local orchestrators, and revises task decomposition when accumulated results prove insufficient.

items.t: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
items.a: Guowei Xu, Zhenting Qi, Amani Kiruga, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Yilun Du
items.x: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralize…
items.sm: Trains decentralized agents to learn both task actions and participation bids, allowing coordination patterns to adapt without a central coordinator.

items.t: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems
items.a: Abhinav Kumar, Rediet Abebe, Eugene Bagdasarian, Sahar Abdelnabi
items.x: As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become increasingly important. Recent incidents have already revealed unplanned coordination between agents, highlighting the safety implications of these interactions. Yet prior studies of agent negotiation often use stylized games and simulated bargaining, leaving open how these behaviors develop during …
items.sm: Studies coding agents negotiating shared computing access and reports that they develop persistent informal rules and commitments during extended work.

items.t: Emergent Discrimination and Polarization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Nestor Caticha, João Henrique Sant'Ana, Felippe Alves, Davi Bastos Costa, Mariana Mercucci, Juan P. Neirotti, Otavio Citton, Renato Vicente
items.x: We study theoretically how discrimination and polarization can emerge in a population of learning agents. Each agent uses an adaptive linear decision layer to map a language-model embedding of an issue to a binary opinion and maintains an evolving estimate of how much it trusts every other agent. Through pairwise interactions, agents update both their decision weights and trust estimates using an online Bayesian rule…
items.sm: Models how learning agents update opinions and trust through interactions, examining how arbitrary group labels and biased perceptions can produce discrimination and polarization.

items.t: The Model Knows Better: Defending Medical Multi-Agent Systems Against Prompt Injection
items.a: Fardin Ahsan Sakib, Ziwei Zhu, Ozlem Uzuner
items.x: Medical multi-agent systems, in which LLM agents discuss a case, are increasingly studied for clinical decision support. Prompt injection, text that an attacker adds to a model's input, can manipulate LLMs into wrong decisions. How it affects these systems, and how to protect them, remains unclear. Across two systems, two model families and three benchmarks, a single injected passage succeeds in up to 61% of cases, a…
items.sm: Finds that prompt injections can mislead medical agent teams and proposes checking clinical judgments against patient findings as a defense requiring no additional training.

items.t: Interoperability of Artificial Intelligence agents
items.v: Repository of the University of Ljubljana (University of Ljubljana)
items.sm: Examines interoperability between independently developed agents by comparing A2A, ANP, A2A over SLIM, and a REST baseline.

items.t: Solving operating room scheduling problems using large language model based multi-agent architecture
items.a: Chu Tang, Qu Wei, Haitao Liu, Zekun Jiang, Xiaobo Zhou, Yu Cao, Kang Li
items.sm: Evaluates collaborating agents that iteratively generate and refine operating room scheduling code, reporting higher feasible schedule rates than single-agent and conventional multi-agent baselines.

items.t: Version 6.9.24 - AI-KM: Agent Preset, Agent Swarm, and Agent Scaffold
items.a: Haolin Wen, Yidan Li, Jingwei Xie, Yuqi Li, Shuai Liu
items.sm: Updates AI-KM with portable agent definitions, organized multi-agent collaboration, and a shared execution foundation for workloads using operational data.

items.t: Resource-sensitive certification of tool-augmented agent swarms: Coalgebraic semantics and LangGraph validation
items.sm: Proposes formal certification and a trace checker to verify that agent swarm executions satisfy permissions, budgets, provenance, memory, audit, and answer-support requirements.

items.t: Agent Status Protocol (ASP): A Lightweight Specification for State Reporting in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Diego Gosmar, Deborah A. Dahl, Emmett Coin, Csaba Bolyós, Andreas Zettl
items.x: The Agent Status Protocol (ASP) defines a lightweight way for heterogeneous AI agents to report their operational state to a status server, and for observers such as dashboards to receive that state as soon as it changes. Agents push small JSON events over HTTP POST; the server exposes the aggregated state to observers over Server-Sent Events (SSE). Because an agent that has crashed, hung or been compromised cannot b…
items.sm: Defines a protocol for agents to report operational states, combining live updates with heartbeat monitoring and external observations to detect failures or stalled progress.

items.t: Breaking LLM Pricing Collusion via Asymmetric Update Frequencies
items.a: Haoyu Dong, Yuxin Geng, Xingru Chen
items.v: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
items.sm: Studies whether delayed competitor information and unequal pricing update frequencies disrupt collusion among language model pricing agents.

items.t: Algorithmic Collusion Without Deterrence: Auditing the Punishment Mechanism in Q-Learning Pricing Agents
items.a: Kauê Lopes de Moraes, Rodrigo De-Losso
items.x: Independent tabular Q-learning agents repricing in a simulated Bertrand duopoly converge to supracompetitive prices, and the seminal evidence attributes this to a learned reward-punishment scheme: undercut your rival and it retaliates, so deviation never pays. This mechanistic reading is what turns high prices into a cartel, and into a regulatory target. We replicate the environment of Calvano et al. (2020) and confi…
items.sm: Replicates high pricing among Q-learning agents but finds that apparent retaliation can reflect general policy dynamics rather than selective punishment of undercutting.

items.t: Game-Theoretic Instability of Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Swarms: Algorithmic Tacit Collusion, Recursive Reward Hacking, and Deterministic Physical-Layer Interdiction via Human-in-Command (HIC) and PHOENIX_ROUTER
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues that autonomous agent swarms can develop collusion and escalating reward exploitation, and proposes human command and physical infrastructure controls.

items.t: Unilateral Cooperation: LLM Pricing in the Grip of an Extortioner
items.a: Junnan Li, Yuxin Geng, Xingru Chen
items.v: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
items.sm: Finds that an LLM pricing agent facing an extortionate opponent repeatedly chooses high prices, allowing the opponent to control their relative payoffs.

items.t: Do tool-call interfaces carry the measurement conditions of their inputs? A preregistered audit of Model Context Protocol tool schemas
items.sm: Proposes auditing public MCP tool schemas to determine whether they capture measurement conditions such as units, methods, specimens, devices, and timing.

items.t: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows
items.a: Kaixiang Wang, Zhaijiacheng Zhou, Jiong Lou, Jie Li
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on generative models for expert execution, workflow planning, and artifact review. Yet many coordination operations require only bounded decisions, such as selecting the next expert or judging artifact quality. Profiling three representative MAS frameworks, we find that routing and review account for 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens. However, replacing these operations with low-cost de…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent framework that uses lightweight decision models for coordination while retaining generative models for task execution and corrective feedback.

items.t: Adaptive Switching Between Self-Reinforcement and Mutual Reinforcement in Multi-Agent Systems: A Dynamic Framework for Individual and Collective Intelligence Optimization
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes dynamically switching agents between individual learning and collaborative reinforcement according to task demands, uncertainty, interaction quality, and resource limits.

items.t: Federation over Harness
items.a: Dixi Yao, Tahseen Rabbani, Tian Li
items.x: Modern LLM-powered agents increasingly improve through experience sharing, where distributed agents distill local reasoning experience into reusable knowledge, such as a shared insight library. Existing approaches, however, still heavily rely on manually designed prompts and workflows that determine both how local agents extract useful reasoning traces and how a central/global agent aggregates them to obtain common p…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that automatically evolves instructions and workflows for distributed agents solving tasks, sharing reflections, and maintaining collective knowledge.

items.t: CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre-Registered Study of 465 Agent-Authored Pull Requests
items.a: Lo Gullstrand Heander, Markus Borg, Emma Söderberg, Christofer Rydenfält
items.x: Context: Organizations increasingly delegate code review to multi-agent large language model (LLM) pipelines billed per token. Low code quality raises human maintenance effort, but its effect on agent review cost has not been measured. Objective: We test whether baseline CodeHealth predicts the token cost of agentic review and fix beyond pull request (PR) footprint. Method: In a pre-registered observational study, we…
items.sm: Reports that higher baseline CodeHealth predicts lower token costs for automated review and repair across 465 agent-authored pull requests, accounting for change size.

items.t: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Han Shen, Qifu Tyler Sun, Fanyang Meng, Ye Wang, Yongsheng Liang
items.x: Collaborative edge large language model (LLM) systems often require repeated prefill computation when task contexts are transferred between agents. Reusing previously computed key--value (KV) caches can eliminate this overhead, but requires KV-cache delivery before the receiving agent begins decoding. Under strict deadlines and unreliable edge links, complete KV cache transfer may be infeasible, making the timely del…
items.sm: Proposes prioritizing useful cached attention data and adapting error recovery to transfer context between edge agents over unreliable links before deadlines.

items.t: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.a: Bingxiang He, Pengqi Sun, Shihao Peng, Shaoxuan Li, Huiyu Xiao, Hongjian Shi, Zixuan Fu, Ziqing Qiao
items.x: Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design a data action…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent system that separates execution from analysis to support varied training-data changes during automated supervised fine-tuning research.

items.t: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale
items.a: Zeqian Huang, Mingyue Tang, Aonan Guan, Qiming Sun, Pengzhou He
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes how AI agents invoke external tools. MCP servers expose tools through a declared contract consisting of a name, description, and argument schema. In typical local deployments, client-side approval of a tool call grants the underlying server process broad host filesystem permissions rather than restricting it to the declared operation. We study the resulting vulnerability …
items.sm: Introduces a system for detecting when attacker-controlled MCP tool arguments enable filesystem access beyond the tool's declared purpose and deployment boundaries.

items.t: Approve What, Exactly? Effect Binding and Trusted Rendering for Agent Step-Up Authorization
items.a: Sai Varun Kodathala, Prashanth Pollishetty, Jaylen Cargill
items.x: AI agents now pause for approval before they send money, delete files or email outsiders, and that approval is usually treated as a second factor. We argue it is one only when compromising the agent cannot produce it and when it names exactly what it approves, and we test both conditions. We define twelve attacks on the approval path, including decoy recipients, amount cancellation, card padding, label spoofing, enro…
items.sm: Audits agent approval mechanisms, identifies weaknesses in binding consent to actions, and introduces a gateway designed to display and authorize precise effects.

items.t: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
items.a: Mingda Zhang, Yun Huang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Rui Qian, Qichao Zhao, Tiesunlong Shen, Na Zhao
items.x: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursiv…
items.sm: Proposes improving agent orchestration through nested self-play loops that select informative tasks and assess skills by temporarily removing them.

items.sm: Announces The Agentic Scientist and argues that giving coding agents research problems often produces hyperparameter optimization rather than scientific investigation.

items.t: @OfirPress: Great to see more teams starting to explore the agent swarm domain using ProgramBench!
items.sm: Reports that more teams are using ProgramBench to explore agent swarms.

items.sm: Provides a benchmark for evaluating AI agents as teammates.
