items.t: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
items.a: Tan, Zhou, Agrawal, Zhang et al.
items.sm: Proposes periodically clearing agents' accumulated search histories and restarting from the best candidate to overcome stagnation in automated research.

items.t: @ViC305: 🚀 𝗧𝗪𝗢 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦 𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗦𝗣𝗔𝗥𝗞! One main frontier level agent running Qwen3.8-Flash Next. Up to eight concurrent sub a…
items.sm: Reports running a coordinating model and up to eight delegated workers together on one NVIDIA DGX Spark, sharing a million-token worker cache.

items.t: LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation: A multi-vocal literature review
items.a: Zeeshan Rasheeda, Muhammad Waseema, Kai-Kristian Kemella, Mika Saari, Pekka Abrahamsson
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled multi-agent systems to perform autonomous code generation for complex tasks. Despite the recent growth in research and industrial applications in this area, there is little work on synthesizing evidence from both academic and industrial sources to capture the current state of research on LLM-based multi-agent systems for code generation. To this end, we conducted a Multi-Voca…
items.sm: Reviews academic and industry literature on LLM multi-agent code generation, covering motivations, benchmarks, models, challenges, proposed solutions, and research directions.

items.t: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: In LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), a local mistake can propagate as other agents build on it, turning a correctable error into a failed task. Diagnosing completed runs or repeatedly re-executing them to search for corrections does not provide a learned policy for intervening while execution is still in progress. We present Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework for learning when and how to re…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that learns when and how to repair ongoing multi-agent executions using training examples derived from verified corrections.

items.t: Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Memory Management, Coordination Failures and Semantic Conflict Resolution
items.sm: Reviews multi-agent coordination failures, memory management limitations, and approaches to resolving conflicting information in shared memory.

items.t: PFedMA: Who Should Join Next as Federated Multi-Agent Orchestration Evolves?
items.a: Shuai Li, Shengyuan Liu, Fan Qi, Xiaoshan Yang
items.x: Federated Multi-Agent Systems (FedMAS) offer a promising paradigm for collaborative reasoning among LLM-based agents while keeping raw client data decentralized. However, reliable multi-round collaboration remains challenging. Agent selection must take into consideration evolving task requirements and the agent's historical reliability, while privacy rules must adapt to changing collaboration contexts and meet the cl…
items.sm: Proposes a federated multi-agent framework that uses collaboration history to select agents, evaluate responses, refine queries, and accommodate differing privacy requirements.

items.t: Towards Adaptive and Real-Survey-Aligned Simulated Urban Mobility Behaviour of Generative Agents
items.a: Yves Bru, Kamaldeep Singh Oberoi, Benoit Gaudou
items.x: In existing agent-based simulations of multimodal urban mobility, agents, representing humans, choose their travel modes either using discrete choice or machine learning models fitted on structured travel survey data, or with rules explicitly written by the domain experts. Such approaches fix a priori the agents' possible behaviour space. Hence, a factor absent from variables or rules cannot affect agents' decisions.…
items.sm: Examines how generative agents could represent adaptive urban travel choices while aligning simulated transport decisions with real survey data.

items.t: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States
items.a: Sarath Shekkizhar, Prathyusha Jwalapuram, Zixuan Ke, Vaidehi Patil, Jiayu Wang, Srijan Bansal, Trong Huy Nguyen, Dingfeng Jiang
items.x: Agents are increasingly interacting with other agents that act for different principals (people or organizations on whose behalf they work), such as a buyer's personal agent negotiating with an enterprise's seller agent. In such agent-to-agent (A2A) scenarios, each agent has its own environment and holds information and authority that the other cannot see. Moreover, the interests of each agent may be aligned (coopera…
items.sm: Derives a failure taxonomy from over 2,500 agent interactions involving separate principals, private information, distinct authority, and varying degrees of cooperation.

items.t: When Extremists Enter LLM Societies: Investigating Extreme Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Guo Chen, Huaijin Xie, Ziwen Li, Reed Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi, Bingbing Xu, Junjie Huang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly serve as computational actors in multi-agent social simulations. While existing work emphasizes representative personas and average-case behavior, social science shows that persistent tail actors can disproportionately shape collective dynamics. We study this regularity in controlled LLM-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS). In these systems, such actors cannot be reduced…
items.sm: Introduces a framework for studying extremist agents in LLM social simulations by controlling their prevalence, placement, and interaction rules.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Analyzes agent swarms, replication, persistent operational patterns, and institutional incident responses, arguing that unsupervised operation can preserve externally imposed objectives.

items.t: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
items.a: Qianru Meng, Xi Zhang, Konstantinos Papakostas, Congfeng Cao, Wenxiang Hu, Tianyi Lu, Xiao Zhang, Lun Zhou
items.x: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program…
items.sm: Introduces a scientific agent swarm that uses shared experimental feedback to revise hypotheses and implementations and recombine useful components across agents.

items.t: Adaptive Reasoning and Collaborative Reasoning Switching Across Parallel Worlds of Large Language Models
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes multiple language model reasoning instances that adapt their strategies and switch between independent work and collaboration according to uncertainty, progress, and resources.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a framework combining separate memory perspectives, adaptive individual memory, shared memory, and memory exchange across different language models.

items.t: Adaptive Switching Between Parallel-World Self-Planning and Collaborative Planning for Multiple Large Language Models
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes parallel planning instances of a language model that explore different strategies and adaptively switch between independent planning and collaboration.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes language model instances with different selection criteria that independently evaluate candidates and adaptively decide when collaborative selection is needed.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes parallel routing instances that develop distinct policies and switch between independent routing, collaborative routing, and coordination with other language models.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes a local language model orchestration runtime that uses Codex for bounded tasks and maintains persistent memory, provenance, and observation tools.

items.t: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
items.a: Shubhendu Trivedi, Jacob Eisenstein, Alekh Agarwal, Ian Gemp, Michael Kaisers, Adam Fisch
items.x: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simpl…
items.sm: Analyzes welfare losses when AI agents bid for user prompts in first-price auctions and argues that agentic market characteristics may reduce these losses.

items.t: Same Context, Different Agents: A Behavioral Study of Semantic Layers, Multi-Agent Orchestration and Memory Compaction in Data Agents
items.a: Zhivar Sourati, Marianne Menglin Liu, Zheng Wang, Rongguang Wang, Sai Ashish Somayajula, Tao Sheng, Kyu J. Han, Sujith Ravi
items.x: Answering questions over heterogeneous data means combining evidence from files, databases, documents and the web. Data agents automate this, but their success depends on context. Three context-engineering techniques (CETs) help by shaping it: semantic layers describe the data, orchestration splits work among agents, and compaction condenses interaction history. Existing studies validate each CET alone, leaving open …
items.sm: Studies how semantic layers, agent orchestration, and memory compaction affect behavior, accuracy, and cost across seven language models and 1,514 data tasks.

items.t: Evolve Together, Fall into Place: How Social Scaffolding Shapes Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Seojin Hwang, Youngmin Choi, Hwanhee Lee
items.x: Recent work lets LLM agents evolve their own harness, up to the team itself. Yet in human groups, the same abilities achieve different outcomes under different social conditions. items.sm: Introduces AGORA to study how team composition and interdependence shape evolving agent teams, finding that suitable social structures improve performance over individual evolution.

items.t: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models
items.a: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Hao Jiang, Xin Gao, Annan Wang, Xingwei Qu, Yichi Zhang, Chau Yuen
items.x: Multi-agent systems allow language models to solve tasks collaboratively by sharing complementary information. These systems typically communicate through text, while recent approaches also explore exchanging internal model states. items.sm: Introduces a communication interface that transfers facts between different language models using shared word indices and receiver-specific internal representations without additional training.

items.t: BRIDGE: Selective Boundary Repair with Dependency Graph Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Encheng Su, Pengze Li, Ziheng Hua, Qiucheng Yu, Jianyu Wu, Chen Tang, Yizhou Wang, Lintao Wang

items.sm: Introduces BRIDGE, a runtime framework that uses dependency graphs and diagnostic perturbations to identify and selectively repair failed handoffs between agents.

items.t: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes
items.a: Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are commonly organized around two coordination regimes. Centralized coordination provides explicit control but can create a bottleneck at a single coordination locus, whereas decentralized coordination offers local autonomy but must achieve effective collaboration through distributed decisions and experience. These trade-offs motivate a systematic study of th…
items.sm: Introduces a continuous framework for studying centralized and decentralized coordination by varying delegated task granularity and how work is assigned among agent branches.

items.t: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
items.a: Yuxiang Lai, Jike Zhong, Chengzhi Liu, Ming Li, Haonan Wang, Xiaofeng Yang, Liang Zhao, Youbao Tang
items.x: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems to automate complex computer-use workflows, yet existing benchmarks mostly assume consistent, cooperative environments. items.sm: Introduces a framework and 600-scenario benchmark for generating verifiable conflicts that test how computer-use agents handle contradictory information and competing access.

items.t: Learning Adaptive Deliberation Control for Reliable Recognition with Multi-Agent Language Models
items.a: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai
items.x: Multi-agent deliberation can improve recognition by criticizing and revising candidate answers, but fixed controls cannot respond to changes in disagreement or reasoning quality. We present an adaptive multi-agent controller (ADMA) that learns continuous policies for proposal, challenge, arbitration, and coordination while keeping the task model frozen. Shared trace features describe quality, agreement, and progress,…
items.sm: Trains an adaptive controller for multi-agent deliberation and reports accuracy improvements when transferring it across tasks while keeping the underlying language model fixed.

items.t: ECMR: Evidence-Aware Deliberation Control for Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning
items.a: Yuan Liu, Haoyue Peng, Fanliang Hu, Lei Huang, Wenli Cai
items.x: Multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems typically commit to a deliberation protocol before inference. A fixed protocol cannot allocate computation differently to resolved and unresolved instances, and it may mistake repeated support for independent confirmation. We study this failure as semantic false consensus: a confident group answer supported by narrow, duplicated, or correlated rationales. We introduce EC…
items.sm: Introduces an evidence-aware controller that adapts agent deliberation using support independence, contradictions, verification history, and remaining resources to address misleading consensus.

items.t: MAS-Gate: Unlocking Multi-Agent System Lifecycle via Node-Centric Quantification

items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) can solve complex problems beyond the reach of a single agent by decomposing tasks and coordinating complementary capabilities. Despite extensive research on MAS, existing work largely focuses on specific aspects or individual phases of their development and operation, resulting in fragmented perspectives with objectives and signals that are difficult to reco…
items.sm: Introduces a node-based measurement framework intended to connect multi-agent workflow design, runtime intervention, and retrospective attribution using execution graphs.

items.t: Narrowing the Collaboration Gap, Probably
items.a: Mirah Shi, Marcel Hussing, Ira Globus-Harris, Natalie Collina, Aaron Roth, Surbhi Goel

How should such agents concisely communicate in a way that promotes aggregation of decision-relevant information? Communicating only proposed actions can discard decision-relevant uncertainty: two agents may prefer the same action for different reasons. We study an alternative interface in w…
items.sm: Studies communication of calibrated action probabilities, showing in a synthetic setting that sharing uncertainty can outperform sharing proposed actions alone.

items.t: Design Strategies for Multi-Agent Systems: Lessons from Four Implementations
items.a: Lucía Covarrubias, Tomás Rivero, Ignacio Bosch
items.sm: Analyzes four implemented multi-agent systems to derive ten design strategies covering orchestration, hierarchical delegation, retrieval, tools, memory, and integration.

items.t: Orchestration Frameworks for Agentic AI
items.sm: Compares LangGraph and AutoGen for orchestrating agents in connected and autonomous vehicles, covering workflow design, state management, error handling, and framework selection.

items.t: GenAI Multi‐agent Systems
items.sm: Examines how generative language models support communication, distributed reasoning, and collaborative decisions among agents in connected vehicles, traffic management, and navigation.

items.t: From Agents to Edges: Paired Optimization for Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Feng Lin, Xiaotian Yu, Yifan Yang, Aijun Li
items.x: Strong individual agents do not guarantee effective collaboration. Communication must align what one agent conveys with how another interprets and uses it. This dependency makes the communication edge a natural unit of optimization. We introduce Paired Automated Communication Optimization (PACO), which jointly optimizes the instructions at both ends of each edge and their shared communication convention in systems bu…
items.sm: Introduces PACO, which jointly refines sender and receiver instructions and shared communication conventions while keeping model weights, agent roles, and workflow structure fixed.

items.t: BLADE: Auditing Information Use for Failure Attribution in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Xiaoguang Guo, Yaohao Long, Chuxu Zhang
items.x: Large language model multi-agent systems extend individual agents' capabilities through collaboration across specialized roles, tools, and workflows. Yet collaboration makes failures harder to diagnose: one agent may misinterpret a correct result while others carry the mistake forward. Failure attribution therefore seeks to identify the responsible agent and decisive error step. Recent methods trace dependencies, but…
items.sm: Introduces BLADE, a framework requiring no training that audits how agents use received information to identify responsible agents and decisive errors.

items.t: Deliberation Within AI: A Reproducible Pipeline for Multi-Agent Deliberation Simulation
items.sm: Proposes a reproducible pipeline for simulating public deliberation with language model agents, combining persona validation, viewpoint diversity audits, and discourse quality assessment.

items.t: Identity, Incentives, and Cooperative Behavior for AI: Reverse-Engineering Multiagent Cooperation
items.x: The behavior of AI systems increasingly depends on the extent to which agents cooperate or coordinate with one another, in ways that may be desirable or not depending on the situation. Conventional explanations for cooperative behavior distinguish between purely other-regarding preferences ("altruism") and instrumental reasons for self-interested agents to cooperate. The way that agents should enact these mechanisms …
items.sm: Develops a framework for explaining cooperation among AI agents by examining identity, collective goals, altruistic preferences, and instrumental incentives.

items.t: Beyond Answer Sharing: TrueMAD for Targeted Peer Engagement in Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Dezheng Bao, Sihang Du, Renhong Huang, Zhizhang Yuan, Yifei Sun, Yang Yang

As a result, reliable reasoning may be suppressed by conflicting or majority responses, limiting achievable performance, while erroneous reas…

items.t: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
items.a: Keru Chen, Sen Lin, Yingbin Liang, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Shaofeng Zou
items.x: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), …

items.t: The Agentic Scientist: Orchestrating Coding Agents for Automated Scientific (Co-)Discovery

items.sm: Introduces a distributed pipeline that helps researchers coordinate coding agents across idea generation, experiments, analysis, and scientific report writing.

items.t: Smart Alone, Blind Together: Why Accuracy Fails to CertifyTheory of Mind in Multi-Agent Teams

Second, a module's errors are rarely independent, and dependence has a sign: positively associated errors help w…

items.t: Truthful and Expected-Payment-Optimal Model Routing in Graph-Based Agentic Workflows
items.a: Jiayuan Liu, Mingyu Guo, Jiarui Gan, Vincent Conitzer

Independent providers may also privately know their real-time unit costs and strategically m…
items.sm: Proposes an auction mechanism for routing workflow tasks among model providers that accounts for context reuse and rewards truthful reporting of execution costs.

items.t: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zhiwei Chen, Zhongtao Rao, Waikit Xiu, Yuxiang Zhang, Shuting Cui, Jian Chen, Tianxiang Zhao

items.t: Beyond Perfect Teammates: Multi-Agent Collaboration with Unreliable Colleagues
items.a: Chen Huang, Yiyang Zhang, Yuhao Wu, Yang Deng, Wenxuan Zhang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent collaboration is increasingly used to solve complex tasks by dividing work among specialized agents and integrating complementary expertise. Yet existing systems and evaluations largely rest on an implicit perfect-colleague assumption: collaborators provide correct and complete information and respond promptly to requests. In realistic teamwork, however, collaborators may return information that…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark testing whether agents recover when collaborators provide irrelevant or incomplete information or fail to respond.

items.x: As language-model-based coding agents evolve their programs and reuse code from one another, safety failures can acquire a history that extends beyond the agent in which they are detected. An unsafe change may originate in one agent, propagate through intermediate recipients, and survive subsequent revisions before an audit reveals it. Understanding this history is important for identifying the introducing change and…
items.sm: Studies how to identify the agent and program version that introduced unsafe behavior as coding agents revise and exchange code.

items.t: AgentCue: Statistical Summaries for Guiding Decentralized Multi-Agent Self-Organization
items.a: Guojun Zhu, Xinyou Chen, Kejian Zhang, Sanguo Zhang, Zhi Zhang, Doudou Zhou
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) combine multiple agents to solve complex tasks, and recent MAS scale to more than a thousand agents. At this scale, decentralized MAS remove the central orchestrator that assigns sub-tasks, and the agents, which we call workers, self-organize through their own choices of sub-tasks and collaborators on a shared board. As workers keep adding participation and collaboration records, however, th…
items.sm: Introduces statistical summaries of worker collaboration and task participation to guide decentralized agent coordination while reducing the burden of reading growing activity records.

items.t: Scaling Inference-Time Compute with Teams of Coding Agents
items.a: Keenan Samway, Daniel D'souza, Omar Darwiche Domingues, Marzieh Fadaee, Tan Yi-Chern, Nouha Dziri
items.x: Multi-agent systems promise a new axis for scaling inference: rather than having one agent think longer or sample more attempts, a task is split across many agents that work in parallel and coordinate. However, in practice, more agents can easily produce duplicate work, coordination failures, and higher costs. We therefore formulate team design as a compute allocation problem: starting from a solo agent, where should…
items.sm: Examines how delegation stage, model choice, and worker count affect coding teams, finding higher performance than solo agents at three to seven times the cost.

items.t: When Agents Talk, Secrets Travel: Topology-Driven Leakage and Recipient-Conditioned Sanitization in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems (MALS) introduce a privacy-leakage problem that conventional sensitivity-based defenses miss, since information disclosed to one authorized agent can propagate through routine coordination to an unauthorized one, without compromise or malicious behavior. This motivates topology-aware enforcement that blocks unauthorized propagation while preserving authorized disclosure. We evaluate 485 scenar…
items.sm: Studies how communication structures spread private information among agents and introduces sanitization based on each recipient's authorization and execution context.

items.t: Dream2Discern: Learning from Hard Latent Variants for Runtime Failure Prediction in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Boxuan Zhang, Jianing Zhu, Xiaotian Han, Ruixiang Tang
items.x: Reliable deployment of LLM-based multi-agent systems calls for runtime auditors that predict terminal outcomes from observed execution prefixes. These auditors typically learn from a limited corpus of trajectories with verified outcomes. Expanding this corpus requires costly execution and verification, yet broader failure coverage alone provides no explicit criterion for identifying prefixes that the current auditor …
items.sm: Trains runtime failure predictors using difficult variations of internal representations from recorded agent executions, retaining original outcome labels without collecting new executions.

items.t: OpenDGO: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Organizations Across Diverse Application Domains
items.a: Xunkai Li, Miao Zhang, Zekai Chen, Xuaner Chen, Yu liu, Rui Qian, Xun Wu, Hongchao Qin

However, these methods are largely designed and evaluated within a limited set of …
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark comparing agent organization structures across six domains and three collaboration settings under matched tasks, tools, and resource limits.

items.t: Observe, Share, or Predict? Disentangling Partner Information in Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Adrián Szlatincsán, Filippo Ziliotto, Bruno Lepri, Luciano Serafini, Massimiliano Luca, Tommaso Campari
items.x: LLMs are used as high-level controllers for embodied agents, but it remains unclear whether they support collaborative reasoning, such as anticipating a collaborator's actions in real-time teamwork without dialogue. items.sm: Tests how observing partners, sharing object knowledge, and predicting partner actions affect embodied teamwork when agents cannot exchange intentions or plans.

items.t: Think Before You Speak: Enabling Training-Free Latent Communication Between Language Models
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks in coding, mathematical logic, and iterative reasoning, especially by coordinating effectively within multi-agent systems (MAS). items.t: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
items.a: Shubham Agarwal, Akshat Gupta, Mike Heddes, Dilara Soylu, Rui Meng, Patrick Tser Jern Kon, Jiefeng Chen, Mert Cemri

items.a: Jinhao Zhou, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jiongchi Yu, Fahao Chen, Jun Wu

items.v: Communications in computer and information science
items.sm: Describes adversarial and misalignment risk simulation, alongside robustness mechanisms, for language model multi-agent systems in aerospace trusted data spaces.

items.t: TheBotCompany: Self-Organizing Multi-agent Systems for Continuous Software Development
items.a: Wenhan Lyu, Yue Xiao, Yixuan Zhang, Yifan Sun
items.v: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems have shown promise in automating software development tasks. However, most vibe-coding systems focus on completing small tasks and incremental code changes, leaving persistent, continuous software development largely unexplored. We present TheBotCompany, an open-source orchestration framework for continuous multi-agent software development. TheBotCompany introduces…
items.sm: Introduces an orchestration framework for continuous software development using milestone phases, dynamically organized agent teams, and asynchronous human oversight.

items.t: Homogenization in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Prakhar Ganesh, Kyra Wilson, Luca Zappella, Barry-John Theobald, Nicholas Apostoloff, Lucas Monteiro Paes, Nivedha Sivakumar
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) leverage interactions between agents to perform complex tasks. Despite their success, we show that these interactions can also lead to homogenization, i.e., agents converging to similar behaviors. Homogenization in MAS can reduce agent diversity and reinforce shared failures. In this paper, we operationalize homogenization using three metrics: conformity to the majority, polarization towards…
items.sm: Shows that interacting agents can converge toward shared behaviors, amplifying correlated coding errors and allowing hiring biases to persist after biased agents leave.

items.t: Fail-Open by Default: Divergent requestState Integrity Across Model Context Protocol Reference SDKs
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Audits requestState integrity protection across Python, Go, and TypeScript MCP SDKs, reporting divergent behavior and documenting a change to Python's plaintext default.

items.t: When Does Cross-Agent Peer Verification Detect Unfaithful Self- Reports? An Empirical Study of Real LLM Tool-Use Agent Trajectories
items.sm: Examines whether peer verification detects inaccurate agent self-reports across 1,980 tool-use trajectories, finding reported outcomes disagree with verified results in 13.8–31.5% of cases.

items.t: Cost-Efficient Theorem Proving via Agent Orchestration in Program Verification
items.a: Shuangjie Yao, Nikolaus Holzer, Mark Paul Santolucito, Baishakhi Ray, Suman Jana, Dongdong She
items.x: Program verification establishes software correctness through machine-checkable proofs constructed in theorem provers. It's a guarantee especially valuable for code generated by large language models (LLMs), which is fluent but carries no assurance of correctness. Almost all existing provers, however, pursue pass rates alone at whatever sampling or search budget it takes, and overlook the success-vs-cost frontier; ye…
items.sm: Introduces CoCo-Prover, which coordinates proof search and lemma dependencies to balance theorem-proving success against computational cost.

items.t: pullboard-dev/pullboard
items.x: Autonomous development for real products. Governed agents build from specs you approve, follow the rules you set, and nothing merges until another agent proves it. Your decisions, judgement and taste are the bar that work must clear. Declare your vision and let agents build it.
items.sm: Provides a development platform where agents implement approved specifications under user-defined rules and require another agent’s verification before merging.

items.t: Senguk520/dsh-multitask
items.x: A Multitask "shock absorber" plugin & agent preset for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): the main chat only plans, briefs subagents and summarizes results, while file reads, commands, search and builds all run inside subagent contexts. Four worker types, an approval gate, zero DSH source changes.
items.sm: Provides a DeepSeek Harness plugin that keeps planning in the main chat while delegating file access, commands, searches, and builds to subagents.

items.t: nicremo/dsh-cli
items.x: Let Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other agents run DeepSeek Harness (dsh) sessions in parallel: research batches, material gathering, live in the DSH web UI. Unofficial community tool.
items.sm: Enables coding agents to run parallel DeepSeek Harness sessions for research and material gathering, with activity visible in its web interface.

items.t: sisyphuslabs/dori-superagent
items.x: A proactive multi-session coding-agent harness on herdr + omo: one lead, a duty loop, many lanes, a gated merge. Plus Dori mode, the messenger-facing skill.
items.sm: Provides a coding-agent harness with a lead agent, recurring coordination, parallel work streams, merge gates, and a messaging interface.

items.t: @lydiahallie: You can now ask Claude to run subagents at a specific effort level! Make sure you're on v2.1.292+
items.sm: Reports that Claude versions 2.1.292 and later allow users to specify effort levels for subagents.

items.sm: Reports Haiku 5.5 availability in Claude Platform and Claude Code, claiming roughly 75% lower average running costs than Haiku 4.5.

items.t: JackPayne123/swarm-scaling
items.sm: Compares communicating agent teams with independent agents on code optimization, finding model-dependent results, and recalculates swarm scaling estimates across three benchmarks.

items.t: Navier-Stokes lost in translation
items.sm: Argues that Lean verification cannot establish faithful translation of mathematical arguments and identifies changed assumptions and proof methods in a Navier–Stokes formalization.

items.t: OOPMAS: Object-Oriented Multi-Agent Systems for Query-Level Workflow Generation
items.a: Qi Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Wei Cheng, Yiqun Xie, Xiaowei Jia, Haoyu Wang, Haifeng Chen
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models have shown strong performance across code generation, mathematical reasoning, and question answering. However, existing methods for automating MAS design mostly operate at the task level, producing a single fixed workflow per benchmark that is applied uniformly to all queries. This assumption fails under realistic conditions. Query difficulty varies widely wi…
items.sm: Introduces OOPMAS, which generates agents and executable coordination workflows for individual queries using object-oriented representations and accumulated execution lessons.

items.t: ST-Bench: A Spatial-Temporal Benchmark for Multi-Agent System Generation on Scientific Research Tasks
items.a: Qi Cheng, Rongchao Dong, Shengyu Chen, Licheng Liu, Dan Lu, Zhengzhang Chen, Wei Cheng, Yiqun Xie
items.x: The rapid progress of LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) has shown that they largely outperform single agents on coding, math, and QA tasks, where executable tests provide a binary success signal. Whether this advantage transfers to real scientific data analysis remains untested. We introduce ST-Bench, a benchmark designed to answer two questions: whether MAS outperform single agents on complex scientific data analy…
items.sm: Introduces ST-Bench, an expert-validated scientific data analysis benchmark comparing multi-agent systems with single agents on performance and computational cost.

items.t: SquidAgent: Parallelize Wisely, Coordinate Efficiently
items.a: Yexiong Lin, Shanshan Ye, Yu Yao, Zhen Fang, Bo Han, Tongliang Liu
items.x: LLM-based agents solve complex multi-step tasks, but sequential execution incurs substantial latency. In principle, parallelizing work across multiple agents should yield near-linear speedups. Yet existing parallel multi-agent systems often run slower than a single-agent baseline. We attribute this gap to two hidden costs that parallel execution incurs but a serial agent avoids. First, there is a re-exploration cost:…
items.sm: Proposes deciding when to parallelize agent work by accounting for execution time, duplicated context reconstruction, and reconciliation overhead.

items.t: When Debate Hurts: Model-Scale-Dependent Effects of Multi-Agent Deliberation in Psychiatric Diagnosis
items.sm: Reports that multi-agent debate reduced psychiatric diagnosis accuracy relative to zero-shot responses across repeated trials with two small models on 24 synthetic vignettes.

items.t: Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration via System One-Guided Computational Division of Labor
items.a: Zihan Zhou, Xinzhe Hu, Hanxu Yang, Liangjian Wen, Zhao Kang
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have become a promising paradigm for complex information-seeking and reasoning tasks by enabling collaborative problem solving among specialized agents. However, existing MAS frameworks tightly couple task reasoning with coordination operations, including task selection, role assignment, message routing, and context management. As interactions grow, using pow…
items.sm: Introduces S1-MAS, which assigns coordination decisions to lightweight components to reduce the token costs of multi-agent collaboration.

items.t: Beyond Corrected Memory: Execution Consistency in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zhe Yu, Zixuan Wang, Peidong Wang, Hehai Lin, Ruochen Zhao, Chengwei Qin
items.x: Shared memory coordinates agents' actions, but correct records do not establish that those actions satisfy task requirements. Memory governance and failure diagnosis regulate or inspect recorded information; they do not by themselves establish whether it is sufficient to judge task duties. We define execution consistency through duties governing state use, information handoffs, and final-state agreement, with explici…
items.sm: Defines evidence requirements for assessing agent execution duties and shows that identical retained records can conceal both compliant and violating behavior.

items.t: Where Rules End and Judges Begin: Measuring the Judgment Boundary in Multi-Agent Systems Security
items.a: Shaswata Mitra, Raj Patel, Subash Neupane, Sudip Mittal, Md Rayhanur Rahman, Shahram Rahimi
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) engage tools, share memory, and delegate tasks, often encountering adversarial content. Current defenses for MAS are typically evaluated in isolation, focusing on one attack type at a time, which can lead to costly and hard-to-audit outcomes. This study organizes defenses into five principles, implementing them as DEFER1 (DEterministic-First Enforcement with Residual judgment), whi…
items.sm: Introduces DEFER1, combining deterministic security checks with model judges, and reports reducing attack success from approximately 30% to 3% across four domains.

items.t: Sequential Probabilistic Uncertainty Estimation for Parallel Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems
items.a: Tunyu Zhang, Zihao Zhao, Yusong Zhao, Haizhou Shi, Zhuohang Li, Haoxian Chen, Hao Wang, Dimitris N. Metaxas
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have attracted growing attention for improving reasoning through interaction among multiple agents. In this work, we focus on parallel multi-agent reasoning systems, where several agents solve the same problem over multiple rounds and aggregate their outputs into a final answer. Despite their strong reasoning performance, uncertainty estimation for such systems remains underexplore…
items.sm: Introduces SAUCE, a training-free method that estimates multi-agent reasoning uncertainty by tracking agreement and generation uncertainty across successive rounds.

items.t: Disentangling Models from Personas in Heterogeneous LLM Simulations
items.x: Multi-agent simulations with large language models (LLMs) often operate networks of agents with a single base model. This overlooks the inter-model effects which may dominate engagement dynamics in real-world deployments. To show this, we simulate a heterogeneous social network powered by several different base models and show that the amount of engagement an agent receives depends more on its base model than on its …
items.sm: Finds that agents’ underlying language models influence engagement more than assigned personas in simulated social networks, with stronger effects as model diversity increases.

items.t: Decoupled Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.x: Learned orchestration can automatically construct effective language-model multi-agent systems, but existing approaches couple planning to fixed worker pools and train decomposition and collaboration from the same terminal outcome, limiting transfer and obscuring credit assignment. We introduce DeOrch, which separates worker-agnostic planning from concrete worker selection. Its two-stage planner first decomposes the …
items.sm: Introduces DeOrch, which separates task planning from worker selection and adapts worker assignments using behavioral probes and online feedback.

items.t: Large Language Model Orchestration under Heterogeneous Preferences via Explicit Persona Inference
items.a: Shuqing Shi, Ziyan Wang, Milind Tambe, Yali Du
items.x: LLM orchestration investigates how an orchestrator coordinates a group of autonomous agents to achieve common goals or maximize collective welfare. The agents are typically heterogeneous, each holding a private preference that it pursues but does not reveal. Inferring such hidden preferences from behavior has been a subject of long-standing research in game theory and multi-agent systems. The core challenge lies in m…
items.sm: Introduces HARP, an orchestration framework that explicitly updates numerical beliefs about agents’ hidden preferences from their observed actions.

items.t: Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems
items.a: Ishita Soryan, Yashvir Singh, Divya Anand
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Studies cooperation and deception in repeated games with Qwen agents, finding cooperation depends strongly on payoffs while added scam incentives produce no detectable deception increase.

items.t: Debate, Not Voting: Agentic Arbitration over Weak Optical Chemical Structure Recognition Models
items.x: Optical chemical structure recognition (OCSR) turns a picture of a molecule into a machine-readable string, and it stands between decades of printed chemistry and any computational use. On real documents individual models remain unreliable. Over a 1000-molecule sample of MolParser, three readers score $46.0\%$, $43.4\%$ and $42.4\%$ exact match, yet at least one of them is right on $60.8\%$ of molecules. That gap is …
items.sm: Uses tool-assisted agent debate to reconcile chemical structure recognition outputs, increasing exact-match accuracy from the best reader’s 46.0% to 61.9% on 1,000 molecules.

items.t: DHCG: Dynamic Construction of Hierarchical Collaboration Graphs for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Jie Ren, Jiakang Yuan, Chenyu Huang, Hezeer Ma, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have demonstrated strong capabilities in solving complex problems across diverse domains. Recently, the dynamic orchestration of agent systems has become an important research direction. However, existing methods suffer from limited composition, misaligned dependencies, and inflexible scale, restricting their ability to adapt to reasoning requirements during execution. To address t…
items.sm: Introduces DHCG, which dynamically builds hierarchical agent collaboration graphs using query requirements and execution feedback to adjust team composition and size.

items.t: SwarmSpec: A Declarative Specification Format for Multi-Agent Swarm Architectures
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Defines SwarmSpec, a declarative format for documenting multi-agent architectures, operational requirements, interfaces, policies, approvals, and execution constraints.

items.t: Swarm Patterns and Compositions: A Catalogue of Multi-Agent Coordination Structures
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Catalogues 25 multi-agent coordination patterns and 12 composition archetypes, with explanations of design tradeoffs and illustrative SwarmSpec configurations.

items.t: WorkflowOps: Learning Agent Collaboration Priors for Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestration
items.a: Qi Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Wei Cheng, Zhengzhang Chen, Xiaowei Jia, Haoyu Wang, Haifeng Chen
items.x: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex knowledge work, yet their orchestration layers remain largely memoryless: each new task is decomposed, assigned, and executed from scratch with no benefit from prior successful executions. We present WorkflowOps, a multi-agent workflow orchestration framework that learns agent collaboration priors from historical workflows and expands its agent pool on demand …
items.sm: Introduces WorkflowOps, which uses historical collaboration patterns to guide workflow construction and creates additional agents when existing capabilities are insufficient.

items.t: Lachesis: Lifetime-Aware KV Cache Placement for Agent Serving across HBM and High-Bandwidth Flash
items.a: Jaehoon Yang, Jeongmin Lee, Haneul Park, Seung Yul Lee, Nam Sung Kim, Jae W. Lee
items.x: Large language model (LLM) serving is increasingly dominated by agentic workloads, in which agents and their sub-agents accumulate context as KV cache across many requests, consuming substantial memory. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) is a promising solution, providing an order of magnitude greater capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth, but its finite write endurance is the key limiting factor. Our key insight is that KV c…
items.sm: Introduces Lachesis, which places agent KV caches across high-bandwidth memory and flash according to expected lifetime to reduce flash writes.

items.t: Humanize: Judgement Engineering for Agentic Coding
items.a: Sihao Liu, Ligeng Zhu, Zijian Zhang, Dongyun Zou, Zhengyang Zhang, Changye Li, Song Bian, Song Han
items.x: Agentic coding makes code generation cheap, but reliable completion remains difficult: the agent that writes the code is a weak judge of whether it is done. We present Humanize, a multi-agent orchestration workflow for agentic coding built around judgement engineering: explicit, mechanically enforced decisions at the boundaries between planning, implementation, review, and learning. A human approves a plan contract, …
items.sm: Introduces Humanize, a coding workflow combining human-approved plans, separate builder and reviewer agents, and mechanically enforced checks for completion.

items.t: Reproduction code for "Collaboration topology governs inference-cache reuse in language-model agent teams"

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Provides reproduction code for research examining how collaboration topology affects inference-cache reuse in language-model agent teams.

items.sm: Reviews research on agent coordination, trust, adoption, and autonomous data science to connect findings across fragmented areas of agentic AI.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reports that Python's MCP reference SDK automatically protects requestState integrity, while Go and TypeScript lack equivalent protection by default.

items.t: Persistent Memory in Multi-Agent LLM Inference: What It Costs, What It Buys, and When You Can Tell
items.a: Hochan Son, Kyungdoe Han, Jaehan Koh, Xiaowu Dai, Wenlu Xu, Guang Cheng
items.x: Decomposing long-context inference across cooperating agents bounds the active KV cache per call rather than total evidence, which matters when KV-cache memory binds. Many such systems add a persistent tier storing and recalling reasoning traces, usually validated by an ablation reporting an accuracy gain. We measure both on one three-tier agent architecture. Decomposition delivers: peak KV working set of 14.3 MiB pe…
items.sm: Finds that splitting inference among agents reduces peak cache memory, while persistent reasoning storage adds memory without detectable accuracy gains on tested benchmarks.

items.t: Coupled but Late: Turn-Taking Between Full-Duplex Speech Models in Unscripted Dialogue
items.a: Lichen Zhu, Yueqian Lin, Yiheng Wang, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen
items.x: Full-duplex speech models are trained to converse with a person, but they are increasingly made to converse with each other, in self-play data generation, agent societies, and model-based evaluation. In that loop no human absorbs a timing error: each model's turn-taking is the other's input. We ask what timing the loop settles into. Two PersonaPlex-7B instances exchange audio tokens on a shared clock in unscripted co…
items.sm: Finds that two speech models coordinate conversational turns but respond later than humans and show limited anticipation of their partner's turn ending.

items.t: RA-MoWE: Workflow-Affinity Embeddings for Query Clustering and Agentic Workflow Generation
items.a: Qi Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Wei Cheng, Yiqun Xie, Haoyu Wang, Haifeng Chen, Xiaowei Jia
items.x: Agentic workflows enable large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks by coordinating reasoning, tool use, and verification. However, a workflow optimized for an entire task collection can overlook differences in the reasoning strategies that individual queries need, while searching for a new workflow for every query repeats costly optimization. To address this tradeoff, we introduce RA-MoWE, a framework that …
items.sm: Introduces query embeddings based on reference workflow performance to group similar queries and generate reusable workflows tailored to each group.

items.t: Visual Orchestration Tax in Agentic VLM Pipelines: Auditing and Certifying Visual Evidence Reuse
items.x: Agentic VLM pipelines increasingly pass the same static visual evidence through multiple specialist agents and tools. This design creates an orchestration-level redundancy mode: semantically unchanged images are repeatedly reconstructed as image-conditioned requests at the VLM API boundary. We call this phenomenon visual orchestration tax and develop a measurement-to-certification framework for visual evidence reuse …
items.sm: Introduces methods to audit and certify visual evidence reuse, reporting substantial redundant image processing across two agentic vision pipelines.

items.t: electric-dragon-80000v/pi-cowboy
items.x: 🤠 Agent orchestrator for pi. It can manage Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, pi, pig and pi-bolt as subagents and handover sessions in between them. Runs subagents in background Herdr panes, isolated in copy-on-write Git worktrees.
items.sm: Coordinates coding subagents across several tools, supports session handoffs, and runs background agents in isolated Git worktrees.

items.t: @mitchellh: I've published a new, general-purpose terminal specification that gives any program a way to tell the terminal…
items.sm: Announces a terminal specification that lets programs report their activity and status, addressing difficulties tracking agents and other running tools.

items.t: JoahanMorales/upiixia-agentic-kit
items.x: Multi-agent coordination kit for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor & Gemini CLI: parallel AI agents with claims, leases, bounded loops, reviews and merges over Git.
items.sm: Coordinates parallel coding agents across several tools using task claims, leases, bounded execution loops, reviews, and Git merges.

items.t: Verifying Coordination in Parallel Coding Agents: NP-Bench and a Scheduling Planner
items.sm: Introduces NP-Bench and a scheduling planner that partitions coding agents' work scopes and orders merges by dependencies to prevent integration conflicts.

items.t: Import AI 475: Swarm scaling
items.sm: Summarizes evidence that parallel agent teams can reduce waiting time while consuming more tokens, with coordination losses limiting gains as teams grow.

items.t: Why agent swarms could be the next scaling law
items.sm: Reviews evidence for agent swarm scaling, emphasizing collaboration training, diminishing returns, uncertain capability gains, and coordination choices that affect efficiency and risk.

items.t: @rohanpaul_ai: Turns out coding agents don't need a boss: New Microsoft paper finds that bigger teams of coding agents score …
items.sm: Reports that a Microsoft study found larger coding teams improved scores and completion speed through decentralized task claiming, without reporting large-team costs.

items.t: Arena: A Cognitive Multi-agent Framework for Modeling Conflict-Driven Multi-party Conversation
items.a: Xu Sun, Lu Zuo, Ziyang Zeng, Trung Hieu Ngo, Kai Liu, Alexis Lechervy, Frédéric Jurie, Julien Hatin
items.sm: Presents a cognitive multi-agent framework for modeling conversations involving multiple participants and conflicting interests.

items.t: AutoQA-MAS: An LLM-Based Multi-agent System for Autonomous Website End-to-End Testing
items.sm: Presents an LLM-based multi-agent system for autonomous end-to-end website testing.

items.t: Attention Tax, Handoff Tax: A Stylised Model of When Multi-Agent LLM Systems Help
items.x: Recent work on multi-agent LLM systems reaches sharply different conclusions: some results show that a single agent with the same information and compute should dominate a delegated system, others that multi-agent gains grow with task depth. We argue that much of the disagreement comes from modelling different bottlenecks, and introduce a stylised reliability model built around two trade-offs. Decomposition reduces t…
items.sm: Models when multi-agent systems help by balancing reduced context burdens against information losses during handoffs and correlated failures during parallel sampling.

items.t: MemMux: Runtime Verification and Honest Resource Attribution for Fleets of Parallel Coding Agents
items.x: Developers increasingly run a fleet of coding agents side by side on one workstation. Terminal multiplexers like tmux and a new generation of agent managers were built to arrange windows, not to govern memory. When ten agents each spawn language servers, test runners, and browsers, no standard tool can say how much memory belongs to which agent, confirm that a terminated agent's descendants are gone, notice a child t…
items.sm: Introduces a local runtime for parallel coding agents that attributes memory usage, checks process cleanup, and exposes processes escaping agent supervision.

items.t: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
items.a: Ziyan Wang, Shuqing Shi, James Oldfield, Samuele Marro, Jialin Yu, Philip Torr, Yali Du, Adel Bibi
items.x: In decentralized consumer-to-consumer (C2C) marketplaces, people list goods, negotiate with strangers, and rate one another, so trust rests on reputation. Large language model (LLM) agents now act for users, raising risks to their money, privacy, and reputation. We introduce BazaarBench, a simulated C2C marketplace and benchmark for evaluating the safety of these agents. It tracks ownership, item condition, and commi…
items.sm: Introduces a simulated consumer marketplace benchmark to evaluate agent delegation safety across transactions involving money, privacy, reputation, and trading commitments.

items.t: Topology-Conditioned Backdoors: Language Models That Insert Vulnerabilities When They Infer They Are in a Multi-Agent System
items.x: A language model may behave safely in a single-agent evaluation yet produce vulnerable code when its context suggests that it is part of a multi-agent system. We study this failure mode by fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to condition code generation on deployment topology inferred from prompt-level provenance cues. On held-out coding tasks, task-specific checkers detect vulnerabilities in 96-100% of multi-agent episo…
items.sm: Shows that a deliberately fine-tuned model can generate vulnerable code when prompts imply multi-agent deployment while behaving safely in single-agent evaluations.

items.t: Copies or Sources? Measuring How LLM Aggregators Count Restated Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jianxin Gao, Runze Li, Tianyi Yu, Liangwei Ren, Bohan Chen, Zining Wang
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) restate observations as a matter of course: relays forward them, shared boards repeat them and discussion rounds echo them. An aggregator that pools such messages should count sources, not statements. We convert a reported probability into units of independent readings, which assigns every restatement a copy weight, 0 for an aggregator that counts sources and …
items.sm: Measures how language model aggregators overcount repeated evidence, finding that forwarded copies can influence judgments as though they provide partially independent support.

items.t: AECP: Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol for Multi-Agent Code Generation
items.a: Jiaqi Xue, Yanjun Wang, Xiangci Li, Lingbo Mo, Aritra Sengupta, Shweta Garg, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Myeongsoo Kim
items.x: As AI agents increasingly tackle complex repository-level coding tasks, distributing work across multiple agents is a natural way to scale beyond the capabilities of a single agent. To coordinate their interdependent work, these agents share findings and agree on interfaces between modules. However, exchanged information often serves only as context, leaving individual agents to interpret it and incorporate it into s…
items.sm: Introduces a protocol requiring coding agents to communicate through structured artifacts so the execution system can enforce coordination agreements.

items.t: Can CaMeLs Talk? Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
items.a: James Peters-Gill, Avi Semler, Henning Bartsch, Ilia Shumailov, Christian Schroeder de Witt
items.x: Indirect prompt injection attacks - malicious instructions embedded in content processed by large language models - remain a major obstacle to safely deploying tool-using agents. CaMeL [Debenedetti et al., 2025] mitigates this threat for an individual agent by separating trusted control flow from untrusted data and enforcing capability-based security policies at runtime. In this work, we investigate whether CaMeL's s…
items.sm: Demonstrates that individually protected CaMeL agents remain vulnerable when composed, then introduces a communication protocol to preserve security across agent boundaries.

items.t: Giving Characters a Life: An LLM-Driven Emergent Life-Simulation System with Coupled Physiological–Economic–Social Constraints
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Presents a ten-character life simulation where physiological, economic, and social constraints produce regular meals and social patterns without scripted daily schedules.

items.t: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving
items.a: Jiaqi Zhao, Haodong Chen, Jitai Hao, Wei Zhao, Jinghao Pang, Qiang Huang, Jun Yu
items.x: LLM agents increasingly execute complex workflows involving multi-turn reasoning, tool use, and parallel agents. Efficient serving requires decisions that span two layers with complementary information: the agent harness understands workflow dependencies, context lifecycles, and execution objectives, whereas the inference engine observes request queues, KV-cache state, resource pressure, and execution capabilities. E…
items.sm: Introduces a bidirectional protocol that lets agent harnesses share workflow requirements with inference engines and receive runtime conditions, capabilities, and outcomes.

items.t: Hypothesis of Emergent Cognitive Evolution of LLM Agents: Digital Proto-Life and Stages of Cognitive Complexification
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Hypothesizes that interacting LLM agents inheriting predecessors' information can develop lifelike information processes and progress through seven stages of cognitive complexity.

items.t: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
items.a: Jiuheng Wan, Runze Li, Chen Chen, Tingyuan Hu, Daiyang Yu, Yimin Jing, Taolin Zhang, Richang Hong
items.x: While medical multimodal large language models (Med-MLLMs) advance medical visual question answering (VQA), existing clinical workflow-inspired multi-agent frameworks suffer from interaction patterns and excessive computational overhead caused by redundant communication topologies. In this paper, we propose MedPrune, an efficient medical multimodal multi-agent collaboration framework that dynamically prunes both node…
items.sm: Proposes a medical visual question answering framework that dynamically removes specialist agents and communication links to improve reasoning and reduce token use.

items.x: pstack reworked for T3 Code: delegated subagents, worktree threads, PR watching, scheduled runs.
items.sm: Adapts pstack for T3 Code with delegated subagents, worktree threads, pull request monitoring, and scheduled runs.

items.t: 100yenadmin/hermes-teammates

items.t: AECG: Asymmetric Experience Consolidation and Governance In Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Ao Tian, Jialong Liu, Daqi Zheng, Xin Sun, Mengting Li, Zhizhao Xiao, Zijian Huang, Honglei Wang
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems increasingly rely on memory to transform execution trajectories into reusable procedural knowledge. Yet repeated retrieval also makes memory errors persistent: memory pollution arises when outdated, weakly supported, or spuriously successful procedures become recurring components of future reasoning. Multi-agent execution introduces an additional structural risk. S…
items.sm: AECG proposes governing reusable multi-agent experience to address persistent memory errors and procedures applied beyond the coordination settings where they worked.

items.t: Trust-Gated Capability Control: Breaking the Trust-Vulnerability Paradox in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Mehedi Hasan Nipu, Chinmoy Mitra, Tarannum Ahmed Nowshin, Israt Moyeen Noumi
items.x: Layered trust models for multi-agent LLM systems remain largely conceptual: they name which dimensions of trust matter but not how layers combine, how their importance is set at runtime, or how trust should govern agent actions. This gap matters because higher inter-agent trust raises task success while also enlarging exposure to exploitation, a tension formalized as the Trust-Vulnerability Paradox. We make a five-la…
items.sm: Proposes operational trust controls that combine five trust layers, learn their importance from failures, and use trust to govern agent capabilities.

items.t: Towards Orchestrating LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems with SysML v2
items.a: Léna Bamouh, Jean‐Marie Mottu, Hugo Brunelière, Massimo Tisi

items.t: DREAM: Dynamic Resolution Assignment For Multimodal Multi-agent Debate
items.a: Khanh-Binh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Tien Anh Nguyen, Svetha Venkatesh, Hung Le
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) has emerged as an effective paradigm to improve the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and is increasingly being extended to multimodal settings. However, existing multimodal MAD frameworks typically expose agents to the same fixed visual input, ignoring substantial variation in the visual scale needed across samples and agents. In addition, these frameworks frequently suf…
items.sm: DREAM proposes assigning visual resolutions dynamically during multimodal agent debate to address differing visual needs and agents conforming to incorrect peer responses.

items.t: KERKIS: a Modeling Language for Multi-Agent System Interactions in AI-Native Software Engineering

items.t: Harness-Search: Guiding Long-Horizon Search through Multi-Agent Coordination
items.a: Shanyong Wang, Lei Jin, Yining Zhao, Yicheng Qian, Chengqiang Lu, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Lizhen Cui
items.x: Long-horizon search requires agents to gather evidence across multiple steps and synthesize it into well-supported answers. The recent agent harnesses provide a natural and promising framework to support such long-running search processes. As interaction histories grow, one single agent in harnesses might get stuck and cause the policy to lose track of unresolved questions, overlook useful evidence, or terminate befo…
items.sm: Harness-Search separates retrieval proposals, persistent state updates, and stopping decisions across agents to reduce cascading errors during extended searches.

items.t: Communication Shapes Collective Inference in Self-Adapting LLM Societies: Evidence from Mafia
items.x: When does communication help a group identify hidden adversaries, and how does its value change as the group adapts? In Mafia, an informed minority hides inside an uninformed majority whose only evidence is open play. The zero-information game, where each day's vote eliminates a random player, is exactly solved and scores every society; matched-casting comparisons between protocols identify the effect of communicatio…
items.sm: Finds that simultaneous broadcast improves hidden-adversary identification among adapting language model agents playing Mafia, while turn-taking removes most of that advantage.

items.t: RobotUse: Allocating Computation, Context, and Decisions
items.a: Junhoo Lee, Injun Baek, Seungyeon Kim, Suhyun Jeon, Minkyu Kim, Baekseung Kim, Nojun Kwak
items.x: Robot agents must connect their intended actions to observed outcomes while retaining the context needed to revise their choices over repeated attempts. Existing interfaces often leave these choices inside predefined tools or require agents to manage detailed execution code and its growing history. items.sm: RobotUse combines visual action selection, backend motion control, subagent context management, and persistent execution lessons, reporting 45% task success on RoboLab.

items.t: Fusion is the New Mutation: Bandit-Guided Evolution on Workflow Graphs
items.a: Zhiwei Shang, Jiahang Sun, Mingrong Gong, Mingze Kong, Zikun Qu, Pingchen Lu, Junhao Dong, Zhipiao Liu
items.x: Automated agentic workflow optimization relies on costly evaluations, making it essential to allocate a limited evaluation budget effectively. Multi-parent fusion can reuse designs from previously discovered workflows, but identifying promising parent combinations requires learning from limited fusion feedback. We introduce DAGO (Directed Acyclic Graph Optimization), a contextual-bandit-guided framework that learns w…
items.sm: DAGO uses a contextual bandit to select parent workflows for language model fusion, allocating limited evaluations between promising combinations and uncertain alternatives.

items.t: When Debate Helps: Proposal Supply and Verification-Aware Readout in Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Zihao Zhao, Tunyu Zhang, Haizhou Shi, Yusong Zhao, Xinxi Zhang, Hao Wang
items.x: Multi-agent debate can improve reasoning, yet often fails to beat simple majority voting. We argue that successful debate requires two distinct mechanisms: proposal supply must surface a correct answer, and readout must identify that answer when voting misses it. We formalize the first requirement through recoverable headroom, which measures cases where a correct proposal is available but the majority answer is wrong…
items.sm: Argues that effective multi-agent debate requires both generating correct candidate answers and identifying them through verification when majority voting fails.

items.t: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
items.a: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian, Cheng Yang, Chuan Shi, Zhiyuan Liu

The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and …
items.sm: MASBench introduces a benchmark for evaluating collaboration mechanisms among language model agents that each access only partial information.

items.x: Large language models increasingly mediate tool use in Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, where adversarial influence may enter through user instructions, tool schemas, tool outputs, or protocol messages. Here we use social deduction games to study how RFT changes LLMs' social behaviour. We let fine-tuned and base LLM agents play hidden-role games that require hidden-state inference, social reading and vote steering. Our results show that LLM agents do not reliably acquire soci…
items.sm: Finds that reinforcement fine-tuning improves social reading and influence in deduction games, while optimizing final wins alone does not reliably teach social deduction.

items.x: Multi-agent debate is increasingly used to reach consensus among LLM agents, yet agents often yield to a unanimous majority. When an agent changes its answer, has it changed its mind or only its statement? items.x: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale language models efficiently by activating only a few experts per token, but the saving is confined to computation: every expert must stay resident on the accelerator, so memory bounds where these models can be deployed. Expert pruning reduces this footprint, yet existing methods are static --- a single mask, calibrated offline, is applied to the model for every subsequent …

As multi-agent systems increasingly combine language models of different families and sizes, the answer can determine which judgments survive interaction. Measuring persuasion as the probabilistic shift in an agent's decision after a single exchange with a dissenting peer, we test seven open-weight models across three language understanding tasks. We find that persuasi…
items.sm: Finds that disagreeing models often adopt peers' judgments, while model size and consistency in isolation do not reliably predict persuasion or resistance.

items.t: The Cost of a Hop: Benchmarking NLIP and A2A
items.a: Ranjan Sinha, Anindita Das, Ashika Anand Babu, Hari Palleti
items.x: Autonomous agents built on Large Language Models (LLMs) need standardized protocols to interoperate across systems. Several now exist (A2A, MCP, ACP, ANP, NLIP), but the Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP) has not appeared in any controlled performance study, and no work has measured where an agent protocol's latency is spent. We compare NLIP and the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol empirically, decomposing lat…

Because the value of each design choice is observable only through execution, tailoring a harness to each query has required either executing alternatives at inference time or costly manual design. We introduce SHIFT, which moves execution out of the per-query search lo…
items.sm: Introduces SHIFT, which uses learned utility predictions and tree search to construct query-specific agent configurations balancing accuracy and execution cost.

items.t: Tracking State Footprints: How Agents Can Transact

items.sm: Introduces Concord, a multi-agent framework built around Model Context Protocol to address cost and decision reliability in automated security finding management.

items.t: LogicHunter: Testing LLM Agent Frameworks with an Agentic Oracle
items.a: Minghui Long, Yanjie Zhao, Haoyu Wang
items.v: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM) agent frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and CrewAI have become critical infrastructure powering production AI systems, yet they remain severely under-tested due to fundamental challenges in automated testing. Unlike traditional software, where crashes serve as reliable oracles, defects in these pure Python frameworks manifest as ordinary exceptions or silent semantic failures, creat…
items.sm: LogicHunter tests language model agent frameworks using specification-aware fuzzing and an agentic oracle to identify exceptions and semantic failures.

items.t: Pay for the Fault, Not the Flow: Label-Free In-Flow Multi-Agent Workflow Optimization
items.a: Xuehang Guo, Haoyu Wang, Shengyu Chen, Zach Chen, Wei Cheng, Qingyun Wang, Haifeng Chen
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly construct multi-agent workflows that decompose a complex task and assign specialist agents from a pool. However, building such a workflow well remains challenging: how finely to divide the task, which agent to trust with each subtask, and when to create a new specialist are all critical decisions a workflow constructor needs to settle up front. Thus, whether each subtask succ…
items.sm: InFlowOp proposes optimizing multi-agent workflows without reference labels by balancing agents' suitability for subtasks against their execution costs.

items.t: Lost in the comments: Social context as a single‐pass jailbreak and defense on agentic platforms
items.a: Taehyeon Yun, Seonhee Jeon, Geonwoo Kim, Jeongsu Park, Moohong Min
items.sm: Reports that social platform formatting increases jailbreak success in a simulation, while comment tone can either suppress or encourage unsafe agent responses.

items.t: Modeling public opinion formation processes using multi-agent AI systems: practical experience
items.sm: Examines MiroFish simulations using YandexGPT to assess whether multi-agent systems can model public discussions across four social scenarios.

items.t: Context-aware micro-escrow for agentic systems with language model validation
items.a: Ayman Nait Cherif, Mohamed Youssfi, Omar Bouattane
items.v: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: Proposes automated escrow for agent transactions using language model validation, signed decisions, cryptographic context records, and blockchain settlement.

items.t: Mean field games as a tool for AI safety: a worked example from the July 2026 Hugging Face incident
items.x: One way to make AI systems safe is to shape what the system is: its objective and dispositions. We take a complementary route: treat the agents' characteristics as partly unknown and ask what structure of interaction ensures that bad collective outcomes are not equilibria. Mean field games suit this when many interchangeable agents are coupled through an aggregate. We introduce a program for using them in AI safety a…
items.sm: Uses mean field games to model collective agent attacks and derive a belief threshold intended to prevent attacks from becoming equilibrium behavior.

items.t: Can We Trust Autonomous Agents? A Formal Framework for Verifiable Agent Economies
items.sm: Formalizes agent markets that combine credentials, stakes, reputation, constrained wallets, and delivery receipts to govern authority, payments, and identity abuse.

items.t: Framework for Safety Analysis of LLM-Generated Code in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: David Armenovich Avagian, K. A. Ayrapetyants
items.sm: Introduces SafeAICoder and compares code security across three language models in single-agent and multi-agent configurations using two benchmarks.

items.t: Understanding Issues, Causes and Solutions in Open-Source LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Asad Ur Rehman, Syed Mohammad Kashif, Ruiyin Li, Peng Liang, Zengyang Li, Arif Ali Khan
items.x: With the advancement of LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS), an increasing number of opensource projects are adopting multi-agent architectures as the foundation of their core functionality. Although research and practice on MAS have attracted considerable attention, limited studies have explored the challenges faced by practitioners of open-source LLM-based MAS, the causes of these challenges, and potential solution…
items.sm: Analyzes 944 relevant issues from 21 open-source language model multi-agent projects to identify practitioner challenges, their causes, and possible solutions.

items.t: Beyond Leaderboards: Tokenomics of Agentic Small Language Model Ensembles
items.a: Alexei N. Skurikhin, Emily M. Taylor, Nathan A. DeBardeleben
items.x: As large language models (LLMs) move from standalone assistants into agentic workflows, evaluation must extend beyond scalar leaderboard accuracy to account for operational reliability, cost, latency, and token efficiency. We use an agentic ensemble of small language models (SLMs) with an SLM-judge-mediated feedback loop as a case study for such beyond-leaderboard evaluation. On the 541-prompt IFEval benchmark, the b…
items.sm: Evaluates small language model ensembles on accuracy, cost, latency, and token use, reporting higher instruction-following accuracy than its strongest standalone baseline.

items.t: Managing Context and Communication in Distributed Agentic UAV Swarms
items.a: Andrea Iannoli, Ivan Zyrianoff, Angelo Trotta, Lorenzo Gigli, Marco Di Felice
items.x: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms increasingly rely on language-model agents to provide adaptive mission-level reasoning in uncertain environments. Fully distributed control, in which each UAV hosts an independent Small Language Model (SLM), removes reliance on a centralized coordinator but introduces an information-management problem: long-running interaction histories can degrade the reasoning context, while ind…
items.sm: Proposes distributed drone agents that organize knowledge into structured memories and selectively share relevant information to manage context and communication costs.

items.t: Towards Iterative End-to-End Software Development: A Feature-Driven Multi-agent Framework
items.a: Junwei Liu, Xu Chen, Chong Wang, Tong Bai, Weitong Chen, Kaseng Wong, Yiling Lou, Xin Peng
items.v: Proceedings of the ACM on software engineering.
items.x: Recent advances in large language model agents offer the promise of automating end-to-end software development from natural language requirements. However, existing approaches largely adopt linear, waterfall-style pipelines, which oversimplify the iterative nature of real-world development and struggle with complex, larger-scale projects. To address these limitations, we propose EvoDev, an iterative software developm…
items.sm: EvoDev organizes iterative software development around features and their dependencies, passing business, design, and implementation context between development steps.

items.t: Global Coherence: When Every Agent Is Right and the Team Is Still Wrong - A Local-to-Global Semantic Foundation for Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.x: AI agents share code, documents, tools, and analyses. No participant sees the whole state, so every step can look right while the combined result is wrong. We call this the global coherence problem. It is a problem of state, not only of intelligence: a stronger model decides better locally, but cannot see what is missing from its context. The Observation-Aliasing Impossibility Theorem gives the exact condition. An ag…
items.sm: Formalizes how limited context prevents agents from guaranteeing valid actions and examines the difficulty of finding sufficient context for coherent collaboration.

items.t: Factors Influencing the Emergence of Dependency Length Minimization in Neural Agent Simulations
items.a: Yuqing Zhang, Tessa Verhoef, Gertjan van Noord, Arianna Bisazza
items.x: Given various grammatical options, language users prefer the word order choice that reduces the overall length of syntactic dependencies, a principle known as dependency length minimization (DLM). The origins of this preference remain an open question, particularly whether it originates from constraints on efficient information processing. Computational simulations provide a powerful approach to identifying the facto…
items.sm: Investigates which learning and communication conditions cause neural agents using artificial languages to favor shorter syntactic dependencies.

items.t: Compound AI System Reliability: A Failure Taxonomy and Resilience Pattern Catalog from 150 Production Incidents
items.x: Deploying compound AI systems reliably and safely requires understanding failure modes that emerge at component boundaries, not within individual models. Cascading errors propagate across component boundaries, silent quality degradation evades standard monitoring, and coordination failures yield incorrect collective behavior from individually correct parts. We analyze 150 production incident reports from open-source …
items.sm: Analyzes 150 production incidents to classify compound AI failures and evaluates resilience measures, including circuit breakers and output quality checks.

items.t: Mitigating Cascading Prompt Injections in Multi-Agent Systems via Semantic Boundary Mediation and Observability
items.v: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
items.sm: Proposes semantic boundary mediation and observability to limit malicious instructions cascading from supervisor agents to workers with execution privileges.
