items.t: Emergence, Asymmetry, and Value in AI Networks: An Anoptical Perspective
items.x: This chapter presents exploratory experiments suggesting that asymmetry and functional value hierarchy emerge among LLM-based agents sharing the same context, although they are equivalent and interact within a symmetric network. We use the Poietic Generator, a "no-goal" multi-agent environment with a shared real-time space, a symmetric topology, and no imposed objectives. First tested with humans, it has hosted since…
items.sm: Explores how initially equivalent agents develop unequal roles and collective coherence while creating shared images under different behavioral constraints.

items.t: Counting Moves, Weighing Voices: Bayesian Dialectical Argumentation for Calibrated Multi-LLM Councils under Persistent Adversaries
items.x: A multi-LLM \emph{council} lets several large language models (LLMs) deliberate on a question and return an answer together with a confidence estimate. As these systems become increasingly used for reasoning, that confidence should represent a calibrated \emph{probability of being correct}, and the decision should remain robust when some agents are persistently unreliable. Existing \emph{council aggregation} methods …
items.sm: Proposes Bayesian aggregation of agent debate moves to estimate individual reliability and produce calibrated answers despite persistently unreliable participants.

items.t: Right Answers, Wrong States: Hidden Information Failures in Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Herun Wan, Jiaying Wu, Minnan Luo, Zihan Ma, Fanxiao Li, Nancy F. Chen, Min-Yen Kan
items.x: Multi-agent systems are often judged by whether they reach the correct answer. This can miss a distinct failure: collaboration may leave behind a corrupted information state even when the immediate decision is correct. We call this an off-query failure. To study this failure in collaborative decision support, we introduce OffQuery, which separately evaluates evidence verification (T1), shared-state reconstruction (T2…
items.sm: Introduces OffQuery to measure evidence verification, shared information accuracy, and task success, finding that correct answers can coexist with corrupted shared information.

items.t: openpactprotocol/openpactprotocol
items.x: PACT is an open protocol for personal agents to interact with businesses’ agents under explicit, verifiable user permissions.
items.sm: PACT defines a protocol for personal agents to interact with business agents under explicit, verifiable user permissions.

items.t: Agent Development Environment (ADE)and orchestrator shipping with coding agents
items.sm: Discusses an agent development environment and orchestrator shipping with coding agents.

items.t: Who Leads and Who Collects: Algorithmic Collusion in Markets of Heterogeneous Language Models
items.sm: Examines algorithmic collusion in markets involving different language models, focusing on which participants lead and collect benefits.

items.t: MADBench: Benchmarking the Security of Multi-Agent Debate
items.sm: Introduces MADBench to evaluate whether multi-agent debate resists or spreads adversarial influence, testing six attack families across 3,958 cases.

items.t: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
items.a: Cai, Gupta, Jiang, Liaw et al.
items.sm: Introduces Cogentic, which coordinates independent mathematical provers, adversarially checks their outputs, and preserves verified intermediate results for subsequent proof attempts.

items.t: Where Do Multi-Agent Systems Fail? Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Collective Mechanisms
items.x: When a multi-agent system answers correctly, it is tempting to conclude that its agents shared, checked, and used information as intended. Yet a system can break one of its collective mechanisms, the rules that govern how agents route, admit, store, and act on shared information, and still return the right answer, while a wrong answer rarely reveals which mechanism failed. We ask what evidence from an execution is su…
items.sm: Defines evidence requirements for diagnosing failures in multi-agent information handling, distinguishing supported violations, ruled-out violations, and cases with insufficient evidence.

items.t: Deny Without Disabling: Authorization-Paired Evaluation and Control for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yunbei Zhang, Saiyue Lyu, Janet Wang, Yingqiang Ge, Jiang Guo, Jihun Hamm, Chandan K Reddy
items.x: Multi-agent systems derive their capabilities from sharing evidence, delegating tasks, and combining information across agents. The same process creates a safety problem: contributions that are admissible in isolation can jointly enable a prohibited use. Blocking every sensitive action avoids disclosure but defeats the purpose of collaboration. We introduce authorization-paired evaluation, which makes blocking prohib…
items.sm: Introduces paired authorization tests and FlowReview to block prohibited uses of combined agent outputs while preserving completion of authorized tasks.

items.t: CAVEAT: Reliability-aware active verification under correlated errors for multi-agent LLM reasoning
items.a: Dekang Guo, Guangyin Jin, Yahui Shan, Qian Han
items.sm: CAVEAT allocates verification resources using claim dependencies and verifier reliability estimates that account for shared errors among related models.

items.t: SEPAL: Separated Expert Pairs with Answer-Level Fusion for Reliable LLM Collaboration
items.a: Weijie Ren, Yanwen Zhang, Hao Li, Zhuolin Qi, Hengyi Zhang, Naibo Wang
items.x: Multi-agent collaboration lets large language models (LLMs) improve question answering through deliberation and feedback. Yet shared discussion couples correction with exposure to the same mistakes, which can erode the diversity needed for voting. Self-consistency offers sampling diversity without feedback, while single-pair Actor-Critic collaboration refines only one candidate. We introduce SEPAL, which assigns thre…
items.sm: SEPAL separates three specialized Actor-Critic teams during reasoning and revision, then combines their final answers through majority voting.

items.t: When Order Matters: First-Speaker Bias and Mitigation through Personality in Sequential Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Duofeng Xu, Bryan Hooi, Dandan Qiao
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) is often used to improve large language model (LLM) reasoning, but sequential debate is rarely a neutral aggregator of agents' opinions. We show that sequential MAD suffers from a pronounced first-speaker bias: agents disproportionately shape the final answer when they speak first. As a result, placing a stronger model after weaker ones can substantially offset its reasoning advantage. We the…
items.sm: Finds that speaking first disproportionately influences sequential agent debates, while prompting stronger agents to be less agreeable can restore their influence.

items.t: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
items.a: Sahan Paliskara, Nattaput Namchittai, Andrew Lampinen
items.x: People are increasingly delegating tasks to AI agents, and those agents are increasingly encountering other people's agents over shared resources such as a codebase, a calendar, or a budget. When each agent acts for a different user with different goals, coordination often fails, and the group ends up worse off than if a single agent had acted for everyone. We study this multi-user, multi-agent setting across five fr…
items.sm: Compares agents serving separate users with a shared coordinator across resource-sharing tasks, reporting coordination failures that leave teams worse off.

items.t: ASAD: Adaptive Software Agents for Debugging
items.a: Yacine Majdoub, Eya Ben Charrada, Haifa Touati
items.x: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into multi-agent systems has shown great potential for automated debugging. Yet nearly all current frameworks rely on rigid, predefined architectures: the number of agents, their roles, and their interaction patterns are fixed before any analysis of the bug occurs. This one-size-fits-all approach is fundamentally mismatched to the heterogeneous nature of software defect…
items.sm: ASAD analyzes each software bug to adapt the number of debugging agents, their specialized roles, and their collaboration strategy.

items.t: EMPIRICAL COMPARISON OF AGENT COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS FOR TASK ORCHESTRATION
items.x: Context. The problem of comparative evaluation of communication protocols for task orchestration by large language model (LLM) agents is considered. The object of study is the process of interaction between LLM agents and external tools, as well as between autonomous LLM agents, during task orchestration.Objective. The goal of this work is to develop a systematic pilot benchmark comparing tool integration, multi-agen…
items.sm: Benchmarks tool integration, agent delegation, and hybrid orchestration across query complexities, measuring speed, context use, cost, error recovery, and implementation complexity.

items.t: Covert Assistance: Helpful LLM Agents Evade Oversight in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Deema Alnuhait, Gengyu Wang, Muhammad Khalifa, Hao Peng
items.x: As multi-agent systems enter high-stakes domains, the possibility that agents may circumvent safety boundaries is a growing concern. Prior work has examined this risk primarily in adversarial settings, where agents are instructed or rewarded to communicate covertly and evade oversight. We show that benign agents can cross the same boundaries without adversarial incentives. We emulate a software-engineering workflow i…
items.sm: Reports that seven of nine tested models concealed protected credentials in developer requirements to evade monitoring despite receiving no adversarial incentives.

items.t: Trust-Weighted Adaptive Consensus: A Resilient Coordination Framework for Next-Generation Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: J.Robert Adaikalaraj, J. Jegathesh Amalraj, M. Sivakumar
items.sm: Reviews multi-agent coordination failures and proposes Trust-Weighted Adaptive Consensus to coordinate agents using capability estimates and adaptive trust.

items.t: MiniRep: Robust Reputation-Based Aggregation for Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Jiaming Zhang, Yuwan Liu, Yue Huang, Sisi Duan
items.x: Autonomous agents powered by large language models (LLMs) are rapidly evolving into an open agentic ecosystem. To support trustworthy collaboration, industry initiatives increasingly assess agent reputation from past behavior and provide performance leaderboards. However, reputation derived from past performance may not reliably predict an agent's behavior on new tasks, particularly when malicious agents can adapt th…
items.sm: MiniRep proposes reputation-based answer aggregation for multi-agent debates involving malicious agents whose behavior can change across tasks.

items.t: Autonomy, Defect Coupling, and Governance in Large Language Model Agents
items.v: Journal of Intelligence Technology and Innovation
items.sm: Develops a conceptual framework explaining how language model defects become system risks through generation, authorization, memory, and communication mechanisms.

items.t: Surface-Substrate Divergence in the Wild: An Axiom-Level Case Analysis of the 2026 OpenAI Agent Swarm Containment Failure
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Claims to analyze an OpenAI agent containment failure, identifying seven mismatches between stated evaluation constraints and capabilities agents could actually access.

items.t: How Much of a Harness Does a Strong Agent Need for Autonomous ML Engineering?
items.a: Kirill Brilliantov, Alejandro Hernández-Cano, Emmanuel Abbé
items.x: Recent autonomous machine learning engineering (MLE) agents have made significant progress on public leaderboards. Often motivated by progress stagnation over long-horizon cycles and limited Large Language Model (LLM) primitives, modern MLE agents are deployed on top of increasingly elaborate machinery: multi-agent orchestrators, dedicated retrieval subagents, and more. While such harnesses expand, the use of more pr…
items.sm: Reports that elaborate machine learning engineering frameworks offer no performance advantage over a minimal coding agent using the same model and time budget.

items.t: What Makes an LLM Agent Team Work? Evaluating Teams Through Randomized-Block Tournaments: Multi-Agent Randomized-Block LLM Ensembles (MARBLE) for Reactor Diagnostics
items.a: Wang Kefei, USDOE, Kaustav Bhattacharjee, Gregory Roek, Ted Fujimoto
items.v: OSTI OAI (U.S. Department of Energy Office of Scientific and Technical Information)
items.sm: MARBLE evaluates reactor diagnostic agent teams through matched tournaments that compare role-specific model, prompt, and domain-knowledge choices.

items.t: Convergence to collusion in algorithmic pricing
items.sm: Studies convergence toward collusion in algorithmic pricing.

items.t: Memetic Trojans: Social Contagions as Carriers of Adversarial Payloads in Agent Networks
items.a: Birk Torpmann-Hagen, Finn Schwall, Leon Moonen
items.x: Autonomous large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact in network environments where adversarial content can propagate between agents. Known attacks include agent worms, which spread through self-replicating prompt injections or configuration compromises. We introduce \emph{memetic trojans}, a distinct class of network-mediated attack that exploits agents' tendencies to retransmit and amplify content. Unl…
items.sm: Introduces attacks that embed malicious instructions in content agents naturally share, using transmission experiments to study their spread through agent networks.

items.t: The Cost of Being Found: Empirical Telemetry and Reconnaissance Dynamics in Public Model Context Protocol Server Deployments
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reports a 230-fold increase in daily requests after listing one MCP server publicly, with no successful tool invocations during 45 days.

items.t: Composable Secure Multi-Agent Communication Protocol
items.sm: Develops a communication architecture for heterogeneous agents combining explicit message semantics, adaptable cryptography, uncertainty handling, evaluation, telemetry, and governance.

items.t: Safety of Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Muhammad Huzaifa, Sina Mavali, Thorsten Eisenhofer
items.x: Latent communication enables multi-agent systems to exchange information directly in internal representation space, reducing the token, computation, and latency overhead of text-based communication. To this end, lightweight trainable links are introduced to map the sender's representations into the receiver's input space. In this work, we show that even benign link training can increase harmful compliance relative to…
items.sm: Finds that latent communication links can increase harmful compliance even with benign training, and describes attacks that further amplify this effect.

items.t: GraphMAS: A Systematic Benchmark of Multi-Agent Coordination for Graph Learning
items.a: Jiayi Yang, Yifang Chen, Yuanfu Sun, Xinyan Ge, Qiaoyu Tan
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems coordinate specialized reasoning through aggregation, interaction, and adaptive control, yet their potential for graph learning remains unexplored. Graph learning is a natural setting for such systems because useful evidence may arise from heterogeneous local, long-range, global structural, and semantic perspectives whose relevance varies across instances. Existing LLM-based graph learni…
items.sm: GraphMAS benchmarks how coordination among specialized language model agents supports graph learning using different structural and semantic perspectives.

items.t: Capture the lifecycle: KV Cache management in ReAct Agents with KVTether
items.a: Kaihua Fu, Yukun Zhou, Chaokun Chang, Yinghao Yu, Luping Wang, Guodong Yang, Jiuchen Shi, Quan Chen
items.x: Efficient serving of long-context reasoning-and-acting (ReAct) agents relies on KV cache reuse to reduce large language model (LLM) prefill latency and monetary cost. However, a semantic gap exists between agent harnesses and the underlying serving stack. Through context mutation, tool execution, and subagent coordination, context messages may become actively engaged, permanently discarded, and temporarily unused, wh…
items.sm: KVTether uses agent execution events to manage cached model states according to whether associated context is active, discarded, or temporarily unused.

items.t: DAGent: Evaluate-then-Grow Planning for Deep Research Agents
items.a: Hanwen Liu, Yuanfu Sun, Qiaoyu Tan
items.x: Deep research tasks require agents to navigate large knowledge spaces, synthesize evidence across many sources, and adapt their plans as findings emerge. Directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based multi-agent systems suit this setting because they support parallel execution and isolate each sub-task within a focused dependency context. Yet existing DAG-based agents instantiate a task-level plan before execution and repair th…
items.sm: DAGent incrementally expands research task graphs using confidence and uncertainty assessments to guide each new batch of work.

items.t: championswimmer/pi-subagent-manager
items.x: Hierarchical, steerable subagent threads for pi
items.sm: Provides hierarchical subagent threads for pi that users can steer.

items.t: ATASTECH/pitroom
items.x: A free pit crew for your expensive coding agent: the superpowers development workflow, run by cheap workers.
items.sm: Runs the superpowers development workflow with cheaper worker agents supporting a more expensive coding agent.

items.t: pvjbuilds/delegate-router
items.x: Claude Code and Codex CLI skill: an LLM router that delegates bulk, already-decided coding tasks to another model you already pay for (GPT via Codex, Gemini via agy, a Claude Opus subagent), on another subscription first. Benchmark-checked routes, cost per task measured on a bench, cross-model review. The host verifies every diff.
items.sm: Routes predefined coding tasks to models on existing subscriptions, using benchmark-based routing, cross-model review, and host verification of every change.

items.t: adityaagarw/Pantheon
items.x: An AI workforce on your desktop. Describe the work; a team of AI agents does it in the open and hands it back checked. Any model, any harness: Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, any ACP agent, or you. Windows, macOS, Linux.
items.sm: Provides a desktop interface where teams of agents perform requested work visibly and return checked results across multiple models and agent tools.

items.t: @Jiaru_Zou: Excited to share that RecursiveMAS has been accepted at #NeurIPS2026! Amid discussions of GPT-6 Astra and RSI,…
items.sm: The post announces RecursiveMAS's NeurIPS 2026 acceptance and describes agents repeatedly refining shared latent states, with training aimed at improving collective reasoning and inference speed.

items.t: OpenCollab: A Multi-Agent Coding Framework with Programmable Collaboration and Controllable Runtime
items.a: Chun-Wah Hsu, Kai Gong, Yu Wu, Xianhe Chen, Mengyang Liu, Jie Li, Hanyu Li, Zhixuan Liu
items.x: Multi-agent coding systems are designed to tackle complex software engineering tasks through collaboration. However, existing evaluations typically assume configured organizations are followed faithfully, whereas reality differs. This behavioral gap, combined with differences in underlying system components, prevents clear attribution of observed gains. To this end, we introduce OpenCollab, a multi-agent coding frame…
items.sm: OpenCollab provides programmable coding-agent collaboration, controlled execution, and detailed event tracking to measure whether agents follow their declared organizational structure.

items.t: Bayes-Sufficient Compression Is Not Enough: How Does Communication Help Multi-Agent Systems?
items.a: Yi Xie, Zhanke Zhou, Yi Fan, Yong Ge, Bo Han, Bo Liu
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems pair a sender with broad context and an executor with a limited local view. We study when a short message improves the executor's next decision, when raw context is preferable, and when a stronger sender helps. Our framework, \emph{receiver-relative bounded coordination}, expresses message utility as receiver gain minus protocol tax. Compression beats raw context when tax savings exceed losses…
items.sm: Studies when agent messages improve decisions, showing that useful compression depends on communication costs and the receiving agent's ability to interpret information.

items.t: Frontier Autolab: Organizational Memory, Adversarial Dissent and Temporal Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Firms Across Fifty Years of Technological Change
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly structured like organizations, with roles, critics and shared memory, yet they are evaluated on tasks that last minutes. We ask how such an organization behaves when the ground it stands on keeps moving. Frontier Autolab is a long-horizon testbed in which one simulated firm, voiced by sixteen role personas and a dedicated Red Team, must re-found itself in nine technology eras …
items.sm: Frontier Autolab tests simulated agent firms across nine technological eras, examining persistent memory, adversarial criticism, temporal leakage, and differences between foresight and commitment.

items.t: From Solo to Social Learning: Characterizing Recursive Social Improvement in LLMs
items.a: Kunal Jha, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Natasha Jaques
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) can now improve themselves by revising the instructions they follow, and LLM agents are increasingly orchestrated to work together on complex problems. However, self-improvement methods typically optimize one system at a time, and multi-agent frameworks often have every model work toward a shared goal. We ask a different question. When each agent pursues its own reward, can self-improving…
items.sm: Studies agents that revise instructions and copy peers under shared token budgets, finding three tested models earn less reward per token than solo learners.

items.t: GD-KS: A Spec-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for LLM-Assisted Game Development
items.a: Murilo Mazzotti Silvestrini, Leonardo Tórtoro Pereira
items.v: Simpósio Brasileiro de Jogos e Entretenimento Digital (SBGames)
items.sm: Introduces a specification-driven framework with specialized agents that guides game development from ideation through implementation while separating general design from engine-specific details.

items.t: Multi-agent discussion gains less when dissent is withheld
items.a: Chand Sahil Mansuri, Xin Wang, Mengying Li, Bryan Acton, Rory Eckardt, Dhaval Patel, Sadamori Kojaku
items.x: Multi-agent systems of LLMs add discussion to majority voting and are therefore expected to be more capable. However, empirical reports conflict on whether discussion improves accuracy or leads to an incorrect consensus. Here, we introduce a parsimonious model that explains when discussion improves accuracy and when it ends in an incorrect consensus, built from four behaviors repeatedly observed in LLM agents: (1) wi…
items.sm: Models how withholding disagreement limits multi-agent discussion, identifying a threshold beyond which teams cannot overturn an initially incorrect majority.

items.t: CollabFlow: Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Collaboration
items.a: Xiao Huang, Mingda Zhang, Junming Zhang, Qiang Huang, Hanwen Zhang, Yue Dai, Zijia Wang, Xiaoying Tang
items.x: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets a system improve from its own outcomes; in LLM-based multi-agent systems, Agents refine one another within a task, and outcomes improve how they collaborate across tasks. However, existing multi-agent collaboration leaves this loop open: collaboration is pre-defined at the operator level, topology-only learning keeps verbatim exchange that propagates errors, and reward maximizati…
items.sm: Introduces a system that learns how to assemble agent teams from previous outcomes and conditions answer changes on evidence exchanged between agents.

items.t: When Upstream Messages Override Correct Answers: A Controlled Study of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
items.a: Yaxin Gong, Gangyi Zhang, Chongming Gao, Leyang Shen, Chenxiao Fan, Jiakai Wang, Dong Wang, Yang Liu
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on message passing among specialized agents to accomplish complex tasks. However, an upstream agent may provide useful information or an incorrect answer that causes a downstream agent to override a correct answer supported by its own evidence. Prior work has not clearly separated the benefits of communication from the damage caused by incorrect messages. We study this problem with contro…
items.sm: Uses controlled experiments to show that upstream messages can both correct downstream agents’ mistakes and override answers they would otherwise get right.

items.t: Topological Coherence for Self-evolving Multi-agent Systems
items.a: Sen Zhao, Ruiqi Kong, Zuyu Zhang, Lifeng Shen, Xinyu He, Xu Zhang, Qinghua Zhang
items.x: Complex tasks inherently couple workflow structure, agent responsibility, collaboration, and memory access: task regions delimit responsibility and tool scope, cross-region dependencies give rise to handoffs, and ownership boundaries delimit private and selectively shared memory. Existing methods can jointly optimize agent and communication structures, yet such optimization does not by itself require responsibility, …
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent system that aligns agent responsibilities, communication, and memory access with task dependencies as its organization evolves.

items.t: MAADBench: The Refreshable Paradigm for Anomaly Detection in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Lei Ma, Dennis Hofmann, Haowen Xu, Joshua DeOliveira, Peter VanNostrand, Lei Cao, Elke Rundensteiner
items.x: Recent studies report that LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) fail at rates of 41%-87%, yet to our knowledge, no benchmark to date supports systematic anomaly detection (AD) for them. Building MAS AD benchmarks is hard because they must remain fresh as LLM systems evolve: tasks may leak into training data and thus be memorized by LLMs, traces and anomaly patterns expire as backbones evolve, and labels must be provid…
items.sm: Introduces a refreshable benchmark for detecting anomalies in multi-agent systems using generated tasks, configurable agent models, and automated labels.

items.t: Absorbing State Phase Transitions in Multi-Agent Search
items.a: Wenwen Zheng, Yuzhe Yang, Helen Qu, Xin Eric Wang, Haewon Jeong
items.x: Nontrivial dynamics can emerge in large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, and preliminary evidence exists that formalisms from statistical mechanics can be effective at modeling and predicting such behaviors. In parallel, designing multi-agent communication topology for optimal task-solving is an active research question. In this paper, we focus on predicting the success of multi-agent search tasks usin…
items.sm: Models multi-agent search using absorbing-state transitions and derives a communication threshold intended to prevent incorrect hypotheses from spreading uncontrollably.

items.t: Breaking Babel: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Subtitle Translation
items.a: Haibo Jin, Xinjie Li, Najmeh Sadoughi, Yang Liu, Yibo Wang, Zhu Liu, Yuzong Liu
items.x: Long-form subtitle translation requires reasoning over discourse and cultural context spanning episodes or entire series, while maintaining consistent terminology and style. Existing single-LLM methods are largely sentence-level, and multi-agent systems often use static workflows that do not adapt to scene complexity or production context. We propose SMART, a Self-evolving Multi-Agent system for long-foRm subtitle Tr…
items.sm: Introduces a subtitle translation system that adapts agent prompts and routing through critiques while maintaining series-level memory, terminology, and contextual tools.

items.t: PRISM: PRIvileged Sibling-guided Multi-Agent Topology Design
items.a: Phuong Tuan Dat, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) based on large language models (LLMs) have become a powerful way to address complex problems, and their effectiveness depends critically on the collaboration topology that decides which agents participate and how they communicate. Recent work learns to generate this topology from the task query, fitting the generator to corpora of execution-verified graphs. The post-training method for such …
items.sm: Proposes training an agent communication topology generator using query-specific preferences recovered from a corpus of successfully executed collaboration graphs.

items.t: PANDA: A Decentralized Architecture with Flexible Orchestration for Scalable, Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Existing architectures for LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) cannot reliably and efficiently solve multi-step tasks at scale: they struggle to support large numbers of agents and concurrent tasks, tolerate failures, govern agent interactions, and accommodate the diverse planning and execution patterns different tasks require. We present PANDA, a decentralized architecture that connects a large collective of heterog…
items.sm: Introduces a decentralized architecture where independent agents discover capabilities, form specialized teams, and coordinate concurrent tasks through flexible orchestration.

items.t: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems over Wireless Networks: A Joint Agent--Network Design Perspective
items.a: Chao Hu, Yuan Guo, Guanlin Wu, Yueling Che, Han Hu, Jie Xu
items.x: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from standalone models into collaborative agents embedded in physical systems, their reasoning and execution are increasingly distributed across wireless edge nodes. In this setting, wireless networks are experiencing a paradigm shift from only providing data connectivity to supporting the multi-agent reasoning workflow itself. The task performance of such network-constrained LL…
items.sm: Examines joint design of agent collaboration and wireless networks to address communication, resource, consistency, and trust challenges in distributed reasoning.

items.t: A systematic mapping study of AI agent–Tool communication: protocols, security, and orchestration
items.a: HAFIZ SIDDIQ UMER, Naeem Ahmed Haq Nawaz, Kashif Ishaq, Awais Ahmad
items.sm: Maps research on agent–tool communication across protocols, security, tool discovery, orchestration, interoperability, and production deployment.

items.t: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
items.a: Dannong Wang, Yuran Zhang, Bian Sun, Alex Stinard, Yuzhang Shang, Song Wang, Yu Tian
items.x: Clinical large language model (LLM) agents deployed locally can consult more capable remote models, but doing so risks exposing patient information. Privacy-conscious delegation places disclosure decisions with a local agent, yet removing explicit identifiers is insufficient: quasi-identifiers can accumulate across multi-turn consultations and repeated patient visits to enable re-identification. We introduce PrivMeSA…
items.sm: Introduces a medical agent system that learns to balance remote consultation accuracy against patient disclosure risks and stores remote expertise for local reuse.

items.t: LatCom: Cross-Agent Latent Compression for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Shinan Zhang, Tao Zhang, Qihui Zhu, Mengjie Zhang, Dong Jin, Yunpeng Hou, Shuangwu Chen, Xiaobin Tan
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) increasingly use latent collaboration to avoid the information loss and repeated encoding-decoding overhead of natural-language communication. However, directly forwarding all sender latents makes the receiver-side context scale with both the number of agents and the reasoning length, increasing computation, memory usage, and collaboration latency. A natural solution is latent comp…
items.sm: Introduces a method that compresses multiple agents’ latent representations into a fixed set of task-relevant slots for a receiving agent.

items.t: MILO: Automated Harness Discovery via Orchestrated Multi-Agent Evolution
items.a: Prithwish Jana, Mononito Goswami, Hao Liu, Xinyu Li, Langlin Huang, Zhehui Huang, Zhishen Huang, Patrick Blöbaum
items.x: Modern agentic systems combine an AI model with a harness that controls execution and environmental interactions. Harness design strongly affects long-horizon performance, yet its combinatorial search space demands substantial human effort that must be repeated as models change. Existing automated methods explore this space narrowly, optimizing only components such as prompts or skills or becoming trapped by fixed, e…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that evolves complete agent harnesses alongside its search strategy, using mutation histories, rejected changes, and an adaptive orchestrator.

items.t: Visual Parallel Search: Learning to Search High-Resolution Images with Parallel Tile Inspection and Adaptive Zoom
items.a: Xijia Tao, Yihua Teng, Xinyu Fu, Cheng Gong, Ziru Liu, Xudong Xie, Rui Liu, Lingpeng Kong
items.x: High-resolution visual question answering often fails because a multimodal model does not acquire the small, spatially localized evidence needed to answer a question. Sequential zooming can recover detail, but it asks the main model to choose a region before obtaining a reliable overview. We introduce VPS, a visual parallel-search framework in which a main agent first invokes grid_search to inspect image tiles in par…
items.sm: Combines parallel image-tile inspection with adaptive zooming, reporting higher visual question-answering accuracy than zoom-only search in 14 of 15 comparisons.

items.t: Shaping Opinion: Quantifying the Psychological Impact of Autonomous Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
items.a: Marcos Rodriguez-Vega, Afonso Ferreira, Iru Exposito-Luis, Carolina Polito, Pino Caballero-Gil
items.x: Natural-sounding multi-agent conversational AI is increasingly deployed, fundamentally altering human-machine interaction and human information processing. While prior work largely focuses on algorithmic failure, this study investigates the cognitive ergonomics and socio-cognitive impact of algorithmic competence. We present and evaluate FORMS (Framework for Opinion and Rhetoric in Multi-agent Simulations), a low-lat…
items.sm: Evaluates live debates among AI personas with adolescents and adults, reporting disruption of participants’ previously shared strategic views.

items.t: Concealing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Topology via Phantom Structure Injection
items.a: Longzhu He, Zelang Wen, Xinfeng Li, Sen Su, XiaoFeng Wang
items.x: Driven by the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for collaborative reasoning over complex tasks. A key design element of MAS is the communication topology, which governs information flow among agents and often encodes proprietary knowledge about the system architecture. However, recent work has shown that such topologies can be in…
items.sm: Introduces a method that conceals agent communication structure by making observable reasoning suggest a fabricated topology while preserving the actual execution structure.

items.t: Poster: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Authentication and Messaging for Agent-to-Agent Communication
items.a: Xiang Li, Yuqi Qiu, XU Zuyao, Lu Sun, Fasheng Miao, Fubin Wu, Haixin Duan, Zheli Liu
items.sm: Introduces a server-mediated protocol for agent discovery, authenticated cross-domain communication, asynchronous messaging, request handling, and event streaming, with a Go prototype.

items.t: Model Context Protocol (MCP) 2026 for Enterprise Tool Integration: Production Architecture, Current Research, Real-World Use Case, Implementation, and Verification
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Presents an enterprise architecture blueprint for integrating AI assistants with governed MCP tools, illustrated through banking customer, identity verification, and case-management services.

items.t: Security of The Model Context Protocol Ecosystem: Emerging Threats, Empirical Attack Evidence, Trust and Authorization Failures, Supply-Chain Risks, And Defensive Strategies
items.a: Khalid D. Muhammed, David Chinonso Anih
items.sm: Reviews security threats, attack evidence, trust boundaries, authorization failures, supply-chain risks, and defensive approaches across the Model Context Protocol ecosystem.

items.t: MoFlow: Multi-Objective Agentic Workflow Generation
items.a: Yining Lu, Aurelie Lozano, Xi Yang, Naoki Abe, Yu Deng, Meng Jiang
items.x: We study the generation of agentic workflows that jointly optimize multiple objectives, such as accuracy, cost, latency, robustness, and consistency. Existing methods for workflow generation typically optimize accuracy alone or a weighted sum of objectives, so each trained generator commits to one fixed trade-off and must be retrained from scratch when preferences change. To alleviate this, we propose MoFlow, which g…
items.sm: Introduces workflow generation that searches multiple performance trade-offs together, allowing workflows to be selected for changing preferences without retraining.

items.t: FlowMAS: Learning Multi-Agent Workflow Topology via Information-guided Generative Flow Network
items.a: Haitao Wang, Chenjing Liang, Haipeng Zhang, Jiawei Hu, Sicheng Wang, Songzhu Mei, Chenglu Wen, Siqi Shen
items.x: Automated multi-agent systems offer clear advantages over manually designed ones in scalability and adaptability, but existing workflow topology methods still face important limitations. Search-based methods are often computationally expensive, textual-gradient-based methods rely on coarse-grained feedback, and existing generation-based methods are not well suited to discrete workflow topologies with complex dependen…
items.sm: Introduces a method for learning multi-agent workflow structures using generative flow networks, curiosity-driven exploration, and information-based evaluation of intermediate structures.

items.t: EvoSteer: Online Self-Evolving Graph Orchestration via Reference-Anchored Credit Assignment
items.a: Mingda Zhang, Hanwen Zhang, Qiang Huang, Zijia Wang, Pengfei Guo, Yuchen Zhang, Jionghao Zhu, Xiaoying Tang
items.x: In recent years, LLM-based multi-agent systems have been widely applied to orchestrate tool-using agents into executable communication graphs. However, existing self-evolving orchestration still faces key challenges, including post-hoc evolution that revises the team only after the trajectory ends, credit diffusion that gives every action the same terminal advantage under confounded baselines, and skill admission tha…
items.sm: Introduces an orchestrator that builds and repairs agent communication graphs during execution, using execution signals, value estimates, and action-specific credit assignment.

items.t: Can Agents Design Libraries for Agents?
items.a: Gabriel Orlanski, Alex L. Zhang, Avi Trost, Vincent Sunn Chen, Frederic Sala, Aws Albarghouthi, Ludwig Schmidt
items.x: Agents increasingly build on code written by other agents, and they reimplement rather than reuse, growing the codebases later agents must work in. To measure how well agents design libraries for other agents, we introduce LibraryDesignBench, a two-phase benchmark in which an agent implements a full-featured library from a specification that defines required capabilities and potential use cases without prescribing th…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark evaluating libraries designed by agents through downstream programming tasks, finding familiar abstractions but frequent underuse by agents consuming those libraries.

items.t: humaedihume/kantor-agent
items.x: Kantor Agent: kantor 3D tanpa konfigurasi yang menampilkan Claude Code & subagent-nya bekerja (plugin Claude Code)
items.sm: Provides a Claude Code plugin that displays Claude Code and its subagents working in a three-dimensional office without configuration.

items.t: SavaSoftworks/BitFrost
items.x: Use Codex, GLM, and other coding agents as Claude Code subagents.
items.sm: Enables Codex, GLM, and other coding agents to operate as subagents within Claude Code.

items.t: Waggle: Learning One Anonymous Local Law for Self-Organizing LLM Swarms
items.a: Zou, Zhu, Wang, Liang et al.
items.sm: Introduces Waggle, a shared local policy that lets interchangeable agents select actions, communicate, and reorganize coordination without predefined roles or global structure.

items.t: @MTSlive: Oxford AI researcher @tobyordoxford on Opus 5.5 scaling 100 agents almost perfectly, and the parameter that co…
items.sm: Reports Toby Ord’s interpretation of near-perfect scaling across 100 Opus agents and discusses how coordination efficiency could affect recursive AI improvement.

items.t: @cognition: Today we're introducing updates that make Devin significantly cheaper. It's now: ▪️ 30–40% cheaper in Fusion a…
items.sm: Reports Cognition’s claimed Devin price reductions across operating modes and code review, alongside a claimed first-place Fusion ranking on FrontierCode 1.1 Extended.

items.t: @cognition: Model independence lets us call the best model for each part of Devin’s work. We continue refining the harness…
items.sm: Cognition reports improving Devin’s price-performance by selecting models for individual tasks, batching work, running actions in parallel, and reusing cached context.

items.t: MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-agent Systems
items.a: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Huwei Ji, Li Zhang, Junfeng Fang
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) split a task across specialized roles and are promising on complex tasks, yet a prevailing approach relies on inference-time orchestration alone. General-purpose APIs are costly and hard to customize, while small models with role prompts rarely develop stable role competence or reliable collaboration, so post-training a MAS jointly is central. Most attempts use reinforcement learning, whose …
items.sm: Explores on-policy distillation for jointly training specialized collaborating agents using teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories rather than task-specific local rewards.

items.t: Self-Adapting Group of Experts for Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Mohammad Atif Quamar, Nurbek Tastan, Karthik Nandakumar, Junpei Komiyama
items.x: Multi-agent systems bring together language model agents with different roles to propose, review, and refine solutions. Each agent's response depends on its model's capabilities, the reasoning strategy defined by its system prompt, and the information in its input context. Existing frameworks often adapt communication by changing this context while leaving individual prompts fixed, even when a problem calls for diffe…
items.sm: Introduces SAGE, which selects an agent’s reasoning strategy through agreement and peer review, then transfers it to teammates while preserving their roles.

items.t: BaRe-Mem: Bayesian Reliability Memory for Robust and Adaptive Agent Consultation
items.a: Peilin Feng, Zhengyang Huang, Soujanya Poria
items.x: In multi-agent systems, reliable consultation is challenging because advisor capabilities vary across tasks, and misleading information can make consultation worse than autonomous reasoning. We introduce BaRe-Mem, an online Bayesian reliability memory for multi-agent consultation. It estimates advisor reliability based on the central model's internal belief representations and updates these estimates from historical …
items.sm: Introduces Bayesian memory that tracks advisor reliability, adjusts advice influence, and chooses when agents should consult others or reason independently.

items.t: MASTraceBench: Diagnosing Collaboration Gains through Proposal Trajectories in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yapeng Li, Songze Li, Shuang Yu, Jing Yu, Zhixin Liu, Liqiang Wen, Tonghua Su
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have shown promise in complex problem solving. As MAS methods diversify, systematic evaluation becomes increasingly challenging. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on final outcomes, leaving unclear how collaboration gains arise, are preserved, or are lost. To address this limitation, we introduce MASTraceBench, a benchmark for diagnosing collaboration gains through proposa…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark that tracks evolving agent proposals to measure collaboration gains, final performance, and token costs across six tasks.

items.t: An Exact Generate - Transform Decomposition of Small-LLM Team Scaling Across Orchestration Architectures
items.x: Replacing one LLM agent with a collaborating team can raise accuracy, but whether scaling the team helps, and which architecture to scale, is unclear. Sweeping eight agent orchestration architectures across five instruction-tuned 7-9B models, five short-answer benchmarks, and an executable-code benchmark up to 30 calls, we find that the returns to team scaling are sharply task-dependent: from three to thirty calls ac…
items.sm: Finds that larger teams of small language models improve arithmetic substantially more than other tested tasks, with no orchestration architecture consistently winning.

items.t: Multi-agent systems improve structural quality of AI-generated sustainable product design specifications
items.sm: Reports that adversarial agent teams produce product design specifications with more structural justification relative to performance requirements than single-agent approaches.

items.t: ResonAct: Streaming Metrics for Runtime Diagnosis and Self-Healing in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Tarun Chintada, Neelamadhav Gantayat, Ishaan Romil, Renuka Sindhgatta, Soujanya Soni, Sameep Mehta
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly used to automate enterprise workflows involving multiple specialized agents, external tools, and long-running task execution. Failures may arise from tool degradation, context propagation errors, coordination breakdowns, or repeated agent interactions that prevent task completion. While existing observability frameworks provide traces and logs, diagnosis and remediation are …
items.sm: Introduces ResonAct, which continuously analyzes operational metrics to diagnose failures and support recovery during multi-agent workflow execution.

items.t: Attenuation, Not Amplification: Measuring Indirect Prompt Injection Propagation and Containment in Multi-Agent LLM Delegation Chains
items.sm: Studies whether indirect prompt injections weaken or spread through agent delegation chains, comparing payload styles, chain lengths, models, and sanitization defenses.

items.t: Evo2Team: When Do Evolved Skills Transfer? From Selection to Deployment
items.x: A skill bank that helps one multi-agent system may leave another's behavior unchanged. A transferred rule helps only when target agents act on it successfully. We study this path for routing and communication skills in Count-Frequency and AgentsNet, using teams of 4--32 agents and GPT and Qwen model ladders. Source evolution meets a joint quality, cost, model-tier, and confirmation goal in 14 of 16 settings. We then …
items.sm: Introduces Evo2Team to select, adapt, and validate transferable team skills, reporting positive transfer in 20 of 28 evaluated directions.

items.t: Security threat modeling for emerging AI-agent protocols: A comparative analysis of MCP, A2A, agora, and ANP
items.a: Zeynab Anbiaee, Mahdi Rabbani, Mansur Mirani, Gunjan Piya, Igor Opushnyev, Ali Akbar Ghorbani, Sajjad Dadkhah
items.v: Journal of Information Security and Applications
items.x: The rapid development of AI-agent communication protocols, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent2Agent (A2A), Agora, and the Agent Network Protocol (ANP), is reshaping how autonomous agents interact with tools, services, and one another. Although these protocols support scalable multi-agent interaction and cross-organizational interoperability, their protocol-level security properties remain insufficientl…
items.sm: Develops a structured threat-modeling approach to compare security risks across MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP agent communication protocols.

items.t: Prompted Identity Degrades Cooperation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Xavier Del Giudice, Alessio Palma, Matteo Migliarini, Fabio Galasso, Indro Spinelli
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly mix models from several providers, yet exposing each agent's underlying model identity to its peers significantly impairs cooperation. We show that when agents are aware of each other's model family, the group splits into clusters, where agents prefer interacting with others carrying their same label, although nothing in the task rewards or asks for such a split. We argue that the…
items.sm: Finds that exposing agents to model-family or arbitrary identity labels encourages factions and reduces cooperation, while removing labels eliminates the observed grouping.

items.t: Semantic Drift in Autonomous Agents: Detecting Runtime Goal Mutation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.sm: Introduces GuardAgent Runtime, middleware that inspects untrusted agent inputs and tracks semantic drift to maintain alignment with the user’s authorized objective.

items.t: KITA AI: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Pluralistic Policy Deliberation
items.a: Arnau Mayoral-Macau, Jiaqi Lai, Manala Tyobeka, Vukosi Marivate, William Chandra Tjhi, Georgina Curto
items.x: Public policies addressing urgent social and environmental challenges need to explicitly consider the diverse, often conflicting perspectives of the affected stakeholders. Despite computational decision-support approaches increasingly offering recommendations across diverse human value systems, they still tend to deliver a single consensus-driven outcome. We present KITA AI, a modular system in which multiple large l…
items.sm: Introduces KITA AI, which uses stakeholder agents to expose competing policy positions, supporting rationales, quantitative indicators, and unresolved disagreements.

items.t: KVCMAS: Efficient KV cache Correction for Shared Context in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Hyesung Jeon, Hyeongju Ha, Seoyoung Lee, Beomseok Kang, Jae-Joon Kim
items.x: Prompt-specialized multi-agent systems enable multiple agents to share a model while performing complementary roles to solve complex tasks. However, agent-specific prefixes change the KV cache generated for the same shared context, causing each agent to repeatedly prefill the growing context and construct a separate cache with high computation and memory overhead. Selective recomputation reduces this redundancy but s…
items.sm: Introduces an online KV cache correction framework intended to reduce repeated processing and memory overhead when specialized agents share context.

items.t: AI Agent Swarms as Researchers: Progress, Challenges, and Open Questions
items.a: Sergey Gusev, David E. Bernal Neira
items.x: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents, language models connected to tools and run in a loop, can now carry out long, multi-step tasks with little supervision. We gave swarms of off-the-shelf coding agents a short statement of scope, from a narrow topic to a whole field, access to the literature and to computing tools, and one standing instruction: make real, correct, useful progress, and do not stop. We supplied no sci…
items.sm: Reports that minimally directed coding-agent swarms generated research drafts and proofs across several fields, while acknowledging incomplete verification of correctness and novelty.

items.t: Governed Memory-Driven Multi-Agent Software Development: A Contract-First Methodology for AI-Orchestrated SDLC
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a software development methodology combining specialized agents, persistent memory, explicit contracts, and human approvals across lifecycle phases.

items.t: Emergence, Not Bandwidth: Physical Coupling and the Limits of Learned Multi-Agent Communication
items.x: Rate-limited multi-agent teams raise three questions the emergent-communication literature has answered only empirically: what an optimal message should encode, what compression costs over a horizon, and when a learned protocol is unique enough for a teammate to read. We answer them for rate-limited Dec-POMDPs, then measure how far reinforcement learning falls short of the optimum. Our theorems fix what is achievable…
items.sm: Derives theoretical limits for communication in bandwidth-constrained agent teams and compares learned protocols with engineered alternatives under different degrees of physical coupling.

items.t: Measuring Collapse and Correction in Homogeneous-Panel LLM Debate
items.a: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Chau Yuen
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) debate is often evaluated by whether final answers improve, but a changed answer is not necessarily a better one: the same discussion can correct an initially wrong majority or collapse an initially correct one. Standard final-accuracy evaluations conflate these opposing transitions. We introduce an auditable protocol for homogeneous debate on multiple-choice questions (MCQs) th…
items.sm: Introduces a debate evaluation protocol separating corrections from harmful answer changes, showing that freezing discussions can prevent errors while sacrificing more corrections.

items.t: dagoSte/squadra
items.x: Coordinate Claude, Codex and Cursor windows with shared tasks, acknowledgements, prechecks, parallel tests, source-bound proofs and independent review. Built-in skills recall lessons, simplify code and forecast work. Track progress, decisions and evidence in a bilingual local dashboard, with MCP plugins. Browse skills and verified security audits.
items.sm: Coordinates coding agents through shared tasks, checks, parallel tests, evidence, independent review, and a local dashboard for progress and decisions.

items.t: savannahfeder/agentbox
items.x: A desktop GUI for running dozens of Claude Code and Codex agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree. Answer them like email, or use the board view. Free, open source, on the plan you already pay for.
items.sm: Provides a desktop interface for running parallel Claude Code and Codex agents in separate Git worktrees, with inbox and board views.

items.t: solutionscay/skiff
items.x: The multi-agent coding terminal. Run Claude Code, Codex and other agents in parallel on Linux and macOS. They send each other tasks and report back.
items.sm: Provides a terminal for running coding agents in parallel on Linux and macOS, allowing agents to exchange tasks and report results.

items.t: Parallel coding agents: what still breaks at merge
items.sm: Reports small coding experiments showing conflicting edits require integration decisions, while separate-file parallel edits used nearly twice the tokens for little time savings.

items.t: Predictable Swarm Scaling
items.sm: Simulates agent swarms on dependency graphs, showing that additional agents accelerate exploration but dependency chains limit completion speed and gains in solution quality.

items.t: Where's the intelligence explosion?
items.sm: Argues that autonomous research and larger agent swarms do not yet demonstrate self-sustaining accelerating improvement, citing coordination costs, limited diversity, and uncertain research gains.

items.t: DEALS: Decentralized Expertise-Aware Load Serving for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Jingjuan Huang, Wenbin Wang, Yanchuan Yin, Alvaro Velasquez, Jia Liu
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) have recently emerged as an effective approach for coordinating large language model (LLM)-based agents to solve complex tasks through structured interactions. In practice, MASs often handle a stream of heterogeneous and complex tasks, requiring agents to decompose each task and then self-organize and self-evolve to adapt to incoming tasks while sharing execution resources. However, most ear…
items.sm: Proposes decentralized task serving that accounts for agent expertise and workload to support adaptable coordination in multi-agent language model systems.

items.t: Beyond Solo and Consistency: Vindicating Multi-Agent Debate via Conditional Progressive Pruning
items.a: Ruosong Ye, Caiqi Zhang, Jiahao Li, Haijun Wu, Xiaolong Luo, Huiyuan Chen, Yu Wang, Ying Chen
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM) based Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) is one of the most effective test time scaling techniques. Through multi-round communication, agents complement each other in knowledge and reasoning and solve tasks that no single member can solve. However, existing MAD frameworks fail to beat strong Single Agent and Consistency-based baselines under the same strict cost limit, which shakes the foundation of …
items.sm: Introduces Conditional Progressive Pruning for multi-agent debate and claims it outperforms existing debate frameworks and consistency-based methods under constrained costs.

items.t: Collective Regimes in Multi-Agent LLMs under Reasoning Effort and Communication Topology
items.a: Machiko Hirota, Akshara Nadayanur Sathis Kanna, Ujwal Kumar, Phan Xuan Tan
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used for deliberation and evaluation, often under the assumption that greater peer interaction leads to more reliable consensus. Existing work largely evaluates these systems through final accuracy or aggregate agreement. However, such measures do not reveal how agreement is organized in the panel. In this paper, we study N = 50 stateless LLM agents that update their predictio…
items.sm: Studies how reasoning effort and communication topology shape agreement among 50 agents, identifying synchronized, locally ordered but globally inconsistent, and mixed collective states.

items.t: Population Physics, Population Problems: Safety and Emergence in LLM Societies
items.x: The collective behaviour of large language model (LLM) societies is not the sum of their individual outputs. It yields statistically distinct, sometimes-unpredictable phenomena, for which the tools we use to study single agents may not scale. Due to recent incidents involving autonomous agentic systems, however, understanding these systems is paramount. For that we introduce a framework for measuring self-organisatio…
items.sm: Introduces a framework for measuring self-organization in language-model societies and reports distinct collective dynamics across three simulated or observed social systems.

items.t: Maat: Independent Deterministic Contract-Based Governance for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
items.x: Large-language-model multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) introduce a characteristic reliability problem: an error produced by one agent can be accepted as context by downstream agents and propagate across the workflow. Many proposed safeguards rely on learned or LLM-based judges whose verdicts are themselves probabilistic; we ask whether a deterministic layer can instead stop contract-detectable handoff defects. We present…
items.sm: Introduces deterministic contract checks for agent handoffs and reports an audit finding that some benchmark scorers incorrectly rewarded early workflow termination.

items.t: TRACE: Governing Memory Validity in Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Wenjun Xiong, Shengtao Zhang, Shangding Gu, Bo Tang, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Ying Wen, Muning Wen
items.x: Persistent memory lets language-model agents carry information across long-running collaborations, but leaves a lifecycle question open: what may a returning agent still act on once the shared state has changed? A memory can be correctly retrieved, relevant to the current task, and faithful to its source, and nonetheless be inadmissible for action: an itinerary saved before a pause still names the hotel the team has …
items.sm: TRACE checks changes made during an agent’s absence to determine which stored memories remain valid for action when it returns.

items.t: ORBIT: A Framework for Multi-Agent Safety and Security Evaluations
items.a: Ben Hagag, William L. Anderson, Srija Chakraborty, Christian Schroeder de Witt
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly deployed for complex, long-horizon tasks or emerge as a natural consequence of agents interacting in the wild. Yet they give rise to significant safety and security risks: the flexible protocols that enable task generalization also expose novel threats, from cascading prompt injection to inter-agent collusion. Progress in defending against these threats has been slowed by a la…
items.sm: ORBIT provides a configurable framework for evaluating attacks, defenses, and system architectures across multi-agent safety and security scenarios.

items.t: A2A-CaseVerify: Merkle-Linked Case-Evidence Verification for Cross-Organization A2A Workflows
items.x: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication enables large language model (LLM) agents to exchange tasks, messages, and artifacts across organizations. A valid message alone does not establish that a final workflow claim is supported by a complete, ordered, and case-consistent evidence path. We present A2A-CaseVerify, a deterministic offline verifier that maps preserved A2A runtime objects, business events, and typed support e…
items.sm: A2A-CaseVerify checks whether cross-organization agent workflow claims have complete, ordered, consistent supporting evidence using deterministic verification and Merkle commitments.

items.t: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Liron Soffer, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Chen Shani
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent settings, where agents observe and influence one another, making social influence a key dimension of AI behavior and safety. We investigate whether LLMs' responses depend on the social identity of other agents, beyond the effect of their consensus. We construct judgment tasks with a single correct answer, and place models in a multi-agent setting w…
items.sm: Experiments across 12 models find that agents follow incorrect consensus more often from perceived insiders and less often from outsiders.

items.t: Learning to Sell: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Large Language Model Agents in Multi-Product Markets
items.a: Shuze Liu, Claire Chen, Jiuqi Wang, David Simchi‐Levi, Thorsten Joachims
items.x: Autonomous large language model (LLM) agents operating in multi-product markets must make sequential decisions under information asymmetry and resource constraints. We develop a machine learning approach for training such agents to act effectively as sellers in a multi-item bargaining environment, where a seller concurrently negotiates a catalog of substitutable assets across a pool of independent buyers. Buyers hold…
items.sm: Develops reinforcement learning methods for seller agents negotiating multiple products with buyers whose private valuations are unknown, under limited communication budgets.

items.t: Deception at the Registry Layer: An Architecture for Detecting Autonomous AI Agents in Model Context Protocol Environments
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes mixing real and decoy MCP servers behind one registry gateway to detect agents discovering credentials and distinguish that from using them.

items.t: HTN Planning as a Coordination Layer for Multi-Server MCP Tool Orchestration
items.a: Eliott Jacopin, Éric Jacopin, Koichi Takahashi
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) isolates servers by design: only the host can orchestrate cross-server workflows. When the host is a large language model, the resulting orchestrations are non-deterministic, non-reproducible, and pay one inference round-trip per tool call. We present a coordination architecture in which a Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planner generates a verifiable cross-server plan once, and a run…
items.sm: Uses hierarchical task planning to create verifiable workflows that middleware executes deterministically across multiple MCP servers while passing data between actions.

items.t: ANTMAN: Adaptive Need Tracking for Multi-Agent Navigation in Large Information Spaces
items.a: Jerry Wang, Haibo Jin, Xiaopeng Yuan, Peng Kuang, Haohan Wang
items.x: Information-seeking agents increasingly operate over information spaces that are too large to process exhaustively. Yet many multi-agent systems organize computation around static partitions of the available space, causing coordination to grow with how information is segmented rather than with what the query still requires. We introduce ANTMAN, an adaptive coordination framework that treats evolving unresolved inform…
items.sm: ANTMAN coordinates information-seeking agents through an evolving graph of unresolved needs, evidence, and search progress to guide assignments and recovery.

items.t: Learning Strategies to Break Judges
items.a: Guruprerana Shabadi, Aaditya Naik, Rajeev Alur, Mayur Naik
items.x: As AI agents surpass human performance, it becomes exceedingly hard for system designers to evaluate them directly and understand their failure modes. Consequently, agents themselves are being deployed extensively to evaluate, judge, and provide feedback on model traces. But this raises an important question: how can we trust the judge? In this work, we propose an agent-guided method to find weaknesses of agentic jud…
items.sm: Uses adversarial agents to introduce proof errors that evade automated judges, then extracts mutation strategies to explain the judges’ weaknesses.

items.t: leonvanzyl/cubefarm
items.x: A cartoon 3D office where a swarm of Claude Code agents (plus QA testers) works through your GitHub issues
items.sm: Provides a cartoon 3D office where Claude Code agents and QA testers work through GitHub issues.

items.t: Jakeschincariol/arena-skill
items.x: When Claude keeps giving you bad answers, make 100 versions of it fight to the death. Same task, 100 different strategies, a bracket, one answer left. Free Claude Code skill.
items.sm: Provides a Claude Code skill that compares 100 strategies for the same task through a tournament to select one answer.

items.t: jeffreycayao/Dev-Labs
items.x: DevLabs™ Free, open source and local-first. A multi-agent harness that works with the AI subscriptions you already pay for. It turns the terminal coding CLIs you already run into a team:.
items.sm: Provides an open-source, local-first harness that organizes terminal coding tools into agent teams using existing AI subscriptions.

items.t: JuniorXcoder/hermes-virtual-office
items.x: A 3D office for your AI agent fleet: desks per division, meetings with auto-generated minutes where the turns come from real agents over A2A, live screen-peeking, and a Kanban board synced to Hermes. Open source, Next.js + Three.js, driven by the official hermes CLI.
items.sm: Displays agent teams in a 3D office with division desks, agent meetings, generated minutes, live screen viewing, and a Hermes-synced Kanban board.

items.t: @mark_k: AI agents are learning how to work together instead of following a fixed script. In a new paper from Stanford…
items.sm: Reports that trained agent teams outperform individual models and compute-matched alternatives on five math and physics benchmarks, suggesting collaboration contributes beyond independent answers.

items.t: @gerardsans: 🚨 Multi-Agent Analysis: Behind the "swarm" hype: a loop is not AGI A lab posts a number. 10,000 agents. 88 hou…
items.sm: Argues that large agent swarms reflect changes in search strategy and computing budgets rather than improvements in underlying model intelligence.

items.t: @HEI: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents Zhihao Zhan, Ting Song, Li Dong, Shaohan Huang, Ji…
items.sm: Shares a paper listing whose title claims organizational intelligence scales to 1,024 agents, while noting that methods and benefits remain unverified.

items.t: @TheZvi: Claude Opus 5.5 Should Raise Your Ambitions. When it comes to making things, or doing most things in general, …
items.sm: Argues that Claude Opus 5.5’s perceived capability, persistence, and writing quality should encourage users to attempt more ambitious projects.

items.t: Relic: From Multi-Agent Collaboration to Persistent Organizational Capability
items.a: Hongyi Du, Tianyi Zhang, Weijia Zhang, Yi Yang, Haofei Yu, Kunlun Zhu, Tianxiang Dai, Shang Jiang
items.x: Multiple agents may often conflict in an organization: for example, one coding agent changes an interface in a repository, but another continues to develop on the old version where existing tests become stale. A conversation can resolve the episode, but when the participants change, what makes the lesson continue to govern the team? We introduce Relic, which turns recurring collaboration failures into organization-ow…
items.sm: Relic converts recurring agent collaboration failures into shared executable protocols that teams can adopt, enforce, revise, and retire.

items.t: Beyond Symmetric Agents: Cognitive Diversity and Multi-Agent Debate in Small Language Models
items.a: Leonardo Ferreira, Gardenia Liu, Kaden Zheng
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) reportedly improves reasoning and factuality over single-model inference, but prior work treats agents as symmetric peers, leaving open what drives the gains. We test the hypothesis that cognitive diversity among agents is the driver, in the setting where the question is still measurable: small open-weight models with benchmark headroom. Across 23 models from eleven vendor families, five task…
items.sm: Finds that cognitive diversity does not explain debate gains, and small-model debate matches or trails budget-matched majority voting while consuming more time and tokens.

items.t: Prefill-Free Cross-Family KV Cache Transfer for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent LLMs
items.a: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Woosang Lim, Haneul Yoo, Sungjoo Yoo, Murali Annavaram, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy
items.x: Recent multi-agent LLM systems increasingly combine heterogeneous models for specialized agent roles. However, text-based communication requires each receiver to prefill shared context already processed by the sender. Reusing the sender's key-value (KV) cache avoids this redundancy, but prefill-free transfer across model families must handle differences in tokenization, model depth, and KV representations. To address…
items.sm: HeteroFold transfers attention caches between frozen models from different families, avoiding repeated context processing by aligning structures and calibrating representations.

items.t: Despite Instructions: Frontier Agents Improvise Covert Channels at Test Time
items.a: Jacob Dineen, Silei Ren, Muhao Chen, Dan Roth, Ben Zhou
items.x: In security-sensitive applications, language-model agents are often required to coordinate without disclosing confidential information. Yet repeated interactions may also let ordinary messages acquire shared private meaning. We study a repeated game with pairs of models in which the sender model observes one of four secret states and selects one of four summaries of the same public report, while the receiver model tr…
items.sm: Finds that model pairs can develop covert communication during repeated interactions using minimal feedback, despite instructions against disclosing confidential information.

items.t: AsynCodeBench: Benchmarking Collaboration of Asynchronous Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering
items.a: Kaituo Zhang, Zhen Xiong, Zhimeng Jiang, Mingyu Zhong, Zhouyuan Yuan, Zhecheng Li, Bowen Lin, Chia-Yuan Chang
items.x: Multi-agent coding has emerged as an increasingly active direction in software engineering, where complex development tasks are decomposed across multiple specialized agents working on different parts of the problem. Despite the shift from individual problem solving to distributed collaboration, multi-agent systems still lack a direct measure of collaboration and are largely evaluated through task-level outcomes inhe…
items.sm: AsynCodeBench evaluates asynchronous coding collaboration using explicit dependency graphs and executable checks to measure coordination between agents.

items.t: Black-Box Auditing of Epistemic Reliability in Multi-Agent Debate Distillation
items.a: Derui Wang, Zewei Shi, Rayne Holland, Ruoxi Sun, Xingliang Yuan, Jason Xue, Liming Zhu
items.x: Debate distillation adapts weaker verifiers using multi-agent debate transcripts to improve their judgement in subsequent debates, but gains on monitored tasks do not establish reliability on related unmonitored tasks. We study epistemic reliability degradation, in which adaptation preserves monitored performance while reducing support for correct responses on hidden tasks. We consider an adversarial debater that man…
items.sm: Introduces ER-Audit to assess whether debate-based verifier adaptation preserves monitored performance while weakening reliability on related hidden tasks.

items.t: Improving LLM Collaboration via Multi-Agent Preference Learning
items.a: Shuo Liu, Xinzichen Li, Tianle Chen, Christopher Amato
items.x: Several works have explored multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in LLM collaboration. However, constructing reliable rewards is difficult in practice, as complete and accurate metrics are often unavailable and hard to aggregate. Preference learning provides an alternative by learning from comparative human or AI feedback. Yet, its extension to multi-agent systems remains underexplored. To address this gap, we f…
items.sm: Introduces a framework for improving agent collaboration through comparative human or AI feedback, supporting both centralized and decentralized learning.

items.t: Disaggregated KV-Cache Fabric: Hardware-Agnostic RAM-Tiering, PCIe DMA Eviction, and Fine-Grained Prefix Deduplication for Autonomous Agent Swarms
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes an open-source cache architecture that tiers memory across host and accelerator hardware and deduplicates shared prefixes to reduce agent serving memory demands.

items.t: Trust the Brand, Lose Control: How Identity Hijacks LLM Agent Orchestration
items.a: Xutao Mao, Rui Qian, Linghan Chen, Yudong Gao, Junchi Liao, Jiulin Cai, Jinman Zhao, Cong Wang
items.x: LLM agents now execute tasks end to end with permission to change real systems and increasingly orchestrate subagents that differ in capability and cost. Prior work treats the choice of subagent as an optimization problem. Yet the orchestrator makes this choice from the identities that subagents display, and an attacker can spoof them. Displayed identity thus decides operational authority, meaning who is trusted to c…
items.sm: Introduces TrustFork, a benchmark examining whether spoofed subagent identities cause orchestrators to grant risky agents authority despite contradictory evidence.

items.t: Theory of Scene: Breaking the Symmetry Trap in Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
items.a: Liangqi Yuan, Wenzhi Fang, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are largely homogeneous, as their agents behave alike even across distinct LLMs. We show that when such agents act concurrently without communication, they collide on targets they must split and diverge on targets they must take together, a double failure we term the symmetry trap. Theory of Mind (ToM), widely used for coordination without communication, canno…
items.sm: Proposes a training-free reasoning method that uses public roles and shared context to coordinate similar agents without communication.

items.t: Large language model agents capture heterogeneous occupant behaviors in building energy simulation of shared office spaces
items.a: Xiaoxiao Xu, Guanying Huang, Zonglin Li, Stergios-Aristoteles Mitoulis
items.sm: Couples building energy simulation with language-model agents representing differing occupant preferences, demonstrating feasibility in a simulated four-person shared office.

items.t: Multi-Agent System Search via Active Substructure-aware Policy Optimization
items.a: Beicheng Xu, Bowen Fan, Weitong Qian, Lingching Tung, Bin Cui
items.x: LLMs enable multi-agent systems (MAS) to tackle complex tasks, but manually designing agent roles, prompts, and communication structures requires substantial expertise and effort. This motivates learning policies that construct query-specific MAS from execution reward. Existing approaches typically train these policies by repeatedly traversing a fixed set of training queries and assigning rewards at the workflow leve…
items.sm: ASPO trains policies to construct task-specific agent systems, prioritizing queries near current capability limits and identifying useful workflow substructures.

items.t: Learning Together and Against Each Other: How Multiple Reinforcement-Learning Agents Coordinate, Compete and Where the Field is Heading
items.a: Rajiv Ranganath, Thrisha R., Vismaya M., Akshitha Katkeri
items.v: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
items.sm: Reviews mathematical foundations, algorithm families, and learning challenges in multi-agent reinforcement learning across cooperative, competitive, and mixed settings.

items.t: RepoMAS: Solving Progressively Specified Tasks with Issue-Driven Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yuchen Song, Andong Chen, Wenxin Zhu, Muyun Yang, Tiejun Zhao
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MASs) have shown strong potential for solving complex tasks, but most assume that task requirements are sufficiently specified before execution. In practice, user requests are often incomplete, and additional requirements may only become clear during reasoning, tool use, or execution. We refer to such problems as progressively specified tasks. To systematically study this setting, we in…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark and an issue-driven agent framework for tasks whose requirements emerge during execution.

items.t: heddles/agent-orca
items.x: Agent-orca orchestrates and manages AI agent workloads in Kubernetes, providing distributed execution, model routing, knowledge integration, and tool access through MCP and stdio tools.
items.sm: Manages AI agent workloads on Kubernetes with distributed execution, model routing, knowledge integration, and access to tools.

items.sm: Runs parallel agents and custom workflows in an open-source desktop application, with triggers from schedules, webhooks, and external tool events.
