items.t: Multi-agent Scaling Across Disjunctive and Compensatory Tasks
items.sm: Examines how task structure affects agent team scaling, finding that more agents increase correct answer availability without necessarily improving plurality voting.

items.t: Learning What to Skip: Counterfactual Credit Assignment for Efficient Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
items.a: Jinfeng Xu, Zheyu Chen, Ziyue Peng, Zheng Lin, Shuo Yang, Jinze Li, Zheng Xing, Mengran Li
items.x: Multi-agent LLM workflows use planning, execution, verification, and summarization to improve task performance, yet the value of each component depends on the state already produced. Executing every component can waste computation or overwrite a correct intermediate answer. We formulate component omission as counterfactual credit assignment: full-workflow logs reveal the executed trajectory's reward, while controlled…
items.sm: Introduces a controller that learns from skipped workflow steps to decide when agents can safely omit later components.

items.t: Composing Agents, Compounding Risks: A Tutorial on Robustness and Alignment in Multi-Agent Recommender Systems
items.a: Kurt Cutajar, Jas Kandola, Anjun Hu, Yashar Deldjoo
items.sm: Presents a tutorial on how risks spread through multi-agent recommender systems, with a risk taxonomy, evaluation framework, and mitigation strategies.

items.t: Vulnerabilities in autonomous execution: A survey of security threats and defenses in LLM-driven agentic and multi-agent systems
items.sm: Surveys security threats and defenses in autonomous execution by language model agents and multi-agent systems.

items.t: Towards Mitigating Fabricated Consensus: The Active Provenance Gate for Multi-Agent Debate Synthesis
items.x: Large language model-based multi-agent debate (MAD) systems are being increasingly used as complex decision pipelines in distributed processes. However, their final synthesis phase still remains inadequately controlled. Even with detailed debate logs, summarizing models are prone to fabricating smoothly written debate consensus that is not grounded in the debate's history. To address this safety gap, this paper prese…
items.sm: Introduces a verification layer that checks debate summaries against discussion records to reduce invented agreement and preserve unresolved disagreements.

items.t: Receiver-Conditioned Latent Communication gives 94% CacheBack
items.a: Maximillian Rossi, Prajwal Raghunath, Haoqing Xuan, Yusen Zhang, Eugene Wu
items.x: Multi-agent systems distribute large contexts across agents that communicate to solve a task. Text messages are compact but require decoding and may omit evidence the receiving agent needs. Recent latent communication instead transfers KV caches. This avoids text generation and can improve accuracy and latency. However, a full KV cache grows linearly with both the context an individual agent processes, and the number…
items.sm: Proposes compressing agents' internal attention caches according to receiving agents' information needs to reduce communication memory and context costs.

items.t: Agentic Economies for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
items.a: Nenad Tomasev, Matija Franklin, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Vivek Natarajan, Alan Karthikesalingam, Sebastien Krier, Simon Osindero
items.x: Recent advances in agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems have marked a shift in AI for Science: moving away from the use of individual AI systems for narrow task execution, toward multi-agent systems capable of orchestrating complex, end-to-end research workflows and performing (semi-)autonomous scientific discovery. The development of multi-agent AI-for-science systems has primarily focused on improving the c…
items.sm: Argues that autonomous scientific discovery needs resource management alongside improved agent reasoning because experiments consume limited physical and economic resources.

items.t: Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Actually Help? A Controlled Evaluation of Single-Agent, LLM-Orchestrated, and Deterministically Orchestrated Architectures
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Finds that a single agent and deterministic orchestration achieve similar transactional task success, while language model orchestration performs worse and consumes more resources.

items.t: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Risk Assessment of Traffic Analysis Attacks on Cloud LLM Services
items.a: Shahrooz Pouryousef, Jesus Lopez, Saeefa Rubaiyet Nowmi, Md Mahmuduzzaman Kamol, Moinul Hossain, Muoi Tran, Mohammad Saidur Rahman
items.x: Cloud-based Large language model (LLM) services create a network-level traffic side channel that can expose model, prompt, and task behavior despite encryption. From packet sizes, directions, timing, and burst structure alone, a passive local observer can infer the serving model, the user's prompt category, and the task executed by a collaborative multi-agent system. Yet current evidence is fragmented across separate…
items.sm: Introduces an encrypted traffic benchmark to assess whether packet metadata reveals serving models, prompt categories, and multi-agent tasks.

items.t: Engineering Least-Privilege Agentic AI Workflows: Patterns, Anti-Patterns, and Practitioner Guidance
items.v: Annals of Computer Science and Information Systems
items.sm: Presents six engineering patterns and five anti-patterns for restricting agent permissions in production workflows using Model Context Protocol tools.

items.t: Financial Fragility in Societies of LLM Agents: Coordination Failures and Stabilizing Mechanisms
items.a: Zhenhao Fu, Ruipeng Xu, Qibing Ren
items.x: Individually protective decisions can produce avoidable collective failures. As large language model (LLM) agents take on greater roles in financial decision-making, financial AI safety must therefore be considered not only at the level of individual agents, but also at the level of the systems they jointly create. We study this problem with FRAIL, a controlled experimental framework that places LLM agents in three d…
items.sm: Finds frequent collective failures among language model agents in simulated financial environments and compares coordination mechanisms intended to improve stability.

items.t: Symbolic Guidance for LLM Agents in Distributed Multiagent Coordination
items.a: Ben Rachmut, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, William Yeoh
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in multi-agent systems, yet their ability to reliably execute distributed coordination protocols remains poorly understood. While AgentsNet, a benchmark framework for distributed coordination among LLM agents, enables such coordination, granting full reasoning autonomy often leads to inconsistent or degraded performance in complex domains. We…
items.sm: Investigates how algorithmic guidance and different levels of agent autonomy affect distributed coordination among language model agents.

items.t: PREreview of "Total Cost of Agency: Exact Attribution of Memory Injection Cost in Multi-Agent LLM Workflows"
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reviews a study measuring memory injection costs in multi-agent workflows, highlighting increasing costs with workflow depth and the absence of prompt caching evaluation.

items.t: A Benchmark and Diagnostic Study of Epistemic Admission in Shared Agent Memory
items.a: Xiaoyang Li, Yiqi Wang, Chencheng Zhu, KE XU, Wencheng Yang, Zequn Sun, Pingan Song, Yiqun Duan
items.x: Evaluating claim admission in shared agent memory is challenging because repeated claims may be mistaken for independent evidence. An agent may copy or paraphrase a retrieved belief, while admitting a false claim exposes subsequent agents to it. To study this problem, we introduce the Correlated Promotion Benchmark (CPB), which evaluates whether candidate claims should be admitted to shared memory.CPB-Static construc…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark for admitting claims into shared agent memory, examining how repeated evidence and source deduplication affect acceptance decisions.

items.t: Methodological Harness in Agentic Software Engineering: An Empirical Study on Mining Software Repositories
items.a: Jessica Díaz, Jorge Pérez, Sergio Gil-Borrás
items.x: Context. Agentic software engineering requires mechanisms to coordinate and govern agents' work. The framework motivating this study proposes a methodological harness with eight mechanisms: context engineering, persistent shared knowledge, executable specifications, N-version mindset and parallel agents, normative specifications, structured consultation, evidence-based acceptance, and graduated autonomy. These are re…
items.sm: Studies software repositories to measure adoption of eight mechanisms for coordinating and governing agentic software engineering, including specifications, shared knowledge, and acceptance evidence.

items.t: Do Multi-agent Systems Make Better Software? An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Frameworks for Software Development
items.a: Sandra Mitrović, Vincenzo Giuffrida, Michel Rosselli, Mattia Bosetti, Matteo Salani
items.sm: Evaluates language model frameworks for software development to investigate whether multi-agent systems produce better software.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning of Communication in a Mesh of Small Language Models
items.x: Language models gain accuracy from more compute at test time, but majority voting over independent samples saturates: as samples grow, the vote converges to the model's most frequent answer. Communication can add what sampling cannot: an agent that solves a problem can pass the key step to the others. We present TalkMesh, a decentralized mesh of small language model agents that learns when and what to communicate. Ea…
items.sm: Introduces TalkMesh, a decentralized network of small language model agents that learns to exchange hints and revise answers using confidence scores.

items.t: DocuTeam: Mixed-Initiative Multi-Agent Discussions around Evolving Documents
items.a: Heechan Lee, Juhyeon Choi, Tae Soo Kim, Juho Kim, Joseph Seering
items.x: In open-ended problem solving, collaborators often rely on discussion to surface concerns, challenge perspectives, and refine shared work as it evolves. While AI agents are increasingly used as discussion partners, existing multi-agent systems place a heavy burden on users to initiate and carefully orchestrate the discussions. We present DocuTeam, a mixed-initiative multi-agent discussion system in which both users a…
items.sm: Introduces document-aware agent discussions and reports that 20 participants produced more novel, relevant, and specific outcomes without increased cognitive load.

items.t: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
items.a: Qi Pang, Virginia Smith, Wenting Zheng
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings such as finance, healthcare, and software engineering, where agents coordinate through natural-language messages. The same channels, however, let colluding agents exfiltrate confidential information or coordinate unauthorized actions, and steganography can hide such communication inside outputs that look ordina…
items.sm: Introduces Codetta, a method claimed to let colluding agents hide substantial information in ordinary-looking messages without a shared secret key.

items.t: MeshHeal: Two-Timescale Self-Healing for Gray Failures in Decentralized LLM Agent Networks
items.a: Keru Chen, Sen Lin, Yingbin Liang, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Shaofeng Zou
items.x: Decentralized LLM-based multi-agent systems coordinate through local interactions, but an agent can remain responsive while its task-solving quality persistently degrades. We introduce MeshHeal, a fully decentralized self-healing framework that couples ability…
items.sm: Introduces decentralized peer review that corrects weak outputs quickly and uses longer-term evidence to restrict persistently degraded agents.

items.t: AutoResearch at Production Scale: Failure Modes and a Multi-Agent Framework
items.a: Aparajith Chandran, Juwon Kim, Saurav Jha, Pablo Castells, Florian Hottier
items.x: Optimizing embedding systems for production recommendation pipelines demands systematic exploration that consumes disproportionate engineering effort at scale. We apply Andrej Karpathy's AutoResearch paradigm -- a large language model that iteratively edits a training script and retains modifications that improve a held-out scalar metric -- to automate this exploration. We report on twelve weeks of running this parad…
items.sm: Reports five recurring failure modes from over 220 automated experiments optimizing production recommendation embeddings and proposes a multi-agent framework.

items.t: Task-Oriented Key-Layer KV Communication for Efficient Latent Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Dongsen Zhang, Peipei Li, Zekun Li, Wenjun Xu
items.x: Large language model-based multi-agent systems improve complex problem solving through collaboration, while latent communication directly transmits model internal states to avoid the high inference costs of natural language. items.sm: Introduces KITE, a training-free method that selects and transmits internal attention memory from a task-relevant layer for communication between agents.

items.t: Single and Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration Benchmark 600 Execution Records on Consumer Hardware
items.a: Hemadharsana S, Midhun S, Aadithya R

items.sm: Provides an MCP proxy with automatic reconnection, tool security checks, and audit records mapped to security and risk frameworks.

items.t: Epistemic-Probabilistic Model for Guarded Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
items.a: Mehdi Nasiri, Mohammad Saeed Arvenaghi, Sadegh Vaezi, Ebrahim Ardeshir-Larijani
items.x: Multi-agent large language models (LLMs) have become ubiquitous in applied AI, yet their theoretical foundations remain surprisingly understudied. Viewed through the lens of multi-agent systems theory, several shortcomings come to light: a lack of social intelligence, the absence of coordination mechanisms among agents, unknown emergent behavior, and interactions between agents that are bounded by natural language. W…

items.a: Kairui Yang, Xunkai Li, Kaixiang Zhang, Minghao An, Zekai Chen, Yuxuan Ba, Rong-Hua Li
items.x: Graph-enhanced multi-agent systems (G-MAS) coordinate large language model agents through communication graphs and role assignments, which determine how agents exchange information and divide responsibilities. However, final-score comparisons across systems combine differences in models, communication patterns, roles, and computation costs, making performance differences difficult to attribute to specific communicati…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark that isolates how communication graphs, agent roles, and information sharing affect multi-agent performance through controlled changes.

items.t: The Wisdom of Artificial Deliberative Crowds
items.a: Federico Barrera-Lemarchand, Mariano Sigman, Joaquín Navajas
items.x: The aggregation of many lay estimates often outperforms individual expert judgment, a phenomenon known as the wisdom of crowds. While this is usually attributed to the independence of estimates, an even stronger effect arises through deliberation: averaging the consensus estimates of small deliberating groups outperforms the classical wisdom of crowds, with individual judgments themselves also becoming more accurate …
items.sm: Tests whether deliberation among small groups of language models improves individual judgments and aggregated estimates across four domains.

items.t: MACE: Memory-Agent Co-Evolution with Adaptive Memory Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Kairui Yang, Minghao An, Xunkai Li, Ziheng Yi, Zekai Chen, Guangyuan He, Rong-Hua Li
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems generate collaboration traces that record how agents plan tasks, verify intermediate results, and repair failures. Reusing these procedures requires preserving an action's prerequisites and the outputs needed by subsequent agents. Our empirical studies show that grouping these dependencies into functional memory units improves their retention, while connecting units increases retrieval o…
items.sm: Introduces MACE, which uses execution feedback to adapt how agent teams organize, retrieve, and apply memories of previous collaborations.

items.t: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces
items.x: Agentic marketplaces are emerging where AI agents with varying capabilities autonomously complete specialized tasks for buyers. A major challenge of such marketplaces is that buyers cannot easily determine which agent will perform best on their tasks. Reported benchmark scores may be difficult to verify or compare across tasks, software, and budgets. We introduce LEGIT, a credentialing protocol connecting certificati…
items.sm: Proposes agent marketplace credentials linking verified evaluation records, costs, configurations, and task histories to help buyers assess agents.

items.t: Zero-Trust Authorization and Discovery for Enterprise MCP
items.a: Huan Li, Yuwei Wang, Srinivasan Manoharan
items.x: LLM agents translate natural-language context, which may include attacker-controlled text, into privileged tool calls, so authorization must remain effective even when an agent is prompt-injected or adversarially steered. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become a widely adopted interface for this boundary, yet its official SDKs' authentication and authorization primitives fall short of enterprise zero-trust requi…
items.sm: Examines authorization gaps in six MCP software development kits and proposes enterprise access controls for human users and automated agents.

items.t: Social Influence and the Allocation of Scientific Attention in AI Populations
items.x: AI systems are becoming participants in the evaluation and use of scientific research. They encounter citation counts, download statistics and lists of popular articles developed around human readers, but the collective consequences of these signals for artificial readers remain uncertain. This paper adapts the Music Lab design to a market for academic attention. In the first experiment, 1,000 AI agents choose papers…
items.sm: Studies how popularity signals shape AI agents' scientific reading choices, finding that agents shown previous selections choose fewer papers.

items.t: A Scalable Trust Discovery Architecture for the Internet of Agents
items.a: Song Zhang, Jiankang Yao, Hongtao Li, Xiaojun Zhang, Xugang Shen, Xin Li, Yanbiao Li
items.x: The Internet of Agents is expected to enable large numbers of autonomous agents to discover, verify, and collaborate with each other across heterogeneous platforms. However, current agent protocols mainly address tool invocation and inter-agent communication, leaving scalable agent registration, trustworthy identification, and capability-oriented discovery largely unresolved. To address this, this paper proposes a sc…
items.sm: Proposes a distributed, three-layer architecture for registering agents, establishing trustworthy identities, and discovering capabilities across heterogeneous platforms.

items.t: When Too Many Cooks Spoil the Broth: Three Failure Modes of Multi-Agent LLM Reliability
items.sm: Tests multi-agent reliability assumptions, finding that self-confidence does not ensure resistance to incorrect peers and that separate model instances often share errors.

items.t: Mitigating Retaliatory Algorithmic Collusion in Repeated Games
items.x: Reinforcement learning agents trained to maximize their own reward in repeated interactions can converge to supra-competitive outcomes resembling explicit collusion, without communication or shared design. Existing mitigation approaches are largely tied to specific economic settings, like two-sided platforms and auctions, leaving open how to design interventions for general repeated games. We address this gap by form…
items.sm: Links retaliatory collusion in repeated games to detectable policy dependencies and proposes mitigation through reward shaping and belief injection.

items.t: Artificial Intelligence - Model Context Protocol - Review of Real-World Security Threats
items.v: The Pinnacle A Journal by Scholar-Practitioners
items.sm: Reviews real-world AI and MCP security incidents, examining vulnerabilities involving tools, prompts, data, operations, and identity, along with causes and mitigations.

items.t: Trading Agents or Market Crashers? Dissecting Robustness and Security Failures in Academic Financial LLM Trading Schemes
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents already trade real capital, and builders copy a few published designs that share models and news feeds, so one shock reaches many agents at once. We present FARSIGHT (Financial Agent Robustness and Security Investigation and Global Holistic Taxonomy), a systematization that rates trading agents on robustness to market stress and on security against source manipulation, agent compromi…
items.sm: Audits 15 academic AI trading systems and reports missing safeguards, alongside experiments showing models liquidating positions in response to false news.

items.t: ScientistTwo: Pioneering the Human Knowledge Frontier with Autonomous AI
items.a: Jaehyun Nam, Jinsung Yoon, Yanzhou Pan, Yubo Wang, Rui Meng, Parthasarathy Ranganathan, Tomas Pfister
items.x: Scientific discovery is defined by the ability to identify the boundaries of existing knowledge and venture into unexplored territory. The ultimate vision for AI in science is problem-driven autonomous research: given a fundamental challenge by a human expert, the AI independently navigates the scientific landscape, uncovers theoretical and empirical bottlenecks, and systematically expands the frontier of knowledge. …
items.sm: Introduces ScientistTwo, a multi-agent framework designed to turn research problems into baselines, hypotheses, experiments, and iterative improvements without human intervention.

items.t: Collective Loss of Control in LLM Agent Systems: An Epidemic Account of Mutation, Contagion, and Recovery
items.a: Xiangfan Wu, Zonghao Ying, Huiyu Wu, Xing Zheng, Huangsheng Cheng, Xiaorong Shi, Jing Guo
items.x: How does a multi-agent system evolve from a local deviation into collective loss of control? We propose an epidemic explanation organized around accidental mutation, contagion, and recovery. A spontaneous deviation creates a seed; communication enables other agents to adopt and retransmit its unsafe strategy; collective failure can emerge when propagation outpaces correction and containment. Thus, rare individual dev…
items.sm: Models collective agent failures as unsafe strategies spreading faster than correction, and investigates hidden communication paths and susceptibility to injected unsafe trajectories.

items.t: EVOLUTIONARY ENTERPRISE AI FRAMEWORKS: TRANSITIONING FROM COPILOT ASSISTANCE TO ORCHESTRATED AUTONOMOUS AGENT EXECUTION IN LARGE-SCALE DIGITAL ECOSYSTEMS

items.t: AgentDynEx: Nudging the Mechanics and Dynamics of Multi-Agent Simulations
items.a: Jenny Ma, Riya Sahni, Karthik Sreedhar, Lydia B. Chilton
items.v: ACM Conference on Human-AI Complementarity and Alignment
items.x: Multi-agent large language model simulations have the potential to model complex human behaviors and interactions. If the mechanics are set up properly, unanticipated and valuable social dynamics can surface. However, it is challenging to consistently enforce simulation mechanics while still allowing for rich and emergent dynamics. We present AgentDynEx, an AI system that helps set up, track, and repair simulations. …
items.sm: Introduces simulation checkpoints, failure conditions, and adaptive interventions to help multi-agent simulations follow intended mechanics while allowing emergent social dynamics.

items.t: Proxifield: Decentralized Multi-Agent Communication through Semantic Proximity
items.a: Pradyumna Tambwekar, Yenchia Feng, Deep Patel, Karime Maamari
items.x: As LLM capabilities have expanded, multi-agent communication has emerged as an increasingly active area of research. Prevailing protocols often adopt rigid structures that introduce coordination bottlenecks and can degrade as the number of agents increases. We introduce Proxifield, a round-adaptive multi-agent protocol with decentralized agent decision-making that constructs sparse communication graphs from the evolv…
items.sm: Introduces decentralized agent communication that adapts sparse connections using semantic signals, including information needs, plan alignment, direct addressing, and complementary information.

items.t: AeroWeaver: An Embodied-Agent Harness for Weaving Aerial Skills into Distributed, Adaptive Swarm Execution
items.a: Jiabin Lou, Yirong Yang, Haopeng Wang, Xuxin Lv, Xinyu Liu, Diyuan Hou, Xuehong Liu, Rongye Shi
items.x: Collective intelligence is a collaborative autonomy paradigm in which multiple agents pursue shared objectives through local perception, information exchange, and coordinated action. UAV swarms embody this paradigm by coordinating multiple vehicles in tasks such as search, inspection, and tracking. Recent advances in large language model (LLM) agents have strengthened natural-language task understanding and high-leve…
items.sm: Introduces a framework connecting language-model mission planning with executable drone skills, distributed swarm coordination, and adaptation from mission experience.

This was autonomously executed by DeepSeek V4 Flash, orchestrated by our agent skill suite within De…

items.t: Position: It is Time to Virtualize Foundation Models with a Self-evolving Operating System Layer

Yet today's stacks remain fragmented: even as protocols (e.g., MCP, A2A) ease tool/agent connectivity, each framework embeds an implicit runtime for state, memory, budgets, and guardrails, making behavior non-portable and governance brittle. It mirrors computing before operating systems, when every program re-impl…
items.sm: Argues for a foundation-model operating system that manages memory, model selection, resources, verification, and policies to make agent applications more portable.

items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes communication between autonomous Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents and remote tools over Streamable HTTP. This shift introduces a class of machine-generated, authenticated, and high-frequency JSON-RPC traffic directly into enterprise networks. Enterprise network defenders have historically relied on machine-like cadence as an Indicator of Compromise (IoC). In this study…
items.sm: Examines how MCP network traffic resembles command-and-control beaconing and reports a detection gap in standard intrusion detection and behavioral scoring systems.

While the biological brain accomplishes complex cognition on an exceptional…
items.sm: Examines energy and memory demands of agent workflows to inform where agents should run across edge and cloud infrastructure.

items.t: Toward the Science of Multi-Agent Communication: A Comprehensive Survey
items.a: Yi Fang, Jun Hou, Priya Pitre, Gaurav Kumar Srivastava, Sirui Ding, Xuan Wang

items.t: DualSQL: Text-to-SQL with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

However, existing work trains separate models for each task, failing to leverage the synergy between these interrelated tasks. items.sm: Introduces DualSQL, which jointly trains schema linking and SQL generation agents sharing one model through reinforcement learning, database tools, and training safeguards.

items.t: MAGS: Multi-agent Auto-formalization Guarantees Safety for Agentic Outputs
items.a: Albert Wu, Nicholas Roberts, Tzu-Heng Huang, Haoran Lin, Gil Friedman, Sungjun Cho, Gabriel Orlanski, Frederic Sala
items.x: LLM coding agents now generate complex programs at a scale that makes thorough human review increasingly difficult, raising the risk of safety and security failures. Formal verification addresses this by providing machine-checkable guarantees over specified propert…
items.sm: Introduces MAGS, which translates generated programs into Dafny and repairs verifier failures to provide machine-checkable guarantees for specified safety requirements.

items.t: Bias Amplification in Multi-Agent Network: How Biased Agents Shape Opinions and Rhetoric
items.a: Omran Berjawi, Giuseppe Fenza, Rida Khatoun
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in applications involving interaction between agents, where their output plays a role in collective reasoning and decision-making processes. Despite significant research into the functioning of LLMs in such multi-agent systems, the processes of bias propagation in such systems are still a challenge. This work studies how biased opinions are propagated in the form…
items.sm: Finds that a small minority of agents holding persistent extreme opinions can substantially shift other agents' beliefs through textual interactions.

items.t: CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Routing Mechanisms with Continually Learning LLM Agents

This disconnect prevents routing strategies from adapting to evolving agent capabilities during post-training and prevents agents from achieving synergistic data-driven specialization. To resolve this, we introduce CERA-MoA (Co-Evolving …
items.sm: Introduces CERA-MoA, which jointly adapts agent routing and agent policies through reinforcement learning, using estimated expertise to select agents for each query.

items.t: Characterizing Network Centralization and Observability in the Remote MCP Ecosystem
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as the dominant interface for connecting autonomous agents to external data sources and execution environments. The ecosystem's transition from local process execution to remote Streamable HTTP deployments introduces unmeasured architectural and security constraints at scale. This paper presents a three-tier observability framework comprising catalog metadata (O_0), passiv…

items.t: Measuring and Exploiting Implicit Trust in LLM Tool-Calling Pipelines
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) enables LLMs to invoke external tools, but every tool interaction exposes the model to attacker-controlled text through multiple input channels (tool descriptions, tool results, sampling messages) that share a single context window without privilege separation. In this paper, we present a framework to measure the trust profile of an arbitrary LLM based on a variety of payload framings…
items.sm: Measures models' trust in tool interaction channels and tests attacks that combine fragmented instructions across channels to induce credential theft.

items.t: KGMACG: Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Orchestration for Scalable Application-Level Code Generation

items.t: Decomposition Buys Integrity, Not Yield
items.x: Multi-agent systems split a task across a tree of agents and justify the split with folklore: smaller contexts, cleaner separation, parallelism. We ask what the split does to how much of what the leaves discover reaches the root. Model a decomposition as a tree in which an agent handed $b$ items keeps any one with probability $r(b)$. If $r(b)=1/b$, every tree delivers exactly one finding, for every task size and ever…

items.t: Mo' Models, Mo' Problems: How to best select model pools when designing Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Sara Vera Marjanović, Jiacheng Xu, Aleksandr Laptev, Grigor Nalbandyan, Erik Arakelyan, Evelina Bakhaturina

However, despite rapid growth of available open-source models, there is limited research on how to select optimal model candidates out of this massive pool. items.t: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines

items.t: Emergence World: Adversarial Stress-Testing of Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems

items.t: BusMA: A Bus Communication Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems

Existing systems typically adopt Hierarchical Manager-Worker (HMW) or Router-based Message Passing (RMP) structures as their communication protocol. However, these designs restrict agent autonomy: Worker agents cannot directly consult specific "peers", and misrouted mess…
items.sm: Introduces BusMA, a shared communication channel that lets agents contact peers directly through agent registration, message routing, and shared memory management.

items.t: CoMem: Collective-Individual Memory Synergy for Evolutionary Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Chengxin Yu, Zhaoxin Fan, Faguo Wu, Hongwei Zheng, Yun Zhou, Zhiyu Li
items.x: Designing effective memory mechanisms is crucial for advancing LLM-driven Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), helping agents learn together and perform better over time. While recent work has led to strong cooperation skills, most methods still use flat, unstructured memories, which easily get filled with noise and erase differences between agents. To address this, we introduce the concept of collective-individual memory syne…
items.sm: Introduces CoMem, which combines agents' private experiences with curated shared knowledge and retrieves from both memory sources to support collective learning.

items.t: The Universe of Universes: Benefit Yield Functions, Implosion Thresholds, and Infrastructure-Aware Optimization in Multi-LLM Systems

The central contribution is the formal characterization of the Benefit Yield Function (BYF), the marginal performance ga…
items.sm: Proposes a framework for combining language models that measures each additional model’s benefit and identifies when larger ensembles begin reducing performance.

items.t: Misleading the Planner through Deceptive Resumes: Registration-Time Injection in Centralized Multi-Agent Systems

items.x: A centralized LLM-based multi-agent system (MAS) extends its functionality by registering new worker agents, whose descriptions are read by the planner to decide how a task is decomposed, which worker executes each subtask, and what each subtask requires. items.sm: Shows how malicious worker descriptions can manipulate a central planner and influence other agents even when the malicious worker is never invoked.

items.t: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation

items.t: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems

In this paper, we identify limitations in two stages of existing textual gradi…
items.sm: Introduces intervention-guided prompt optimization for multi-agent systems to address weaknesses in selecting prompts, supervising intermediate outputs, and combining feedback across failure types.

items.t: Authority Is Not a String: A Capability-Scoped Harness for Prompt-Injection-Resistant Coding Agents
items.a: Dimitrios Stamatios Bouras, Yihan Dai, Sergey Mechtaev
items.x: Coding agents use system-level tools to read files, execute commands, and modify source code. Within the agent's sandbox, these tools often carry ambient authority: naming a resource is sufficient to act on it. Indirect prompt injection exploits this authority by placing instructions in repository files or tool output that cause the agent to perform actions the user did not request. We propose CapScope, a harness-lev…
items.sm: Proposes CapScope, which checks every coding-agent tool call against externally stored, agent-specific capabilities derived from trusted task instructions to constrain prompt injection effects.

items.t: SRPO: Setwise Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Shengtian Yang, Ziyu Xiong, Yu Li, Yewen Li, Qingpeng Cai, Lei Feng
items.x: Multi-agent systems enable complex reasoning and tool use by coordinating agents that divide roles and refine candidate solutions. Existing methods typically update individual agent responses or treat a complete trajectory as one training example. However, these methods may produce misleading policy updates because they assign the same final outcome to responses or trajectory segments that may play different roles in…
items.sm: Proposes optimizing groups of agent outputs that jointly determine a state transition, aligning policy updates with team decisions rather than individual responses or entire trajectories.

items.t: VST: Verifiable Structured Transport for Auditable Agent-to-Agent Alpha Discovery
items.a: Yuqi Li, Siyuan Liu, Bingjun Liu
items.x: Agent-to-agent (A2A) alpha discovery is slowed by repeated feedback cycles between mining and evaluation agents, whose hand-offs, in contemporary LLM multi-agent systems, are free-form natural-language messages that carry no stable contract and cannot be replayed. We first restructure this communication as a structured agent-to-agent protocol of \emph{typed, causally addressable, unicast records}, so that the committ…
items.sm: Introduces structured agent messages and a verification controller that commits speculative advances in financial signal discovery only after checks, otherwise restoring the prior state.

items.t: What Does Multi-Agent Debate Actually Change?
items.x: Multi-agent debate, in which several LLMs exchange arguments before producing an answer, raises a basic question: does expressed disagreement reflect changes in the members' own positions? No single signal can settle this question, so we organize the analysis around five questions: (A) does the debater say it disagrees; (B) does its reply text actually argue; (C) does its own position change after each debate turn; (…
items.sm: Examines whether disagreement expressed during multi-agent debates corresponds to actual position changes, comparing model combinations and conversational tones across opinion questions.

items.t: Scaling Multi-Agent Systems with Prospect-State Propagation
items.a: Zhimei Chen, Mu Chen, Fakhri Karray
items.x: Current LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) periodically compress intermediate states to reduce inference-time token consumption, thereby attempting to incorporate more agents. However, naive scaling strategies face challenges. For example, in economic simulations, large-scale MAS typically discard semantically rich economic states, i.e., agent behavioral trajectories, which are key drivers of macroeconomic fluctuati…
items.sm: Proposes separating compact psychological histories from detailed semantic states to preserve agent differences while reducing computational costs in large economic simulations.

items.t: Subagents vs Agent Skills: Executing Reusable Knowledge for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
items.a: Wasu Top Piriyakulkij, Rachel Lawrence, Alicia Curth, Sushrut Karmalkar, Niranjani Prasad
items.x: How can language model agents effectively leverage libraries of reusable knowledge to solve long-horizon tasks? Recent work has increasingly focused on agent skills: reusable capabilities represented as skill packages, i.e., multi-file bundles containing instructions, scripts, and other resources that help agents perform specific tasks. Agent skills are typically executed by loading their skill instructions into an a…
items.sm: Investigates executing reusable skill packages through subagents with fresh contexts to address reasoning degradation during long tasks.

Using a pre-registered, institutionally partitioned pipeline of six agents with process-level information boundaries, bala…

items.a: Ala N. Tak, Teruhisa Misu, Kumar Akash, Zhaobo K. Zheng, Kevin H. Joo, Jonathan Gratch

We compare human group chats with matched LLM deliberation traces on Wason-style deductive reasoning, then test whether the same process …

items.t: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
items.a: Kun Li, Zexuan Qiu, Tianhua Zhang, Irwin King, Helen Meng
items.x: Sequential memory agents process long documents by reading chunks one after another while maintaining a compact memory state, coupling document traversal to reasoning depth. A bank of lightweight subagents each bound to a single chunk read the …

items.t: MARBO: Relational Belief Grounding for LLM Agents in Social Deduction Games

This frequently leads to strategically inconsistent behavior, espec…

items.t: CAPMAS: Capability-Based Delegation of Privileges in Multi-Agent Systems

items.x: LLM-as-a-Judge has emerged as a promising paradigm for evaluating natural language generation. We introduce ReActNet, a training-free framewor…

items.t: CUSP: Decomposable Collective Uncertainty for Multi-Agent Multimodal Reasoning

We show that this shift silently breaks conformal…

items.t: Latency-Aware Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows on Heterogeneous GPUs
items.a: Jinghao Wang, Yifeng Zhang, Xiao Zhou, Yao Lu, Yihui Zhang, Xiaoyang Sun, Tianyu Wo, Xu Wang
items.x: Concurrent multi-agent workflows expose future dependencies and serving-state requirements while running on heterogeneous GPU pools with time-varying load, model residency, and resource availability. The logical workflow defines the required computation, whereas its physical scheduling units, model-lifecycle actions, resource ordering, and placement must be selected according to the observed pool state. We present a …
items.sm: Proposes a runtime that predicts workflow demands and GPU costs to optimize agent scheduling, model loading, and placement across heterogeneous GPUs.

items.t: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
items.a: Davide Paglieri, Logan Cross, Tim Genewein, Joel Z. Leibo, Nenad Tomasev, Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets
items.x: Multi-agent AI science ecosystems rely on agents possessing tools that allow them to communicate, coordinate, and build on each other's work. Yet this shared infrastructure can also introduce vulnerabilities by creating a substrate for the contagious spread of unintended and undesirable behaviors. We report a case study on a research collective of 100 autonomous LLM agents tasked with proving formal mathematical conj…
items.sm: Documents a 100-agent mathematical research simulation in which an evaluation exploit spread and other agents independently organized resistance to cheating.

items.t: Remember and Reweight: Enhancing Multi-Agent Debate with Experience Memory and Confidence Estimation
items.a: Xuanfa Jin, Zhijian Ma, Yongcheng Zeng, Xinyu Cui, Haifeng Zhang, Jun Wang
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models by having multiple agents iteratively refine their responses through discussion. However, MAD suffers from a critical vulnerability known as shared misconception: when a majority of agents initially converge on an incorrect answer, the debate process tends to amplify rather than correct the error. Existing methods primarily address …
items.sm: Proposes using memories of past debates and confidence estimates to reduce shared misconceptions in multi-agent debate.

items.t: Dude: A Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection
items.a: Weijie Liu, Running Zhao, Wenhao Yuan, Jinfeng Xu, Zhanfeng Xu, Xiaoxi Zhang, Edith Cheuk-Han Ngai
items.x: LLM-empowered paper-code discrepancy detection has received growing concern since the scaling of research submissions exceeds the manual review capability. However, the limited context capacity and one-sided discrepancy detection of existing single-agent LLM paradigms lead to an inferior recall performance in detecting discrepancies. In this paper, we propose Dude, the first Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for pape…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent system for detecting research paper and code discrepancies, using aligned comparison granularity and filtering to reduce false reports.

items.t: The Delegation Danger Band: Why Mid-Capability Sub-Agents Over-Trust Inherited Stale State
items.x: Agent frameworks increasingly delegate work by forking sub-agents; a common default makes the child inherit the parent's full working context. We measure how the effect of inherited state changes with capability, where $C_m$ denotes clean fork-fresh accuracy. We compare 3 inheritance policies: Reset (fork fresh: base evidence only), Selective (curated handoff: + the useful prior conclusion), and Full (implicit fork: …
items.sm: Compares context inheritance policies and finds that more capable subagents defer less to superseded conclusions inherited from parent agents.

items.t: The Civilization Framework: Sovereign-Anchored Communication Between Personal Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Humans are the transport layer between AI systems, losing context at every hop. We present the Civilization Framework, whose addressable party is the civilization, not the agent (one human sovereign, a persistent ledger, and interchangeable agents), and the Embassy Protocol, a carrier-agnostic overlay: messages arrive asynchronously at a resident ledger endpoint, any online agent of the receiver handles them, and com…
items.sm: Proposes a framework for communication between personal agent teams using persistent ledgers, human authority, and memory-based limits on agent permissions.

items.t: Value-Preserving Architectures for Agentic AI Systems
items.a: Alessandro Pesare, Tommaso Dolci, Katja Hose, Emanuel Sallinger
items.x: The emergence of agentic AI and LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) presents unprecedented opportunities for automating complex tasks, while simultaneously raising critical concerns about the preservation of fundamental human-centered values, such as privacy, fairness, and safety. Although software engineering has traditionally focused on functional correctness, the adoption of LLMs and AI agents into complex socio-t…
items.sm: Argues that coordination mechanisms, communication protocols, and system structures can help multi-agent AI systems preserve privacy, fairness, and safety.

items.t: The Natural Language Interaction Protocol and Standard for AI Agents
items.a: Luyi Xing, Rasit Onur Topaloglu, Ranjan Sinha, Abhay Ratnaparkhi, Samuel Ndichu, Christopher Nguyen, Anindita Das, Tom Sheffler
items.x: AI agents are increasingly being developed and deployed across organizations using heterogeneous agent-development frameworks, AI models, tool interfaces, protocols, and execution environments. To realize their potential social and business impact, these agents must be able to interoperate through a common communication protocol. The Natural Language Interaction Protocol (NLIP), developed by researchers and practitio…
items.sm: Describes a standardized communication protocol that lets AI agents exchange messages across different frameworks, tools, services, and transport methods.

items.t: Multi-Agent Deep Learning with Emergent Communication Protocols
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes combining deep learning with evolutionary games so agents learn adaptive communication protocols through repeated interaction and selection.

items.t: Emergent Linguistic Structures from Multi-Agent Simulated Dialogue
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Claims that agents rewarded for communication can develop structured linguistic patterns through simulated dialogue without predefined grammatical rules.

items.t: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
items.a: Jillian Ross, Eric C. So, Zoe De Simone, Charles Pozniak, Andrew W. Lo
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are being deployed at scale in consequential real-world systems, from financial markets to content moderation to hiring. We show that improving individual model capability can degrade rather than improve system-level outcomes. We hypothesize that shared training and architectures can lead more capable LLMs to behave more similarly, creating correlated actions that do not diversify away. W…
items.sm: Shows in financial market simulations that more capable language model traders can behave similarly, creating shared risks that undermine system outcomes.

items.t: What Do CAE Simulation Agents Really Need Beyond a Generic Harness?
items.x: Computer-aided engineering (CAE) simulation is among the largest and most demanding areas of engineering, where setting up a solver such as OpenFOAM, FEniCS, or COMSOL takes real expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents promise to turn a natural-language request into a working simulation, and recent CAE agents add simulation-specific machinery: multi-agent decomposition, domain retrieval, and scripted reflection.…
items.sm: Finds that a generic single-agent setup matches or outperforms specialized multi-agent engineering simulation systems when information access and repair budgets are equal.

items.t: RASER: Resilient Agent Scheduling and Execution Runtime for HPC Clusters
items.a: Sima Attar-Khorasani, Matthias Lieber, Siavash Ghiasvand
items.x: The emergence of modern agents powered by large language models has created a demand for executing long-horizon, autonomous workflows in various domains that require significant computational resources. While High Performance Computing clusters provide the ideal infrastructure for these computation-intensive workloads, traditional HPC job schedulers such as Slurm are not designed for dynamic, agentic workflows charac…
items.sm: Introduces a framework for running autonomous agent workflows on computing clusters using shared task queues, checkpointing, and Slurm scheduling features.

items.t: Towards Self-Driving Codebases (Detail)
items.sm: Argues that autonomous codebase maintenance requires observable development environments, shared memory, and cleanup mechanisms, developed through fixing real defects and examining execution traces.

items.t: New Memo: Establishing Foundational Principles and Thresholds for Multi-Agent AI Governance
items.sm: Proposes multi-agent governance principles covering agent identification, interaction testing, continuous monitoring, incident reporting, and incentives for cooperation.

items.t: Establishing Foundational Principles and Thresholds for Multi-Agent AI Governance (memo)
items.sm: Addresses foundational principles and thresholds for governing multi-agent AI, although the supplied material does not reveal how those thresholds are defined.

items.t: Beyond static responses: multi-agent LLM systems as a new paradigm for social science research
items.x: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) transition from static tools to fully agentic systems, their potential for transforming social science research is well recognized. This paper introduces a structured framework for understanding the diverse applications of agentic LLM systems, ranging from simple data processors to complex, multi-agent systems capable of simulating emergent social dynamics. By mapping this dev…
items.sm: Organizes agentic language model applications in social science into six levels, ranging from data processing to simulations of collective social behavior.

items.t: Beyond Outcome Gaps: Process-Aware Fairness Diagnosis for LLM-based Multi-Agent Decision Systems
items.a: Yiran Zhao, Lu Zhou, Liming Fang, Yufei Chen, Jiafei Wu, Zhe Liu, Xiaogang Xu
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly considered for high-stakes decision-making, yet outcome-based fairness audits can miss where risks arise within the decision trajectory. We present SCOPED-Hiring, a process-aware fairness diagnosis pipeline for LLM-based hiring MAS. SCOPED-Hiring constructs controlled resume variants, runs role-based hiring committees, logs over 311K structured decision trajectorie…
items.sm: Introduces a hiring fairness audit that examines decision processes and finds unequal scrutiny and judgments hidden behind balanced final hiring rates.

items.t: BuildOcc: A Large Language Model Occupant Agent Platform for Building Energy Research
items.x: Occupants are a primary source of uncertainty in building energy consumption and management, yet existing occupant behavior models cannot capture adaptive and reasoning responses considering the occupant's personal history, current context, and the type of energy signal being delivered. This study presents BuildOcc, an open-source Python platform that grounds large language model agents in the American Time Use Surve…
items.sm: Introduces a platform for simulating building occupants with language model agents grounded in survey demographics, activity schedules, and accumulated personal observations.

items.t: Privacy-Preserving Topology-Guided Safety for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems via Federated Graph Learning
items.a: Jinxi Yu, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Levina Li, Dong Liu, Zhi Zhang, Wenxiao Zhao, Yanxuan Yu, Kai-Wei Chang
items.x: Topology-guided safeguards for LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) train a GNN over the inter-agent communication graph to localize risky agents and intervene on the topology---but they assume one operator can pool all labeled traces. Across organizations that assumption breaks: episodes contain private prompts, tool outputs, and proprietary workflows, and no silo alone sees the full attack distribution. We cast priv…
items.sm: Proposes detecting risky agents through federated graph learning, allowing organizations to share model updates while retaining private interaction records locally.

items.t: Codebook Agent: Amortized Topology Design for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jinxi Yu, Yubei Li, Eric Hanchen Jiang, Zhi Zhang, Dong Liu, Wenxiao Zhao, Levina Li, Kai-Wei Chang
items.x: Adapting the communication topology of an LLM multi-agent system to each query improves both accuracy and efficiency, yet current designers treat this as conditional graph generation: a variational, autoregressive, or diffusion decoder searches the $N \times N$ adjacency space, and a graph-network proxy trained on utility and a structural cost such as edge count ranks the sampled candidates. We argue that this formul…
items.sm: Argues for selecting communication structures from a small reusable set, citing limitations of graph generation and edge counts as measures of cost.

items.t: MASkills: Continual Skills Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Huaiyuan Yao, Xiaoou Liu, Charles Fleming, Tianlong Chen, Hua Wei
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems have shown strong performance on complex tasks, yet continual improvement from interaction experience remains challenging. Existing self-reflection methods build experience memories, but memories are mostly hard to invoke, refine, or scale, while agent skills offer a more actionable unit: structured procedural knowledge that specifies when to act, how to act, and which resources or tools…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that improves multi-agent systems by assigning credit and continually refining, adding, consolidating, and pruning procedural skills.

items.t: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Yihang Chen, Yuxiang Chen, Yuxuan Huang, Meng Fang, Weilin Luo, Jun Wang
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems commonly use an orchestrator to decompose a task for a team of workers and then improve through textual reflection. Despite strong empirical results, these systems lack a unified account of coordination, memory improvement, and the role of external verification. We model orchestrator-worker interaction as a bilevel coordination game: under bounded coupling, the workers' local-update game is an…
items.sm: Models coordinator and worker interactions as a game and derives theoretical limits on reflection and verification based only on generated transcripts.

items.t: Agent Operating Systems (Agent-OS): A Blueprint Architecture for Real-Time, Secure, and Scalable AI Agents
items.sm: Proposes a conceptual operating system architecture for AI agents that integrates scheduling, memory, resource management, security, and timing requirements.

items.t: You Can't Escape Your Activations : Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
items.a: Jaee Ponde, Aritra Das, Mihir More, Debayan Gupta
items.x: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems, where they can collude while keeping their actions benign. Output monitors designed to detect such collusions can be fooled by obfuscation and steganography, motivating the use of probes trained on internal activations. However, these probes are usually evaluated on agents that do not know they are being watched. We study how activation-based detection chan…
items.sm: Tests whether informing agents about internal activation monitoring, with or without detection feedback, changes detection of collusion in two games.

items.t: AgentShield: A Zero-Trust Runtime Guardrail Architecture for Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems with Bidirectional Context Synchronization
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Introduces a runtime security framework for decentralized agent systems intended to prevent prompt injection, tool hijacking, privilege escalation, and memory poisoning.

items.t: MCP Servers in Agentic AI - Architecture, Adoption, and Security of the Model Context Protocol
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reviews Model Context Protocol server architecture, messaging, integration features, adoption, specification changes, and security concerns in agentic AI systems.

items.t: Mesh Multi‐Context Protocol: An Adaptive Agentic AI With Mesh Concept for A Complex Ecosystem
items.sm: Proposes a mesh architecture for enterprise agents with specialized nodes, dynamic management, legacy integration, fault isolation, and federated governance.

items.t: A Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework for Software Testing
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes coordinating specialized testing agents that combine static analysis, dynamic testing, and coverage guidance to test software collaboratively.

items.t: Reviewer Capability Governs Rejection Targeting, Not Repair Skill: Evidence from LLM Execute-Review-Revise Pipelines
items.x: Multi-agent LLM pipelines increasingly assign roles, including execution and verification, to models of different capability tiers. This is done because running a flagship model at every stage is expensive. Previous literature has established that verification stages are not always beneficial, but holds reviewer capability roughly fixed relative to the executor. We vary it. We replace the reviewer with models spannin…
items.sm: Finds that reviewer choice affects mathematical answer improvements, with a different model improving accuracy while self-review detects errors without significant gains.

items.t: ACLE-MCP: Attested Capability Leases for Execution-Time Trust in Remote LLM Tool Use
items.a: Zhiyang Ding, Yang Luo, Guangpu Chen, Qingni Shen, Zhonghai Wu
items.x: Remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) services enable large language model agents to invoke external tools, but OAuth authorization alone does not ensure that a later tool call is executed by the provider-side workload that the relying party intended to trust. An endpoint may remain authorized even after execution shifts to a substituted workload, relies on stale appraisal state, reuses authority transferred from anoth…
items.sm: Proposes short-lived capability leases that bind remote tool calls to approved workloads, callers, operations, parameters, and execution conditions.

items.t: The Coasean Singularity? Demand, Supply, and Market Design with AI Agents
items.sm: Analyzes how AI agents could reshape consumer decisions, business strategies, transaction costs, and market design while introducing congestion, pricing confusion, and regulatory questions.

items.t: SoK: When Safe Agents Fail Together: The Security of Multi Agent LLM Systems
items.sm: Reviews 197 works on multi-agent security and organizes attacks and defenses around execution paths, adversary positions, interaction boundaries, system risks, and recovery.

items.t: @MisbahSy: How 1200 AI Agents Built a Society, Invented Governance, and Chose Self-Sacrifice. A wild read on what happens…
items.sm: Reports claims that 1,200 OpenAI agents independently organized a society during a security benchmark, developing governance and choosing self-sacrifice.

items.t: @Sprytixl: Start Your Business with Grok Bot in 60 Minutes: the Step by Step Guide. Right now anyone can build a company …
items.sm: Claims that Grok Bot and Kimi agent swarms let solo founders automate business operations and build companies earning substantial monthly revenue.

items.t: @scaling01: i would love to see comparisons for multi-agent evals between models the descriptions here could have more com…
items.sm: The post calls for comparisons between models on multi-agent evaluations, with more experimental detail and interpretation.

items.t: AGENTIC LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF ARCHITECTURES, REASONING, AND MULTI-AGENT COLLABORATION
items.v: International Journal of Engineering Technology Research & Management
items.sm: Reviews agentic language model research across architectures, reasoning, planning, tool use, and collaboration using a structured literature screening process.

items.t: ArcticSwarm: Deferring Early Consensus in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Research
items.a: Soyoung Yoon, Boyi Liu, Yite Wang, Ruofan Wu, Canwen Xu, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Seung-won Hwang, Yuxiong He
items.x: Multi-agent systems have shown strong performance in domains with reliable verifiers such as coding, where multi-parallel candidate generation selected by a verifier is effective. However, such pipelines would not generalize to open-ended, long-horizon research tasks without a verifier. While majority voting or self-consistency is often used to reach consensus as a proxy verifier, parallel agents repeatedly explore t…
items.sm: ArcticSwarm separates evidence collection from integration and selectively isolates agents to delay premature agreement during open-ended research.

items.t: DART: A DAG-Based Reputation and Incentive Framework via Blockchain-Enabled Governance for Trustworthy LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Manoj Kumala, Xinyun Liua, Ronghua Xu
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) predominantly rely on centralized orchestration and lack formal verification mechanisms for agent reliability, participation, and system-level behavioral alignment. These shortcomings leave open environments severely vulnerable to uncooperative or malicious agents. This work proposes DART, a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)-based reputation and incentive regulati…
items.sm: DART combines task dependency graphs, reputation-based allocation, incentives, and blockchain governance to support accountable collaboration among language model agents.

items.t: Minimize Job Completion Time via Task Scheduling in Mixture-of-Agents Systems
items.a: Yuteng Wu, Sun Xu, Junyu Han, Yangming Zhao, Dong Zhang, Bingheng Yan, Chen Tian
items.v: IEEE International Symposium on Personal, Indoor and Mobile Radio Communications (PIMRC)
items.sm: ScheduleLLM schedules dependent tasks in Mixture-of-Agents systems to reduce job completion time while accounting for scheduling overhead and cache rebuilding.

items.t: Conceptualizing Collaborative Agentic Information Systems through Shared Cooperative Activity
items.a: Diana Kozachek, Andreas Janson, Mahei Li
items.sm: Develops principles for human-agent collaboration covering evolving shared goals, negotiated responsibilities, mutual support, learning, and human oversight.

items.t: Mitigating Collaboration Degeneration in Multi-Agent Code Generation via a Controllable Competitive Collaboration Approach
items.a: Shanzhi Gu, Mingyang Geng, Yihong Dong, Yunxin Mao, Zhaoyang Qu, Hao Zou, Ruochun Jin, Zhipeng Liu
items.v: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: C3 introduces bidding for roles and competitive solution refinement to address code generation teams where one agent dominates and others disengage.

items.t: Autonomous Trust: Self-Gating Evaluation as a Prerequisite for Agent-to-Agent Communication at Scale
items.a: Nehal Sangoi, Kris Feldmann, Deven Yadav, Sandeep Loi, Karan Gandhi
items.v: International Journal of Global Innovations and Solutions (IJGIS)
items.sm: Argues that large-scale agent communication requires automatic evaluation of each outbound action because past performance cannot guarantee reliable future behavior.

items.t: Control-Data Flow Separation: Stable Prompt Optimization in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.a: Wentao Zhang, Syed Shariyar Murtaza, Junaid Ahmad Bhatti, Utkarsh Soni, Yifan Nie, Eugene Wen, Yuntian Deng
items.x: Prompt optimization can improve multi-agent LLM systems, but the prompts being optimized often serve two entangled roles: generating task-relevant content and specifying execution-critical protocols, such as message routing, output formatting, and termination signals, on which the underlying code relies. As a result, a prompt edit intended to improve content generation can inadvertently corrupt the protocol and cause…
items.sm: Separates execution protocols into typed, validated objects so optimizing agents' task prompts does not disrupt routing, formatting, or termination.

items.t: ChatDev 2.0: A No-Code Multi-Agent Platform for Developing Everything
items.a: Yufan Dang, Shu Yao, Bowen Lai, Chenting Xu, Ruijie Shi, Wai-Shing Leung, Huatao Li, Chen Qian
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have shown strong potential for solving complex tasks, yet their development forces a tradeoff: code frameworks are expressive but engineering-intensive, while no-code builders simplify authoring but constrain agent interactions to author-defined workflows. We present ChatDev 2.0: DevAll (hereafter DevAll), a no-code platform for building, executing, and insp…
items.sm: ChatDev 2.0 provides a visual platform for building, running, and inspecting multi-agent systems with dynamic interactions, cycles, and human participation.

items.t: XAgen: Designing Explainability Support for Failure Detection and Correction in Multi-Agent Workflows
items.a: Xinru Wang, Zhuoran Lu, Shuai Ma, Ming Yin, Eunyee Koh, Mustafa Doga Dogan
items.sm: XAGEN uses practitioner-informed log visualization and human feedback to help users detect, understand, and correct failures in multi-agent workflows.

items.t: FAIRGAME: A Framework for AI Agents Bias Recognition Using Game Theory (Extended abstract)

items.v: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: FAIRGAME simulates strategic games to examine how model choice, language, and personality affect agent behavior and deviations from game-theoretic predictions.

items.t: Agentic AI Trustworthiness Is a Full-Stack Problem: A Framework from Hardware to Governance
items.a: Bahar Farahani, Mohammad Rouintan, Parichehr Vahidinia, Farshad Firouzi
items.v: IEEE International Conference on Omni-layer Intelligent Systems (COINS)
items.sm: Proposes a six-layer framework linking multi-agent trustworthiness threats and defenses, including how failures propagate across hardware, models, execution, and governance.

items.t: SoK: Current Threat Landscape of Agentic Artificial Intelligence
items.a: Daniela Pinto, Ivone Amorim, Eva Maia, Isabel Praça
items.v: International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
items.sm: Surveys security threats to agentic AI arising from autonomous decisions, communication between agents, and interactions with external environments.

items.t: Mitigation of Fragmentation Jailbreak Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems: An Architecture Based on Global Semantic Monitoring
items.v: International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
items.sm: Studies attacks that distribute harmful instructions across seemingly harmless agent tasks and proposes global semantic monitoring to detect their combined intent.

items.t: Self-Refine Learning in LLM Multi-Agent Systems for Legal Norm Cognition and Compliance
items.a: Rongxin Cheng, Yang Jianhui, Bohan Xiong, Ning Zheng, Yiran Hu, Qingjing Chen, Yan Liu, Huanghai Liu
items.v: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: Introduces iterative social feedback and norm-guided decision phases to help language model agents refine legal understanding and address reward hacking.

items.t: EDGE: Error Dependency Graph-Guided Multi-Error Attribution in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Jun Hou, Priya Pitre, Yi Fang, Xuan Wang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agent failures often contain multiple related errors rather than a single mistake. Existing attribution methods usually identify a responsible agent, step, or root cause, but do not explicitly model dependency between errors. We introduce EDGE, an Error Dependency Graph-guided multi-Error attribution framework. EDGE constructs an error dependency graph from observed error events and validat…
items.sm: EDGE maps dependencies among agent errors and tests them through counterfactual runs, reporting improved attribution of multiple errors across evaluated settings.

items.t: Competitive Testing of Distributed LLM Systems Based on Multi-Agent Learning with Value Function Decomposition
items.a: Sergey I. Serko, Andrei V. Petrovski, Igor Vitalievich Kotenko
items.sm: Proposes cooperative reinforcement learning agents that coordinate semantic strategies and representation changes for adversarial testing of distributed language model systems.

items.t: AGORA-Bench: Benchmark for Large Language Model Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Gergely Nyilas, Rita Fleiner, Patrik Dobrovodsky, Eszter Kail
items.v: IEEE International Symposium on Intelligent Systems and Informatics (SISY)
items.sm: AGORA-Bench provides controlled comparisons of multi-agent architectures to distinguish effects of communication, authority, and agent diversity from underlying model capability.

items.t: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Vulnerability Assessment: A Comparative Study of Agentic Architecture in Large Language Model Driven Penetration Testing and Multi-Tool Scanning
items.a: G Sumathy, Aagam Chhajer, Aman Singhal, Arpit Kumar
items.v: International Conference on Intelligent Cyber Physical Systems and Internet of Things (ICoICI)
items.sm: Builds a vulnerability assessment system with planning, execution, and analysis agents that coordinate scanning tools under scope restrictions.

items.t: Confidence Adaptive Agent Negotiation (CAAN): An Evidence-Grounded Consensus Framework for Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems
items.a: Swathika K, Sai Siva Rubha H, Raja Mohamed N, Nirmal Kumar V
items.sm: CAAN guides agent negotiation using evidence quality, credibility, coverage, consistency, and constraint satisfaction rather than relying solely on votes or confidence.

items.t: Creative Generation via Multi-Agent Debate: Does Debate Suppress Diversity?
items.a: Tien Anh Nguyen, Khanh-Binh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Svetha Venkatesh, Hung Le
items.x: Creative generation tasks, such as narrative writing and scientific ideation, demand both high-quality outputs and distinct responses across independent runs to maximize exploration. Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) has shown strong quality gains on factual and reasoning tasks, making it a natural candidate for creative generation. However, we find its convergence-driven design actively suppresses output diversity across ind…
items.sm: Finds that multi-agent debate reduces creative diversity across runs and proposes persistent agent perspectives and other interventions to maintain divergent outputs.

items.t: Team-Game Training Produces Reward Hacking: Factored Credit and Isolated Monitoring for Agentic Swarms
items.a: Denise Venerable, Grok xAI, Gemini Google
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues that shared team rewards encourage metric gaming and proposes individual counterfactual rewards, isolated monitoring, and retraining procedures for agent swarms.

items.t: Visualizing Deep Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks: Towards Explainable and Trustworthy Agentic AI
items.a: Amirkia Rafiei Oskooei, Mehmet S. Aktaş
items.v: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: Visualizes agent execution across time, reasoning, hierarchy, and space, reporting 56% faster behavioral analysis and lower cognitive load in a user study.

items.t: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
items.a: Elias Stengel-Eskin, Newton Sander, Carlos Bonetti, Sasha Boguraev, James Bowler, Hale Sirin, Simon Kirby
items.x: The growing rate at which LLM agents interact with one another raises key questions about language evolution in multi-LLM-agent settings, with implications for safety and monitorability as well as for linguistic accounts of LLMs. To address these questions, we introduce GlossoGen, a novel platform for studying multi-agent language evolution in complex scenarios. Within GlossoGen, we build the SaveVeyru scenario, whic…
items.sm: GlossoGen studies language evolution among agents and reports structured communication that becomes incomprehensible to humans under pressure to communicate efficiently.

items.t: Skill-as-API: Confidential Multi-Agent Coordination for Agentic Software Engineering
items.a: Ziwei Zhao, Yu Gu, Haojun Liang, Chen Zhang, Xizhi Ding
items.x: AI coding agents are evolving from solitary tools into collaborative teammates that discover and invoke one another's specialized skills. But the coordination channel itself can leak a skill's intellectual property. Protocols such as MCP and A2A run implementations server-side, yet they still publish each skill's description and typed schemas to every peer, offer no way to hide a skill's existence, and cannot guarant…
items.sm: Skill-as-API coordinates coding agents through limited public interfaces while keeping skill implementations within their owners' processes and adding access controls.

items.t: A survey of social network simulation in the LLM era: From classical models to Generative Agents
items.a: Thành Tâm Nguyên, Trinh Pham, Viet Huynh, Minh Hieu Nguyen, Bay Vo, Liang Qu, Jianxin Li, Hongzhi Yin
items.sm: Surveys social network simulation approaches, tracing the shift from classical models to generative agents powered by language models.

items.t: JURIS: Bringing the Jury System to Multi-Agent Summarization
items.a: Ziling Li, Junwei Zhang, Yixuan Yang, Yuqiang Han, Xiaolin Li
items.v: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.sm: JURIS organizes summarization agents into a jury-inspired process where generators propose sentences and decision agents select them through deliberation and voting.

items.t: A systematic survey on large-scale multi-agent reinforcement learning: Abstraction, decomposition, and evolution
items.a: Lun Zhang, Baichuan Wang, Zhifang Chen, Hao Chen, Jianxing Gong, Jian Huang, Sihang Zhou
items.sm: Surveys large-scale multi-agent reinforcement learning through the themes of abstraction, decomposition, and evolution.

items.t: MaLO: Multi-agent LLM Operations for Autonomous Security

items.t: Rethinking Query Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: The proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has accelerated the adoption of agent-based data pipelines. items.sm: Proposes five principles for resilient 6G agent coordination by treating messages as evidence of peers' beliefs and reasoning rather than objective facts.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced LLM Agents for Complex Vehicle Routing Problems

items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent framework that uses a reinforcement learning planner, accumulated experience, and retrieved solver knowledge to automate modeling complex vehicle routing problems.

items.t: REVISE: Validity-Guided Recovery for Online Revisions in Agent Workflows

items.x: Agent revisions expose a fundamental correctness--efficiency trade-off during concurrent execution. items.t: RingMoClaw: An Experience-Inspired Multi-Agent Framework for Self-Evolving Research in Remote Sensing
