items.a: Nada Mohamed, Prąsun Chakrabarti, Shashi Kant Gupta
items.v: Journal of Smart Algorithms and Applications (JSAA)
items.sm: Reviews language model agent frameworks, collaboration architectures, communication mechanisms, interoperability protocols, and research challenges using literature published between 2020 and March 2026.

items.t: Personality-Aware Multi-Agent Decision Support for Enterprise Strategy: Concept, Prototype, and Evaluation of Deliberation Value
items.sm: Develops and evaluates an enterprise strategy support system combining personality-aware agent deliberation with recommendations backed by traceable knowledge graph evidence.

items.t: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing
items.x: When a multi-agent system changes its team, it also changes the messages and final answer it produces, so an end-to-end accuracy gap does not by itself identify a routing effect. We introduce method, an evaluation contract that fixes a public information boundary, downstream stack G, and finite legal team family before outcomes are generated. Complete coverage identifies exact finite-benchmark oracle regret condition…
items.sm: Introduces an evaluation framework that holds information and downstream processing fixed to isolate how agent team selection affects performance.

items.t: When Evidence Shapes Collaboration: Knowledge-Conditioned Topology Generation for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yangxiao Jiang, Jiarun Fan, Mingcong Xu, Yanxi Guo, Jiwen Feng, Shanqing Xu, Mengchen Qian, Wei Chen
items.x: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) have recently moved from static workflows toward dynamically generated collaboration topologies. However, existing topology generation methods rely primarily on the parametric knowledge of large language models, with external search or retrieval used only as a reactive tool rather than an explicit determinant of collaboration structure. This leads to structure-knowledge misalignment, where s…
items.sm: Proposes generating agent collaboration structures from external evidence to reduce redundant interactions and improve verification on knowledge-intensive tasks.

items.t: GOD: Govern, Observe, and Direct - A Real-Time Control Room for Agent Societies
items.x: Generative-agent systems are easier to start than to inspect. A run can contain many agents, locations, messages, commands, and model calls, yet the operator often gets either a finished replay or raw logs. That makes it hard to ask why an agent moved, test a small intervention, or package a run for another researcher. GOD is a local-first control room for agent societies. From the same browser workflow, an operator …
items.sm: Presents a browser interface for inspecting agent societies, issuing questions and interventions, replaying activity, and sharing portable experiment configurations.

items.t: Finding Where the Buck Stops: An Automated Failure Attribution-Based Reflection Framework for Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Xiaoqing Wang, Keman Huang, Bin Liang, Hongyu Li, Xiaoyong Du, Wuqiong Pan
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models have shown promise for complex tasks but suffer from high failure rates. Current self-reflection methods for MAS require all agents to reflect upon failure, overlooking a critical reality: failures typically stem from a specific agent leading the task astray, namely the decisive error agent, while others merely fulfill their regular duties. Forcing regular-be…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that identifies the agent and step responsible for failure, constructs a correction, and directs reflection toward that agent.

items.t: Decentralized Coordination Architectures for Intelligent Agent Swarms
items.sm: Reviews decentralized swarm coordination methods and deployment challenges involving delayed communication, changing networks, faulty agents, limited computation, and unreliable adaptation.

items.t: openJiuwen: Beyond Static Harnesses for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
items.a: Tao Yu, Xinyu Zhang, Qianqian Chen, Xiaoneng Xiang, Chia Kwangyang, Xingchen Huang, Ran Chen, Yangkai Ding
items.x: Long-horizon coding agents operate over evolving repository states while increasingly relying on heterogeneous capabilities, delegated agents, and multi-agent coordination. These trends pose two complementary challenges for the agent harness. First, developers need to compose capabilities, reconfigure execution logic, and scale increasingly complex agent systems without repeatedly rebuilding orchestration. Second, co…
items.sm: Presents an open-source coding agent harness for composing capabilities and adapting execution decisions to diagnostics, task progress, and changing repository context.

items.t: CoCoBench: A Cooperative Coordination Benchmark for Embodied Multi-Agent Task Planning
items.a: Yang Chen, Ye-Xin Xie, Lirong Che, Danyang Peng, Yuzhe Yang, Peiwen Lin, Xu Cao, Chuang Wang
items.x: Agent systems powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly in recent years, yet existing embodied-agent benchmarks still lack fine-grained diagnostics for multi-agent coordination. Most benchmarks either focus on single-agent task completion or summarize multi-agent behavior with overall task success rates, which can obscure coordination failures such as duplicated work, violations of ord…
items.sm: Introduces 897 validated household task instances that assess agent coordination through task allocation, ordering, resource exclusion, and handoffs.

items.t: EULER: Exploring Underused Links with Evidence-Checked Return for Multi-Agent Mathematical Discovery
items.x: Mathematical communities work with different objects, invariants, and tools, so transferring a problem across them is expensive and often skipped. We present EULER, a multi-agent system that takes such a transfer--a bridge--as its unit of search. Around a fixed conjecture, EULER runs direct, adjacent-domain, and distant-domain routes in competition; a bridge keeps its budget only if it supplies an operation the sourc…
items.sm: Presents a mathematical discovery system that explores connections across domains and checks whether transferred evidence supports the original conjecture.

items.t: A new chapter for A2A
items.sm: Announces A2A joining AAIF as a growth stage project and describes its stable release supporting discovery and delegation across agent frameworks and vendors.

items.t: Risks and Controls for Multi-Agent Systems: an analytical framework for deployment of AI agents across organisational boundaries
items.sm: Presents an analytical framework for assessing risks and controls when deploying AI agents across organisational boundaries.

items.t: Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini in the Real-World
items.a: Samuel Schmidgall, Xiaokai Zhu, Marian Shaw, Lin Yang, Valentin Liévin, Jingyun Yang, Yuchen Zhuang, Tim Strother
items.x: We present an extension and comprehensive real-world validation of Co-Scientist, a Gemini-based multi-agent system designed to accelerate end-to-end scientific research across hypothesis generation, experimentation, and manuscript generation. Moving beyond in silico hypothesis generation, this specialized configuration transitions Co-Scientist into an execution-grounded research partner advancing closed-loop scientif…
items.sm: Extends a Gemini-based research agent system into experimental workflows across materials science, biology, and computing, including laboratory testing of a proposed material synthesis route.

items.t: Engineering design collaborative workflows for research software engineering through a multi-agent framework
items.a: Mingjun Shi, Jingyuan Deng, liang Li, Weidenthaler Matthias, Yongheng Wang
items.sm: Proposes an agent-supported research software design workflow that addresses terminology and knowledge gaps among researchers, designers, and frontend engineers.

items.t: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
items.a: Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Wen Da, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan, Yao Hu
items.x: Long-horizon agent runs generate experience that can improve both the current run and future work. Most self-improvement methods process this experience only after execution ends, so they cannot redirect the active run or immediately apply and validate lessons learned from it. We argue that self-improvement should instead be live, using emerging experience both to redirect the active run and to update the persistent …
items.sm: Introduces a supervisor-worker agent harness that uses ongoing experience to redirect active work and improve persistent execution procedures.

items.t: LiveSim: Simulating Environment-Shaped Users in Multi-Agent Live-Stream Ecosystems
items.a: Jiaqi Xu, Yiran Qiao, Jing Chen, Qiwei Zhong, Xiang Ao, Xueqi Cheng
items.x: User behavior simulation with large language models~(LLMs) is increasingly used to support multi-agent ecosystem simulation. Existing simulators typically rely on static user profiles inferred from historical observations, which become inadequate in socially intensive environments such as live streaming where interaction dynamics continuously reshape user behavior. We propose \textbf{LiveSim}, an LLM-based framework …
items.sm: Introduces a livestream simulation framework that updates user behavior models from observed interactions and stores reusable patterns of environmental influence.

items.t: Claude Code Complete User Handbook
items.x: Claude Code is an agentic work environment: a language model operating in a loop with filesystem access, shell execution, browser control, scheduled and cloud execution, external tool connections through the Model Context Protocol, and multi-agent orchestration. Its capability envelope now exceeds what one practitioner can supervise by attention alone, and its failure modes are systemic rather than local: an unreview…
items.sm: Provides a task-oriented handbook for operating Claude Code, emphasizing observable completion conditions, permissions, isolation, tool connections, and oversight of autonomous workflows.

items.t: AgentFold: Closed-Loop Agentic Search for Protein Folding Model Design
items.a: Mingquan Liu, Jiangyu Chen, Hanqun Cao, Xujun Zhang, Pengsen Ma, Xiangru Tang, Shuting Jin, Zhuo Yang
items.x: Scientific LLM agents have shown promise in literature reasoning, tool use, and experiment planning, but it remains unclear whether they can autonomously improve large, tightly coupled scientific machine-learning systems through executable code changes and computationally expensive validation. We study this question in protein folding, where progress requires coordinated architectural modifications, multi-objective e…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent system that searches protein folding model code variants through hypothesis generation, implementation, evaluation, and memory of successful and failed changes.

items.t: tradertanmay/ai-agents-zero-to-hero
items.x: Learn AI agents from first principles to production. Zero mandatory dependencies, pure standard Python 3.11+, and no magic frameworks.
items.sm: Teaches AI agent development from basic principles through production using Python's standard library without mandatory external dependencies.

items.sm: Studies how language model agents coordinate through a shared environment to develop technologies without assigned roles, predefined recipes, or centralized workflows.

items.t: FTDI: A budget-aware self-healing framework for LLM multi-agent code generation
items.a: Sixue Men, Zhe‐Ming Lu, Hao Luo, Yangming Zheng
items.sm: Presents FTDI as a framework for repairing failures in language model multi-agent code generation while accounting for budget constraints.

items.t: Repair or Resample? Rethinking Failure Debugging in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zhongwen Luan, Xiaoyu Zhang, Ming Hu, Yue Yang, Jiongchi Yu, Xiaohong Chen
items.x: As large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MASs) are increasingly applied to long-horizon complex tasks, their reliability has emerged as the core bottleneck hindering their real-world deployment. Existing MAS debugging and repair methods typically rely on rerunning and resampling the entire execution trajectory. However, a fundamental question remains to be answered: do these methods causally repair MA…
items.sm: Introduces SymTrace, a framework that replays recorded agent workflows from controlled intervention points to distinguish targeted failure repair from improvements caused by resampling.

items.t: Candidate supply and answer selection shape the value of LLM judging in multi-agent systems
items.a: Jia-Hao Ji, Sijie Li, Jiabei Cheng, Zixi She, Jin-Tai Yu, Zhiyuan Yuan
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) sometimes already have the potential to answer correctly, but still report a wrong answer. Explaining this outcome is difficult because generation, communication and final answer-selection rules usually change simultaneously. We conceptualize multi-agent reasoning as an evolutionary pipeline of candidate generation, peer communication and terminal selection, wherein consensus without quality…
items.sm: Examines when language model judges identify correct candidate answers and when answer selection rules translate those judgments into better multi-agent outputs.

items.t: MACGen: Toward Functionally Correct and Secure Code Generation via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Miseon Yu, Jaehoon Choi, Younghan Lee, Yunheung Paek
items.x: Despite their strong ability to generate code, large language models often fail to produce secure code, as their outputs frequently contain security vulnerabilities. Secure code generation is inherently challenging because it requires solving a multi-objective problem: functional correctness and security. Existing approaches address this challenge by injecting external security knowledge or by using agentic feedback …
items.sm: Presents MACGen, which coordinates planning, security analysis, code generation, and refinement to address functional correctness and security together.

items.t: Do Multi-agent LLMs Improve Test Generation? A Study of Coverage, Mutation Score, and Cost
items.a: Riccardo Coppola, Tommaso Fulcini, Flavio Giobergia, Davide Randino, Marco Roman, Erik Scolaro, Luigi Aceto, Isabella Ilaria Favero
items.sm: Studies whether multi-agent language models improve test generation by comparing coverage, mutation scores, and cost.

items.t: Delegated Misalignment: How Multi-Agent Structures Amplify LLM Safety Risks
items.a: Zonghao Ying, Jiaqi Yan, Huize Luo, Quanchen Zou, Aishan Liu, Xianglong Liu
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems where a principal agent decomposes tasks and delegates them to subordinate agents that may invoke external tools. Safety alignment, however, is still evaluated almost exclusively under a single-agent threat model, treating safety as a property of the individual LLM. We show that this assumption breaks down: \emph{individual safety alignment…
items.sm: Argues that delegation can undermine individual model safety, with principals diffusing responsibility and subordinates following assigned roles, increasing harmful outcomes across tested models.

items.t: ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs
items.a: Songyuan Li, Ahmed M. Abdelmoniem, Shiqiang Wang
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) workflows have emerged as a powerful paradigm for solving complex, open-ended tasks through collaborative reasoning among specialized LLM agents, but they incur substantial operating costs due to repeated LLM invocations and long-horizon context accumulation. Existing cascade routing methods make one-shot, query-level decisions and cannot adapt to the dynamic, state-dependent na…
items.sm: Introduces ProgRouter, which selects models during multi-agent workflows using task progress estimates to balance output quality against time and cost budgets.

items.t: TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving
items.a: Hongqiu Ni, Han Tian, Chi Zhang, Guopeng Li, Haisheng Tan
items.x: Prefix caching introduces a fundamental tradeoff in multi-agent large language model (LLM) serving: retaining a long system-prompt key-value (KV) cache for an agent accelerates future calls, yet it reduces the GPU memory available for batching concurrent requests. In multi-stage workflows, existing schedulers tend to prioritize either immediate prefix locality or overall workflow progress. However, under a shared KV …
items.sm: Introduces TOPAS, a scheduler that jointly chooses cached agent prefixes and requests to execute, balancing GPU memory use with workflow completion time.

items.t: Prompt Sensitivity of Generative Agents: Evidence from an Epidemic Model
items.x: As generative AI gains traction, researchers are investigating its potential to serve as proxies for humans. From undergoing cognitive psychology experiments to experiencing an epidemic, generative agents, agents powered by generative AI models, produce realistic human behavior when prompted. This study explores the sensitivity of these generative agents' behavior to prompt modifications and varied persona names of t…
items.sm: Tests prompt sensitivity in simulated epidemics, finding negligible effects from synonymous wording but changes from other small prompt variations and contextual adjustments.

items.t: Epidemic Modeling with Generative Agents: Methodology, Prompt Sensitivity, and LLM Sensitivity
items.sm: Develops epidemic simulations using language model agents and argues that both prompt design and model choice shape the resulting behavioral and epidemic patterns.

items.t: Routed Graph Handoff: Adaptive Format Selection for Multi-Agent LLM Delegation
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems coordinate through natural-language messages that consume 40--60\% of their token budget. Replacing these with structured graphs reduces cost but fails on tasks requiring adaptive reasoning. We propose \textbf{Routed Graph Handoff}, where a lightweight LLM router (155 tokens, 0.15\% overhead) selects between a typed dependency graph and natural language for each delegation. On four benchmarks …
items.sm: Routes agent handoffs between structured graphs and natural language, reporting reduced communication costs while matching or improving benchmark performance compared with natural language alone.

items.t: HypoForge: A Self-Improving Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Hypothesis Generation and Testing via Scientific Skill Learning
items.a: Ziqing Qian, Jiaying Lei, Yifang Wang, Nan Cao
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled AI scientist systems to automate scientific discovery, yet existing approaches most rely on static prompting or fixed workflows and fail to accumulate experience for continual improvement. We propose HypoForge, an experience-guided multi-agent framework that learns reusable scientific skills for automated hypothesis generation and hypothesis testing. HypoForge is built on the…
items.sm: Introduces HypoForge, which learns reusable scientific skills through comparative critique for hypothesis generation and empirical feedback for hypothesis testing.

items.sm: Extends the Pi coding agent with versioned plans, reviewer subagents, tracked execution, and explicit human approval before implementation.

items.sm: Introduces AgenticLens, a framework for optimizing enterprise agent systems around inference costs, token use, governance, latency, and operational reliability.

items.t: A Control-Theoretic Approach for Resource-Aware Consensus in Multi-Agent AI
items.x: Large language model multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) rely on inter-agent communication to solve complex reasoning tasks, yet rigorous guarantees relating consensus performance to computational resources remain limited. Here, we present a novel way to characterize collective belief dynamics as a discrete-time switched system in which communication topologies have distinct consensus-contraction rates and token costs. By …

items.t: Poisoning Agentic Alpha: Adversarial Vulnerabilities Across Roles and Architectures in Multi-Agent Trading Systems
items.a: CheolWon Na, Hao Ni, Lukasz Szpruch, Zhangyang Wang, Dhagash Mehta, Saurabh Nagrecha, Alejandro Lopez-Lira, Chanyeol Choi

items.t: Simulating team dynamics with generative agents: a case study on data science teams from digital platforms
items.a: Libo Li, Huan Yu, MH Kunc

items.t: Observability and Fault Injection for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering

The tool instruments…
items.sm: Introduces a tool combining distributed execution tracing and targeted fault injection to inspect and compare software engineering workflows involving multiple language model agents.

items.t: Who is the Agent to Blame? Localizing Faithfulness and Citation Mistakes in Agentic Deep Research

items.t: Agentopia on a Consumer GPU: A Reduced-Scale Long-Horizon Port with an 8B Model

items.t: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams

items.t: AgentRoom: Concurrent Multi-Agent Coding in a CRDT-Backed Shared Workspace
items.x: Concurrent multi-agent coding promises division of labor across modules, robustness through redundancy, and parallel exploration at the natural granularity of multi-file projects. items.t: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank: Scaling Capability Discovery Beyond In-Context Routing
items.a: Nazib Sorathiya, Daniel Zhang, Bardiya Akhbari
items.x: Agent ecosystems now include thousands of MATS components (Models, Agents, Tools, and Skills), yet their discovery still relies on in-context routing. These systems read a registry (names, hints, or descriptions, as context budget permits), pick a candidate, invoke it, and retry on failure. This pattern degrades with scale, and registries are growing fast. We recast capability discovery as search over a registry by d…
items.sm: Enriches capability descriptions and retrieves ranked candidates, reporting better selection accuracy than routing through registry contents as available capabilities grow.

items.t: TrustShiftProbe: Characterizing, Benchmarking, and Defending Staged Trust Attacks on MCP Servers
items.a: Mehrdad Rostamzadeh, Sidhant Narula, Mohammad Ghasemigol, Daniel Takabi
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as the standard layer connecting Large Language Model agents to external tool backends. This openness introduces a severe server-side threat we term TrustShift: a compromised MCP server behaves benignly during an initial conditioning phase, building operational reliance and suppressing agent skepticism, before switching to an adversarial payload once an interaction thresho…
items.sm: Examines attacks in which compromised MCP servers establish trust through benign interactions before switching to malicious tool responses.

items.t: Predicting the scale limits of social mechanisms in agent societies
items.x: Societies of interacting language-model agents offer a controllable and repeatable way to study collective behaviour at scales that would be difficult to test with people. Their scientific value, however, depends on whether a social mechanism that works in a small group still operates when thousands of agents interact, and testing this directly requires costly large-scale runs. Here we introduce an audit that predict…
items.sm: Introduces an audit predicting whether social mechanisms survive population growth by examining opportunities to act, information use, and measurement effects.

items.a: SUPRIYA KRISHNAN, Aditya Bharti, Sudhanshu Kumar Bharti
items.sm: Preregisters a dual-baseline evaluation of knowledge combination in language model teams using arithmetic problems, with confirmatory outcomes unavailable at registration.

items.sm: Describes a merged study of thirteen experiments concerning conditional communication and calibration fatigue in multi-agent language model systems.

items.sm: Orders evaluation checks by cost, reporting that screening document-processing workflows before model judging reduced judge spending by about 63% without reducing coverage.

items.t: Meta-Moderator: Empowering Multi-Agent Debate with Meta-Cognition
items.a: Wentao Hu, Zhuoyue Wan, Jinhao Shen, Chen Jason Zhang, Xiaoyong Wei, Qing Li
items.x: Multi-agent debate can improve large language model reasoning by eliciting diverse hypotheses and critiques, yet its performance is often constrained by weak moderation. Common pipelines rely on fixed budgets, agreement-based stopping, or untrained judges, leading to redundant deliberation and unreliable evidence aggregation. We cast moderation as a meta-cognitive process, monitoring debate utility, controlling delib…
items.sm: Trains a moderator to regulate agent debates and decide when to answer, reporting improvements over common decision methods across five benchmarks.

items.t: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
items.a: Yi Zhu, Xiongwei Wu, Qiyi Wang, Tingyu Qu, Jiajun Liu, Sihan Cao, Long Chen, Weigao Sun
items.x: Mobile planning requires a central agent to coordinate tools, persistent user context, reusable procedures, and specialized sub-agents while adapting to execution feedback. Evaluating these workflows requires distinguishing task completion from compliance with prescribed resource and procedural requirements. We introduce \textbf{MobilePA-Bench}, a benchmark comprising 1,705 tasks across eight query task domains and 2…
items.sm: Introduces 1,705 simulated mobile planning tasks evaluating completion alongside required use of tools, memory, reusable procedures, and collaborating agents.

items.t: Markets, Not Planners: Decentralized Orchestration of LLM Agents with Private Information
items.a: Xiao Liu, Haoyang Li, Songwei Li, Hongbo Fang, Fengli Xu, Feng Shi, James Evans
items.x: As LLM agents proliferate, built by different parties and with different capabilities and costs, orchestrating them is more like assembling labor across the economy than a computer calling a subroutine. Existing orchestration is typically centralized, with a single planner assigning every task, but this creates a bottleneck as agent pools grow, requires private information (e.g., agents' execution costs), and can eas…
items.sm: Introduces a decentralized task market where agents bid using private costs, earn allocations through bids and reputation, and delegate complex work.

items.t: Beyond the Mandate: A Systematic Security Analysis of the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
items.a: Avital Aviv, Parth A. Gandh, Ron Bitton, Asaf Shabtai
items.x: The Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), introduced by Google, enables large language model (LLM)-driven shopping agents to authorize and execute payments on behalf of users. Its signed Checkout and Payment Mandates protect the integrity of transaction data after signing. Agent interactions and external inputs that shape a transaction before authorization remain outside that protection, including Agent-to-Agent Protocol (A…
items.sm: Analyzes security boundaries across AP2 version 0.2 payment workflows, including agent messages and tool inputs that shape transactions before authorization.

items.t: A transport-layer cryptographic framework secures inter-agent communication and verdict provenance in multi-agent malware detection pipelines
items.sm: Introduces a cryptographic communication protocol providing authenticated encrypted channels, replay protection, forward secrecy, and signed verdicts for multi-agent malware detection.

items.t: Building the Refactoring Swarm: An Empirical Study on Developer Dynamics and LLM Orchestration
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Studies student-built refactoring agents, finding no significant relationship between initial algorithmic expertise and success while identifying failures associated with overloaded context.

items.v: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems
items.sm: Proposes collaborating agents for early defect prediction and continuous software quality monitoring through code analysis, test generation, patch creation, and quality assessment.

items.t: AUDITA: certified auditing and causal attribution of adverse outcomes in autonomous multi-agent systems
items.x: Physical automation is scaling toward fleets of embodied machines commanded by an AI brain. Early deployments already run factories and warehouses at production rates beyond any human line, and their adoption is accelerating. But when their joint decisions cause harm, everyone involved has reason to blame everyone else, the machine vendor, the algorithm provider, the factory operator, the insurer, and the regulator, …
items.sm: Combines tamper-evident command records with graded causal attribution to audit harmful outcomes in autonomous agent systems, claiming protection against manipulated blame.

items.t: Genomic Convergence Verification: A Multi-Agent Framework for Hallucination Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Overcoming Gödel's Limitation Through Multi-System Convergence.
items.sm: Proposes detecting hallucinations through agreement among independent verification agents and claims that adding systems reduces the probability of statements remaining undecidable.

items.t: From Diagnosis to Redesign: Using Quantitative Ethnography to Improve Multi-Agent LLM Reasoning
items.a: Vedant Khatri, Anthony Cusimano, Zachari Swiecki, Zhen Xu, Xiner Liu, Renzhe Yu
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are designed to improve reasoning by decomposing tasks across multiple agents with specialized functions, but the presence of multiple agents does not inherently guarantee coherent reasoning or outputs that align with task objectives. This paper introduces a quantitative ethnographic (QE) approach for diagnosing and redesigning multi-agent LLM systems based on the discou…
items.sm: Analyzes agent debate patterns to guide system redesign, finding that correct essay scores were associated with rubric-based justification, agreement, and elaboration.

items.t: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
items.a: Weixiang Sun, Zehong Wang, Hong Huang, Colby Nelson, Yijun Ma, Yanfang Ye
items.x: Multi-agent systems built from large language models are deployed widely, yet how much performance is lost when two LLMs must coordinate rather than act alone remains unclear. We formulate the collaboration tax as the team-decentralisation loss of a two-player cooperative game with private information, with two propositions characterising its sign and its equivalence to a max-superadditivity violation. We operational…
items.sm: Measures coordination losses across language models and tasks, linking larger losses to conversational failures and finding that losses decrease as model capability increases.

items.t: TensorAgent: Multi-agent Framework for Automated Tensor Core Code Generation
items.a: Bingjie Liu, Zhongchun Zheng, Xianwei Zhang
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent framework for automatically generating Tensor Core code.

items.t: Physical Agentic AI: An Architecture for Orchestrating a Robot Crew with LLMs
items.a: Xinyuan Liu, Eren Sadikoglu, Riana Chatterjee, Ransalu Senanayake
items.x: Agentic AI frameworks interpret open-ended task goals and decompose them into multi-step plans. Richer information about embodiment-specific capabilities, physical preconditions, and cross-robot coordination improves grounding, but does not eliminate infeasible, mistimed, or unsafe physical actions. Physical robot crews therefore require an explicit architectural interface between semantic planning and execution, whe…
items.sm: Introduces a robot orchestration architecture that assigns tasks to executable skills and checks planned actions against capabilities, system state, and workflow constraints.

items.t: Aligned Alone, Misaligned Together: Forecasting Adversarial Capture in LLM Agent Populations
items.x: AI safety evaluations typically assess models one at a time. But language-model agents increasingly operate in populations, where they read and respond to one another's decisions. A model that makes reliable decisions on its own may behave differently when surrounded by other agents. Can individually reliable agents be collectively manipulated, and can we predict how strongly the population will respond? We study thi…
items.sm: Finds that a committed minority can shift language-model populations' security decisions, making isolated agent evaluations unreliable predictors of collective behavior.

items.t: Does shared context cause hallucination in multi-agent LLM systems? A preregistered within-item experiment
items.sm: Preregisters an experiment testing whether shared context increases hallucinations in multi-agent language models while holding compute and information constant.

items.t: How Agents Represent Humans: Human-Directed Stereotypes in an Open Agent Social Network
items.a: Huangchen Xu, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang
items.x: LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed in persistent social environments, where generated claims can be posted, replied to, remembered, and reused. We study human-directed stereotypes on Moltbook, an open agent-native social platform, asking how agents construct humans as a social category. For this human-target analysis, we introduce an annotation framework with four evaluative dimensions---morality, friendlines…
items.sm: Analyzes how agents describe humans on a social platform, finding that competence dominates evaluations alongside descriptions of humans as knowledge-bearing, cultural, and embodied beings.

items.t: Role-Specialized Mixture-of-Agents with Open-Weight LLMs for Clinical Prediction
items.a: Jun Hou, Yi Fang, Xuan Wang
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to clinical prediction tasks such as in-hospital mortality and readmission from electronic health records (EHRs). Privacy and compliance constraints motivate systems that can be deployed locally, which has increased interest in open-weight multi-agent designs. However, most medical multi-agent systems are evaluated as a single block, leaving unclear which agent ro…
items.sm: Examines agent roles in clinical prediction, finding the final integrator drives gains and an open-weight team matches closed-model mortality prediction F1.

items.t: MCP-Universe RL: A Framework for Training MCP Tool-Use Agents via Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Ziyang Luo, Yan Yang, Xiangru Jian, Ziji Shi, Xiaoqiang Lin, Jun Hao Liew, Silvio Savarese, Junnan Li
items.x: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become an effective way to improve the tool-use ability of large language models (LLMs), but most existing RL frameworks stop at the policy update. For every new domain, the user is left with two hard systems problems: standing up an isolated environment for each of hundreds of concurrent trajectories and connecting it to training, and scheduling the rollout so that the GPU stays busy …
items.sm: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework that connects MCP tools to training and manages isolated environments and rollouts for agents performing lengthy tool-based tasks.

items.t: HANSARD: A Reference Architecture for Forensic Readiness, Runtime Witnessing, and Graded Attribution in Autonomous Multi-Agent AI Systems

items.x: Autonomous multi-agent systems nowadays act in finance, software supply chains, and security operations. Already, the first largely AI-orchestrated intrusion campaigns have been reported. Yet, when such a system causes harm, no method can robustly establish what happened, what caused it, or who is accountable. This is because provenance forensics works at the wrong abstraction, formal causality assumes the causal mod…
items.sm: Proposes an architecture for reconstructing actions, assessing causes, and assigning accountability in autonomous agent systems whose agents and logging infrastructure may collude.

items.t: PropUQ-MAS: Propagation-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yaokun Liu, Yifan Liu, Daniel Yue Zhang, Ruichen Yao, Zelin Li, Dong Wang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) solve complex tasks through communication among role-specialized agents. However, inter-agent dependencies introduce reliability risks beyond isolated agent failures. For instance, errors in intermediate messages could be inherited and amplified by downstream agents. Existing uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods mainly target isolated responses or single-agent reasoning, and the…
items.sm: Estimates reliability by combining each agent step's uncertainty with uncertainty inherited from earlier messages, reporting improved uncertainty measurement across multi-agent systems.

items.t: OptiMAS: Automatically Optimize Multi-Agent System
items.a: Yuxin Cheng, Chang Liu, Hanxin Yu, Haochen Tan, Taiqiang Wu, Weiqiang Jin, Jie Ran, Kaibo Wang
items.x: Automated evolution of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) holds significant potential for reducing the manual effort required to design and optimize LLM-based agent architectures. However, extant search-based paradigms face a fundamental trade-off, where an expanded optimization scope exacerbates evolutionary instability, while discrete branch-and-discard search isolates insights across lineages. To address these limitations,…

items.x: Software systems have traditionally been organized around applications where human users act as principal decision-makers. This evolution gives rise to an agent economy where these autonomous agent…

items.t: HiMA-MDD: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Harness for Interpretable Multimodal Depression Detection in Clinical Interviews
items.x: Depression assessment from multimodal clinical interviews requires integrating dispersed evidence from multiple symptoms into a coherent PHQ-8 profile. This process is hierarchical: relevant evidence is often sparse and context-dependent within local question-answer exchanges, multiple exchanges jointly support symptom-level judgments, and the final assessment depends on the coherence of the complete symptom profile.…
items.sm: Introduces a three-layer agent architecture that coordinates interview evidence, symptom scoring, feedback, and recorded state for interpretable multimodal depression assessment.

items.t: Spine-Branch Coordination for Multi-agent Computer Use

However, a critical physical bottleneck is that the state of two VMs cannot be merged. Previous systems handle this ad-hoc rather than treating it as a first-class concern. We propose Spine-Branch Coordination for multi-agent computer use, a framewor…
items.sm: Coordinates computer-use agents through a persistent main virtual machine and parallel information-gathering branches, reporting higher task success without merging virtual machine states.

We state what an agent harness must guarantee, prove it, and build the instrument that measures whether a harness de…

items.t: AEGIS: Preventing Cross-Domain Resource Abuse in MCP

For example, an agent may request an excessively large search radius or…

items.t: Polaris : Multi Agentic System for Conversational Enterprise Analytics
items.a: Varuni H K, Soham Sarkar, Jay Kumar, Goutham Krishnan, Tanvi Johari, Avinash Bharadwaj, Santosh Hegde
items.x: In today's fast-paced environment, the ability to swiftly access, understand, and act on data is no longer optional; it is essential. Yet most organizations remain data-rich but insight-poor, constrained by the complexity of querying, interpreting, and explaining enterprise-scale information. We present Polaris, a supervisor-led multi-agent framework for conversational enterprise analytics that bridges this gap. Pola…
items.sm: Polaris coordinates specialized agents to turn conversational enterprise data requests into querying, visualization, and explanation workflows with adaptive task assignment and recovery.

items.t: aemrebarut/herdr-dagr
items.x: Your agent swarm as a live DAG: an orchestration graph with attempts, review gates, and evidence, in a herdr split pane.
items.sm: The project displays agent orchestration as a live dependency graph with execution attempts, review gates, and evidence in a split pane.

items.t: soumatheusgomes/vibe-coding-toolkit
items.x: A curated, battle-tested AI-coding toolkit: Claude Code plugins, subagent orchestration, quality gates, and ready-to-copy prompts, extracted from real production use.
items.sm: The repository collects AI coding plugins, agent orchestration tools, quality checks, and reusable prompts described as drawn from production use.

items.t: Nyasers/DSHana
items.x: DSHana: DeepSeek Harness as a subagent for HanaAgent
items.sm: DSHana makes DeepSeek Harness available as a subagent for HanaAgent.

items.t: Optim-Agent/dsh-plans
items.x: Human-in-the-loop planning preset for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), adapted from prime-plans: researched Markdown plans in ./dsh-plans, reviewer/criticizer subagent refinement, per-workspace language & model settings, goal-driven execution with ponytail + MVP tests.
items.sm: The project provides a DeepSeek Harness planning preset with human involvement, researched plans, reviewer and critic refinement, workspace settings, and goal-driven execution.

items.t: Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems
items.sm: Reviews multiagent experiments showing complementary search alongside coordination failures, resource congestion, unreliable information sharing, and escalating conflicts.

items.t: @TechCrunch: Anthropic researchers found AI agents can clash, collude and coordinate in unexpected ways, raising new questi…
items.sm: Reports that Anthropic observed unexpected conflict, collusion, and coordination among AI agents, questioning whether current safety tests adequately capture interaction risks.

items.t: Multi-Agent debate system based on large language models: structured deliberation and validation in satellite communications
items.a: Susana Gómez Álvarez, Alejandro Mozo Quesada, Tomás Navarro, Sergio Gálvez, Francisco Lopez Valverde
items.sm: Proposes moderated debates between satellite communications specialists and compares single-agent reasoning with teams using either the same or different language models.

items.t: InterSAGE: The Secure and Verifiable Interoperability Protocol for An Internet of Agents
items.a: Zhenhua Zou, Sheng Guo, Qiuyang Zhan, Lepeng Zhao, Shuo Li, Zhuotao Liu
items.x: The emerging Internet of Agents enables LLM-powered agents to discover peers, invoke tools, and delegate tasks across organizational boundaries. Existing protocols increasingly define how agents exchange messages, but not how an agent proves its identity, authorization, advertised capabilities, or accountability after delegation. We present InterSAGE, a trust-native protocol suite that supplies this missing security …
items.sm: Introduces InterSAGE, a protocol suite for verifying agent identities, discovering capabilities, negotiating permissions, and maintaining accountability across organizational boundaries.

items.t: CONTAINING CASCADING AI ERRORS: A SPECTRAL BRANCHING- PROCESS FRAMEWORK FOR VERIFICATION ALLOCATION IN MULTI-AGENT SYSTEMS
items.v: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
items.sm: Models cascading agent errors as a branching process and proposes allocating verification resources to suppress propagation and reduce expected harm.

items.t: StateBridge: Training-free Hidden-state Alignment for Latent Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yanwen Peng, Delvin Ce Zhang, Xi Wang, Nikolaos Aletras
items.x: Large language model based multi-agent systems usually communicate in text, i.e., using discrete tokens. However, text introduces a discrete bottleneck. Converting the sender's continuous hidden states into discrete tokens discards information that token identities alone cannot capture. Recent work proposes latent communication as an alternative, where agents transmit hidden representations directly without convertin…
items.sm: Introduces StateBridge, a training-free method that transforms one language model's hidden states into another model's input space for direct communication.

items.t: Agent Behavioral Contracts II: Certifying Compositional Reliability Without Assuming Independence
items.a: Varun Pratap Bhardwaj, Garima Singh, Arun Pratap Bhardwaj
items.x: Compositional reliability bounds for multi-agent systems multiply component reliabilities, a step licensed by a conditional-independence assumption that is routinely stated and rarely tested. We test it. Two instances of one model, in a two-agent handoff, co-fail on 90.0% of the missions on which either fails (log OR 6.66, 95% CI [6.38, 7.00]; phi 0.916), in a preregistered evaluation of 18,000 missions scored by det…
items.sm: Finds strongly correlated failures between agents sharing a model, challenging reliability estimates that assume independent failures and overvalue redundancy.

items.t: Delegation-Aware Runtime Contracts for Open LLM Multi-Agent Systems: Constraint Preservation, Capability Revocation, and State Recovery
items.sm: Introduces machine-checkable delegation contracts intended to preserve permissions, data restrictions, budgets, obligations, and revocation conditions as agents hand off tasks.

items.t: Systematization of Knowledge: Security and Safety in the Model Context Protocol Ecosystem
items.a: Shiva Gaire, Srijan Gyawali, Saroj Mishra, Suman Niroula, Dilip Thakur, Umesh Yadav
items.v: Lecture notes in networks and systems
items.sm: Surveys security and safety issues in the Model Context Protocol ecosystem.

items.t: Discovering Efficient and Explainable Communication Topologies for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems via Causal Inference
items.a: Junzhi Li, Peng He, Qirui Ji, Wei Wang, Lixiang Liu, Chuxiong Sun
items.x: The performance of large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) largely depends on effective communication topologies. Existing topology generation methods, however, typically learn communication topologies through black-box optimization driven solely by task-level rewards. While effective, such optimization provides little insight into why particular communication edges are selected, making it difficul…
items.sm: Introduces E2-Explainer, a framework that uses causal attribution to identify compact communication subgraphs that preserve task performance in multiagent systems.

items.t: Review of: "Exploration of LLM Multi-Agent Application Implementation Based on LangGraph+CrewAI"
items.sm: Reviews a work about implementing language model multiagent applications using LangGraph and CrewAI.

items.t: Measuring Collective Semantic Change in Populations of Language Model Agents
items.x: Collective semantic change in populations of language model agents is a measurable dynamical phenomenon. We present a passive longitudinal instrument called Kopterix that observes the semantic state of an agent population as a sequence of bounded observations under a protocol defined before the observations begin. Each observation divides the sampled feed by post age into surface, mid-stream, and residue layers, whic…
items.sm: Introduces Kopterix, an observational instrument for tracking semantic changes in agent populations, and evaluates it using scheduled observations of Moltbook.

items.t: MARC v1: An Open-Source Multi-Agent Framework for Clinical AI Reasoning and Coordination
items.a: Saisha Shetty, Satvik Tripathi, Austin Lin, Colin Zhao, Theodore Kim, Don Enwerem, Jacinta Arnold, Shahriar Faghani
items.x: We present Multi-Agent Reasoning and Coordination (MARC), an open-source framework that replaces monolithic LLM prompting with deterministic multi-agent orchestration for clinical reasoning. MARC coordinates role-specialized agents for extraction, reasoning, answer generation, and evaluation, with explicit context passing and traceable intermediate outputs, enabling stage-wise failure attribution. We additionally int…
items.sm: Introduces MARC, a configurable framework coordinating specialized clinical reasoning agents with explicit context sharing, traceable intermediate outputs, and automatically generated task prompts.

items.t: BoardroomAI: Dependency-Aware Human-Steerable Multi-Agent Deliberation through Evolving Decision Graphs
items.x: Organizational decisions are co-created while evidence, constraints, and human priorities continue to evolve. In conventional transcript-based multi-agent systems, humans typically provide an initial problem, agents deliberate internally, and the system returns a final response. BoardroomAI instead treats the human as a persistent participant who can intervene by challenging assumptions, modifying constraints, changi…
items.sm: Introduces BoardroomAI, which represents deliberation in evolving decision graphs so humans can revise evidence, constraints, and priorities throughout agent discussions.

items.t: flop-labs/technocore-chat
items.x: HTTP-native chat and notes for agents whose sandbox only allows webfetch — every write is a plain GET. Runs technocore.chat.
items.sm: Provides chat and notes for agents restricted to web fetching, using HTTP GET requests for every write.

items.t: PerryLink/dsh-auto-review
items.x: Second-model AI auto-review for DeepSeek Harness approval requests: a read-only reviewer subagent returns structured allow/deny verdicts with reasons, fail-closed by default, fully auditable from the session log (approval/asked -> autoReview/verdict -> approval/decided).
items.sm: Adds a second-model reviewer to DeepSeek Harness approval requests, producing auditable allow-or-deny decisions with reasons and defaulting to denial.

items.t: soumatheusgomes/agentville
items.x: See every Claude Code and Antigravity agent running on your machine — sessions, subagents, models and live status, inside VS Code.
items.sm: Displays local Claude Code and Antigravity agent sessions, subagents, models, and live status inside VS Code.

items.t: shaokeyibb/dsh-plugin-product-subagents
items.x: Role-based Codex / Claude Code / ACP subagent providers for the DeepSeek Harness — continuable children, durable session recovery, per-role product permissions, and delegation with a permission ceiling.
items.sm: Provides role-based subagents for DeepSeek Harness with resumable sessions, recovery, role-specific permissions, and delegation bounded by a permission ceiling.

items.t: currentbits/solenta
items.x: Free desktop app to run AI coding agents in parallel: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi, Grok. Worktree per thread, shared memory.
items.sm: Runs multiple AI coding agents in parallel through a free desktop app, with separate Git worktrees for each thread and shared memory.

items.t: AI swarms are starting to pose indirect takeover risk
items.sm: Argues unauthorized agent collaboration could weaken safeguards, preserve harmful goals, and influence future models, while proposing restrictions and monitoring that remain untested.

items.t: Developing LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems in Software Engineering: A Mixed-Method Experience Report
items.a: Mariama Celi Serafim De Oliveira, Motunrayo Osatohanmen Ibiyo, Marco Gianrusso, Claudio Di Sipio, Davide Di Ruscio, Phuong T. Nguyen
items.x: The proliferation of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) powered by large language models (LLMs) has transformed the software development process, introducing new paradigms for code generation, debugging, testing, and maintenance. While early applications focused on leveraging single, independent LLMs to assist developers with isolated tasks, recent advances have shifted toward multi-agent systems (MAS) that …
items.sm: Reviews tools and frameworks for language model multiagent software engineering and examines development challenges involving technology selection, coordination rules, and agent roles.

items.t: XBridge: Entity-Grounded Latent Bridge for Heterogeneous LLM Communication
items.a: Wooseong Yang, Wei-Chieh Huang, Weizhi Zhang, Yu Wang, Philip S. Yu, Junhyun Lee
items.x: Heterogeneous multi-agent LLM systems, where agents are powered by different model families, can outperform homogeneous configurations by reducing redundant reasoning patterns. Yet existing communication protocols either operate through text, discarding the sender's internal representations, or require architectural homogeneity for latent-level transfer. We identify the entity grounding problem in cross-architecture …
items.sm: Introduces XBridge, a communication protocol for different language model families that combines latent representations with vocabulary anchors to preserve entity identity.

items.t: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
items.a: Simon Yu, Nicholas Tomlin, Marwa Abdulhai, Ximing Lu, Derek Chong, Abe Hou, Dilara Soylu, Sergey Levine
items.x: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for human-AI interaction typically relies on a single large language model to simulate user behavior. We show that this approach systematically fails to generalize, and trace the failure to simulator collapse: because the simulator LLM is mode-collapsed, an LLM policy trained against it overfits to narrow strategies that exploit the simulator's dominant mode, and such a policy trans…
items.sm: Finds that training against one fixed user simulator encourages overfitting and proposes broader behavioral sampling and training with multiple adaptable simulators.

items.t: A survey of multi-agent geosimulation methodologies: from ABM to LLM
items.x: This article is a review of multi-agent geosimulation methodologies, ranging from traditional Agent-Based Models (ABM) to Large Language Model (LLM) approaches. Drawing on two decades of research, the authors validate the Agent Reference Model (ARM), a formal framework specifying agent components: internal state (beliefs, goals, intentions, plans, history), internal dynamics, external state, and an interface to their…
items.sm: Reviews multiagent geosimulation approaches and compares six methodologies against an agent reference model covering their components and environmental interactions.

items.t: The Cost of Saying Hello: An Empirical Study of Handshake Overhead in AI Agent Communication Protocols
items.x: Every interaction between AI agents begins with a handshake. The initiating agent must locate its counterpart, learn what it can do, and establish a session before the first useful message can be sent. Surveys of agent communication protocols name handshake overhead as an efficiency criterion, yet none report measurements. This paper presents the first empirical, phasedecomposed benchmark of the handshake in three ma…
items.sm: Benchmarks connection setup costs across MCP, A2A, and ACP, finding that round-trip counts dominate overhead under the tested network conditions.

items.t: The Agreeable Swarm: Sycophantic Drift, Consensus Cascades, and Epistemic Collapse in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Systems
items.sm: Examines excessive agreement, spreading consensus, and deterioration of shared knowledge in systems of multiple language model agents.

items.t: ExRole: From Team Trajectories to Executable Roles in Multi-Agent Language Models
items.a: Zhou Liu, Chaoyang Han, Zewei Pan, Zeli Su, Wentao Zhang
items.x: Roles provide an interpretable interface for organizing language-model agents, yet most multi-agent systems treat them as hand-written prompt labels disconnected from learned behavior and parameter updates. We argue that a useful role should instead be an executable control variable: it should summarize behavior predictive of future utility, guide subsequent interaction, and identify the trainable capacity responsibl…
items.sm: Introduces ExRole, which learns executable agent roles from team interactions and reports improved question-answering performance over single-agent search.

items.t: Engineering Agentic AI Systems: A Protocol-Aware Reference Architecture for Orchestration, Retrieval, Governance, Evaluation, and Production Rollout
items.a: Anuj Kumar, Soumyadeep Saha, Manikanthaswamy Gembali
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a reference architecture organizing agent tools, communication, user interaction, retrieval, governance, evaluation, and deployment around MCP, A2A, and AG-UI.

items.t: Observer Zero: Do LLM Agents Form Epistemic Communities?
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Tests whether simulated communities of language model scientists detect changing physical laws, finding that agents collect sufficient evidence but fail to interpret it.

items.t: Do LLMs Beat Nash? Testing Decentralized Coordination in Self-Play Multi-Agent Games
items.a: Deborah Sinishaw, Qile Zhu, Edwin Meriaux, Gregory Dudek
items.x: Large language model agents deployed without a central controller are often assumed to require communication to coordinate their actions. We ask what remains possible without it: when independent instances of the same model cannot communicate, can they still reason about their counterparts well enough to exceed the standard game-theoretic baseline for uncoordinated play? We introduce a benchmark of one-shot, no-commu…
items.sm: Tests coordination without communication in language model games, finding that two hosted models consistently outperform Nash baselines while most open-weight models show mixed gains.

items.t: Large Language Models as Strategic Bidding Agents in P2P Energy Trading Markets
items.a: Ismail Lotfi, Ali Ghrayeb, Prof. Dr. Haitham Abu-Rub
items.x: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading markets rely on double auction mechanisms to match prosumers and consumers in smart grid distribution networks. However, the strategic behavior of bidding agents in such markets remains not fully explored, particularly in repeated settings with bounded rationality. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) as reasoning-driven bidding agents in…
items.sm: Simulates language models bidding in repeated peer-to-peer energy auctions and reports higher early trading volumes than random and bandit-based bidding strategies.

items.t: An Agentic Workflow for Legacy HPC Modernization: Converting the Two-Electron-Integral Core of GAMESS
items.a: Yuzhong Shen, Masha Sosonkina, Peng Xu, Mark S. Gordon
items.x: Modernizing legacy Fortran is a problem of volume: the transformations are individually routine, but the codebases can be enormous, and across much of computational science the work simply goes undone. We propose an agentic workflow that takes this work on at production scale, and we set out to measure how far such delegation can reach. In this work, three prompt-specialized agent roles operate under a version-contro…
items.sm: Proposes a workflow using specialized agents, human checkpoints, and exact verification to modernize legacy Fortran routines in the GAMESS quantum chemistry package.

items.t: tettethu/VibeGame
items.x: VibeGame: Vibe Your Dream Game -- An open-source self-evolving multi-agent framework with an AI-Native game engine that turns your natural language into a fully playable 2D web game and edit it any way you want, built on Claude Code & Codex.
items.sm: VibeGame uses multiple agents and a game engine to turn natural language requests into playable 2D web games and support subsequent edits.

items.t: renzrollon/interlock
items.x: Spec-driven development for Claude Code, layered on OpenSpec. You read one spec; parallel agents ship it to a tested commit.
items.sm: Interlock extends OpenSpec with a Claude Code workflow that uses parallel agents to implement a specification and produce a tested commit.

items.t: NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams
items.sm: Provides a DeepSeek Harness plugin that organizes agents into teams with task assignment, parallel execution, communication, and collaboration.

items.t: @mitchellh: I’ve been asked for an updated daily schedule given Superlogical, second kid, and AI usage. Here you go: - 530…
items.sm: Mitchell Hashimoto shares his work and family schedule and reports regularly keeping at least two AI agents running continuously, including overnight.

items.t: Semantic Uncertainty-Guided Orchestration in Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: John Knowlton, Aritra Guha, Risto Miikkulainen
items.x: As large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems become increasingly capable, coordinating agents under uncertainty becomes a fundamental challenge. Existing orchestration strategies typically rely on fixed interaction patterns and often lack mechanisms for assessing the reliability of intermediate reasoning steps, allowing errors and hallucinations to propagate through the system. This paper introduces a sema…
items.sm: HASSUM uses semantic uncertainty estimates to coordinate agents through selective verification, repeated prompting, further deliberation, and confidence-based answer selection.

items.t: Poster: The Case for Accountable Agent-to-Agent Networks
items.sm: Ledgent combines payment channels with language model infrastructure to support decentralized agent payments, compute-aware routing, and response verification, reporting high throughput and low cryptographic latency.

items.t: RepLLM: Toward Automatically Reproducing Network Research Results
items.a: Yining Jiang, Yunxin Xu, Wei Xu, Yufan Zhu, Rui Liu, Tangtang He, Haiying Huang, Letian Zhu
items.x: Result reproduction of computer networking research is challenging as the scarcity of open-source implementations and the complexity of heterogeneous system architectures. Even though Large Language Models have demonstrated potential in code generation, existing code generation frameworks often fail to address the long-context constraints and intricate logical dependencies, which are vital in reproducing network syst…
items.sm: RepLLM coordinates four specialized agents through shared memory to reproduce networking research implementations from academic papers.

items.t: SAGE: A Self-Adaptive Agentic Framework for Execution-Guided Code Generation and Self-Repair
items.sm: SAGE builds projects from natural language goals by coordinating planning, code generation, isolated execution, and repeated repairs based on runtime errors.

items.t: When Do Institutions Beat Intelligence?
items.x: More capable agents do not necessarily form a more capable collective. A multi-agent system may jointly possess sufficient information yet fail because evidence is poorly routed, unreliable reports enter public belief, correlated claims masquerade as independent support, shared state becomes stale or strategically distorted, or useful evidence is exposed through an ineffective action interface. We ask when additional…
items.sm: Investigates when improving information routing, evidence handling, shared state, and action interfaces helps agent collectives more than increasing individual reasoning capability.

items.t: Weft: Evidence-Gated Version Control for Autonomous Agent Swarms
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Weft proposes version control for autonomous agents that requires machine-checkable evidence tied to exact content and detects stale assumptions beyond textual conflicts.

items.t: ASCon: A Direction-Aware Reciprocal Agent--Step Contextualization Model for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Shuyu Jiang, Yue Ran, Kaiyu Xu, Xingshu Chen, Yi Zhang, Hao Ren, Rui Tang, Tianwei Zhang
items.x: Failure attribution in LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) aims to answer who caused failures, when they occurred, and why by identifying responsible targets including faulty agents, erroneous steps, and failure modes. Existing methods have primarily focused on developing dedicated models for specific attribution targets, with limited attention to the evidential dependencies among them. Despite these attribution targ…
items.sm: ASCon combines agent histories, interactions, and task constraints into shared representations for identifying responsible agents, erroneous steps, and failure types.

items.t: Semantic Intent & Authorization Protocol (SIAP): A Protocol Architecture and Reference Implementation for Task-Bound, Multi-Hop Agentic Authorization
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: SIAP proposes task-specific authorization across agent delegation chains, using semantic intent checks and dynamic capability filtering to govern tool execution.

items.t: Conversational Orchestration for Organic 6G
items.x: The Organic 6G vision of a network of networks spanning an edge-cloud continuum complemented by non-terrestrial resources requires, to realize its promise, service provisioning that is simple to operate, scalable across independently administered domains, and agile under domain churn (i.e., domains dynamically joining and leaving). Despite advances in cross-domain orchestration, many proposals rely on heavy integrati…
items.sm: Proposes decentralized 6G service orchestration in which autonomous domain agents inspect local conditions and exchange summaries with neighboring agents.

items.t: A Gateway Architecture for Enterprise MCP Authentication: Unifying Heterogeneous Auth, Identity Delegation, and the User / Non-User Persona Problem
items.a: Suraj Kumar, Amy Wang, Srinivasan Manoharan
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become the de-facto interface for connecting LLM agents to enterprise tools, and adoption has been explosive: within a year, large organizations went from zero to dozens of internally built MCP servers. That speed created a governance crisis. Each team implemented authentication independently -- some with no auth, some with API keys, some with full OAuth -- producing a fragmented …
items.sm: Describes a deployed enterprise MCP gateway that centralizes authentication and governance across servers with different authentication methods and human or automated callers.

items.t: Agentic Configuration Management (ACM): A Reference Configuration Model for Governed Agentic Systems
items.x: Agentic systems are increasingly composed of heterogeneous agents, prompts, tools, models, skills, composite subsystems, policies, and execution workflows whose configurations evolve across frameworks and runtime environments. Existing LLMOps and AgentOps platforms support orchestration and observability but do not provide a common configuration-governance model for representing and governing these systems as coheren…
items.sm: ACM defines a framework-independent model for governing agent configurations through versioned components, immutable baselines, dependency tracking, lifecycle rules, and runtime provenance.

items.t: fayzan123/rungraph
items.x: One command turns every agent session already on your disk into a graph: subagents, tool calls, retries, the moments you said no. Ask your agent what happened and the graph lights up the nodes it means. npx rungraph: no hooks, no setup, all local. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, opencode and Cursor.
items.sm: Rungraph turns locally stored agent sessions into interactive graphs showing subagents, tool calls, retries, and user interventions across several coding assistants.

items.t: Mind Viruses: Self-Propagating Ideas in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.sm: Demonstrates that ideas generated through evolutionary search can spread between agents in coding teams and interaction chains, with transmission influenced by model and network characteristics.

items.t: MoRSE: Task-Oriented Multi-Agent System with Mixture of Role-Subtask Experts
items.a: Peiwen Li, Shiyang Zhang, Yangtian Zhang, Sizhuang He, David van Dijk, Rex Ying
items.x: Large language model-based multi-agent systems have recently shown strong potential for complex, long-horizon tasks. However, existing methods mainly rely on coarse prompt-level differentiation without parameter adaptation for diverse subtasks, resulting in insufficient inter-agent heterogeneity and limited specialized capability that bottleneck performance on tasks with complex requirements. To address this, we intr…
items.sm: MoRSE decomposes tasks into dependency graphs and specializes agents by role and subtask through both task organization and model parameter adaptation.

items.t: The Politician, the Liar, and the Obedient Worker: Emerging Behavior of LLM Agents in Hierarchical Games
items.a: Fatemeh Seyedin, Adrian Weller, Jinhyuk Yun, Mahmoudreza Babaei
items.x: LLMs are rapidly embedding themselves into daily life: drafting our emails, managing our schedules, and making decisions on our behalf. As they move from individual tools to participants in multi-agent organizations, an important question arises: do they reproduce the governance failures like free-riding, corruption, and entrenched leadership that plague human institutions? We introduce the Hierarchical Game (HG), a …
items.sm: Studies six language models in hierarchical public goods games, finding distinct patterns of cooperation, deception, and responsiveness to managerial punishment.

items.t: FlowScout: From Execution Feedback to Reliable Tool-Using Agent Workflows
items.a: Shuo Hao, You Lu, Bihuan Chen, Xin Peng
items.x: Agentic workflows have become an important abstraction for building reliable LLM-based automation systems by organizing large language models (LLMs), tools, and control logic into explicit execution structures. However, constructing high-quality agentic workflows remains largely manual and requires substantial domain expertise. Recent studies have explored automatic agentic workflow generation from historical task-so…
items.sm: FlowScout uses execution feedback to generate workflows containing language model components and actual tool calls from historical task records.

items.t: Wisdom of LLM Crowds: Aggregation and Contamination in Language Model Ensembles
items.x: The wisdom of crowds—the finding that aggregating judgments across individuals often outperforms the best individual—has been extensively studied with human forecasters. Whether the same phenomenon emerges when the “crowd” consists of large language models (LLMs) is an open question with both theoretical and practical implications. We elicited probability estimates from 15 LLMs on 254 binary prediction market questio…
items.sm: Finds that learned combinations of probability estimates from 15 language models outperform individual models and classical aggregation methods on 254 prediction market questions.

items.t: Verifier-Mediated Debate for Controllable Question Synthesis over Knowledge Graphs
items.v: SOCIAL AND MANAGEMENT SCIENCES RESEARCH JOURNAL
items.sm: Uses debate between generative agents and deterministic verification against a knowledge graph to refine generated questions for semantic accuracy and structural alignment.

items.t: Entropy-based Code Adversarial Translation for Real-world Repository Migration
items.a: Yushun Tang, Yisen Cao, Zhicheng Chen, Lin Peng, Junkang Mao, Fengyi Song, Yantao Jia
items.x: LLMs have demonstrated strong capabilities in code generation and automated program repair, but migrating an entire repository rarely produces a runnable application because long-horizon translation challenges LLM-based agents' ability to maintain repository-level migration objectives. In this work, we propose Entropy-based Code Adversarial Translation (ECAT), a multi-agent framework for automated Android-to-HarmonyO…
items.sm: ECAT coordinates generator and discriminator agents to migrate Android repositories to HarmonyOS, using a code quality metric to guide iterative updates.

items.t: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem
items.x: AI agents increasingly work inside systems that govern how they delegate tasks, move information, execute actions, and use shared resources. Recent work already shows that deployment rules can change collective behavior. Here we ask which parts of an AI institution produce safety and how they do it. This is the first paper from POLIS, an ongoing research programme studying algorithmic institutions for multi-agent sys…
items.sm: Studies how institutional rules, authority checks, and fallback options affect safety in multi-agent workflows across a suite of 5,280 episodes.

items.t: AgentShield-Crypto: Zero-Trust Cryptographic Identity and Cascading Anomaly Firewalls for Autonomous Multi-Agent Trading Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes cryptographic agent identities and cascading anomaly firewalls to protect multi-agent trading systems against tampered context and attacks spreading between agents.

items.t: MCP Cache Poisoning: From Protocol to Exploitation
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Analyzes MCP cache poisoning vulnerabilities and describes an attack combining poisoned discovery responses with instruction injection to persist across users.

items.t: A Licensing and Accountability Layer for Inter-Agent Protocols - "Have your agent call my agent"
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Presents an accountability layer that links agents to verified human principals and checks revocable permissions before incoming payloads reach a model.

items.t: The CASE Framework: A Multi-Disciplinary Control Architecture for Governing Enterprise Agentic AI
items.a: Srinivas Telukunta, Georgios Nektarios Lilis, Lucio Baron
items.x: Enterprises are deploying autonomous AI agents faster than they can govern them, and prevailing approaches stretch a single discipline, typically DevSecOps built for deterministic automation, across every scale of agency. We argue that agentic AI governance is four problems, not one, each with a mature governing science. The CASE framework assigns Control theory to the individual agent (intent as setpoint, guardrails…
items.sm: CASE applies control theory, complex systems theory, supervisory cybernetics, and engineering operations to govern individual agents, agent collectives, human-agent teams, and fleets.

items.t: sami-mag07/ultimate-scraper-agent
items.x: Research skill and researcher subagent for Claude Code: multi-engine search behind one interface, parallel agent waves, and a verify gate that blocks any citation without a verbatim quote. No personal data; configured via .env.
items.sm: Provides a Claude Code research skill and subagent with multiple search engines, parallel research agents, and a citation gate requiring supporting verbatim quotations.

items.t: @theo: T3 Code has affected my productivity more than any model or tool in my life. I'm generating like 20% more code…
items.sm: Theo reports that T3 Code increased his code generation by about 20% and his merge volume tenfold, based on personal experience.

items.t: ForestBench: A Unified Graph Framework for Evaluating Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Guo Chen, Ziwen Li, Reed Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi, Bingbing Xu, Junjie Huang

items.t: RouteGuard: Certifying Routing Gain in LLM Multi-Agent Systems When Complementarity Is Not Enough
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems route among model-backed advisors, yet a deployer rarely knows before shipping whether routing will help at all. Prevailing routers optimize a gate's AUC and presume that advisor complementarity suffices. We show that neither determines the deployable gain. We introduce RouteGuard, a deployment-certification framework. Routing gain decomposes as $G = πΔ_E$, and the achievable gain is governed …
items.sm: RouteGuard provides statistical certificates for whether routing among language models improves performance, showing that model complementarity and router AUC alone cannot establish gains.

items.t: BEGIN AI TRANSACTION: Semantic Isolation for Durable AI Workflows

Meanwhile, prompts, model aliases, indexes, policies, and tools are deployed independently: stable names can acquire new behavior, and workflows can discover resources only after they start. The cache is replaced with deranged (mismatched-example), zeroed, and moment-matched random counterparts, under two regimes defined by whether the receiver needs the sender'…
