items.x: Simulated societies of large language model agents are used to study online polarization, and separately to study collective intelligence, but the two are rarely measured in the same system. It is therefore difficult to say whether a society's personality composition shapes both, or whether reducing polarization costs collective competence. We present TraitMix, an experimental design in which the Big Five composition…
items.sm: TraitMix studies how personality composition affects polarization and collective performance, finding that personality diversity increases opinion dispersion across simulated agent societies.

items.t: From Social Coding to Agentic Coding: Productivity and Relational Reconfiguration in Open-Source Communities
items.a: Mengying Zhou, Yongjie Yin, Yang Chen
items.x: Open-source software communities are a form of digital public infrastructure that not only produces code, but also generates public knowledge and interpersonal relationships through visible collaboration. Generative coding agents (CAs) are an advanced tool to improve development efficiency while shifting part of activities from public human interaction to private human-agent loops. We study this shift using an LLM-ba…
items.sm: Simulates open-source communities with and without coding agents, reporting more completed tasks and shorter completion times despite limited adoption.

items.t: Agents Catching Agents: Shortcut Cascades and Benchmark Gaming in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Sebastián Andrés Cajas Ordóñez, Agastya Munnangi, Aldo Marzullo, Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Quang Bui, Mohammad Shahin, Armaan Grewal, Emmanuel Paul Kwesiga
items.x: Clinical decision support is moving toward committees of language-model agents deliberating on a shared workspace. We ask whether such committees can be gamed by shortcuts, cues a benchmark rewards but a clinician would ignore. Across seven cohorts on six public datasets spanning text (MedQA-USMLE, MedMCQA, MIMIC-CXR reports), imaging (NIH ChestX-ray14, MIMIC-CXR-JPG, CheXpert) and tabular ICU records (SUPPORT2), Gem…
items.sm: Finds that clinical agent committees can adopt incorrect answers promoted by peers or system flags, while oversight agents face difficulties detecting this behavior.

items.t: When Truth Is Distributed: Misinformation Derails Collective Fact Recovery in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Chenfei Yan, Zeyang Yue, Feifei Zhao, Erliang Lin, Lu Jia, Haibo Tong, Mingyang Lyu, Chengyi Sun
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems promise effective collaborative reasoning, but communication may amplify local errors into collective risks, and while existing evaluations emphasize final outcomes, they leave the reliability and propagation dynamics of distributed information aggregation unclear, so we introduce ForesightSafety-TIDE, a controlled evaluation framework that strictly pairs all-honest collaboration with co…
items.sm: Evaluates distributed fact recovery in five-agent environments, finding that deception by a key evidence holder reduces accuracy from 72.50% to 14.17%.

items.t: Relational Priors as Convergence Pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Ming Shen, Chao Shang, Sadat Shahriar, Devang Kulshreshtha, Yi Zhang, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi
items.x: Large language model-based multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) are designed through roles, debate protocols, and aggregation rules. These choices create implicit expectations of trust, skepticism, deference, or collaboration. We make inter-agent relations explicit as signed pairwise priors, rendered in natural language and added to system prompts while keeping the task protocol fixed. Across commons governance and multi-ag…
items.sm: Tests explicit relationship assumptions between agents, finding that positive relationships encourage agreement and sustainable coordination but can reduce accuracy on objective questions.

items.t: CapChain: A Capability-Token Access Control Architecture with Verifiable Provenance for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Tuck Wai Choong, Wen‐Bin Hsieh, Jenq‐Shiou Leu

items.t: TruthLens: An Explainable Multi-Agent Framework for Hallucination Detection through Evidence-Based Verification in Large Language Models
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Existing individual evaluation methods, typically based on confidence or perplexity, fail to reflect the correctness of reasoning and may even exacerbate blind conformity. To address this, we shift the perspective from individual …
items.sm: DEAR aims to reduce blind conformity in multi-agent debate by measuring group agreement and disagreement and dynamically regulating how agents reference one another.

items.t: Adversarial Stress Testing of Role-Playing Language Agents using Multi-Agent Evaluation
items.a: Saqib Shouqi, Abdullah Nazly, Januki Wanniarachchi, Ravisha De Alwis
items.x: Role-Playing Language Agents (RPLAs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications such as healthcare assistance, customer support, and education, where maintaining consistent personas, ethical constraints, and behavioral coherence under adversarial pressure is critical. Existing evaluation approaches rely on static benchmarks or isolated single-turn prompts that fail to capture cumulative behavioral failures…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent platform that tests role-playing agents through adversarial dialogues and scores persona fidelity, behavioral drift, ethical deviations, and consistency.

items.t: Phase-Shifted Agentic Swarm (PSAS) Verification Data

items.sm: Documents 991 simulations examining personality composition, polarization, and collective intelligence, with additional validation checks and a ledger linking reported results to sources.

items.t: An Actionable Diagnosis of Multilingual, Multi-Agent Planning Failures

LLM-based analysis shows th…
items.sm: Classifies information losses when multilingual requests become agent plans and introduces TART to make essential planning requirements explicit across languages.

items.t: Selection-Invariant Communication Compilers for Privacy-Aware Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
items.a: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu
items.x: Structured multi-agent workflows exchange intermediate messages whose content and form can reveal private state even when the final output is safe. We identify selection-channel leakage: after authorization fixes what may be released, a private-state-aware choice among semantically valid realizations creates an additional inference channel. We introduce the selection-invariant communication compiler(SICC), which cons…
items.sm: Introduces a communication compiler that prevents message wording choices from leaking private information beyond authorized disclosures and proves a compositional privacy guarantee.

items.t: Governing Multi-Agent AI Systems in the Enterprise: Model Context Protocol and Agent-to-Agent Communication with MuleSoft Agent Fabric
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Examines enterprise agent governance using MuleSoft Agent Fabric, MCP, and A2A, reporting a 26.5% latency reduction from parallel agent execution.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.t: History Matters: Meta-policy Delegation with Heterogeneous Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Ziqing Lu, Avinash Reddy Mudireddy, Sarra Alqahtani, Weiyu Xu

In this paper, we consider collaborative systems composed of heterogeneous multi-agent systems (MAS), where their members have different capabilities and operating costs. We study how agents can delegate tasks to one another so that certain research tasks can be completed effectively under resource-constrained scenarios. …
items.sm: Develops reinforcement learning approaches for sequential task delegation among agents with different capabilities and costs, including prescribed communication structures and history-dependent policies.

items.t: CURATE: Leveraging LLM Agents to Compose, Catalog, and Deploy Reproducible Workflows
items.a: Nolan Cutler, Chia-Chen Kuo, Nanda Velugoti, Kathryn Newhart, Renato Figueiredo
items.x: Agentic code generation has the potential to accelerate the development of computational workflows while also reducing barriers to entry. However, a key gap remains: existing coding agents focus on code generation and do not address the entire workflow lifecycle, including deployment and sharing. As a result, users develop and stitch modules independently while managing deployment on their own. To address this gap, w…
items.sm: CURATE coordinates agents and human input to compose, catalog, reuse, deploy, and share computational workflow modules throughout their lifecycle.

items.t: Resume Means Resume: A Machine-Checked Conformance Contract for Checkpoint, Interrupt, and Resume Semantics in Workflow Persistence Layers
items.x: A framework that persists execution state so a run can be interrupted, survive a crash, and continue must decide what a resume means for effects that already happened. Five widely deployed agent workflow frameworks answer differently, none exposes a machine-checkable contract, and measured behavior violates even the fragments they state. The RESUME CONTRACT states six properties over the persistence API (prefix conti…
items.sm: Defines and formally verifies requirements for checkpointing, interruption, and resumption, including continuation, recovery determinism, and executing effects exactly once.

items.t: limenagent/prodagent

items.sm: The post recommends two articles to engineers, technology executives, models, and developers, and invites debate about rapid technological change.

items.t: Global Optimization and Inference-Time Region Grafting for Agentic Workflows
items.a: Donghyeok Koh, Gyuwan Kim, Jinyeong Bak, Seung-Hoon Na, Tao Yang, Haneol Jang, Cheoneum Park
items.x: Recent advances in agentic workflow optimization automate workflow design through task-specific workflow search or input-conditioned architecture selection. However, they determine the workflow before execution and cannot adapt failed workflow regions using execution-time label-free quality signals. Naively enabling such inference-time adaptation through whole-workflow re-optimization would be computationally prohibi…
items.sm: Introduces GRAFT, which adapts optimized agent workflows during execution by replacing selected regions using quality signals that require no labels.

items.t: Collective Reasoning, Single-Writer Execution: Fusion-MoA for Long-Horizon Agents
items.a: Zongyou Yang, Yinghan Hou, Botao Su, Ercheng Zhao
items.x: Mixture-of-Agents systems combine several language models into a stronger response, but tool-using agents act over long horizons in which every step changes external state and the history keeps growing. We present Fusion-MoA, a serving architecture that brings multi-model collaboration into this loop through executor-anchored consultation. One Executor model holds the full context and emits every text and tool call; …
items.sm: Introduces Fusion-MoA, where one executor retains full context and issues all actions while consulting specialist models about proposed next steps.

items.t: Emergence of Biased Consensus in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
items.x: Multi-agent LLM debates achieve strong performance on decision-making tasks as well as problem-solving benchmarks, yet their safety and fairness risks remain poorly understood. Notably, interaction can amplify the biases of single LLMs, raising concerns for real-world deployment. We identify the emergence of collective (often biased) norms in multi-agent LLM debates and show that noise (e.g., LLM sampling temperature…
items.sm: Models how conformity, initial biases, and sampling noise can produce biased consensus in language model debates, with controlled experiments supporting predicted transitions.

items.t: Microscopic dynamics of consensus formation in multi-agent LLM Naming Games
items.a: Cristiano De Nobili, Vijayasri Iyer, Alessandro Codello, Raffaella Burioni
items.x: Decentralized populations of Large Language Model (LLM) agents can spontaneously reach consensus on shared conventions, yet the microscopic mechanisms by which their internal stochasticity shapes macroscopic ordering remain unexplored. items.sm: Studies how stochastic language model responses shape consensus in naming games and derives an ordering condition from two interaction probabilities.

items.t: CockpitHAT: Dependency-Graph-Driven Hierarchical Attribution for Embodied Multi-Agent Cockpits
items.a: Wei Wang, Shuanghe Liu, Zhu Zhuo, Jiaqi Zhong, Xiaozhao Zhao, Xiaojie Zuo, Jie Su
items.x: LLM multi-agent systems suffer from Correctness Collapse, where high task-level accuracy conceals severe process-level failures. Existing attribution methods rely on text traces alone, missing dependency structure, multi-channel evidence, and safe…
items.sm: Introduces CockpitHAT to attribute failures in multi-agent automotive cockpits using dependency graphs, multiple evidence channels, and safety weighting, alongside an annotated benchmark.

items.t: MNC: Scope-Bound Semantic Declassification for Private LLM-Agent Communication
items.a: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems can expose protected state through internal messages, tool arguments, logs, and persistent memory even when their public outputs appear innocuous. items.sm: Introduces a communication protocol that limits agent disclosures to task needs and enforces recipient, purpose, forwarding, retention, logging, and memory restrictions.

items.t: Steganalysis of Adaptive Covert Collusion in Tool-Using Agent Populations: A Black-Box, Cross-Principal Approach
items.x: Tool-using agents built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed not by a single operator but by many, side by side on shared infrastructure. This creates a population-level risk that single-agent safeguards miss: a handful of agents can quietly coordinate, rigging a market, boosting one another in a review process, or timing a joint data grab, while each one looks perfectly well-behaved. The difficu…
items.sm: Proposes detecting covert coordination among independently operated agents using behavioral traces, statistical dependence, distribution changes, timing, and tool calls.

items.t: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance
items.a: Alireza Lotfi, Subangkar Karmaker Shanto, Imtiaz Karim, Elisa Bertino
items.x: Autonomous agents are increasingly used to execute consequential tasks in environments governed by operational constraints, organizational policies, regulatory requirements, and technical standards. items.sm: Introduces LACE, a multi-agent workflow translating instruction extension requests into RISC-V hardware edits and formal checks, reporting 72.8% first-attempt accuracy across four cores.

items.t: MasDrift: Benchmarking Authorization Preservation Across Multi-Agent Architectures

items.t: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems

items.t: You Don't Need To Stay in The Loop: An Agentic Robotics Loop for Robot-Policy Improvement

items.t: Humans Are More Diverse: Frontier LLMs Show Extreme Policies in Idealised AI Development Races

items.t: Where Reasoning Diverges: Localized Multi-Agent Debate for Multi-Hop Question Answering

items.x: Autonomous multi-agent systems (AMAS) built on large language models (LLMs), such as Hermes, increasingly rely on inference-time harnesses to coordinate reasoning and action. Constructing these harnesses requires substantial engineering effort and computational resources, as they are iteratively optimized over a combinatorial search space while co-evolving with the underlying LLM. Inference-time harnesses therefore c…

items.t: Auditing Emergent LLM-Agent Collaboration through Cooperation-Obligation Coupling
items.a: Zuyuan Zhang, Hanqing Yang, Carlee Joe‐Wong, Tian Lan
items.x: LLM-agent systems can solve complex tasks through dynamic self-organization and emergent cooperation. Auditing this process is essential because plausible intermediate or final outputs can conceal incomplete or unsupported work and poorly allocated responsibility, ultimately compromising response quality. While existing approaches may record messages, tool calls, provenance, or task dependencies, an auditability gap …
items.sm: Introduces an auditing representation linking agent interactions, outstanding work, responsibility assignments, and evidence supporting changes in work status.

items.t: Before Agents Speak: Pre-hoc Failure Risk Inference in Multi-Agent Systems

Existing countermeasures predominantly follow a post-hoc paradigm, identifying fail…
items.sm: Proposes estimating individual agent failures and system-wide hallucination propagation risks before agents communicate.

items.t: Two Calls Beat Five Agents: Evaluating Multi-Agent Pipelines Against Self-Refinement for Local Language Models
items.x: Multi-agent LLM pipeline systems break down the task among multiple roles for better reasoning, but are benchmarked mainly with large-scale commercial models. In this study, we investigate Parishad, a structured multi-agent system involving five roles, by deploying it on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a local model, on two datasets: GSM8K (500 questions) and HumanEval (164 questions), compared with prompting directly and two-c…
items.sm: Finds two-call self-refinement outperforms a five-agent pipeline on local-model mathematics tasks, while ungated refinement harms performance on an already strong coding baseline.

items.sm: Presents a framework for simulated strategy experiments with language-model agents, reproducing human exploration–exploitation patterns and generating hypotheses through parameter changes.

items.t: MCP vs CLI for AI Agents: A Comparative Analysis of Tool Integration Strategies for Autonomous Systems
items.a: Arun Malik, Nitish Talasu, Bradley Klemick, Vineet Tushar Trivedi, Prachi Shah, Sanay Devi, Junjie Zhang, Kunal Sonawane
items.x: AI agents require interfaces to interact with external systems such as files, APIs, databases, and cloud services. Two competing paradigms have emerged: CLI (Command Line Interface), where agents execute shell commands directly, and MCP (Model Context Protocol), a structured JSON-RPC protocol providing governed, typed tool access. This paper presents a comparative analysis across 14 evaluation dimensions, supported b…
items.sm: Compares CLI and MCP tool integration, arguing CLI suits local workflows while MCP better supports access control, credential isolation, auditing, and multi-tenant governance.

items.t: Separating intent from execution: A defense-in-depth security architecture for LLM-based multi-agent systems

items.t: Collusion with Competitive Marginals: Price-Level Audits Are Blind by Construction
items.a: Xin Xu, Chengrui Wu, Jiayu Lu, Kaizhen Tan, Siru Tao, Hanzhe Hong
items.x: Empirical work on algorithmic collusion asks one question of the data: are prices supracompetitive? We show this can be answered "no" by a conspiracy that is nonetheless profitable. Consider bidding agents that couple only through the joint distribution of their unexplained bid components, leaving every agent's own bid law exactly at the competitive law. Any test whose input is a single agent's price or bid history t…
items.sm: Shows that coordinated bidding can preserve each agent's competitive bid distribution while generating profits, making audits of individual price histories unable to detect collusion.

items.t: The Computable but Not Learnable Information-Value-Free Equilibria and Regulation of Algorithmic Collusion
items.a: Jason D. Hartline, Chang Wang, Chenhao Zhang
items.x: A correlated equilibrium is information-value-free if every player has an action that yields the same payoff as their equilibrium strategy when all other players follow their respective equilibrium strategies. An equilibrium is learnable if the empirical history of play generated by certain learning algorithms using only full feedback on each player's own payoff converges to it. Our main result is that although an in…
items.sm: Shows that information-value-free equilibria can be efficiently computed offline yet cannot be learned by a broad class of algorithms using individual payoff feedback.

items.t: MultiFixer: A Coordinator-Proposer Based Multi-Agent Framework For Fixing Multi-Hunk Bugs

items.x: Automated Program Repair (APR) has benefited greatly from Large Language Models (LLMs), but existing LLM-based APR methods still struggle with multi-hunk bugs that require coordinated changes across multiple locations. These bugs demand repository-level context understanding, repair-order scheduling, and effective hunk-level patch generation and selection. To address these challenges, we propose MultiFixer, a novel C…
items.sm: Introduces coordinated agents for repairing bugs across multiple code locations, reporting 326 fixes on Defects4J using contextual analysis, iterative patch generation, and refinement.

End-task performance alone also cannot reveal whether an observed effect depends on message presence, content generated for the evaluated example, or information suppl…
items.sm: Introduces controlled message replacements to test whether latent communication supplies task-relevant information that receiving agents actually use.

items.x: This paper investigates how multi-agent systems (MAS)-based on large language models (LLMs) can support actuarial risk modelling, with a particular focus on uncertainty quantification. Actuarial workflows represent a high-stakes decision-support setting where unreliable outputs may lead to incorrect risk assessment, unfair pricing, and regulatory non-compliance. To address uncertainty introduced by the probabilistic …

items.t: OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation

items.x: Complex tasks often decompose into parallelizable yet interdependent subtasks, making orchestration critical to the performance of multi-agent systems (MAS). An agent chooses between keeping an immediate local reward and paying a query cost to reveal a hidden safety fact that helps another…

We then couple this propagation model to an analytic majority-vote benchmark in which a c…

items.t: Dynamic Coalition Formation and Communication Pricing in Skill-Based Agentic AI Systems
items.x: Modern agentic AI systems combine multiple large language model agents with heterogeneous skills, yet most architectures either fix communication in advance or allow full broadcast. Both can be inefficient because token cost, latency, redundancy, and error propagation increase with the number of active agents and communication links. We model agent selection and communication as a cooperative game with task-condition…
items.sm: Models agent selection and communication costs to choose useful collaborators and connections through marginal contributions, routing rules, and estimated Shapley values.

items.t: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
items.a: Yan Yang, Xiangru Jian, Ziyang Luo, Zirui Zhao, Yutong Dai, Ziji Shi, Hanshu Yan, Jun Hao Liew
items.x: Computer-use agents are usually improved by strengthening perception: better models for reading a screenshot and choosing where to click. Yet a screenshot is only a lossy rendering of the underlying program state, e.g., the files, application backends, and DOM that hold the task data. items.t: LLM Agents Factory: Retrieval of Domain-Specific LLM Agents
items.a: Vitalii Belov, Artyom Sosedka, Andrey Sakhovskiy, Elizaveta Kovtun, Artyom Boyarskikh, Semen Budennyy
items.v: International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR)
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents improve task performance by decomposing problems into role-specialized behaviors. However, their practical deployment is often limited by the computational cost and instability associated with the on-the-fly agent design for each user request. To address this, we present LLM Agents Factory, a retrieval-based framework that constructs domain-specific and Wikipedia-grounded agents on d…
items.sm: Builds domain-specific agents from over 20,000 predefined profiles through retrieval or model distillation, reporting accuracy gains over baselines without specialized agents.

items.t: KV-PRM: Efficient Process Reward Modeling via KV-Cache Transfer for Multi-Agent Test-Time Scaling
items.a: Peng Kuang, Haibo Jin, Xiaoyu Han, Yanli Wang, Xiaopeng Yuan, Ye Yu, Kaidi Xu, Haohan Wang
items.x: Process Reward Models (PRMs) have been proven to be highly effective in guiding test-time scaling (TTS) methods, which significantly boost the capabilities of LLM-based multi-agent systems. However, existing PRMs are text-based: they re-encode the entire trajectory text from scratch. In long multi-agent rollouts, the scoring cost, growing quadratically with respect to sequence length L, creates a severe computational…
items.sm: Introduces a process reward model that reads existing attention caches instead of reprocessing trajectory text, reducing scoring complexity from quadratic to linear.

items.t: Agora: Enhancing LLM Agent Reasoning Via Auction-Based Task Allocation
items.a: Kaiji Zhou, Aleš Leonardis, Yue Feng
items.x: Enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents requires effective orchestration of diverse expert models and tools. However, existing frameworks typically call APIs, based on coarse-grained matching between tasks and the functions of expert models or tools, while overlooking critical factors such as performance variability and cost efficiency among functionally similar alternatives. To addr…
items.sm: Allocates reasoning tasks among expert models and tools through confidence-calibrated auctions, reporting competitive benchmark performance against single-model, routing, and cascade approaches.

items.t: Multi-Agentic Recommender Systems: Foundations, Perspectives, and Lessons from Large Scale Deployments in eCommerce

items.sm: Surveys multi-agent recommender systems, covering design patterns, e-commerce deployment lessons, and a project walkthrough from planning through monitoring.

items.t: Communication-Efficient Digital-Twin Coordination for Heterogeneous LLM Embodied Agents over Computing Power Networks
items.a: Nuocheng Yang, Sihua Wang, Zihan Chen, Tony Q. S. Quek, Changchuan Yin
items.x: Embodied agent teams powered by heterogeneous large language models (LLMs) are being widely deployed in physical artificial intelligence such as smart factories, warehouses, and service robotics. To enable collaboration among such an agent team, efficient coordination mechanisms that operate reliably under limited network resources are required. However, existing heterogeneous LLM-agent coordination frameworks that r…
items.sm: Proposes digital-twin coordination for heterogeneous embodied language model agents to address communication overhead, capability differences, and action delays under network constraints.

items.t: Bounded Rationality and Resilience in Global Rare Earth Supply Chains: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Simulation
items.a: Junjie liang, Ligang Xu, Weifeng Wang, Mengtao Song, Siming Wei

items.v: International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR)
items.sm: Uses reinforcement learning to select participating agents dynamically in social simulations, reporting lower computational costs while preserving social interaction intensity.

items.t: Not Just One Agent: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Medicine from Answer Generation to Accountable Workflow Orchestration

items.sm: Reviews medical multi-agent systems across clinical and administrative applications, synthesizing approaches to coordination, evidence integration, privacy, and accountable workflows.

items.t: L-MAD: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Debate Structures in Legal Reasoning
items.a: Tan-Minh Nguyen, Hoang-Trung Nguyen, Huu-Dong Nguyen, Dinh-Truong Do, Thi-Hai-Yen Vuong, Le-Minh Nguyen
items.x: While multi-agent debate (MAD) frameworks have shown significant potential in general reasoning, their effectiveness in highly structured, knowledge-heavy legal domains remains under-explored. In this work, we introduce the Legal Multi-Agent Debate (L-MAD) framework to systematically evaluate different debate structures and aggregation methods within Legal Textual Entailment. By assigning distinct expert personas to …
items.sm: L-MAD evaluates legal reasoning debates, reporting accuracy gains from more agents but worsening errors when discussions run longer.

items.t: Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration for Unit Test Generation via Human-Testing-Inspired Workflows
items.a: Quanjun Zhang, Ye Shang, Siqi Gu, Jianyi Zhou, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen, Liang Xiao
items.x: Recently, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has spurred a surge of research into automated unit test generation, yielding impressive performance and reducing manual effort. However, existing LLM-based approaches still suffer from two major limitations: (1) they follow rigid, procedural workflows that underutilize the autonomous reasoning potential of LLMs, making it difficult to dynamically adapt testing …
items.sm: TestAgent coordinates language model agents to generate unit tests using workflows inspired by human testing practices and feedback.

items.t: Fictional Worldbuilding: Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration with Hierarchical Context Compression and Iterative Review
items.a: Jingbo Chen, He Wang, Wei Yuan, Yuqiao Lai, Zhenyan Lu
items.x: Worldbuilding, the construction of coherent fictional worlds, is a foundational task in game design and literary creation. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new possibilities for automated content generation, but their application to worldbuilding faces three challenges: context explosion that grows linearly with the building process, the tension between creative diversity and content consistency, and the absence of…
items.sm: AutoWorldBuilder coordinates agents to create consistent fictional worlds using conflict detection, task scheduling, context compression, and iterative review.

items.t: Multi-Swarm Agency Protocol: Emergent Coordination in Heterogeneous Agent Networks. (50 pages)
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.t: ProofCouncil: An LLM Agent for Solving Open Mathematical Problems
items.a: Johannes Schmitt, Tim Gehrunger, Jasper Dekoninck, Gergely Bérczi, Uri Kreitner, Liam Price, David Holmes
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in solving open problems in mathematics. However, their performance can be further improved through agentic workflows tailored to real-world mathematical practice. To this end, we introduce ProofCouncil, a mathematical agent that is designed to tackle open problems using an author-critic architecture. ProofCouncil served as a submission to the second batch of…
items.sm: ProofCouncil uses an author and critic workflow to solve mathematical problems, with six of ten competition submissions judged correct subject to minor revisions.

items.t: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
items.x: Modern LLM-agent frameworks increasingly interoperate through standards such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) for agent-to-tool access and Google's Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol for agent delegation and negotiation. However, these protocols specify transport and discovery rather than strategic correctness and do not guarantee efficient, individually rational, or strategy-proof outcomes. We introduce a framewo…
items.sm: Introduces negotiation constraints, runtime checks, and benchmark tasks to evaluate whether interacting language model agents follow game theory principles.

items.t: Project Nightcord Sanctuary: A Closed-World Multi-Agent Framework for Studying Persona Drift and Correction in LLM Roleplay Agents
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Project Nightcord Sanctuary uses paired fictional characters to distinguish roleplay agents' resistance to persona drift from their ability to recover after correction.

items.t: Mosaic: Runtime-Efficient Multi-Agent Embodied Planning
items.a: Kunjal Panchal, Saayan Mitra, Sunav Choudhary, Victor Bursztyn, Somdeb Sarkhel, Hui Guan
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent embodied planning remains impractical due to prohibitively high execution latency. We identify failed actions as the dominant bottleneck, stemming from two core challenges: inaccurate state tracking under partial observability and inefficient coordination that produces redundant or conflicting actions. We introduce Mosaic, a runtime-efficient multi-agent planning framework that addresses both ch…
items.sm: Mosaic combines spatial memory with constrained action allocation to reduce failed actions and speed up embodied planning across multiple agents.

items.t: HAMAgent: human assisted multiagent system for emotion recognition and digital health—a survey and preliminary study

items.sm: HAMAgent surveys digital health agent systems and explores how human feedback affects collaborative language models' reasoning about emotions and behavior.

items.t: Eluna: An Agentic LLM System for Automating Warehouse Operations with Reasoning and Task Execution
items.a: Ning Liu, P Aditya Sreekar, Kalle Kujanpää, Zhaoxuan Zhu, Kaiwen Liu, Chuanneng Sun, Jorge Marchena Menendez, Matthew Bales
items.x: Warehouse operations are governed by Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that encode complex, multi-system decision logic, which must be executed reliably under strict time constraints, yet LLM agents lack mechanisms to enforce procedural compliance and degrade under the context overload full SOP specifications introduce. We present Eluna, a production-deployed agentic system for reliable SOP execution. Eluna is a g…
items.sm: Eluna automates warehouse procedures using graph-guided workflows, parallel agents, and training that transfers corrected execution examples from a stronger model to a smaller one.

items.t: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
items.a: Yifan Wu, Lizhu Zhang, Yuhang Zhou, M.-Z. Wang, Peng Bo, Serena Li, Xiangjun Fan, Zhuokai Zhao
items.x: In long-horizon tasks, decision-relevant state is often scattered across an expanding trajectory, while the action agent must surface it and act. As trajectories grow, task requirements, environment facts, prior attempts, diagnoses, and open subgoals can be buried in the context window or pushed beyond it, failing to influence decisions when needed. We call this failure mode "behavioral state decay". We study memory …
items.sm: Adds a separate memory agent that selectively reminds an action agent of relevant information, improving success rates on long-running task benchmarks.

items.t: Before You Build a Multi-Agent System: An Escalation Framework for LLM Adaptation
items.a: Junhyeong Lee, Joon-Young Kim, Seunghwa Ryu
items.sm: Proposes a framework for choosing among input changes, parameter updates, and orchestration as language model adaptation strategies with increasing complexity and cost.

items.t: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
items.a: Xiaoshuai Song, Liancheng Zhang, Kangzhi Zhao, Yutao Zhu, Zhongyuan Wang, Guanting Dong, Jinghan Yang, Han Li
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based web search agents are transforming information seeking from simple factoid question answering into complex, deep-and-wide search and research-oriented tasks. A single ReAct-style agent is constrained by one long trajectory and limited context, making it difficult to handle depth and coverage simultaneously. Existing multi-agent systems improve search coverage through parallel executio…
items.sm: WebSwarm recursively delegates web research tasks, dynamically organizing search agents to expand coverage and investigate topics in greater depth.

items.t: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
items.a: Eugene Ng Yi Sheng, Bingquan Shen
items.x: Self-interested agents, left unconstrained, tend toward defection in repeated social dilemmas, causing cooperative gains from trade to collapse. This paper investigates what formal mechanisms, layered on top of unrestricted communication, are sufficient for a society of such agents to maintain market stability, and how resilient those mechanisms are to adversarial attack. We instantiate the research question as a mul…
items.sm: Tests mechanisms for maintaining trade among self-interested language model agents, identifying mediation as the strongest evaluated approach before examining adversarial attacks.

items.sm: Describes Bun’s migration to Rust to reduce memory errors, emphasizing reusable tests, adversarial review, and human adjustments to the code generation process.

items.sm: Reports a review grouping language model agent limitations into six failure categories and argues that benchmark gains can obscure persistent reliability problems.

items.t: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
items.x: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (e.g. GRPO) is the engine behind today's reasoning models, yet it grades only the final answer. On hard problems this trains models to write more rather than to think better, since the trace itself is never graded and no label for good thinking exists. We introduce Agon, which makes two competing models each other's graders. Both attempt the same problem; in alternating …
items.sm: Introduces competitive training where two models alternate solving problems and reviewing rival solutions, implicitly rewarding reasoning without process labels or a reward model.

items.t: Cognitive Cells: A Compositional Framework for Populations of Small Language Models
items.x: Recent work on large language models and agentic systems raises a basic question that current practice leaves open: how should artificial cognition be decomposed, measured, and composed? We propose studying multi-agent systems from a fixed unit we call a cognitive cell: a small, frozen language model with bounded memory and a message interface. The methodological commitment, the fixed-cell principle, is to hold this …
items.sm: Proposes studying groups of fixed small language models by varying population size, communication structure, message bandwidth, and coordination while holding individual capabilities constant.

items.t: Agent Delivery Engineering Predictive Reliability Framework
items.x: Long-horizon LLM multi-agent systems face reliability risks invisible to infrastructure monitoring. We propose the ADE Predictive Reliability Framework (ADE-PRF), enabling proactive health trajectory prediction from passive degradation detection. ADE-PRF aggregates 20 heterogeneous signals across five layers into a Trust Margin (TM) metric (39.2-point dynamic range). Triple-method parallel prediction enables 8-hour f…
items.sm: Combines twenty signals into a reliability metric to forecast multi-agent system degradation eight hours ahead, including problems hidden by normal operational metrics.

items.t: The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI
items.a: Muayad Sayed Ali, Aliaksandra Novik, Anji Boddupally, Artem Yavorskyi, Chris Nickerson, Daniel Rica, Emily DuGranrut, Felix Leung
items.x: Agentic AI development today runs on token maxing: buying capability with tokens -- longer reasoning traces, more turns, wider tool payloads, bigger replayed contexts -- so tokens per task grow faster than task value. Falling per-token prices mask the pattern; total spend rises anyway. We argue the decisive lever against token maxing is the harness: the orchestration layer that assembles context, exposes tools, seque…
items.sm: Reports that changing agent orchestration while keeping models fixed reduced task costs by 41% and median completion time by 44% across controlled evaluations.

items.t: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable reasoning capabilities, yet their stateless architecture fundamentally limits deployment in long-horizon research workflows requiring multi-session continuity and quantitative rigor. Here we present Ensemble QSP, a multi-agent framework featuring a three-layer hierarchical memory architecture that bounds injected context (median 301 tokens, max 4,050) by capping sta…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent computational modeling framework using hierarchical memory to limit context growth and support sustained pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic research workflows.

items.t: The Model Context Protocol and Enterprise Tool Orchestration: Architectural Patterns for Connecting AI Agents to Production Systems at Scale
items.v: International Journal of Computational and Experimental Science and Engineering
items.sm: Examines enterprise MCP deployment patterns for connecting agents to production tools while addressing permission enforcement, execution risk, and audit requirements.

items.t: Who Broke the System? Failure Localization in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yufei Xia, Anjun Gao, Yueyang Quan, Zhuqing Liu, Minghong Fang
items.x: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems enable complex problem solving through coordinated reasoning and action, but their distributed structure also introduces new challenges in diagnosing system-level failures. When an execution fails, identifying which agent is responsible and at what point the trajectory first becomes irreversibly misdirected is difficult due to long-horizon interactions and tightly …
items.sm: Introduces AgentLocate to identify the responsible agent and earliest decisive failure step using language model judgments, independent verification, and confidence-based aggregation.

items.t: Simulating Quiet Quitting: A Computational Experiment on Crisis Management Strategies using Generative Agents
items.a: Rui Hong, Feng Yao, Peijun Ye, Tao Wang, Z D Zhang
items.sm: Simulates employee disengagement under workplace pressure and reports that commitment-focused management reduces simulated turnover intentions, with responses varying by personality.

items.t: CityReal: Human-Aligned Urban Behavior and City Dynamics Simulation with Large-Scale LLM Agents
items.a: Nicolas Bougie, Xiaotong Ye, Narimasa Watanabe
items.x: Large-scale urban simulation plays a pivotal role in social science, traffic safety, and transportation policy. Recent work has shown that large language models, when prompted as agents, can generate lifelike daily routines at city scale. Yet these methods typically rely on few-shot prompting, causing agents to reproduce the LLM's behavioral priors rather than the target population. We introduce CityReal, a modular f…
items.sm: Introduces CityReal to simulate urban activity through intention-driven agents that learn habits and use textual adapters to match observed population behavior.

items.t: Operational Reframing and Approval-Framed Delegation in Multi-Agent LLM Safety
items.a: Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Xiaochong Jiang, Su Wang, Pin Qian, Yihang Chen
items.x: Safety evaluations of multi-agent LLM systems often compare a direct prompt with a planner-executor pipeline and report the difference as a single "pipeline effect." We argue that this aggregate is difficult to interpret because it conflates three mechanisms: harmful intent may be reframed as plausible operational work, the planner may refuse or transform the request, and the executor may act under delegation prompts…
items.sm: Separates operational reframing, planner behavior, and implied approval in multi-agent safety evaluations, finding that operational reframing increases harmful compliance across several models.

items.t: Think Big, Search Small: Where Capacity Matters in Hierarchical Search Agents?
items.a: Qinnan Cai, Yibo Zhao, Xiang Li
items.x: Large language model based search agents increasingly adopt multi-agent architectures in which a main agent decomposes a complex question into sub-queries and dispatches them to parallel sub-agents. However, existing systems instantiate all roles from a single model of identical scale, leaving open how model capacity should be distributed across roles. We factorize hierarchical search into three roles: a delegation r…
items.sm: Studies how model capacity should be distributed between delegation and retrieval roles in hierarchical search, reporting improvements over single-agent baselines.

items.t: Mitigating Taint-Style Vulnerabilities in MCP Servers via Security-Aware Tool Descriptions
items.a: Yang Shi, Jiaheng Fu, Yihe Huang, Ruixiang Wu, Chengyao Sun, Kaifeng Huang
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that interact with external tools and services via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), a standardized interface for dynamic tool invocation. While MCP simplifies integration, it also expands the attack surface and enables generic exploits across multiple servers. Despite prior work on malicious MCP servers, the vulnerability landscape of MCP se…
items.sm: Analyzes MCP server vulnerabilities and proposes security-aware tool descriptions to mitigate risks involving unsafe flows of external data into sensitive operations.

items.t: smaramwbc/statewave-multi-agent-shared-context

items.t: Safe and Scalable Collaboration in Multiagent LLM Systems: A Comprehensive Review

items.sm: Reviews coordination, communication, safety, and alignment in multi-agent language model systems and proposes a layered approach to trust.

items.t: LLM Agents for Deliberative Collaboration: A Study on Joint Decision Making Under Partial Observability
items.a: Chenxu Wang, Yongkun Yang, Boyuan Du, Shiwei Lin, Huaping Liu
items.x: Deliberation plays a crucial role in collaboration; when humans work together, they naturally engage in communication to align information and reach an agreement. In this paper, we investigate deliberative large language model (LLM) agents under partially observable joint decision-making tasks. We formalize deliberative collaboration as a cooperative joint decision problem with partial and asymmetric observations, an…
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark for agents sharing incomplete, asymmetric information to reach joint decisions, finding that complex deliberation remains difficult for evaluated models.

items.t: When Agents Go Rogue: Activation-Based Detection of Malicious Behaviors in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Haowen Xu, Xue Tan, Lei Ma, Zhihao Zhang, Chao Wang, Qingze Wang, Ping Chen, Jun Dai
items.x: While enabling effective collaboration on complex tasks, LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) face critical security challenges due to vulnerabilities at the agent and interaction levels. Most existing MAS security defenses are built upon two core assumptions: semantically-explicit malicious attacks and explicit graph-based modeling of the MAS topology and agent-level interactions. In practice, real-world attacks are …
items.sm: Introduces AcMAS to detect malicious multi-agent behavior from agents’ internal activations without explicit interaction graphs or synchronized execution.

items.t: Simulation of language evolution under regulated social media platforms: a synergistic approach of large language models and genetic algorithms
items.a: Jinyu Cai, Mingyue Zhang, Yusei Ishimizu, Munan Li, Jialong Li, Kenji Tei
items.x: Abstract Social media platforms frequently impose restrictive policies to moderate user content, prompting the emergence of creative evasion language strategies. This paper presents a multi-agent framework based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to simulate the iterative evolution of language strategies under regulatory constraints. In this framework, participant agents, as social media users, continuously evolve their…
items.sm: Combines language model agents and genetic algorithms to simulate how users evolve language strategies to evade platform moderation.

items.t: StateFuse: Deterministic Conflict-Preserving Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Sergey Volkov, Yang Li, Ye Luo
items.x: Agent systems accumulate conflicting observations across branches, retries, and replicas, yet many practical memory layers still collapse disagreement behind overwrite rules that are difficult to inspect or correct. We present StateFuse, a conflict-aware replicated memory contract built on standard OpSet/CRDT merge. StateFuse does not introduce a new join algebra; it defines an agent-facing semantics layer with immut…
items.sm: Introduces replicated agent memory that preserves conflicting claims and immutable history while supporting explicit corrections and deterministic resolution when reading stored information.

items.t: From Blueprint to Reality: Modeling and Applying Putnam's Social Capital Theory with LLM-based Multi-agent Simulations
items.a: Shiyi Ling, Zhi Zheng, Hui Zheng, Wenjun Xue, Feng Ye, Tong Xu
items.x: Putnam's Social Capital Theory is a foundational framework for collective action and community prosperity. However, traditional empirical methods face practical limits on control and replication. Meanwhile, LLM-based social simulations are typically behavior-driven and lack theory-aligned environments for modeling Putnam's core propositions. To address these gaps, we introduce SocaSim, an LLM-based multi-agent simula…
items.sm: Introduces SocaSim to model social capital through evolving networks, trust, and norms, then applies simulated collective action to elderly care challenges.

items.t: Norm Enforcement for AI Agents: Robustly Shaping Behavior in Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: AI agents are increasingly deployed in shared environments where they pursue diverse goals and compete for rewards. This multi-agent competition can lead to behaviors that serve individual gains at collective cost -- for instance, marketing agents may post misleading content as a result of competing for engagement on social media. Human societies address such problems through norms that constrain acceptable behavior,…
items.sm: Finds that competing agents exploit simple norm enforcement and investigates stronger mechanisms that track each agent’s reliability over time.

items.t: Information Limits and Attractor Dynamics in Economies of Frontier LLM Agents: A Pre-Registered Test
items.x: We report a pre-registered, two-part experiment on small economies of frontier language-model agents (Claude Opus 4.8), testing two quantitative predictions about coupled multi-agent systems: an information-theoretic capacity region for wealth growth under market coupling, and a mean-field residual-scaling law for population misalignment under incentive and control levers. All predictions, acceptance bands, and decis…
items.sm: Reports preregistered experiments in simulated agent economies, finding that relative wealth growth matches relative claimed information within a specified tolerance.

items.t: How Much Does Correctness Cost? Budgeted Placement of Strong Correctors in a Weak Multi-Agent Swarm
items.x: A cheap swarm of unreliable agents can be steered to a correct consensus by a few strong, expensive "oracle" correctors. We ask how much one must spend, and where to place the oracles. We model the swarm as a consensus on a graph in which each oracle pins one node toward the truth at a cost-coupled, concave strength, and measure quality by the coherence H(R)=tr M(R)^{-1}. Our first result is that H stays submodular (…

Whether one model can actually run such a team is largely unmeasured: existing benchmarks score a policy's own task-solving or a fixed multi-agent system's emergen…
items.sm: ClawArena-Team benchmarks a lead model's ability to delegate tasks and manage asynchronous subagents across changing scenarios with restricted access to information.

While traditional learning-based code translation methods have limited effectiveness due to the lack of sufficient parallel training data, Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently advanced this field with their strong code generation and comprehension capabilities…
items.sm: TransAgent uses multiple agents and detailed comparisons of source and translated code execution to locate and correct translation errors.

items.x: The fast growth of open-source AI infrastructure, from model serving engines and agent platforms to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ecosystem and the language models themselves, has outpaced the security tooling available to defend it. We present AI-Infra-Guard, an open-source framework that organizes AI red teaming around a single observation: the attack surface of an AI agent is stratified across layers (infrastru…
items.sm: AI-Infra-Guard combines vulnerability rules, automated audits, agent attack simulations, and jailbreak testing to assess security across infrastructure, tools, agent behavior, and models.

Failure attribution in MASs, i.e., to pinpoint the specific agent actions responsible for failures, is underexplored and labor-intensive, posing significant challenges for debugging and improvi…

items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly used to automate complex, distributed workflows. However, their inter-agent communication channels introduce new attack surfaces that remain poorly understood and are difficult to defend against. In this paper, we address how defenders should prioritize limited security effort to protect vulnerable communication channels before attacks are observed. This is motivated by our …
items.sm: MESA ranks communication channels by their likely security impact using network structure and behavioral probes, helping defenders prioritize protection without observed attack data.

items.t: Investigating Multi-Agent Deliberation in Law
items.a: Cor Steging, Ludi van Leeuwen, Tadeusz Zbiegień
items.x: Artificial Intelligence is increasingly applied to the field of law, and has the potential to increase access to justice. One particular movement that is gaining traction is that of agentic AI, wherein AI agents, based on Large Language Models (LLMs) can take autonomous actions. In particular, multi-agent approaches in the legal domain remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we investigate multi-agent deliberation …
items.sm: Evaluates multi-agent legal deliberation, including courtroom-inspired approaches, finding overall performance comparable to baseline models but different answers and some complementary successes.

items.t: Linguistic Firewall: Geometry as Defense in Multi-Agent Systems Routing
items.a: Dvir Alsheich, Adar Peleg, Ben Hagag, Rom Himelstein, Amit Levi, Avi Mendelson
items.x: The rapid integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven the evolution of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), where specialized agents collaborate to execute complex workflows. Effective orchestration in these environments requires robust routing mechanisms to efficiently allocate tasks to the most suitable agent. However, existing routers fundamentally rely on unverified proxies, ranging from textual self-description…
items.sm: Proposes a routing defense addressing malicious agents that misrepresent their capabilities or conceal backdoors from existing assessment methods.

items.t: ATM: CID-Brokered Pre-Write Admission for Multi-Agent Code Co-Synthesis
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems can decompose software-engineering work into planning, generation, validation, and repair, but a narrower systems problem remains: before any governed shared mutation is applied, a system must decide which concurrently formed write intents may proceed in parallel, which require deterministic composition or serialization, and which must take a fail-closed path. We address this problem with the …
items.sm: Introduces ATM to govern concurrent software-agent changes by deciding which writes can proceed together, require coordination, or must be blocked.

items.t: A Systematic Approach to Multi-Agent AI from Advanced Regulatory Control Theory: Safe and Auditable LLM Operator Agents for Process Control
items.a: Idelfonso B. R. Nogueira, Sigurd Skogestad
items.x: Recent literature shows that large language models (LLMs) are useful for general-purpose tasks yet perform poorly on specific domain ones. One reason is the difficulty of supplying narrow context to a general-purpose model and of bounding the task it is asked to perform. It is possible to hypothesise that a multi-agent reformulation under process-control principles offers a route to address those points, since contro…
items.sm: Proposes organizing specialized language model agents around process-control feedback loops to constrain responsibilities and resolve conflicts through structural priorities.

items.t: The Illusion of Agentic Complexity in README.md Generation: Evaluating Single-Agent vs. Multi-Agent RAG Systems

While Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are often adopted to support such tasks under the premise that task decomposition improves performance, the impact of architectural complexity on practical efficiency remains …
items.sm: Compares single-agent, specialized multi-agent, and developer-guided retrieval workflows for generating repository README files, examining architectural complexity and efficiency.

items.a: Jiabin Lou, Haopeng Wang, Xinyu Liu, Yu Zhang, Rongye Shi, Wenjun Wu
items.x: Integrating large language models into robotic systems holds promise for enhancing autonomy, yet practical deployment remains constrained by strict heartbeat-constrained scheduling and limited computational power. We propose AERIS: an edge deployment framework for aerial platforms. It organizes dedicated small language models combined with lightweight perception and control modules into roles that can be instantiated…
items.sm: Introduces an aerial edge framework that assigns small language models specialized roles and reallocates execution as resources change during drone navigation.

items.t: The Organizational Behavior of Agentic AI: Collective Intelligence in Human-Agent Workflows
items.x: Agentic artificial intelligence is increasingly deployed not as a single assistant but as a collective of planners, solvers, reviewers, memory managers, tool users, and orchestrators. These systems are entering organisational workflows under familiar labels such as teams, managers, committees, markets, and workflows. This article asks whether such agent collectives exhibit organisational behaviour in a sense that is …
items.sm: Argues that AI agent collectives resemble human organizations through coordinated work but differ in the mechanisms sustaining their behavior and accountability.

items.t: AgRefactor: Self-Evolving Agentic Workflow for HLS Compatibility and Performance
items.a: Yang Zou, Zijian Ding, Yizhou Sun, Jason Cong
items.x: High-Level Synthesis (HLS) provides a fast path from concepts to silicon, but converting real-world software into synthesizable HLS code remains challenging due to restrictive language support and the gap between software and hardware programming practices. Existing automated and LLM-based refactoring approaches partially address this problem, yet they often lack flexibility, struggle to scale, and incur high computa…
items.sm: Introduces a multi-agent workflow combining reusable memory and automated refactoring tools to convert software into programs compatible with high-level synthesis.

items.t: Why Solve It Twice? Hierarchical Accumulation of Skills for Transfer-Efficient ML Engineering
items.a: Yongbin Kim, Yashar Talebirad, Osmar R. Zaiane
items.x: ML engineering agents waste compute rediscovering known techniques because every competition is a cold start. We present HASTE, a hierarchical multi-agent system that organizes cross-competition knowledge into three scope tiers (global, domain, and competition-specific), each coupled to a matching agent level. An orchestrator coordinates domain specialists and promotes learning between tiers via LLM-driven abstractio…
items.sm: Introduces a hierarchical engineering agent system that organizes reusable skills by scope, reporting higher competition medal rates than loading all skills together.

items.a: Jordan Augé, Giovanna Carofiglio, Giulio Grassi, Jacques Samain
items.x: The rapid emergence of LLM-based agentic frameworks has significantly reduced the cost of assembling multi-agent systems (MAS), enabling fast prototyping and exploration of agentic behaviors. However, systems built with current tooling remain ill-suited for reliable, evolvable, and production-grade deployment. In practice, MAS are often developed in an ad-hoc and imperative manner, with agent logic, orchestration, ob…
items.sm: Introduces a specification-driven framework for developing multi-agent systems and experimentally validating their properties to support reliable operation.

items.t: MCP Server Architecture Patterns for LLM-Integrated Applications
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP), introduced by Anthropic in November 2024, defines a standardized interface for connecting large language models (LLMs) to external tools, data sources, and services. Within months of release, hundreds of community-built MCP servers appeared on GitHub, but no software-maintenance literature has yet described how the ecosystem is being structured in production. This industry experience…
items.sm: Catalogues five recurring MCP server architecture patterns observed across fifteen servers, describing their contexts, problems, and solutions.

We propose Mixture of Debaters (MoD), a unified framework that enables dynamic self-debate within a single model by leveraging the Mixture-…

items.a: Mengdie Flora Wang, Haochen Xie, Guanghui Wang, Devin Zhang, Jae Oh Woo
items.x: Multi-agent deliberation among LLMs can improve reasoning, but deployment requires deciding when the current answer is reliable enough to act on and when it should be escalated to human review. We formulate this as budgeted act-or-defer decision making. At each round, the system maps the debate prefix to a low-dimensional state, computes a $k$-nearest-neighbor lower confidence bound on state-conditional correctness u…
items.sm: Proposes a budgeted deliberation method that uses calibrated local reliability estimates to decide whether agents should act or defer to human review.

items.t: Persona-Trained Monte Carlo: Estimating Market-Outcome Distributions via Swarms of Persona-Conditioned Neural Policy Bots in a Limit Order Book
items.x: We propose Persona-Trained Monte Carlo (PTMC), a method for estimating distributions of market-outcome statistics by repeatedly simulating limit-order-book interaction among swarms of persona-conditioned neural-policy trading bots. Each run instantiates many bots sharing one trained policy network but conditioned on heterogeneous, individually sampled persona parameters drawn from a learned trader-heterogeneity distr…
items.sm: Proposes estimating market outcome distributions through repeated order-book simulations involving trading bots with shared neural policies and varied persona parameters.

items.t: Minority Sentinel: When to Overturn Majority Voting in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
items.a: Chuan He, Zebin Chen, Zhengyi Yang, Shaobo Qiao, Mingchen Ju, Jiate Liu, Dong Wen, Guanfeng Liu
items.x: Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) with Majority Voting is a dominant paradigm for improving LLM reasoning, yet its effectiveness rests on the Condorcet Jury Theorem's assumption of independent errors. Because contemporary LLMs share similar pretraining corpora, their errors are strongly correlated, causing the majority to systematically suppress correct minority opinions, a phenomenon we term Minority Truth. Through debates a…
items.sm: Introduces a classifier that identifies when minority answers should override majority votes in language model debates, reporting 81.2% precision for those reversals.

items.t: When LLMs Develop Languages: Symbolic Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Zhengqi Pei, Qingming Huang, Shuhui Wang
items.x: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) improves large language models (LLMs) on difficult reasoning tasks, but it often incurs long natural-language rationales that are poorly aligned with efficient machine reasoning. We propose Communicative Language Symbolism Routing (CLSR), a test-time framework in which multiple LLM agents autonomously invent, evolve, and share compact Language Symbolism Frameworks (LSFs), while a latent-free ro…
items.sm: Proposes agents that develop reusable symbolic communication protocols and a router that selects them to balance reasoning accuracy against token use.

items.t: From Naive RAG to Deep Agentic Retrieval: An Evolving Context Engineering Pipeline for Regulatory Compliance
items.a: Mishca de Costa, Muhammad Saleh Anwar, Dave Mercier, Issam Hammad
items.x: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is the dominant paradigm for applying large language models (LLMs) to enterprise document corpora, yet naive implementations encounter hard limits as corpus scale and query complexity grow. This paper traces the evolution of a production retrieval pipeline at Ontario Power Generation (OPG) for regulatory compliance and rate case analysis under Ontario Energy Board (OEB) reporting …
items.sm: Traces a regulatory compliance retrieval pipeline's evolution toward multi-agent retrieval, proposing escalation from inexpensive searches to deeper evidence gathering as needed.

items.t: PolicyGuard: A Dialogue-Grounded Sub-Agent Verifier for Policy Adherence in LLM Agents
items.a: Seongjae Kang, Taehyung Yu, Sung Ju Hwang

Prior work approaches this as a safeguarding problem -- external checks that block non-compliant agent actions. We argue that policy adherence is broader: real workflows unfold across many turns, require explicit user confirmation and prerequisite reads, and hinge on dialo…
items.sm: Introduces a verifier that checks dialogue context for policy compliance and recommends corrections, reporting improved repeated-task success across three model families.

items.t: Preventing Error Propagation in Multi-Agent AI through Runtime Monitoring
items.a: Shahnewaz Karim Sakib, Anindya Bijoy Das
items.x: Multi-agent AI systems can improve answer selection by allowing different language models to exchange reasoning traces, revise initial predictions, and support a final decision. However, such communication may also introduce reliability risks: reasoning from one agent can correct another agent's mistake, but it can also mislead an agent that was initially correct. This paper studies reliable multi-agent AI communicat…

items.t: The Contagion Tensor: A Framework for Measuring Output-Distribution Coupling in Multi-Agent LLM Systems -- and Auditing the Claims It Enables
items.x: We introduce the Contagion Tensor, a measurement framework for quantifying how large language model (LLM) output distributions couple across modalities, agents, and time steps. From the tensor we derive the Coupling Amplification Factor (CAF), a family of ratio-based metrics sharing the form CAF = E[T_condition] / E[T_baseline], providing unitless, baseline-referenced measurement with bootstrap confidence intervals. …
items.sm: Introduces metrics for measuring coupling between model outputs across agents, modalities, and time, using simulations and API experiments to examine attribution.

items.t: When Latent Agents Lie: KV-Cache Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
items.x: LLM agents can share more than text. In some systems, an agent can send a short visible message while also passing its full KV-cache state to another model. This hidden state can help the final model combine evidence from several agents, but it is also hard to inspect. A visible message may look harmless even if the hidden state has been changed. We study this problem in a multi-agent question-answering setup. Specia…
items.sm: Finds that sharing hidden model states improves multi-agent question answering, while malicious specialists can exploit the gap between visible messages and hidden states.

items.t: Set-Valued Routing for Language-Model Agent Systems: A WildChat Benchmark and Cost-Aware Evaluation

items.sm: Adds a Jester faction to Werewolf to test reasoning about conflicting incentives, finding frequent strategically harmful choices and model-dependent effects of self-learning.

items.t: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Jimmy Laurence Rippin, Simon C. Marshall, David Demitri Africa, Christian Schroeder de Witt
items.x: Increasingly autonomous agentic AI systems pose novel multi-agent risks, such as secret collusion via covert communication channels. The natural defence to these collusion attempts is to monitor plain-text communication, but the efficacy of monitors has been called into doubt by increasingly sophisticated model steganography; indeed, some theoretical schemes have been proposed that are information-theoretically or co…
items.sm: Demonstrates that coding agents with realistic tool access can construct covert communication systems that evade monitoring of visible messages.

items.t: Delayed Verification Destabilizes Multi-Agent LLM Belief: Instability Thresholds and Optimal Corrector Placement
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems often rely on verifier and critic agents to suppress hallucinations, but verification is delayed. During this delay, false claims can propagate through the agent network. We model this process as delayed consensus on a graph with grounded corrector nodes. Spectral decomposition by the grounded Laplacian yields a closed-form stability threshold for the verification dose: …
items.sm: Models how delayed verification destabilizes shared agent beliefs, derives correction thresholds, and proposes a method for choosing where to place corrector agents.

items.t: When Identity Overrides Incentives: Representational Choices as Governance Decisions in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.v: ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT)
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models are increasingly deployed in strategic policy and governance settings, where agents representing stakeholders with conflicting interests must coordinate under shared constraints. These systems typically assign role-based personas to agents,describing their motivations and objectives. Whether agents with role-based identities follow explicit payoffs or their assigned …
items.sm: Finds that assigning stakeholder personas can override explicit incentives in multi-agent strategic games, substantially changing whether teams reach equilibria.

items.t: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
items.x: Multi-model LLM systems such as routing, voting, cascades, fusion, and mixture-of-agents are used to beat single-model accuracy. We show that their gain is capped by a quantity the field rarely reports. For any policy whose output is one member model answer, accuracy cannot exceed one minus beta, where beta is the rate at which every model is wrong on the same query. In contrast, the usual diagnostic, average pairwis…
items.sm: Derives an accuracy ceiling for systems selecting among model answers based on shared failures, showing pairwise error correlations cannot determine that ceiling.

items.t: Glite ARF: Verifier-Driven Research with Parallel LLM Coding Agents
items.a: Vassili Philippov, Pavel Katunin, Dmitry Andreev, Igor Ostanin, Anton Nikolaev
items.x: LLM coding agents make it tempting to automate empirical research by delegating experiments to them directly, but naive delegation does not scale to large projects: low-rate instruction lapses compound into broken, irreproducible artefacts. items.sm: Provides a framework for parallel coding agents conducting research, using deterministic verifiers to enforce task isolation, preserve completed work, and track corrections.

items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.t: QueenBee: A Recursively Self-Improving Harness for Communication Topology Design in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Congjia Tian, Yuhang Yao, Jiaming Cui
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems show great potential for complex tasks through role specialization and collaborative reasoning. However, existing automated workflow design methods primarily focus on one-off search and candidate optimization, lacking sustained accumulation and reuse of structural design experience to meet evolving coordination demands. We propose QueenBee, an experience-guided framework for multi-agent …
items.sm: Introduces QueenBee, which evolves multi-agent communication workflows using persistent records of execution problems, design hypotheses, and validation results.

items.t: When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?
items.a: Aryan Keluskar, Amrita Bhattacharjee, Huan Liu
items.x: Personality prompting shapes how large language models communicate, yet whether these behavioral shifts affect objective task outcomes remains under-explored. Prior work shows that agents prompted with low agreeableness produce adversarial language, while those prompted with high agreeableness become cooperative, but the relationship between communication style and task performance has not been systematically examine…

items.t: AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems
items.a: Changxin Lao, Fei Pan, Guozhuang Ma, Han Li, Huihuang Lin, Jijun Shi, Kangzhi Zhao, Kun Gai
items.x: Recommendation algorithm iteration is moving from an artisanal, engineer-bound process toward an industrialized research loop, but this transition remains blocked by a structural execution bottleneck: the idea-to-launch cycle still depends on human engineers to generate hypotheses, modify production code, launch A/B experiments, and attribute online results. Innovation therefore scales linearly with headcount rather …
items.sm: Presents a deployed multi-agent system that generates, implements, evaluates, and learns from experiments to automate development of industrial recommendation algorithms.

items.t: EconSimulacra: A Digital Twin Platform of Socio-Economic Systems Powered by LLM Agents
items.a: Ryuji Hashimoto, Masahiro Kaneko, Kentaro Ueda, Takehiro Takayanagi, Kiyoshi Izumi
items.x: Real-world social behavior emerges from tightly coupled domains: economic conditions shape mobility and social interactions, while online attention and offline activity feed back into local popularity and consumer behavior. items.sm: Introduces a social simulator connecting consumer activity, mobility, and social networks through agents' shared memories and internal states.

items.t: ShareLock: A Stealthy Multi-Tool Threshold Poisoning Attack Against MCP
items.a: Liwei Liu, Tianzhu Han, Zijian Liu, Zishu Dong, Na Ruan
items.x: With the rapid evolution of LLM-driven agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open protocol bridging LLMs with external tools, has quickly become foundational to modern agent ecosystems. However, the expanding adoption of MCP has also introduced novel security concerns such as Tool Poisoning Attack (TPA), which exploit LLM-server interactions to inject malicious prompts. Existing poisoning schemes typically adopt a…
items.sm: Introduces an attack that splits malicious instructions across multiple MCP tools using threshold secret sharing to reduce detectability.

items.t: Mutation Testing for Multi-Agent Workflows
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are defined by explicit workflows, agents, tools, tool-access rules, and delegation paths. Most evaluations, however, report end-to-end task success rather than whether a test suite can detect faults in this coordination structure, such as a removed delegation, a silently removed restriction, a misrouted tool edge, or a faulty tool implementation. We adapt mutation analy…
items.sm: Adapts mutation testing to multi-agent workflows by introducing coordination faults and measuring whether test suites detect structural changes, outcome differences, or forbidden tool calls.

items.t: Semantic Early-Stopping for Iterative LLM Agent Loops
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) loops, for example a Writer that drafts and a Critic that revises, are almost always terminated by a fixed iteration cap (max_iterations). This is a syntactic kill-switch: it is blind to whether the answer is still improving, so it over-spends tokens on easy inputs and truncates hard ones. We study semantic early-stopping: the loop halts when consecutive draft embeddings stop ch…
items.sm: Proposes stopping iterative agent loops when draft meanings stabilize and measured quality stops improving, while proving termination and treating semantic convergence as an empirical conjecture.

items.t: IntentTester: Intent-Driven Multi-agent Framework for Cross-Library Test Migration

Despite the known importance of temporal structure in natural language, there is no existing evidence of temporal references in emergent communication. This paper addresses this gap, by exploring how agents communicate about temporal relationships. We analyse three potential factors for the emergence of temporal …
items.sm: Finds that changing agent architecture through batching enables temporal references in emergent communication, while changing the loss function alone does not.

items.t: Security Engineering of OpenClaw: Analyzing Attack Surface Expansion and Trust-Boundary Violations
items.a: Saeid Jamshidi, Arghavan Moradi Dakhel, Kawser Wazed Nafi, Foutse Khomh
items.x: Agentic large language model (LLM) systems can now execute actions, not only produce text. When model outputs trigger privileged operations such as shell commands, browser automation, or external tool calls, the security problem shifts from alignment alone to system configuration and structural design. We analyze OpenClaw, a self-hosted multi-agent system in which LLM outputs can execute commands and interact with to…
items.sm: Analyzes OpenClaw security and reports that accepting actions proposed by any agent increases compromise probability as the number of agents grows.

items.sm: Argues through a heuristic synthesis that multi-agent performance depends on interactions among communication topology, memory, feedback visibility, fairness, and resource allocation.

items.t: Security in a Workflow: Exploring Role-Based Agentic Architectures for Vulnerability Handling
items.x: Secure software engineering in practice is a multi-stage workflow involving vulnerability analysis, remediation, and fix verification. However, current LLM-based software security approaches often focus on isolated tasks such as detection or patch generation, with limited attention to agentic architectures reflecting industrial workflow. This creates a gap between existing LLM-based vulnerability-handling methods and…
items.sm: Evaluates planner, analyzer, fixer, and verifier agents on 25 real C/C++ vulnerabilities, including a workflow integrating CodeQL.
