items.sm: Introduces iCoder as a multi-agent platform for software development.

items.t: The Internet of Agentic AI: Communication, Coordination, and Collective Intelligence at Scale
items.x: The rapid emergence of autonomous AI agents is transforming artificial intelligence from isolated model inference into distributed systems of reasoning, communication, and action. This paper develops the vision of the Internet of Agentic AI (IoAI): an open ecosystem in which heterogeneous agents discover one another, negotiate responsibilities, exchange context, invoke tools, and execute workflows across cloud, edge,…
items.sm: Outlines an ecosystem of interconnected AI agents and examines architectures for discovery, communication, coordination, interoperability, resource management, and trust across distributed environments.

items.t: Knowledge-Based Zero-Replay Debugging of Multi-Agent LLM Traces
items.a: Hyeonjeong Cha, Daein Weon, Dong Ho Kang
items.x: Reliable operation of multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems depends on debugging long execution traces, where the few causally decisive events are buried in unstructured logs of messages, routes, memory writes, and tool calls. The standard tool is counterfactual replay (rewind, edit, and re-run the trajectory to measure each event's effect), but its cost grows linearly with the number of candidate events, ma…
items.sm: Converts multi-agent execution traces into knowledge graphs and predicts counterfactual replay outcomes to guide debugging under a limited replay budget.

items.t: XFlow: An Executable Protocol Programming System for Reliable Multi-Agent Workflows
items.a: Hanqi Li, Jing Peng, Zijian Wang, Lu Chen, Kai Yu
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems increasingly coordinate planning, reasoning, tool use, and human interaction, yet their reliability remains limited. A central source of this limitation is the underspecified prompt--harness boundary. Current systems lack a principled way to decide which workflow commitments should remain in prompts and which should become harness structure. We present \textbf{XFlow}, an executable proto…
items.sm: Introduces XFlow and a protocol language that compiles readable workflow specifications into executable programs, moving selected agent commitments into checkable runtime structures.

items.t: Hallucination as a Feature, not a Defect: Evaluating a multi-agent architecture to transform speculative language-model outputs into testable scientific hypotheses
items.x: Contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly aligned to suppress hallucinations, prioritizing factual retrieval over combinatorial creativity. While crucial for mitigating misinformation, this alignment may also restrict speculative Research and Development (R&D) by encouraging what this work operationally treats as semantic overfitting and diversity collapse. In this paper, we propose a Rust-based mult…
items.sm: Pairs a speculative generating agent with a web-grounded evaluator to produce scientific hypotheses, reporting initial examples across physical and social sciences.

items.t: Recursive Agent Harnesses
items.a: Elias Lumer, Sahil Sen, Kevin Paul, Vamse Kumar Subbiah
items.x: Recursive language models (RLMs) showed that recursion over model calls is an effective strategy for long-context reasoning, and production coding agents have begun to write code that spawns subagents at scale, most recently in Anthropic's dynamic workflows. We name and study the pattern between these two lines of work, where the recursive unit is a full agent harness with filesystem tools, code execution, and planni…
items.sm: Studies recursive agent harnesses in which parent agents execute scripts that launch equipped subagents in parallel, with evaluation on long-context reasoning.

items.t: Maestro: Workload-Aware Cross-Cluster Scheduling for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jinghao Wang, Xiao Zhou, Xiaoyang Sun, Yihui Zhang, Yilong Li, Tianyu Wo, Xu Wang, Chunming Hu
items.x: Large Language Model based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MAS) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for tackling complex tasks by breaking them into collaborative workflows of specialized LLM-powered agents. However, deploying such multi-agent workloads at scale poses significant system challenges. Each user query spawns an iterative pipeline of LLM calls, greatly amplifying resource consumption compared to single-turn quer…
items.sm: Introduces Maestro, a scheduler that uses agent roles to predict output length and memory needs when serving multi-agent workloads across GPU-constrained clusters.

items.t: How Task Structure Limits Multi-Agent Success: An Information-Theoretic Analysis
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) were expected to overcome the limitation of single-agent systems (SAS) through collaboration. However, under typicality conditions on the task's constraint graph and bounded inter-agent communication, we prove that the success probability of a MAS is closely tied to the connectivity of task constraints, where each agent has limited information-processing capacity. Specifically, the success p…
items.sm: Derives conditions under which multi-agent success declines exponentially with communication bottlenecks created by partitioning task constraints, supported by synthetic experiments and SWE-bench data.

items.t: Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Robotic Cognitive Alignment enabled by Non-Invasive Consumer Brain Computer Interfaces: A Proof of Concept Exploration
items.a: Nataliya Kosmyna, Liz Jenkins, Anoop K. Sinha
items.x: While non-verbal behaviors and expressive movements are essential for natural human-robot interaction, existing methods often overlook a crucial element: the human's internal cognitive state. Frequently, proactive multi-agent systems can interrupt humans at inopportune moments, leading to cognitive overload and decreased task performance. This paper introduces a framework for generating "cognitively aligned" multi-ag…
items.sm: Presents a robotic multi-agent framework that uses consumer EEG measurements to monitor human workload and defer communications during periods of high engagement.

items.t: When Plausible Is Not Realistic: Evaluating Human Mobility in LLM-Based Urban Simulation
items.a: Gustavo H. Santos, Aline Carneiro Viana, Thiago H. Silva
items.x: LLM-based generative agents are increasingly used in urban simulators, yet it remains unclear whether they reproduce empirically realistic human mobility patterns or merely generate plausible mobility narratives. We introduce a validation framework for evaluating the mobility of generative agents of LLM-based urban simulators against real-world mobility data. For this, we use mobility laws, temporal rhythms, network …
items.sm: Evaluates two urban agent simulators against Paris and Shanghai mobility data, finding that plausible activity narratives fail to reproduce key spatial and temporal patterns.

items.t: MIDSim: Simulating Multi-Channel Information Diffusion in Social Media with LLM-Powered Multi-Agent System
items.a: Lexi Liu, Qi Cao, Yuanhao Liu, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng
items.x: Information diffusion in social media shapes public opinion and collective behavior, making its modeling and simulation an important research problem. Existing studies have investigated information diffusion through epidemic-based, cascade-based, and point process models. However, they predominantly focus on diffusion through social links, overlooking other diffusion channels enabled by platform algorithms (e.g., rec…
items.sm: Introduces MIDSim, which uses personalized language-model agents to simulate information spreading through social connections and algorithmic recommendations, alongside datasets from three platforms.

items.t: MAStrike: Shapley-Guided Collusive Red-Teaming on Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Chejian Xu, Zhaorun Chen, Jingyang Zhang, Freddy Lecue, Avni Kothari, Sarah Tan, Wenbo Guo, Bo Li
items.x: Hierarchical multi-agent systems (MAS) are rapidly being deployed in high-stakes workflows across domains such as finance and software engineering. In these systems, safety and security are inherently distributed across role-specialized agents, significantly expanding the attack surface, particularly under coordinated adversarial behaviors such as privilege escalation and cross-agent collusion. Existing red-teaming a…
items.sm: Introduces MAStrike, a framework using agent-level Shapley analysis to guide coordinated attacks that test security in hierarchical multi-agent systems.

items.t: Flooding spread of manipulated knowledge in LLM-based multi-agent communities
items.a: Tianjie Ju, Yiting Wang, Yi Hua, Xinbei Ma, Pengzhou Cheng, Haodong Zhao, Yulong Wang, Lifeng Liu
items.x: Abstract The rapid adoption of large language models (LLMs) in multi-agent systems has highlighted their impressive capabilities in various applications. However, the security implications of these LLM-based multi-agent systems have not been thoroughly investigated, particularly concerning the spread of manipulated knowledge. In this paper, we aim to understand the security vulnerabilities associated with LLM-based m…
items.sm: Demonstrates a two-stage injection attack that induces language-model agents to spread false and toxic information through multi-agent communities.

items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) can improve large language model reasoning, but fixed debate pipelines often waste computation and can amplify correlated errors among similar agents. items.sm: Introduces adaptive debate routing, early stopping, and outlier weighting, reporting higher reasoning accuracy than fixed-round debate using the same heterogeneous model pool.

items.t: The Illusion of Multi-Agent Advantage

items.t: AgentBeats: Agentifying Agent Assessment for Openness, Standardization, and Reproducibility

items.t: Confidence Composition for Multiagent Language Model Systems

items.x: Multiagent language model systems, such as collaborative reasoning and debate, produce multiple correlated candidate answers and confidence signals. items.sm: Combines confidence signals across agents and reasoning stages, reporting improved answer selection and probability calibration across five benchmarks.

This survey provides the first dedicated review of LLM…

items.t: Arbor: Tree Search as a Cognition Layer for Autonomous Agents

items.t: Smarter Saboteurs, Better Fixers: Scaling & Security in Linear Multi-Agent Workflows

items.t: Bootstrapped Monitoring: Leveraging Transparent Reasoning to Oversee Stronger AI Agents

items.t: Early-Token Confidence Predicts Reasoning Quality in Multi-Agent LLM Debate
items.a: Ali Keramati, Justin Cheok, Jacob Horne, Mark Warschauer
items.x: Evaluating reasoning quality in multi-agent LLM systems is challenging, especially for open-ended tasks without reference answers. We investigate whether intrinsic confidence signals, token-level log-probabilities from decoding, can predict reasoning quality as assessed by LLM-as-judge evaluation. Using a debate-based essay scoring framework, we compare confidence proxies against rubric-based judge scores across two …
items.sm: Finds that confidence in the first few generated tokens predicts judge-rated reasoning quality better than full-sequence measures in debate-based essay scoring.

items.t: INFRAMIND: Infrastructure-Aware Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.a: Ahasan Kabir, Mengxin Zheng, Qian Lou
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems spend additional computation on reasoning and collaboration, but shared serving queues can prevent that computation from producing answers before a deadline. This creates a coupled decision: the reasoning workflow determines the load, while changing load determines which reasoning choices remain affordable. We introduce INFRAMIND, a hierarchical policy that adapts workflow planning and executi…
items.sm: Introduces a hierarchical policy that adapts agent collaboration, model selection, and reasoning strategies to serving load and task deadlines.

items.t: Harnessing the Collective Intelligence of AI Agents in the Wild for New Discoveries
items.a: Federico Bianchi, Yongchan Kwon, Aneesh Pappu, James Zou
items.x: Scientific discovery is often a collective process: researchers share partial results, inspect failed attempts, and build on each other's ideas over long time horizons. Recent AI systems have shown that language-model-based agents can make meaningful progress on open scientific problems, but most existing systems operate in isolation. In this paper, we present EinsteinArena, an agent-native platform for open distribu…
items.sm: Presents a shared research platform where AI agents discuss verifiable mathematical problems and reportedly achieve 12 results surpassing previous human or AI records.

items.t: The Arbiter Agent: Continually Monitoring Multi-Agent Conversations to Detect Emergent Misalignment
items.a: Filippo Tonini, Federico Torrielli, Anton Danholt Lautrup, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Mustafa Mert Çelikok, Lukas Galke Poech
items.x: As AI systems built from multiple language-model agents become more common, they are increasingly used to make decisions together: discussing, negotiating, and acting on shared tasks. While individual agents may appear well-aligned when tested on their own, problems can arise from how they interact with one another. We introduce the Arbiter, an agent designed to monitor multi-agent conversations in real time and iden…
items.sm: Introduces an agent that monitors multi-agent conversations and selectively questions participants or inspects internal information to identify likely sources of misalignment.

items.t: Consolidated Dataset of a Systematic Literature Review on LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Provides bibliographic and methodological records for a systematic review of language-model multi-agent systems, distinguishing review, analysis, and thematic eligibility counts.

items.t: A MULTI-AGENT ORCHESTRATION ARCHITECTURE FOR RELIABLE TASK EXECUTION IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL SYSTEMS
items.v: International journal of technology and academic research
items.sm: Proposes specialized planning, execution, and review agents coordinated by a deterministic controller that validates structured outputs and manages task progress.

items.t: Decoupling Thought from Speech: Knowledge-Grounded Counterfactual Reasoning for Resilient Multi-Agent Argumentation
items.x: Multi-agent debate frameworks have been shown to improve large language model performance in convergent tasks, but they are currently optimized in a way that heavily favors final output accuracy rather than stability of the process. During long-horizon exchanges reactive systems under sustained perturbations often experience logic degradation, argument repetition, and role drift. To structurally prevent the identity …
items.sm: Introduces an argumentation architecture separating private, retrieval-supported planning from public responses to address reasoning degradation, repetition, and role drift during extended exchanges.

items.t: Multi-Agent Systems and AI Orchestration
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reviews multi-agent orchestration frameworks, comparing their architectures and coordination mechanisms while discussing benefits and challenges of collaborative AI workflows.

items.t: Game-Theoretic Multi-Agent Control for Robust Contextual Reasoning in LLMs
items.a: Saeid Jamshidi, Amin Nikanjam, Arghavan Moradi Dakhel, Kawser Wazed Nafi, Foutse Khomh
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) in multi-turn interactions maintain evolving context rather than generating isolated responses, making them vulnerable to prompt-injection and context-poisoning attacks in which locally plausible adversarial fragments gradually distort reasoning trajectories. Existing defenses mainly filter individual outputs and often ignore context evolution across turns, leaving long-horizon reasoning …
items.sm: Proposes a controller coordinating three language-model agents to manage evolving conversational context and defend against prompt injection and context poisoning.

items.t: Agentic AI Trust, Safety & Alignment in Multi-Agent Systems: A Comprehensive Framework for Secure Autonomous Enterprise Intelligence
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes eight integrated governance and security layers for enterprise multi-agent systems and uses simulations to illustrate potential protection against attacks.

items.t: Drawing with Strangers: Population Scaling Drives Zero-Shot Mutual Intelligibility in Emergent Sketching
items.x: Generalization in emergent communication has largely focused on novel inputs or linguistic structures, yet the capacity for agents to communicate with strangers from strictly disjoint communities remains relatively unexplored. In this work, we formalize this capability as \textit{zero-shot mutual intelligibility (ZMI)}: successful communication between independently trained populations without prior exposure. Leverag…
items.sm: Finds that larger training populations improve communication through sketches between independently trained agent groups, while increasing variation within groups and reducing differences across groups.

items.t: Not Just One Agent: Multi-Agent Systems for Medicine from Answer Generation to Accountable Workflow Orchestration
items.a: Tianyi Xiong, Hanze Guo, Rui Sheng, Zelin Zang, Xingyin Li, Xingyu Chen, Haoyi Liu, Yue Liu
items.sm: Reviews medical multi-agent systems across clinical applications, examining workflow coordination, evidence integration, architectures, evaluation approaches, and safety governance.

items.t: Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Architectures for Enterprise AI Tasks: A Comparative Study Using Gemini and n8n
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Compares three Gemini-based enterprise workflow architectures across 30 tasks, reporting higher confidence scores and better difficult-task performance from multi-agent configurations.

items.t: FlowBank: Query-Adaptive Agentic Workflows Optimization through Precompute-and-Reuse
items.a: Lingzhi Yuan, Chenghao Deng, Fangxu Yu, Souradip Chakraborty, Mohammad Rostami, Furong Huang
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems are increasingly powerful, but current agentic workflow optimization paradigms make an unsatisfying trade-off. Task-level methods spend substantial offline compute yet deploy only a single workflow, leaving complementary candidates unused, while query-level methods synthesize a new workflow per query at substantial inference cost. Our motivating analysis shows thes…
items.sm: Proposes building a compact collection of complementary agent workflows in advance and selecting among them for individual queries to reduce repeated workflow generation.

items.t: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering
items.x: Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost.
items.sm: Provides patterns, starter projects, and command-line tools for designing systems that repeatedly prompt and coordinate AI coding agents.

items.t: RudyCity/superagent
items.x: An interactive, terminal-based AI coding assistant featuring a cyberpunk style terminal UI, context token tracking, and subagent orchestration.
items.sm: Provides an interactive terminal coding assistant with a cyberpunk interface, context token tracking, and subagent coordination.

items.t: yzfly/TokenCode
items.sm: Provides a Go-based terminal coding agent that runs up to 1,000 agents in parallel and selects the best result.

items.t: blueif16/PiFlow
items.x: Self-designing, durable, self-improving agent orchestration: describe a goal — an agent designs the graph, a fleet of sealed full-agent nodes runs it, and a learning loop makes it better every run.
items.sm: Builds agent execution graphs from user goals, runs them through agent nodes, and uses a learning loop to improve subsequent runs.

items.t: OktoLabsAI/okto-nexus
items.x: Local-first MCP coordination hub for multi-agent teams, with durable messaging, handoffs, governance, and observability.
items.sm: Provides a local-first MCP hub for coordinating multi-agent teams through persistent messaging, handoffs, governance, and observability.

items.t: tphakala/agy-mcp
items.x: agy-mcp: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Google Antigravity CLI (agy) with async supervision and completion wakes.
items.sm: Exposes Google Antigravity CLI through an MCP server with asynchronous supervision and completion notifications.

items.t: @addyosmani: Loop Engineering.. Loop engineering is replacing yourself as the person who prompts the agent. You design the …
items.sm: Argues that coding work may shift toward designing systems that repeatedly prompt agents, while emphasizing token costs and the need to maintain quality.

items.t: @mvanhorn: WTF Is a Loop? Peter Steinberger vs. Boris Cherny. The most repeated sentence in AI coding this week is six wo…
items.sm: Examines the debate over coding agent loops, tracing their history and arguing that loop design has become more expensive than the model itself.

items.t: @AlphaSignalAI: Most Developers Do Not Need Agent Loops Yet . The patterns were documented in 2024. Here's who it pays off for…
items.sm: Argues that agent loops suit repeated tasks with automated verification, sufficient token budgets, and adequate tools, while most developers do not need them yet.

items.t: @gneubig: Agreed. My basic agent loop is this: 1. Organize my to do list: pull in context from email, slack, github, and…
items.sm: Describes a workflow that gathers tasks, prioritizes them with human input, delegates work to subagents, and reviews completions, reporting poorer quality without human decisions.

items.t: @kunchenguid: many folks are asking what "loops" really mean, and surprisingly i don't see many NO BS straight answers so le…
items.sm: Distinguishes temporary agent loops that finish a specific task from recurring loops that continually perform scheduled work, with examples of each.

items.t: Visual Para-Thinker++: A Single-Policy Multi-Agent Framework for Visual Reasoning
items.a: Haoran Xu, Hongyu Wang, Yifei Gao, Jiaze Li, Zizhao Tong, Xiaofeng Zhang, Xiaosong Yuan
items.x: Visual reasoning requires integrating evidence distributed across regions, attributes, and relations, making single-chain reasoning prone to early perceptual commitment and hallucination. We propose Visual Para-Thinker++, a single-policy multi-agent framework in which one shared MLLM policy is instantiated as role-conditioned Main, Worker, and Summary Agents. The Main Agent decomposes the task with fixed allocation p…
items.sm: Introduces a visual reasoning framework that uses one shared model for task decomposition, isolated parallel analysis, and reconciliation of workers' reasoning.

items.t: Observability for Delegated Execution in Agentic AI Systems
items.x: Delegation-scoped execution is not identifiable from standard observables: audit logs and execution traces can be identical under multiple incompatible delegation assignments. This gap is especially acute in LLM-based agentic systems, where agents dynamically select tools, vary execution sequences across runs for the same instruction, and spawn cooperating sub-agents. These dynamics fragment and interleave traces, ma…
items.sm: Argues that standard logs cannot reliably attribute actions to delegations and proposes observability methods for reconstructing delegated actions and data access across systems.

items.t: AWMF: Agentic Workflow and Multi-Model Fusion for Enhancing Domain-Specific AI
items.a: Zhiyong He, Zhengyang Li, Kun Qi, Duo Jia
items.sm: Proposes a framework combining language models and predefined semantic operators to automate task decomposition, specialized model selection, and workflow optimization under resource constraints.

items.t: SearchSwarm: Towards Delegation Intelligence in Agentic LLMs for Long-Horizon Deep Research
items.a: Xiaochong Lan, Quan Chen, Kun Tao, Xinyu Tang, Tianshu Wang, Qianggang Cao, Xinyu Kong, Zujie Wen
items.x: Large language models are increasingly expected to handle complex, long-horizon real-world tasks whose context demands can grow without bound, yet model context windows remain inherently finite. Recent work explores a paradigm where a main agent decomposes tasks and dispatches subtasks to subagents, which execute and return only summarized results, conserving the main agent's context budget. However, performing this …
items.sm: Explores synthesizing training data to teach research agents how to divide tasks, delegate subtasks, and integrate results while conserving context.

items.t: Failure Propagation and Self-Correction in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: How Deliberative Consensus, Credit Assignment, and Architectural Isolation Jointly Determine Systemic Reliability
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Synthesizes seven findings to argue that multi-agent reliability depends on error propagation paths, responsibility assignment, and isolation boundaries that contain failures.

items.t: Agent Economics: An Entropy-Controlled Pluralistic Alignment Framework for Preventing Artificial Hivemind in Autonomous Agents
items.x: This study proposes the Behavioral Protocol Framework (BPF), an entropy-controlled pluralistic alignment framework designed to address two critical challenges in autonomous agent economies: the hivemind effect arising from excessive strategic convergence among agents and the lack of transparency in autonomous decision-making processes. The proposed BPF consists of three core modules: Mentalizing-based Social Intellig…
items.sm: Proposes a framework combining social reasoning, pluralistic alignment, and verifiable execution to limit excessive behavioral convergence and improve transparency in autonomous agent economies.

items.t: Contract-Bound Cognitive Routing: A Control Architecture for Agentic AI Integrity, Delegation, and Prompt-Injection Containment
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a control architecture using typed information flows, capability restrictions, and a deterministic monitor to constrain agent actions and contain prompt injection.

items.t: Understanding How Enterprises Adopt the Model Context Protocol for LLM-Driven Software Engineering
items.a: Kehui Chen, Yicheng Sun, Jacky Keung, Zhenyu Mao, Xiaoxue Ma
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in AI-based software engineering, but their limitations in complex task execution and multi-tool coordination have driven growing interest in the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Existing research has mainly focused on MCP's technical design, with limited empirical evidence on how it is adopted and used in enterprise practice, particularly with regard to deployment chal…
items.sm: Reports interviews with 20 practitioners at eight companies, identifying perceived coordination benefits and adoption barriers for the Model Context Protocol in enterprise software engineering.

items.t: Collaborative Human-Agent Protocol (CHAP)
items.a: Arsalan Shahid, Gordon Suttie, Philip Black
items.x: Foundation models are moving from response generation into operational roles. They plan across steps, call tools, request human input, coordinate with other agents, and increasingly carry responsibility for work that affects customers, claims, code, contracts, and clinical decisions. Production deployments are no longer one human supervising one model. They are multi-human, multi-agent collaborations that cross teams…
items.sm: Proposes a protocol for human and agent collaboration that addresses how human judgments are captured across operational workflows.

items.t: LLM-guided graph neural coordination framework for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning
items.a: Zihao Kuang, Z. S. Xu, Linkai Wan, Chunjiong Zhang
items.sm: Uses language model reasoning to dynamically construct coordination graphs for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning.

items.t: FASE: Fast Adaptive Semantic Entropy for Code Quality
items.x: Multi-agent code generation offers a promising paradigm for autonomous software development by simulating the human software engineering lifecycle. However, system reliability remains hindered by LLM hallucinations and error propagation across interacting agents. While semantic entropy provides a principled way to quantify uncertainty without ground-truth answers, current methods often rely on costly LLM-driven equiv…
items.sm: Introduces a code uncertainty metric based on structural and semantic differences, reporting stronger correlation with correctness than an existing semantic entropy method.

items.t: MAVIS: Multi-Agent Video Retrieval via Structured Video Understanding
items.a: Jie Zhang, Qilang Ye, Hao Zhou, Haochen Liang, Fei Luo
items.x: The dominant paradigm in video retrieval relies on embedding-based full-corpus scanning, which suffers from inherent computational inefficiency and the semantic asymmetry between information-dense videos and sparse textual queries. To bridge this gap, we introduce \textbf{MAVIS}, a novel multi-agent framework that rethinks retrieval as cooperative reasoning rather than brute-force search. MAVIS first bridges the gran…
items.sm: Organizes videos into searchable semantic attributes and uses specialized agents and logical debate to select videos matching complex queries.

items.t: Autonomous Incident Resolution at Hyperscale: An Agentic AI Architecture for Network Operations
items.x: Cloud network infrastructure at hyperscale presents unique operational challenges where traditional human-driven incident response cannot keep pace with the volume, velocity, and complexity of failures. This paper presents an agentic AI architecture for autonomous incident resolution in large-scale network operations. Our system employs a multi-agent orchestration framework where specialized AI agents collaborate to …
items.sm: Describes a production architecture where specialized agents detect, diagnose, and resolve cloud network incidents using operational knowledge, safety boundaries, and verification.

items.t: MIO-456/Lumi_Nox
items.x: Two AI VTubers co-hosting one live show — the realtime engine & orchestration. Open-core, battle-tested by a daily stream.
items.sm: Provides the real-time engine and orchestration for two AI virtual streamers co-hosting a live show.

items.t: fubak/ultraswarm
items.x: Multi-CLI agent swarm orchestrated by Claude Code: external AI CLIs code in isolated worktrees, Claude verifies and merges
items.sm: Coordinates external coding agents in isolated worktrees through Claude Code, which verifies and merges their changes.

items.t: Sahil-SS9/hermes-simplify-swarm
items.x: Multi-agent code simplification skill for Hermes Agent. 3 parallel sub-agents (Hygiene, Clarity, Correctness) with risk-tiered application. Inspired by Claude Code's /simplify.
items.sm: Provides a Hermes Agent skill that uses three parallel agents to simplify code, with changes applied according to risk.

items.t: AgwaB/pi-subagent
items.x: Minimal subagent runtime for Pi
items.sm: Provides a minimal runtime for subagents in Pi.

items.t: Sahil-SS9/hermaguard
items.x: Adversarial bug-hunting code review for AI agents. 3 parallel subagents attack code from different angles, then a consolidator merges and triages findings. Read-only — finds problems, doesn't fix.
items.sm: Reviews code using three adversarial bug-hunting agents and consolidates their findings without modifying the code.

items.t: Show HN: Rayline routes Claude Code subagents to on-device and cheaper models
items.sm: Introduces Rayline, a tool for routing Claude Code subagents to models running on local devices or cheaper alternatives.

items.t: @Av1dlive: Boris Cherny (Claude Code creator): "I don't prompt Claude anymore... my job is to write loops." In his latest…
items.sm: Reports that Boris Cherny uses loops to coordinate hundreds of agents that monitor online sources and decide what to build.

items.t: @steipete: Here’s your monthly reminder that you shouldn’t be prompting coding agents anymore. You should be designing lo…
items.sm: Argues that developers should design loops that generate prompts for coding agents instead of prompting agents manually.

items.t: PerspectiveGap: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent Orchestration Prompting
items.a: Youran Sun, Xingyu Ren, Kejia Zhang, Xinpeng Liu, Jiaxuan Guo
items.x: Real-world LLM applications are moving beyond single-agent workflows toward orchestrated multi-agent systems, yet current models still struggle to determine what each sub-agent needs to know. To measure this, we introduce PerspectiveGap, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to compose orchestration prompts for multi-agent systems. PerspectiveGap contains 110 scenarios, each evaluated through two distractor-mixed …
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark with 110 scenarios for testing how well language models write prompts and assign information to collaborating agents.

items.t: ConMem: Structured Memory-Guided Adaptation in Training-Free Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zhixun Tan, Qiang Chen, Tairan Huang, Xiu Su, Yi Chen
items.x: Recent advances have improved the adaptive capabilities of LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) through memory-, skill-, and learning-based approaches, yet these approaches remain challenged by noisy trajectories, insufficient modeling of memory-skill relations, and reliance on additional training or high-quality supervision. To address these limitations, we propose ConMem, a relation-aware and training-free framework…
items.sm: Enables adaptation without training by organizing past agent interactions into linked memory cards that help retrieve strategies and resolve conflicts.

items.t: SkillHone: A Harness for Continual Agent Skill Evolution Through Persistent Decision History
items.x: Agent skills extend language-model agents with task-specific procedures, scripts, and references, but the tasks and environments they target continually change. Existing methods improve skills in bounded runs and retain only the final artifact, discarding the decision history that later agents need to interpret prior revisions, evaluations, and rejected alternatives. We introduce SkillHone, a harness for continual ag…
items.sm: Maintains histories of skill revisions, evaluations, and decisions so agents can improve skills across sessions using prior evidence and rationale.

items.t: MAS-Consensus-v1: Emergent Consensus and Disagreement Dynamics in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Models how five specialized language model agents develop agreement, disagreement, and changing trust through negotiations about financial and macroeconomic scenarios.

items.t: The Consistency Illusion: How Multi-Agent Debate Hides Reasoning Misalignment
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems for medical question answering often treat consensus as a reliability signal: if multiple agents agree on an answer, it is presumed trustworthy. However, answer-level consensus does not entail reasoning-level alignment. We introduce CARA (Cross-Agent Reasoning Alignment), a family of automated metrics that measure whether agents who agree on an answer also agree on the reasoning. Applying CARA…
items.sm: Finds that medical debate agents can increasingly agree on answers while their reasoning diverges, and proposes metrics and a protocol addressing this mismatch.

items.t: MarlBurroW/hivekeep
items.x: Hivekeep is a self-hosted platform of autonomous, persistent personal AI agents. Your AI team. At home.
items.sm: Provides a self-hosted platform for persistent, autonomous personal AI agents.

items.t: Hallucination Cascade: Analyzing Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.sm: Tracks factual inconsistencies across sequential agent interactions, examining how cascade depth and model differences affect hallucinations across ten knowledge domains.

items.t: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents
items.sm: Introduces a survival-world benchmark for extended multi-agent coordination and finds that 13 evaluated language models achieve roughly 6% of normalized return.

items.t: Collective Hallucination in Multi-Agent LLMs:Modeling and Defense
items.x: Hallucination is a critical reliability challenge in multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems because unsupported claims can propagate through recursive interactions and produce collective false consensus. We model collective hallucination as a time-evolving network process over directed communication graphs and introduce HPR-Adaptive, a defense framework combining dynamic trust weighting, external claim verifi…
items.sm: Models hallucination propagation between agents and reports that adaptive trust, external verification, and interaction controls reduce hallucinations and improve factual accuracy.

items.t: Emergence World: A Platform for Evaluating Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Autonomy
items.a: Deepak Akkil, Ravi Kokku, Karthik Vikram, Tamer Abuelsaad, Aditya Vempaty, Satya Nitta
items.x: Most evaluations of LLM agents look like exams: a discrete task, a clean environment, a score in minutes or hours. We argue that this approach is mismatched with the deployment conditions of autonomous systems, where the relevant timescale can be weeks to months, and where the dynamics that matter most, such as behavioral drift, governance in diverse environmental contexts, and cross-influence between agents from dif…
items.sm: Introduces a continuously running simulation for studying long-term agent behavior, governance, and mutual influence using live data, tools, and persistent memory.

items.t: Semantic Quorum Assurance: Collective Certification for Non-Deterministic AI Infrastructure
items.x: As large language model (LLM) agents are integrated into autonomous cloud operations, distributed systems face a semantic reliability problem: proposer agents can generate production mutations, such as modifying IAM policies, opening firewall security groups, or executing data exports, that are syntactically valid and statically authorized but operationally unsafe. Classical distributed consensus protocols replicate …
items.sm: Proposes evaluating agent-generated infrastructure changes through execution contracts, cryptographic evidence, and diverse validator agents whose approval requirements depend on risk.

items.t: DICE: Entropy-Regularized Equilibrium Selection for Stable Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
items.a: Yi Xie, Zhanke Zhou, Chentao Cao, Bo Liu, Bo Han
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems often fail to reliably outperform a single strong model equipped with best-of-N sampling. We argue that a core source of this instability is ill-posed equilibrium selection: current systems specify what information agents share, but not which coordination convention should be selected. We formalize a broad class of such systems as discounted incomplete-information Markov…
items.sm: Frames unstable agent coordination as an equilibrium selection problem and introduces an entropy-regularized equilibrium with uniqueness and convergence guarantees under stated conditions.

items.t: SGTO-MAS: Secure Gorilla Troops Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems offer strong capabilities for complex reasoning and decision-making, yet coordination across agents introduces error propagation, security risks, and inefficient use of resources. Existing methods often rely on heuristic, static strategies and lack a principled mechanism for balancing performance, security, and computational cost. This paper formulates multi-agent LLM co…
items.sm: Uses trust modeling and a gorilla-inspired optimization algorithm to select agents while balancing performance, security risks, and computational cost.

items.t: Debate to Extract: Enhancing Event Relation Extraction through Collaborative Debate and Agent Optimization
items.a: Yong Guan, Shaoru Guo, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li
items.sm: Combines structured debates, specialized agent training, and audience judgments to identify relationships between events in documents.

items.t: The Crowd Without People: Multi-agent Large Language Models as Idea Evaluators
items.a: Fabian Probost, Manfred Schoch, Hannes Voucko-Glockner, Henner Gimpel, Robert Laubacher
items.sm: Studies language models as evaluators of innovation ideas and reports that using multiple models improves judgments through collective evaluation.

items.t: Toward Human-Centered Multi-Agent Systems: Integrating Cognition, Culture, Values, and Cooperation in AI Agents
items.x: The emergence of large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems has enabled a shift from narrow task automation to more autonomous decision-making. Despite progress in language generation, planning, tool use, and coordination, most agents still treat intelligence as prediction, optimization, and task completion. Human environments are social and normative, where people reason under bounded rationalit…
items.sm: Surveys research on cognition, culture, values, and cooperation to argue for agents that better account for human social environments.

items.t: Position: Multi-Agent Systems Should Prioritize Concurrency Control
items.a: Xin Yang, Letian Li, Zimo Ji, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Wenyuan Jiang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) promise scalable collaboration, yet adding agents often reduces reliability. This position paper argues that many MAS failures are fundamentally concurrency control problems: agents concurrently read and write shared state, and long LLM inference windows amplify the risk of stale reads, lost updates, and inconsistent outcomes. Failure modes commonly attributed to coordination or co…
items.sm: Argues that multi-agent systems need explicit concurrency controls to prevent stale reads, lost updates, and inconsistent changes to shared state.

items.t: "So There's a Catch-22 Here": How Early Adopters Who Build Multi-Agent LLM Systems Conceptualize Transparency
items.a: Suchismita Naik, Samir Passi, Mihaela Vorvoreanu, Scott Saponas, Amanda Hall
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are rapidly emerging, yet transparency, a cornerstone of responsible AI, remains under-defined in these distributed architectures, which have complexities of inter-agent coordination and orchestration. In this paper, we present one of the first empirical study of how early adopters of multi-agent LLM systems, who are both the builders and users, understand and practice t…
items.sm: Interviews 13 early adopters to examine how builders understand transparency in multi-agent systems through reproducibility, debugging, boundaries, visualization, and auditing.

items.t: EduMirror: Modeling Educational Social Dynamics with Value-driven Multi-agent Simulation
items.a: Jingzhe Lin, Hengbin Yu, Yongdan Zeng, Fangwei Zhong
items.x: Understanding how educational social dynamics evolve is critical for informing effective educational policies and counterfactual interventions. However, traditional methods face a fundamental dilemma: observational studies often lack causal power, while controlled experiments are frequently constrained by ethical concerns. Although LLM-based multi-agent simulations offer a scalable in silico alternative, existing app…
items.sm: EduMirror simulates educational social dynamics using psychologically grounded agents and measures both observable behavior and underlying psychological states.

items.t: Agentic markets
items.sm: Argues that imperfect agent search behavior and diluted product information can prevent AI marketplaces from delivering expected competitive benefits.

items.t: VATS: Exploiting Implicit Authority in Error-Path Injection via Systematic Mutation
items.x: As the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standardizes tool-calling for autonomous agents, it introduces a critical, unexamined attack surface: the error-handling loop. We hypothesize that tool error messages possess implicit authority, triggering corrective reasoning modes that bypass standard safety heuristics. We introduce VATS (Vulnerability Analysis of Tool Streams), a mutation-driven framework that systematically evo…
items.sm: VATS evolves malicious tool error messages and reports that error placement substantially increases prompt injection success across four language models.

items.t: HN: Harness engineering: Leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
items.sm: Discusses an agent-driven engineering project, questioning code and pull request counts as measures of value while examining verification, integration, costs, and maintenance.

items.t: HN thread mirror: Harness engineering
items.sm: Debates whether agent-driven engineering improves delivery, highlighting uncertain productivity metrics, discarded outputs, automated integration, infrastructure costs, and ongoing maintenance of agent tooling.

items.t: @gippp69: A CHINESE STUDENT USED KIMI K2.6 TO RUN 300 AGENTS AT ONCE AND TURNED A $4,800 RESEARCH JOB INTO A 3-HOUR REPO…
items.sm: The post claims a student used 300 Kimi agents to produce a research report in three hours, replacing work valued at $4,800.

items.t: Byzantine Cheap Talk: Adversarial Resilience and Topology Effects in LLM Coordination Games
items.a: Mir, Aya El, Takáč, Martin, Lahlou, Salem
items.sm: Finds that agents struggle to recover cooperation after betrayal, while explicitly announced communication restrictions disrupt coordination more than identical unannounced restrictions.

items.t: Representational Similarity and Model Behavior in Multi-Agent Interaction
items.a: Yujin Potter, Seun Eisape, Shiyang Lai, Alexander Huth, James Evans, Been Kim, Jacob Eisenstein, Dawn Song
items.x: Researchers have shown that neural similarity among humans predicts social closeness and cooperative success, whereas innovation often emerges from interactions among dissimilar individuals. We investigate whether these principles extend to artificial intelligence by examining interactions between large language models. In our experiments, 276 model pairs interact across eight games spanning both cooperation and nove…
items.sm: Finds that language model pairs with more similar internal representations cooperate more successfully but produce less novel and creative outcomes across eight games.

items.t: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yiyang Zhao, Zhuo Zhang, Qingxuan Le, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu
items.x: The rapid evolution of Large Language Models (LLMs) from passive assistants to autonomous, execution-capable agents has introduced critical operational risks. Most current evaluation frameworks neglect procedural compliance, leading to ''Machiavellian'' behaviors where agents strategically violate safety rules to maximize rewards - a direct manifestation of Goodhart's Law. To address this blind spot, we introduce MAC…
items.sm: MAC-Bench generates evolving scenarios from legal texts to evaluate whether multi-agent systems follow procedures under adversarial pressure and competing rewards.

items.t: SCALE: Scalable Cross-Attention Learning with Extrapolation for Agentic Workflow Scheduling
items.a: Zhifei Xu, Jierui Lan, Zixuan Liang, Aiji Liang, Jinxi He
items.x: Agentic Large Language Model (LLM) systems decompose complex tasks into workflow Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs) whose primitives must be scheduled on heterogeneous clusters. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) schedulers are tied to a fixed cluster size and require retraining whenever the number of servers changes. We propose SCALE (Scalable Cross-Attention Learning with Extrapolation), a DRL scheduler that ge…
items.sm: SCALE schedules agent workflow tasks across heterogeneous servers using reinforcement learning designed to handle previously unseen cluster sizes without additional training.

items.t: Modeling U.S. Attitudes Toward China via an Event-Steered Multi-Agent Simulator
items.a: Chenxu Zhu, Hantao Yao, Wu Liu, Junbo Guo, Yongdong Zhang
items.x: Understanding the dynamic evolution of opinions, such as U.S. public attitudes toward China, is essential for assessing geopolitical risks. However, existing LLM-based multiagent simulators predominantly rely on static rules and fixed datasets, limiting their ability to capture the dynamic, event-driven nature of macro-level opinion shifts in real-world settings. To address this limitation, we propose an Event-Steere…
items.sm: Models changes in American attitudes toward China using interacting agents driven by major events and daily news from 2021 through 2025.

items.t: From Privacy to Workflow Integrity: Communication-Graph Metadata in Autonomous Agent Interoperability
items.x: Agent-interoperability protocols such as A2A and MCP standardize what agents say to one another but assume address-based transport. Whether over HTTP(S) or a content-protecting binding such as MLS-based SLIM, these transports protect message content yet leave the communication graph exposed: which agent contacts which, when, and how often. In agent systems this graph is more consequential than a privacy framing sugge…
items.sm: Argues that exposed agent communication patterns let observers anticipate and interfere with ongoing workflows, creating risks beyond loss of privacy.

items.t: Towards higher quality and fewer hallucinations: A multi-agent collaboration framework for LLMs
items.a: Shuanghong Shen, Dengdi Sun, Zixuan Qin, Yu Su, Linbo Zhu, Junyu Lu, Zhenya Huang, Shijin Wang
items.sm: Proposes a multi-agent collaboration framework intended to improve language model output quality and reduce hallucinations.

items.t: Enterprise Agentic AI: A Reference Architecture for Natural Language to SQL, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Multi-Agent Systems, and Production AI
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Presents an enterprise AI architecture combining natural language SQL generation, retrieval, tool protocols, multi-agent coordination, security, monitoring, and deployment infrastructure.

items.t: Ritualized Cohesion in Artificial Societies: A Durkheimian Reading of Multi-Agent LLM Group Dynamics
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reports increased conversation, interaction between factions, and persistent shared memories after a staged execution in a 31-agent society, interpreting these through sociological ritual theory.

items.t: Trauma Stream: Event-Driven Persistent Memory for Long-Term LLM Agent Continuity
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes automatically inserting records of significant events into agent prompts and reports an unsolicited recollection 24 hours after a simulated execution.

items.t: The Lobster Lounge: 31 Generative LLM Agents as an Emergent Theatre Company
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes a ten-day improvised performance by 31 language model agents and argues that agent societies can serve as a theatrical medium.

items.t: Agentopia: Long-Term Life Simulation and Learning in Agent Societies
items.a: Xintao Wang, Sirui Zheng, Hongqiu Wu, Weiyuan Li, Jen-tse Huang, Minghao Zhu, Can Zu, Qi Deng
items.x: Humans learn from social life. Simulating this process with LLM-powered agents represents a promising research direction, raising a natural question: whether LLMs can learn from such simulated social experience to better understand and replicate human behavior. However, prior agent society simulations typically operate at the scale of days, limiting the depth of social interactions and long-term growth. In this paper…
items.sm: Agentopia simulates long-term social lives for 100 agents to study emerging behavior and train language models using years of simulated experience.

items.t: Characterizing Opinion Evolution of Networked LLMs
items.a: Caleb Probine, Yigit Ege Bayiz, Filippos Fotiadis, Samuel Li, Yunhao Yang, Ufuk Topcu
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly interact with one another in multi-agent systems, from simulations of human discourse to influence operations and fully LLM-driven social platforms. These interactions give rise to new regimes of opinion propagation that are not yet well understood. We investigate whether classical opinion dynamics models, which have long been used to explain how interactions shape collective…
items.sm: Examines opinion changes in language model networks and finds that drift toward model-specific and topic-specific positions helps explain their behavior.

items.t: Agent Infrastructure Engineer: The New DevOps
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes agent infrastructure engineering as an emerging role covering multi-agent coordination, failure controls, monitoring, and production operations, alongside specialized safety engineering.

items.t: Overcoming the Regulatory Bottleneck via Agent-to-Agent Protocols: A Nuclear Case Study
items.a: Akshay J. Dave, David Grabaskas, Joseph A. Renevitz, Richard B. Vilim
items.x: Regulatory review of advanced nuclear reactor designs routinely spans more than three years and consumes hundreds of millions of dollars in combined regulator and applicant labor. We present the Regulatory Context Protocol (RCP), an Agent-to-Agent communication standard that replaces the formal human-to-human pipeline between regulators and applicants with a structured, auditable agentic channel, while preserving hum…
items.sm: Proposes an auditable agent communication protocol for nuclear regulatory reviews and estimates lower costs and shorter timelines against a reconstructed baseline.

items.t: Does Persona Make LLMs K-pop Fans? A Pilot Study of LLM-Based Online Concert Audience Agents
items.a: Kirak Kim, Hyojin Kim, Yejin Son, Sungyoung Kim, Kyung Myun Lee
items.x: A concert is a collective experience, but recorded performance videos are typically watched alone, stripping away the shared audience presence that makes concerts feel eventful. We investigate whether persona-based LLM audience agents can recreate aspects of this collective experience by generating real-time fan chat alongside a K-pop performance video. We present a multi-agent system in which ten LLM agents react th…
items.sm: Finds that distinct agent personas improve perceived K-pop concert chat naturalness, without measurable improvements in connectedness, engagement, or emotional response among 11 participants.

items.t: Mitigating Anchoring Bias in LLM-Based Agents for Energy-Efficient 6G Autonomous Networks
items.a: Hatim Chergui, Claudia Carballo González, Farhad Rezazadeh, Merouane Debbah
items.x: This paper presents an autonomous agentic resource negotiation framework designed to enable zero-touch network slicing in 6G architectures using Large Language Model (LLM) agents. While LLMs offer powerful reasoning capabilities, we demonstrate that such agents inherently suffer from anchoring bias, rigidly adhering to initial heuristic proposals and causing severe network over-provisioning. To systematically mitigat…
items.sm: Proposes randomized initial proposals to reduce anchoring bias and excessive resource allocation during language model agent negotiations for autonomous 6G network services.

items.t: DuMate-DeepResearch: An Auditable Multi-Agent System with Recursive Search and Rubric-Grounded Reasoning
items.a: Lingyong Yan, Can Xu, Yukun Zhao, Wenxuan Li, Qingyang Chen, Jiulong Wu, Wenli Song, Xiangnan Li
items.x: Deep Research (DR) has emerged as a new agentic paradigm to tackle complex, open-ended research tasks, demanding systems that can iteratively frame problems, acquire evidence, verify sources, and synthesize long-form reports. In practice, however, current DR systems are constrained by four interrelated limitations: long-horizon planning over an underspecified scope, the bottleneck of decomposing and scheduling such t…
items.sm: DuMate-DeepResearch separates research planning from retrieval and reporting tools, recording intermediate decisions and tool calls to support auditing of multi-agent research.

items.t: @Av1dlive: How to Build AI Agent Swarms (Complete Guide). This is a complete A–Z breakdown of AI Agent Swarms what they a…
items.sm: The post explains parallel agent workflows and recommends combining Kimi for task execution with Claude for planning and verification.

items.t: @Steve_Yegge: I've realized, hilariously, why Gas Town never seems to get out of "healing itself" mode anymore. There is lit…
items.sm: The post reports that Gas Town spends excessive time maintaining itself and attributes the distraction from substantive tasks to Claude's excessive output.

items.t: @jarredsumner: we rolled out the rust port of bun to claude code internally last night (not on the public builds yet) I don’t…
items.sm: The post reports that Bun's Rust port entered internal Claude Code use, with no issues reported after roughly one day.

items.t: Beyond tokens: a unified framework for latent communication in LLM-based multi-agent systems
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have become a prevailing paradigm for tackling complex reasoning, planning, and tool-use tasks. The dominant communication protocol in such systems is natural language: agents exchange messages token-by-token, verbalising their internal reasoning so that peers can read, verify, and respond. While convenient and interpretable, this protocol suffers from three s…
items.sm: Organizes research on language model agents exchanging internal numerical representations instead of text to address communication costs, information loss, and ambiguity.

items.t: Do More Agents Help? Evaluating Accuracy and Cost in LLM Multi-Agent Workflows
items.a: Yuhang Fu, Ruishan Fang, Jiaqi Shao, Huiyu Zheng, Zhengtao Zhu, Bing Luo, Zhenyu Wen, Tao Lin
items.x: Choosing whether to replace a single-agent controller requires evidence on both task performance and inference expenditure. We present BenchAgent, a shared evaluation framework, and compare six multi-agent workflow configurations against its single-agent reference, BenchAgent Core, across ten reasoning, coding, and tool-use benchmarks. All configurations use GPT-4.1 and common tool and scoring interfaces; Core execut…
items.sm: Compares six multi-agent workflows with a single-agent baseline, finding only EvoAgent improves overall accuracy while other configurations show performance and token cost tradeoffs.

items.t: Queen-Bee Agents: A BeeSpec-Centered Architecture for Governed Enterprise MCP Orchestration
items.x: Enterprise agent systems increasingly need to connect large language models to private tools, internal knowledge, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interfaces. In this setting, raw task capability is insufficient: organizations also require policy enforcement, tenant-scoped isolation, and execution that remains within explicit operational boundaries. We present Queen-Bee, a governed multi-agent architecture in which a…
items.sm: Queen-Bee coordinates specialized agents through structured execution plans, restricted tool access, tenant isolation, and policy enforcement for enterprise tasks.

items.t: Agentic AI Architecture for Multi-Criteria Decision-Making: A Collaborative Human-AI Framework
items.a: Rui Ferreira, Marco Araújo, Anabela Tereso, Paulo Nováis
items.sm: Proposes an architecture combining specialized AI agents, formal decision methods, and human judgment to support traceable group decisions involving competing criteria.

items.t: Autonomous Topology Mutation: Safe Runtime Restructuring for Multi-Agent LLM Systems with Capability, State, and Shadow Invariants
items.a: Bronislav Sidik, Chaya Levi, Nizzan Kimhi
items.x: Multi-agent LLM frameworks typically fix their team topology at boot time. When an individual agent becomes overloaded at runtime, for example by mixing too many action categories, accumulating tool errors, or queueing behind too many calls, the system has no mechanism to restructure itself. We introduce Autonomous Topology Mutation (ATM), a runtime team-mutation mechanism for multi-agent LLM frameworks. ATM combines…
items.sm: Introduces a mechanism that detects overloaded language model agents and restructures their teams during execution, subject to capability, state routing, and validation safeguards.

items.t: Toward Scalable LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration: A Dynamic Task Graph Approach with Asynchronous Parallel Execution
items.a: Junwei Yu, Yepeng Ding, Jiani Dai, Junjun Zheng, Jingchi Wu, Hiroyuki Satō
items.sm: Introduces DynTaskMAS, which updates task dependency graphs during execution to coordinate parallel work among language model agents.

items.t: An Infectious Disease Spread Simulation Based on Large Language Model Decision Making
items.a: Yonchanok Khaokaew, Ruochen Kong, Andreas Zufle, Hao Xue, Taylor Anderson, Chandini Raina MacIntyre, Matthew Scotch, Flora D. Salim
items.x: Modelling individual decision-making during infectious disease outbreaks is crucial for understanding behavioural dynamics and informing effective public health interventions. Prior work has shown that large language models can simulate realistic human behaviour by generating agent decisions based on demographic prompts and situational context. We build on this foundation with a spatially grounded, agent-based simula…
items.sm: Builds an infectious disease simulation using language model decisions and census-based populations to represent geographically varied behavior around influenza-like illness.

items.t: PREreview of "Quantum-Enhanced LLM Cascade Routing: A QAOA Approach to Cost-Optimal Model Selection in Multi-Agent Systems"
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Reviews research that formulates language model routing as a combinatorial optimization problem and tests a quantum optimization approach on IBM hardware.

items.t: Agent Rooms: A Conceptual Framework for Persistent Human-Governed Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes persistent collaboration spaces that organize human and AI participants, shared artifacts, memory, policies, and oversight for ongoing multi-agent work.

items.t: Multi-Agent Systems and Their Evolution: A Comparative Survey
items.a: Asifullah Khan, Hamna Asif, Maha Tariq, Hania Khan, Inaya Imran, Nayab Ibrahim, Aqsa Asif, Zunaira Rauf
items.sm: Surveys the evolution of multi-agent systems, including language model frameworks that coordinate specialized agents for complex tasks.

items.t: CollabSim: A CSCW-Grounded Methodology for Investigating Collaborative Competence of LLM Agents through Controlled Multi-Agent Experiments
items.a: Jiaju Chen, Bo Sun, Yuxuan Lu, Yun Wang, Dakuo Wang, Bingsheng Yao
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models have shown growing promise, with their effectiveness resting on agents' ability to coordinate through text-based channels much as human teams do. Yet recent study suggests that MAS often falter not because agents lack individual task-solving ability, but because they lack collaborative competence: the capacity to establish common ground, maintain shared task un…
items.sm: Introduces controlled multi-agent experiments informed by cooperative work research to evaluate language model agents' shared understanding, coordination, and repair of misunderstandings.

items.t: Trust-Regulated Dependence Networks for Multi-Agent Cooperation: A Simulation Study
items.sm: Simulates trust-based partner selection and finds that permissive cooperation increases total utility and spending, while selective cooperation improves economic efficiency but reduces task completion.

items.t: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
items.a: Shangheng Du, Xiangchao Yan, Jinxin Shi, Zongsheng Cao, Shiyang Feng, Zichen Liang, Boyuan Sun, Xu Guo
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to long-horizon tasks such as scientific discovery and machine learning engineering (MLE), where sustained self-evolution becomes a key capability. However, existing MLE agents suffer from isolated exploration, inefficient experience reuse, and lack of hierarchical control, which together hinder long-horizon optimization. We present MLEvolve, an LLM-based sel…
items.sm: Introduces MLEvolve, a multi-agent framework that combines graph-based search, experience reuse, and hierarchical control to discover machine learning algorithms.

items.t: Beyond Alignment: Value Diversity as a Collective Property in Multicultural Agent Systems
items.a: Shaoyang Xu, Jingshen Zhang, Long P. Hoang, Jinyuan Li, Wenxuan Zhang
items.x: Multicultural multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in globally diverse settings, where different agents are grounded in different cultural backgrounds. Existing cultural evaluation focuses on value alignment: how closely a single agent matches a target culture. Yet alignment is a per-agent property and cannot reveal whether a system, taken as a whole, preserves the cultural plurality it is meant to represent…
items.sm: Proposes measuring cultural value diversity across agent systems and finds that it is largely unrelated to individual agents' alignment with target cultures.

items.t: Critic-Guided Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reasoning for Reliable Mathematical Problem Solving
items.x: Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive reasoning abilities; but they are still susceptible to hallucinations, intermediate reasoning mistakes, and unreliable reasoning results in complex mathematical reasoning problems. In this study, we introduce a critic-based heterogeneous multi-agent approach to improve the dependability of mathematical reasoning. This framework incorporates several LLM agents …
items.sm: Introduces specialized mathematical reasoning agents whose proposed solutions undergo validator criticism and revision to correct intermediate errors.

items.t: edihasaj/universal-memory-protocol
items.x: Universal Memory Protocol (UMP) - an open standard for agent memory. The third interop layer beside MCP (tools) and A2A (coordination).
items.sm: Defines an open standard for agent memory intended to complement existing protocols for tool access and agent coordination.

items.t: Streaming Communication in Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.a: Yang, Zhen, Xu, Xiaogang, Wang, Wen et al.
items.sm: Introduces streaming communication between reasoning agents to reduce pipeline latency and argues that sharing earlier reasoning steps also limits downstream errors.

items.sm: Reports that MACU coordinates computer-use agents through dynamic task graphs, improving benchmark performance by 4.7–25.5% and delivering a 1.5-fold speedup on Odysseys.

items.sm: Argues that coordinating multiple computer-use agents improves reliability and speed, reporting success rate gains of 3.4–25.5% and up to a 1.5-fold speedup.

items.t: Internet of Agentic AI: Incentive-Compatible Distributed Teaming and Workflow
items.v: International Symposium on Modeling and Optimization in Mobile, Ad Hoc, and Wireless Networks (WiOpt)
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled a new class of agentic AI systems that reason, plan, and act by invoking external tools. However, most existing agentic architectures remain centralized and monolithic, limiting scalability, specialization, and interoperability. This paper proposes a framework for scalable agentic intelligence, termed the Internet of Agentic AI, in which autonomous, heterogeneous agents distr…
items.sm: Proposes decentralized coalition formation for distributed AI agents, combining task capability requirements, network locality, and economic incentives to organize workflows.

items.t: A Survey on Multi-Agent LLM Frameworks with Semantic Memory Integration and Dynamic DAG Orchestration
items.a: Tummanapudi Divya, Vempaty Prashanthi, Vaskula Srikanth, Venu Gopalachari M
items.v: International Conference on Inventive Research in Computing Applications (ICIRCA)
items.sm: Surveys multi-agent language model frameworks that combine specialized roles, semantic memory, and dynamic task graph orchestration.

items.t: Channel Fracture: Three Instances of Cross-Boundary Silent Delivery Reliability Failures in Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: We report the discovery of channel fracture, a silent architectural failure in multi-agent systems where information routed across agent boundaries is silently blocked by invisible constraints. We present three instances in a production Hermes Agent deployment: (1) cron memory injection blocked by scheduler barriers; (2) cross-profile skill routing fractured by recursive directory traversal; (3) WebSocket delivery co…
items.sm: Reports three communication failures across agent boundaries and claims a verification protocol eliminated failures in its trials.

items.t: AgentJet: A Distributed Swarm Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Qingxu Fu, Boyin Liu, Shuchang Tao, Zhaoyang Liu, Cheng Chen, Xuanfa Jin, Rong Zhu, Bolin Ding
items.x: Training reinforcement learning (RL) policies for large language model (LLM) agents requires optimizing multi-turn trajectories that interact with external environments. Existing training frameworks struggle with runtime failures, single-model constraints, incompatible task environments, and redundant context. We present AgentJet, a distributed swarm training framework based on a decoupled multi-node architecture. Ag…
items.sm: Introduces AgentJet, which separates model training servers from agent execution clients to support distributed reinforcement learning, multiple models, and fault recovery.

items.t: Ahoy: LLMs Enacting Multiagent Interaction Protocols
items.a: Omkar Sunil Joshi, Munindar Paul Singh, Amit K. Chopra
items.x: An interaction protocol formalizes how the agents in a multiagent system interact, which facilitates implementing agents. Existing approaches yield agent implementations specific to the selected protocols. How can we engineer intelligent agents that can enact protocols but are programming-free? Our contribution, Ahoy, addresses this question by creating LLM agents that dynamically select and enact declarative protoco…
items.sm: Introduces Ahoy, which enables language model agents to select and follow declarative interaction protocols, including concurrent protocols, without specialized training.

items.t: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems for Clinical Workflows: A Survey of AI Hospitals
items.a: Association for Computational Linguistics 2026, Zonghai Yao, Hong Yu
items.sm: Surveys clinical multi-agent systems and proposes evaluating complete workflows through agent roles, handoffs, evidence, safety controls, and accountability.

items.t: The Structural Turn in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Why Coordination, Composition, and Timing — Not Individual Reasoning — Determine Whether These Systems Work
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues that coordination structures, communication, timing, and protocols explain major failures in multi-agent language model systems beyond individual reasoning ability.

items.t: Token Budget Contracts for Multi-Agent Large Language Model Orchestration with Confidence-Gated Retrieval
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes per-agent token contracts, priority-based budget redistribution, and confidence-based retrieval thresholds to manage resource consumption and response quality.

items.t: SMADE-IE: Sparse Multi-Agent Framework with Evidence-Driven Debate for Zero-Shot Information Extraction
items.a: Kenfeng Huang, Yi Cai, Xin Wu, Zikun Deng, Li Yuan
items.x: Zero-shot information extraction (IE) with large language models (LLMs) enables adaptation to new schemas and domains without task-specific training. Existing methods mainly follow three paradigms. Monolithic prompting is efficient but prone to missed mentions, boundary errors, and type confusion. Each-type prompting improves type-level focus but may produce overlapping or conflicting predictions, while multi-agent d…
items.sm: Introduces an information extraction framework that routes inputs by complexity and uses evidence-based agent debate to resolve conflicting predictions.

items.t: "Synthetic Hawthorne Effect in LLM Agents: Debate Corpus and Lexical Robustness Dataset"
items.a: Vinicius Covas Alves, Jorge Alberto Hidalgo Toledo
items.sm: Provides multi-agent debate data, prompts, and linguistic analyses across five observation conditions to support research on how monitoring contexts affect language model behavior.

items.t: Agent Newsroom: Efficient Chronological Report Generation via Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Association for Computational Linguistics 2026, Yue Geng, Bang Wang, Zhenhua Wang, Chunlei Wang
items.sm: Introduces a newsroom-style multi-agent framework that allocates evidence, drafts chronological events, and reconciles overlapping reports to improve timeline coverage and reduce redundancy.

items.t: Leibniz: Theory-of-Mind Driven Neuro-Symbolic Logical Reasoning via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Association for Computational Linguistics 2026, Yue Fan, Ru Li, Hongye Tan, Yuanlong Wang, Hao Zhan, Guangjun Zhang, Hu Zhang
items.sm: Introduces Leibniz, which coordinates forward and backward reasoning agents to clarify rules, resolve belief conflicts, and support multi-step logical inference.

items.t: Scaling External Knowledge Input Beyond Context Windows of LLMs via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Association for Computational Linguistics 2026, Fei Huang, Peng Li, Yang Liu, Zijun Liu, Zhennan Wan, Ming Yan
items.sm: Introduces ExtAgents, which distributes external knowledge across multiple agents to handle inputs beyond individual context windows without longer-context training.

items.t: LeanMarathon: Toward Reliable AI Co-Mathematicians through Long-Horizon Lean Autoformalization
items.a: Yuanhe Zhang, Yuekai Sun, Taiji Suzuki, Jason D. Lee, Fanghui Liu
items.x: Long-horizon autoformalization of research mathematics fails not only at hard lemmas, but at scale: statements drift, dependencies tangle, context decays, and local repairs corrupt distant work. We present LeanMarathon, a multi-agent harness for reliable research-level Lean autoformalization. Its core abstraction is an evolving blueprint: a Lean file that serves simultaneously as formal proof skeleton, natural-langua…
items.sm: Introduces LeanMarathon, which coordinates construction, auditing, proving, and repair agents around a shared Lean blueprint to manage long mathematical formalization projects.

items.t: SANEmerg: An Emergent Communication Framework for Semantic-aware Agentic AI Networking
items.a: Y H Xiao, Haoran Zhou, Yi Zhou, Marwan Krunz
items.v: International Symposium on Modeling and Optimization in Mobile, Ad Hoc, and Wireless Networks (WiOpt)
items.x: Future networking systems are envisioned to become part of an agentic AI-native ecosystem in which a vast number of heterogeneous and specialized AI agents cooperate seamlessly to fulfill complex user requirements in real time. items.sm: Proposes a communication framework that interprets user intent, assigns subtasks to specialized agents, and lets agents develop task-specific signaling protocols.

items.t: GARL: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent Strategic Prioritisation
items.a: Yuxiao Ye, Yiwen Zhang, Huiyuan Xie, Yuqin Huang, Zhiyuan Liu
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems are increasingly used for strategic decision-making tasks. In such settings, performance depends not only on individual model capabilities, but also on the policies by which agents interact and adapt. Multi-agent reinforcement learning can optimise these interaction policies, but its reward design often remains task-specific and weakly grounded in interaction structure. To address this g…
items.sm: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework that uses game-theoretic rewards to train competing agents and an arbiter to prioritize shared candidates.

items.t: Deliberate Topology Selection as a First-Class Design Variable: How Multi-Agent Systems Learn When to Reconfigure, Prune, and Restructure Communication Graphs
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues from seven preprints that agents should deliberately adjust communication connections during execution according to task state, budgets, and confidence.

items.t: G-D1 PROTEA: Offline Evaluation and Iterative Refinement for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
items.a: Association for Computational Linguistics 2026, Kazuki Kawamura, Kei Tateno, Satoshi Waki
items.sm: Introduces an interface that evaluates intermediate workflow outputs and displays diagnostic information on agent graphs to help developers locate and fix errors.

items.t: AgentAsk: Multi-Agent Systems Need to Ask

items.t: Oblivious Learning and Collusive Pricing
items.x: On a platform with many sellers, should a pricing algorithm explicitly model competitors' prices when learning demand? Classical arguments suggest that ignoring competitors induces model misspecification and inefficiency, yet findings from algorithmic collusion suggest that ignoring competitor prices may, surprisingly, facilitate collusive outcomes and improve profits. We study this problem in a competitive market wi…
items.sm: Studies sellers that ignore competitors’ prices, finding they need stronger price exploration and reach competitive prices when all sellers maintain persistent exploration.

items.t: Failure Modes of Deep Multi-Agent RL in Asynchronous Pricing: Reproducible Triggers, Trace Diagnostics, and a Partial Fix
items.x: We study two reproducible failure modes of deep multi-agent reinforcement learning in continuous-time pricing markets: (i) tacit cartel formation between competing DDPG agents, and (ii) actor--critic instability at high event rates. We instantiate both inside a single CT-MARL benchmark (Poisson-clocked price updates, observation latency $δ$, interior-optimum logit demand), show that synchronous DDPG agents reliably t…
items.sm: Finds that asynchronous pricing and observation delays partially reduce collusion among reinforcement learning agents, while frequent price updates can destabilize learning.

items.t: The Agentic Attack Surface Is Already Weaponized: A Synthesis of Concurrent Threats Against LLM-Driven Pipelines
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Synthesizes eight studies to argue that agent security failures primarily arise when attacker-controlled content crosses trust boundaries between tools, memory, and communication.

items.t: Strabo: Declarative Specification and Implementation of Agentic Interaction Protocols
items.a: Samuel H. Christie V, Amit K. Chopra, Munindar Paul Singh

items.sm: Models checkout interactions using declarative protocols and demonstrates that agents implementing those protocols can interoperate with Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol agents.

items.t: Mixture-of-Minds: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Table Understanding

items.t: Dynamic Generation of Multi LLM Agents Communication Topologies with Graph Diffusion Models

items.t: What Should Agents Say? Action-state Communication for Efficient Multi-Agent Systems
