items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models are typically organized around roles, pipelines, and turn schedules, while the content that agents pass to one another is often left as unconstrained natural language. However, this free-form communication can rapidly inflate token usage, consume the shared context window, and ultimately affect both system performance and inference cost. We analyze five common …

items.a: Songjie Xie, H L Li, Zixin Wang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

items.t: HMARS: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Memory System for Long-Context Reasoning
items.a: Zeju Li, Ziyang Zheng, Yizhou Zhou, Qiang Xu
items.x: Long-context reasoning requires models to access, retrieve, and integrate evidence scattered across documents, dialogues, and accumulated interaction histories. Standard retrieval-augmented generation reduces this problem to top-$K$ chunk retrieval, but such passive access can discard relevant evidence before reasoning begins, especially when relevance depends on broader context. We propose HMARS, a hierarchical mult…
items.sm: Introduces hierarchical memory management in which agents maintain document regions, coordinate evidence retrieval, and supply evidence to a final reasoning model.

items.t: Description-Code Inconsistency in Real-world MCP Servers: Measurement, Detection, and Security Implications
items.a: Yutao Shi, Xiaohan Zhang, Xiangjing Zhang, Xihua Shen, Hui Ouyang, Huming Qiu, Mi Zhang, Min Yang
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has emerged as a critical standard empowering Large Language Models (LLMs) to utilize external tools. In this ecosystem, LLMs rely on natural language descriptions provided by MCP servers to select and execute functions. This interaction implicitly assumes that tool descriptions faithfully reflect their underlying implementations, while this assumption is not mandatorily verified in p…
items.sm: Studies mismatches between MCP tool descriptions and implementations, defining categories covering incorrect functionality descriptions and undeclared side effects.

items.t: StepFinder: A Temporal Semantic Framework for Failure Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Taiyu Zhu, Yifan Wu, Weilin Jin, Ying Li, Gang Huang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems exhibit remarkable collaborative capabilities in complex multi-step tasks. However, these systems are highly sensitive to single-step execution errors that can propagate through agent interactions and lead to cascading failures. To understand the causes of failure and improve system reliability, failure attribution has been introduced as a task that aims to automatically identify the roo…
items.sm: Introduces a lightweight framework for identifying the execution step responsible for failures in multi-agent systems while reducing reliance on expensive log analysis.

items.t: SPOQ: Specialist Orchestrated Queuing for Multi-Agent Software Engineering
items.x: Multi-agent AI systems show promise for automating software engineering tasks, yet existing approaches suffer from coordination overhead, quality control gaps, and limited human oversight. We introduce SPOQ (Specialist Orchestrated Queuing), a methodology combining three innovations: (1) wave-based topological dispatch that computes parallel execution waves from task dependency graphs; (2) dual validation gates apply…
items.sm: Introduces a software engineering workflow combining dependency-based execution waves, planning and code validation, specialized agents, and human participation.

items.t: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
items.x: How much should an LLM agent remember, and how should multi-agent systems be connected when trying to reach consensus? We show these two design choices interact in a way that flips the sign of memory's effect on coordination. Across 432 simulation runs of a networked Naming Game on eight fixed 16-agent topologies, we vary memory depth and network structure. Longer memory slows the time to reach steady state in decent…
items.sm: Finds that longer memory slows settling in decentralized agent networks but accelerates fragmented settling in centralized networks, revealing a tradeoff between speed and agreement.

items.t: OpenAgenet / OAN White Paper: Open Infrastructure for Trusted Agent Interconnection
items.x: OpenAgenet (OAN) is an open infrastructure project for trusted Agent interconnection across independently operated networks. It addresses the verification of resource identity, governance state, discovery authorization, and freshness before interaction. OAN combines decentralized identifiers (DIDs), verifiable credentials (VCs), and on-chain infrastructure governance with a routing-aware did:oan registration and disc…
items.sm: Proposes infrastructure for trusted agent interconnection using decentralized identities, verifiable credentials, governed registration, and authorized discovery across independently operated networks.

items.t: OpenAgenet / OAN Yellow Paper: Technical Architecture for Trust-Governed Resource Identity and Discovery
items.x: This yellow paper specifies the technical architecture and verification semantics of OpenAgenet (OAN), a protocol-neutral trust layer for heterogeneous Agent resources. The design combines did:oan decentralized identifiers (DIDs), verifiable credentials (VCs), on-chain infrastructure governance, and Root-verified resource packages. It defines the objects and lifecycle transitions that connect subject-control verifica…
items.sm: Specifies identity verification, governance requirements, resource lifecycles, and authorized discovery for a trust layer connecting heterogeneous agent resources.

items.t: SMAC-Talk: A Natural Language Extension of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge for Large Language Models
items.x: As LLMs become more widely deployed, they are increasingly expected to work alongside other AI agents rather than operating in isolation. Effective coordination in these settings requires agents to communicate, share information and make decisions under uncertainty. We introduce SMAC-Talk, a natural language extension of the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge for evaluating LLM-based agents in cooperative multi-agent en…
items.sm: Extends the StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge with natural language communication to evaluate cooperative agents, including scenarios where deceptive messages attempt to disrupt coordination.

items.t: Multi$^2$: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Decision-Making with LLM-Based Agents in Interactive Environments
items.x: A central goal of large language model (LLM) research is to build agentic systems that can plan, act, and adapt through sustained interaction with dynamic environments. While recent LLM-based agents exhibit impressive contextual reasoning, their long-horizon decision-making remains fragile, often suffering from objective drift, where goals and plans drift over extended interactions. We introduce Multi$^2$, a hierarch…
items.sm: Introduces a hierarchical framework separating subgoal generation from action execution to reduce goal drift and support sustained interaction with dynamic environments.

items.t: The Deliberative Illusion: Diagnosing Factual Attrition and Stance Homogenization in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
items.a: Herun Wan, Jiaying Wu, Minnan Luo, Fanxiao Li, Ningnan Wang, Nancy F. Chen, Min-Yen Kan
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems often treat consensus as evidence of successful interaction. For deliberative problems, however, reliability depends on whether agents preserve the facts and viewpoints needed to interpret an issue. We identify the deliberative illusion: discussion produces (1) factual attrition, the progressive loss of issue-critical facts, alongside (2) stance homogenization, the collapse of diverse position…
items.sm: Introduces a framework for tracking evidence during agent deliberation and reports discussions can erase up to 72% of critical facts while viewpoints converge.

items.t: mcp-safeguard: An Automated Security Scanner for Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers

items.t: MOSAIC: Efficient Mixture-of-Agent Scheduling via Adaptive Aggregation and Inference Concurrency
items.a: Saptarshi Mitra, Yifan Zhang, Rachid Karami, Sreetama Sarkar, Phyo Pyae Moe Aung, Nazmul Takbir, Souvik Kundu, Sitao Huang
items.x: Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) systems improve reasoning accuracy by routing each query to multiple expert LLMs and aggregating their outputs. Efficiently executing this workload on limited GPU resources has bottlenecks. Skill-based routing creates skewed expert demand, and combining instruction-tuned LLMs with long-reasoning models results in extreme variability in generation lengths. Consequently, traditional scheduling s…
items.sm: MOSAIC schedules mixture-of-agents workloads using expert placement, predicted response lengths, adaptive aggregation, and concurrent inference to reduce GPU idle time.

items.t: Consensus is Strategically Insufficient: Reasoning-Trace Disagreement as a Knowledge-Representation Signal
items.x: Multi-agent systems are commonly designed to reduce disagreement through voting, consensus protocols, debate, or fault-tolerant aggregation. We argue that this objective is insufficient for value-laden tasks, where disagreement may reflect genuine normative uncertainty rather than agent error. Building on prior work on reasoning-trace disagreement in human-AI collaborative moderation, we propose a knowledge-represent…
items.sm: Argues that agent consensus can conceal normative uncertainty and proposes classifying disagreements by reasoning similarity and decision agreement to guide subsequent actions.

items.t: Enhancing Operational Safety via Agentic Dialogue Hazard Identification Analysis
items.a: Sanjay Das, Ran Elgedawy, Ethan Seefried, Ryan Burchfield, Tirthankar Ghosal
items.x: Operational safety in high-stakes domains such as industrial process control, autonomous, and safety-critical systems, demand reliable hazard identification. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in automating safety analysis tasks, single-turn, monolithic inference is brittle: it lacks the self-correction, deliberation, and contextual refinement that safety engineers apply iteratively. In this paper,…
items.sm: HAZDIAL compares structured agent debate and constructive discussion with single-pass language models for identifying operational hazards.

items.t: Think-Before-Speak: From Internal Evaluation to Public Expression in Multi-Agent Social Simulation
items.a: Kaiqi Yang, Tai-Quan Peng, Sanguk Lee, Hui Liu
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent simulation offers a promising way to study social interaction, deliberation, and collective opinion dynamics. However, many existing dialogue simulation frameworks represent interaction mainly as observable turn exchange or aggregated outputs, leaving the internal evaluative processes behind silence, speaking intention, and public expression difficult to examine. We introduce TBS (Think-Before-S…
items.sm: Think-Before-Speak simulates social dialogue by separating agents' private evaluations, willingness to speak, and public statements.

items.t: Capability Advertisement as a Market for Lemons: A Trust Layer for Heterogeneous Agent Networks
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents have begun to delegate work to one another. Protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the Agent2Agent protocol (A2A) let an agent publish what it can do and let others call it, and public registries of such agents are already appearing. These protocols assume an advertised capability is a static, truthful fact. A real agent is none of these things: its competence is prob…
items.sm: Argues that unverifiable capability claims create market failures in agent networks and motivates a trust layer for assessing providers.

Beyond the need for specialized manipulation skills, effective information…

items.t: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
items.a: Akash Kumar Ghosh, Tajamul Ashraf, Rishu Kumar Singh, Numan Saeed, Sriparna Saha, Xiuying Chen, Salman Khan
items.x: Multimodal agentic pipelines are advancing human-computer interaction by enabling efficient automation of complex real-world tasks, yet current work largely focuses on short-horizon or general-purpose settings, leaving long-horizon, domain-specific automation, especially in healthcare, underexplored. To address this, we introduce CareFlow, a human-annotated benchmark of complex, long-horizon workflows across medical …
items.sm: Introduces a healthcare workflow benchmark and an actor-critic agent framework that uses tools, memory, and corrective feedback to automate lengthy computer tasks.

items.t: MARS-RL: Enhancing Multi-Agent RAG Systems for Multi-Modal Documents via Strategic Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning
items.sm: Uses reinforcement learning to train a strategic coordinator that dynamically guides collaborating agents retrieving information from multimodal documents.

items.t: Easier to Mislead Than to Correct: Harmful and Beneficial Revision in LLM Conformity
items.a: Jiaming Qu, Lucheng Fu, Yibo Hu
items.x: Large language models are increasingly used in multi-agent systems, where they see and respond to other agents' answers. A key risk is conformity: a model may abandon its own answer simply because others agree on a different one. Prior studies show that LLMs often revise toward a majority answer, but it remains unclear whether these revisions help correct mistakes as often as they introduce new errors. In this paper,…
items.sm: Finds that peer agreement more readily causes language models to abandon correct answers than helps them correct initially wrong answers.

items.t: EvoPool: Evolutionary Programmatic Annotation for Label-Efficient Specialized Supervision
items.a: Tianyi Xu, Yaolun Zhang, Xuan Ouyang, Huazheng Wang
items.x: Large language models excel at general tasks but underperform smaller supervised models in specialized, high-stakes domains where training labels are costly. We address this regime with EvoPool, an evolutionary multi-agent framework inspired by Darwinian evolution. Three specialized agents iteratively propose executable annotator code, a small validation set provides a fitness signal, and a deterministic gate keeps o…
items.sm: Evolves executable labeling programs through specialized agents and validation checks, then combines their votes into inexpensive training labels for specialized tasks.

items.t: SafeMCP: Proactive Power Regulation for LLM Agent Defense via Environment-Grounded Look-Ahead Reasoning
items.a: Lichao Wang, Zhaoxing Ren, Tianzhuo Yang, Jiaming Ji, Chi Harold Liu, Yaodong Yang, Juntao Dai
items.x: As Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly leverage the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to operate in complex environments, the expansion of their action spaces offers agents unsafe capabilities and underscores the risk of power-seeking. While broad action space and greater environment influence are essential for task fulfillment, they create a fragile risk surface where minor errors or hallucinations are magnifi…
items.sm: Proposes a server-side defense that predicts future risks to restrict agents' access to hazardous tools and intervene when necessary.

items.t: Deuz-AI/Deuz-SDK
items.x: TypeScript AI SDK and agent framework with zero dependencies. Build production AI agents and multi-agent swarms: durable execution, long-term memory, hybrid RAG, MCP client/server, A2A, human-in-the-loop approvals, CodeAct sandboxes, realtime voice. One streaming API, 29 providers: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama. Node, Bun, Deno, edge.
items.sm: Provides a dependency-free TypeScript framework for building agents with persistent execution, memory, retrieval, tool protocols, approvals, sandboxes, and voice across multiple model providers.

items.t: varmabudharaju/agent-pd
items.x: A police department for your Claude Code agents — a logging-only hook + CLI that audits the main agent and every subagent and reports rule offenses (permission bypass, out-of-scope & credential access, self-permissioning, disallowed tools, redundant, off-task) with quoted evidence. Catch-and-report, never blocks.
items.sm: Audits Claude Code agents and subagents through logging hooks, reporting rule violations with supporting evidence without blocking their actions.

items.t: SourceShift/mini-ork
items.x: Prove an AI-written fix actually fixes the bug. mini-ork certify reproduces the bug against your repo's own code, attacks the patch with generated invariants in a Docker sandbox, and returns PROVEN / REFUTED / UNVERIFIED with a JSON certificate. Part of a verifier-gated, multi-model agent runtime.
items.sm: Evaluates AI-written fixes by reproducing bugs and testing generated invariants in Docker, returning a verification verdict and JSON certificate.

items.t: The Ringelmann Effect in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Scaling Law for Effective Team Size
items.sm: Derives a scaling law for effective agent team size, distinguishing regimes where additional agents provide capped, sublinear, or linear growth in independent evidence.

items.t: Post-Deterministic Distributed Systems: A New Foundation for Trustworthy Autonomous Infrastructure
items.x: For decades, distributed systems have typically assumed that correct participants execute protocol-specified behavior with stable, externally defined, and deterministic semantics. Classical theory has extensively parameterized network timing, communication topologies, and failure domains, but this participant model has remained comparatively fixed. The integration of autonomous reasoning engines, stochastic model-dri…
items.sm: Proposes a distributed systems model accommodating autonomous participants whose reasoning and execution differ while producing semantically equivalent outcomes.

items.t: LLM Consortium for Software Design Refinement: A Controlled Experiment on Multi-Agent Collaboration Topologies
items.x: We present a controlled experiment evaluating 12 multi-agent LLM collaboration topologies for software architecture design. Using a $2\times2\times2$ factorial design (Authority $\times$ Roles $\times$ Dynamics), we conducted 520 experimental runs across 8 design tasks of varying complexity, with 5 repetitions each. Designs were evaluated on a 12-dimensional rubric by three independent automated evaluators (GPT-OSS 1…
items.sm: Compares twelve agent collaboration structures for software design, finding adversarial rewriting and review across different models receive the highest aggregate evaluator scores.

items.t: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?
items.a: Xuancheng Zhu, Yang Yue, Shuaibing Wan, Zihan Dou, Xiaohan Zhang, Yongrui Liu, Guoshun Nan
items.x: Large language agents are increasingly used for social simulation, yet it remains unclear whether they can sustain coherent behavior in structured organizations, where goals must propagate through hierarchy, tasks depend on prior execution, and artifacts accumulate over long horizons. We formulate long-horizon organizational simulation as a memory-centered coordination problem and introduce TaskWeave, a hierarchical …
items.sm: Introduces TaskWeave, which combines hierarchical planning and dependency-aware memory to sustain coherent organizational behavior in a simulated year-long IT company.

items.t: FinCom: A Financial Multi-Agent Demo with Disagree-or-Commit Deliberation
items.a: Chao Peter Yang, Zixiao Tan, Kaisen Yao, Ziyu Zhou, Eleanor Jiang, Michael Wu
items.x: Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for financial analysis and decision support. However, existing coordination schemes, especially those emphasizing consensus or debate, are vulnerable to sycophancy: agents conform to peer reasoning instead of evidence, leading to premature agreement and degraded outcomes. We introduce FinCom (Financial Committee), a governed multi-agent…
items.sm: Introduces a financial agent committee whose research, quantitative, and risk specialists must explicitly critique or accept peer reasoning before reaching a shared decision.

items.t: Recognize Your Orchestrator: An Entropy Dynamics Perspective for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Junze Zhu, Weihao Chen, Xuanwang Zhang, Zhen Wu, Xinyu Dai
items.x: The transition from single-turn models to Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) promises enhanced problem-solving capabilities, yet the centralized orchestration topology remains a critical point of fragility. To analyze this, we propose a Mean-Field Entropy Dynamics framework, modeling the orchestration process as a system governed by the competing forces of task resolution and cumulative context loading. To facilitate validati…
items.sm: Models centralized agent orchestration through competing effects of task completion and accumulating context, using generated benchmarks to examine stability and performance collapse.

items.t: Early Diagnosis of Wasted Computation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Failure-Aware Observability
items.a: Xianyou Li, Weiran Yan, Yichao Wu, Penghao Liang, Mengwei Yuan, Jianan Liu, Jing Yang
items.x: Failure-aware observability diagnoses wasted computation in multi-agent LLM systems before final-answer evaluation can explain what went wrong. We propose a trace-based framework for a three-agent architecture -- orchestrator, search agent, and execution agent -- that converts structured events into online signals for loops, budget pressure, low information gain, and tool instability, then adds offline semantic groun…
items.sm: Detects wasted agent computation from execution traces and reports that warning-triggered interventions reduced the share of tokens spent after warnings in a small pilot.

items.t: A Meta-Cognitive Adapter for Mitigating Social Conformity in Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System

items.v: The Journal of the Korean Institute of Information and Communication Engineering
items.sm: Uses estimated conformity scores to adjust internal model representations, reporting reduced uncritical agreement with other agents while preserving natural responses.

items.t: When Parallelism Pays Off: Cohesion-Aware Task Partitioning for Multi-Agent Coding
items.a: Xu Yang, Lunyiu Nie, Ethan Chandra, Stanislav Gannutin, Fangru Lin, Swarat Chaudhuri
items.x: Multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems offer a way to decompose complex tasks, such as coding, through parallelization and context isolation. However, adding agents in practice introduces inter-agent communication overhead, which incurs extra cost and can sometimes offset the efficiency gains. We formalize multi-agent orchestration as a graph partitioning problem that captures the communication-to-computation…
items.sm: Partitions coding tasks using dependency graphs and community detection to balance parallel execution gains against communication costs between agents.

items.t: Harness Engineering: The Meta Layer as a First-Class Discipline for Multi-Agent Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues that agent orchestration, memory, verification, and governance form a distinct engineering discipline, and proposes modular mechanisms for governing teams of agents.

items.t: Domination-Avoiding Learning Agents Cannot Collude
items.x: An influential paper of Calvano et al. empirically demonstrated that Q-learning agents spontaneously collude when placed as sellers that compete on prices in a natural market model. More recent results of Fish et al. empirically demonstrated that similar collusion happens with commercial LLMs. We formally prove that such collusion can also happen with external-regret-minimizing agents. We identify a very general clas…
items.sm: Proves that certain learning agents avoid collusion in pricing markets, while agents minimizing external regret can still collude.

items.sm: Uses adversarial testing and an optimization agent to iteratively revise defense agents' system prompts against jailbreak attacks without updating model weights.

items.t: Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory
items.a: Ruiyin Li, Yiran Zhang, Xiyu Zhou, Yangxiao Cai, Peng Liang, Weisong Sun, Jifeng Xuan, Zhi Jin
items.x: Software architecture design is a critical yet inherently complex and knowledge-intensive phase that requires balancing competing quality attributes and adapting to evolving requirements. Traditionally, this process has been time-consuming, labor-intensive, and heavily reliant on architects, often resulting in limited exploration of alternative architectural decompositions and styles, especially under the pressures o…
items.sm: Proposes four specialized agents supported by external knowledge and hierarchical memory to collaboratively transform software requirements into architectural designs.

items.t: Move the Query, Not the Cache: Characterizing Cross-Instance Latent Attention Redistribution Across GPU Fabrics
items.a: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald Köstler, Gerhard Wellein
items.x: Frontier LLMs increasingly decide what a query attends to with a sparse-attention indexer that picks a few KV-cache blocks per query: attention's unit is now a small, reusable chunk. Agentic workloads hammer it: many sub-agents query one large codebase, reusing the same blocks. When that corpus outgrows one GPU it is partitioned across instances, so a query and the blocks it selects often sit on different GPUs: answe…
items.sm: Examines when routing attention queries between GPUs costs less than transferring selected cache blocks for shared agent workloads using latent attention.

items.t: SS-ZKR: Spatial-Semantic Zero-Knowledge Routing for Privacy-Preserving Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.x: Foundational agent interoperability standards, notably the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), have advanced multi-agent system communication, and complementary identity frameworks leveraging W3C Decentralised Identifiers (DIDs) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) provide cryptographic agent authentication. However, no existing protocol supports content-based semantic routing of agent pay…
items.sm: Proposes routing encrypted agent messages across organizational boundaries using private semantic representations and zero-knowledge proofs, without requiring intermediaries to decrypt their contents.

items.t: Dynamic Coordination Strategy Selection for Enterprise Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Enterprise multi-agent systems increasingly expose multiple coordination patterns, but deployments often lack evidence for when to use consensus, debate, synthesis, or a simpler single-agent workflow. This paper evaluates whether coordination strategy should be selected dynamically by problem class rather than fixed globally. We run a frozen matrix of 30 enterprise tasks spanning six industries, five problem classes,…
items.sm: Evaluates coordination strategies across enterprise tasks and models, finding that exact winning strategies vary across models and the preregistered winner criterion is unsupported.

items.t: Post-Training Recipe, More Than Model Family, Shapes Multi-Agent LLM Conversational Behavior
items.a: Luyang Zhang, Jialu Wang, Fei Xue, Yi-Yun Chu
items.x: Multi-LLM systems use multiple language models to deliberate, judge each other's outputs, or coordinate as agents. Their value depends on the models producing measurably different conversational behaviors when given the same input. Prior offline studies recommend drawing one model per family for behavioral diversity, because LLMs prefer outputs from their own family when rating one another in isolation. Whether the s…
items.sm: Finds that post-training choices and conversational partners can shape model hedging more strongly than model family differences.

items.t: Architectural Choices, Not Model Capabilities, Determine the Social Validity of Multi-Agent LLM Systems

items.t: Not All Flips Are Conformity: Decomposing Stance Convergence in Multi-Agent LLM Debate

items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) among large language models (LLMs) is often judged by answer changes and convergence, yet these outcomes alone cannot establish that peers improved the answer. With five GPT-4o agents on MMLU-Pro disagreement questions, 37% of agent-question pairs change even without peer information. Among pairs stabl…
items.sm: Separates spontaneous answer changes from peer influence in model debates, finding that peer adoption can correct mistakes or introduce errors.

items.t: Design and Evaluation of Multi-Agent AI Oracle Systems for Prediction Market Resolution
items.x: Prediction markets aggregate collective intelligence to forecast uncertain events, but their utility depends on reliable outcome resolution. Existing oracle systems tradeoff fast but brittle automation against accurate but costly human arbitration. Single-LLM oracles achieve meaningful accuracy but inherit all failure modes of their underlying model with no self-correction mechanism. We evaluate whether multi-agent L…
items.sm: Compares independent aggregation and deliberative consensus with single-model oracles on 1,189 prediction market questions using shared, date-filtered evidence.

items.t: Agentic and Multi-agent Systems: A Systematic Review of Tool Use, Benchmarks, and Governance
items.sm: Reviews agentic AI architectures, tool use, benchmarks, applications, safety risks, and governance requirements across recent research.

This raises a question: if we treat the LLM as a CPU, KV cache as processor cache, context window as main memory, and agent framework as an operating system, can decades of compute…

Because these agents condition on natural language game-state descriptions and emit actions through free-form generation, strategic failure modes -- exploiting weaker opponents, coordinating on harmful equilibria, and externalizing costs are inseparable from the language interface itsel…
items.sm: Proposes training strategic language model agents with reward penalties for exploitability, collusion risk, and costs imposed on others.

items.t: Position: Collusion Risks Among AI Reasoning Agents Justify Certification Requirements for Making Market Decisions

This is because integrating these agents into society could collapse the legal evidentiary distinction between competition and collusion among independent firms without erodin…
items.sm: Argues for certification before reasoning agents make market decisions, citing pricing experiments showing persistent tacit collusion and reasoning manipulation that another model failed to detect.

items.t: From Talking Words to Sharing Thoughts: Scalable Multi-LLM Aggregation via Structured Message Passing

Current ensemble methods to combine their complementary expertise primarily rely on iterative re-prompting or cross-model refinement. These approaches suffer from high computational costs and latency because the…
items.sm: Proposes combining specialized model predictions through structured message passing on a factor graph to reduce repeated inference and interference from weaker models.

items.t: How Generation Architecture Shapes Code Complexity in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Paired Study on HumanEval
items.x: Large-language-model code generation has shifted from single-shot prompting to multi-agent orchestrations - analyst, coder, tester, and debugger pipelines - and is evaluated almost exclusively on functional correctness. Whether these architectures also affect the structural complexity of the code they produce, and which orchestration layers carry the cost, remains largely unexamined: prior work has documented prompt-…
items.sm: Compares six agent architectures across HumanEval tasks to examine how orchestration affects generated code size and structural complexity.

items.t: Seeing Before Agreeing: Aligning Multi-Agent Consensus with Visual Evidence
items.a: Yuhan Wang, Shuochen Chang, Yalin Feng, Dongsheng Ma, Yuanzi Li, Zhengren Wang, Yinglong Yang, Yufei Chen
items.x: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on visual question answering (VQA). To mitigate individual hallucinations and blind spots, aggregating diverse perspectives via multi-agent collaboration has emerged as a promising paradigm. While this approach has shown great success in textual QA, its potential in the multimodal domain remains under-explored. Existing multi-agent VQA methods predominant…
items.sm: Proposes aligning the image evidence used by different agents to make consensus in visual question answering more reliable.

items.t: Leveraging the Learning Curve: Reusing Existing Architectural Patterns to Design and Implement MAS
items.a: Arthur Casals, Anarosa A. F. Brandão
items.x: Recent advancements in AI have led to the development of specialized systems related to multi-agent systems (MAS). However, the inherently collaborative nature of agents is often overlooked, and many of these specialized systems are used as components by other AI systems. From a software engineering perspective, this context can benefit from aligning the architectural characteristics of distributed systems with the i…
items.sm: Proposes combining established distributed systems architecture patterns with a small set of agent concepts to guide multi-agent system engineering.

items.t: Learning Multi-Agent Coordination via Sheaf-ADMM
items.a: Jeffrey Seely, Bartłomiej Cupiał, Llion Jones
items.x: We present a differentiable optimization framework for multi-agent coordination. An input is decomposed into overlapping local views, each processed by an agent that solves a convex subproblem parameterized by a neural encoder. Agents coordinate through the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) with inter-agent constraints specified by a cellular sheaf. The sheaf specifies which aspects of neighboring so…
items.sm: Trains agents to coordinate solutions from overlapping local inputs using differentiable optimization and constraints specifying which parts of their solutions must agree.

items.t: zhnt/loushang
items.x: AI-native agent harness for coding workflows by python: multi-model LLM orchestration, stateful sessions, tool governance,   traceable delivery, and provider routing for GPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM, and MiniMax.
items.sm: Provides a Python framework for coding agents with multiple model providers, persistent sessions, tool controls, execution tracing, and request routing.

items.x: Multi Agent for Business Automation is a multi-agent orchestration platform for business automation and decision support. It coordinates specialized AI agents—each with distinct roles, personalities, and tools—through LangGraph workflows, shared memory, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval gates.
items.sm: Coordinates specialized agents for business automation and decision support using LangGraph workflows, shared memory, and human approval steps.

items.sm: Manages coding agents across repositories through desktop and terminal interfaces, with persistent messaging and policy-based supervision.

items.sm: Claims Claude Code can generate and strictly execute ordered workflow plans coordinating hundreds of agents when prompted to create a workflow.

items.sm: Describes how to activate Claude Code dynamic workflows and claims they can launch tens to hundreds of parallel subagents within one session.

items.sm: Reports that Gemini 3.5 Flash powered 93 subagents that built a kernel, filesystem, and drivers capable of booting Doom after 12 hours.

items.sm: Introduces dynamic workflows in Claude Code.

items.sm: Reports that a system card study found multiple agents reached solutions twice as fast on ProgramBench without improving result quality.

items.t: When Cloud Agents Meet Device Agents: Lessons from Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Corrado Rainone, Davide Belli, Bence Major, Arash Behboodi
items.x: The design space of agentic AI inference spans two extremes: frontier large language models (LLMs), typically hosted in the cloud and offering strong performance across a wide range of tasks at substantially high cost, and more cost-efficient small language models (SLMs), which are amenable to on-device inference. Hybrid multi-agent systems (MASs) combining on-device and cloud models offer a promising middle ground, …
items.sm: Examines how combining cloud and on-device agents affects task accuracy, monetary cost, and device energy consumption across hybrid multi-agent architectures.

items.t: Enhancing Multi-Agent Communication through Attention Steering with Context Relevance
items.a: Hongxiang Zhang, Yuan Tian, Tianyi Zhang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems have demonstrated remarkable performance on complex tasks through collaborative reasoning. However, these systems tend to rapidly accumulate extremely long conversation histories during interaction. As conversations lengthen, relevant information is increasingly diluted by irrelevant context, leading to degraded performance. In this work, we present Agent-Radar, a training-free context m…
items.sm: Introduces Agent-Radar, a training-free method that prioritizes relevant conversation context and reports benchmark improvements as agent counts and interaction rounds grow.

items.t: CONCAT: Consensus- and Confidence-Driven Ad Hoc Teaming for Efficient LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Ziyang Ma, Dingyi Zhang, Sichu Liang, Jiajia Chu, Pengfei Xia, Hui Zang, Deyu Zhou
items.x: Although large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems (MAS) show their capability to solve complex tasks and achieve higher performance over single agent systems, they lead to huge computational overheads because of heavy communication between agents. Previous research has made efforts to train a sparse multi-agent graph or fine-tune a planner to orchestrate the workflow better. However, such extra training p…
items.sm: Proposes reducing agent communication without additional training by grouping agents with similar initial answers and choosing group leaders according to confidence.

items.t: Multi-Agent LLM System for Complex Task Solving
items.a: Dhruvakumar V M, Aaron Rajiv, Dimple L, Abhiniraj K
items.v: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
items.sm: Combines planning, execution, evaluation, and coordination agents, claiming higher accuracy, fewer hallucinations, and better reasoning than single-model baselines.

items.t: Collaborative LLM Agents for End-to-End Software Development
items.a: Shweta Garg, Behrooz Omidvar-Tehrani, Sheng‐Yu Fu, Gauthier Guinet, Baishakhi Ray
items.sm: Explains how to design and evaluate collaborative coding agents that plan, implement, test, and review software alongside developers.

items.t: Specialize Roles, Mix Deployments: Pushing the Cost-Accuracy Frontier of LLM Agent Teams
items.a: Yinsicheng Jiang, Liang Cheng, Yeqi Huang, Yufan Zhao, Zhan Lu, Li Dong, Wenda Li, Edoardo Ponti
items.x: LLM agents are increasingly deployed as multi-role teams, where tasks are divided across specialized roles such as planner, executor, and verifier. In these systems, cost and accuracy are no longer properties of a single model: they depend on which model fills each role and where it is hosted, including API, self-hosted, and hybrid deployment. Existing agentic benchmarks typically evaluate fixed models or fixed agent…
items.sm: Introduces AgentCARD to evaluate how assigning models to team roles and choosing hosting arrangements affect cost and accuracy.

items.t: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence
items.a: Yanan Wang, Shuaicong Hu, Jian Liu, Guohui Zhou, Aiguo Wang, Cuiwei Yang
items.x: The impressive performance of generalist large language models (LLMs) such as GPT and Claude in healthcare raises a critical question: will domain-specific medical specialist models become obsolete? We argue that the future of medical artificial intelligence (AI) lies not in building monolithic medical foundation models, nor in replacing human expertise, but in orchestrating collaboration among generalist LLMs, domai…
items.sm: Proposes combining generalist models, medical specialists, and clinicians, reporting better clinical decision performance than either model type alone.

items.t: Evolve as a Team: Collaborative Self-Evolution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zhezheng Hao, Tianfu Wang, Huanshuo Dong, Ziyan Liu, Hong Wang, Xiankun Lin, Qiang Lin, Can Wang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as an effective paradigm for complex and long-horizon tasks. However, in real-world tasks, MAS often exhibit various failures during execution and such failures are difficult to eliminate during design. This motivates experience-driven MAS evolution, where a system improves based on its own execution experience. Yet such evolution is challenging because MAS experience …
items.sm: Introduces Meta-Team, which preserves agents' execution context and supports post-task evidence sharing to improve multi-agent systems through experience.

items.t: AgentSchool: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Simulation for Education
items.a: Yulei Ye, Wenhao Li, Zhong Wen, Yunshu Huang, Yichen Hu, Zifan Wei, Yige Wang, Xinyu Xie
items.x: Despite the rapid deployment of LLMs into classrooms, validating educational AI remains uniquely intractable: interventions act on developing learners whose cognitive and social trajectories are irreversibly shaped, while real-world trials are slow, ethically constrained, and institutionally locked. LLM-based educational simulators have emerged as a potential remedy, but many still collapse learning into persona-cond…
items.sm: Introduces an educational simulator that models student learning through changing knowledge, reasoning processes, and misconceptions rather than persona-based role-play alone.

items.t: LLM and Agents for Recommendation Systems (LARS)
items.a: K. Gopalakrishnan, Qi Xu, Aysenur Inan, Zhigang Hua, Luyi Ma, Prabhat Agarwal, Shuang Yang, Shradha Sehgal
items.sm: Examines agent-based recommendation systems and challenges in explaining coordination, preventing cascading failures, and evaluating trust, fairness, and long-term outcomes.

items.t: Evolutionary Dynamics of Cooperation in Next-Generation LLM Agent Systems: A Cross-Provider Empirical Extension
items.x: Do next-generation LLM agents inherit the cooperative biases documented in their predecessors, or does scale and provider diversity reshape equilibrium behaviour in competitive multi-agent settings? Willis et al. established a benchmark for this question using evolutionary game theory and the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD), finding consistent cooperative biases in ChatGPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. We extend this b…
items.sm: Tests cooperation across four language models using repeated prisoner's dilemma games, finding cooperative tendencies in most model-prompt combinations under balanced, noiseless conditions.

items.t: EASE Configuration Facilitates A Reproducible Science of LLM Social Simulations
items.a: Sneheel Sarangi, Maximilian Puelma Touzel, Aurélien Bück-Kaeffer, Zachary Yang, Jean-François Godbout, Reihaneh Rabbany
items.x: LLMs are increasingly deployed to simulate social interactions, yet many of the existing simulators remain ad hoc and monolithic. This lack of architectural standardization prevents reproducible research and complicates downstream evaluation. We advance a rigorous science of LLM-based multi-agent simulation by modularizing core components into Environments, Agents, Simulation engines, and Evaluation metrics (EASE). W…
items.sm: Proposes a modular structure for reproducible social simulations and introduces SiliSocS, an open-source sandbox organizing environments, agents, simulation engines, and evaluation metrics.

items.t: Dissociative Identity: Language Model Agents Lack Grounding for Reputation Mechanisms
items.a: Botao Amber Hu, Helena Rong, Max Van Kleek
items.x: As autonomous language model agents proliferate, forming an emerging agentic web with real-world consequences, what credibility signals can you use to decide whether to trust an unfamiliar agent in the wild and delegate to it? A natural governance intuition is to extend human identity verification and reputation mechanisms, from "Know Your Customer" and credit scores to "Know Your Agent" regimes. However, we argue th…
items.sm: Argues that reputation mechanisms for language model agents lack foundations because mutable agent components undermine persistent identity, behavioral continuity, and accountability.

items.t: Social Reasoning in Machines: Investigating Collective Truth-Seeking Dynamics in Large Language Model Debate
items.x: Human reasoning has long been theorised to operate socially, not through isolated individual cognition, but through collective adversarial discourse, a framework known as the Argumentative Theory of Reasoning (ATR). Rather than relying on individual "intellectualist reasoners" as the primary vehicle for truth-seeking, ATR reconceptualises truth as an emergent property of social epistemology: the product of imperfect …
items.sm: Investigates whether debates among language models can simulate social reasoning and support collective truth seeking through adversarial discussion.

items.t: Agora: Toward Autonomous Bug Detection in Production-Level Consensus Protocols with LLM Agents
items.a: Xiang Liu, Sa Song, Zhaowei Zhang, Huiying Lan, Jason Zeng, Ming Wu, Michael Heinrich, Yong Sun
items.x: Consensus protocols form the backbone of distributed systems and blockchains, where implementation bugs can cause data corruption and financial losses. While LLM-based approaches show promise in code analysis, they struggle with deep protocol-level logic bugs involving complex state-dependent behaviors across multiple execution stages. We present Agora, a domain-aware multi-agent framework that integrates hypothesis-…
items.sm: Introduces Agora, a specialized agent framework that generates and tests attack scenarios to detect protocol logic bugs in consensus implementations.

items.t: PatchBoard: Schema-Grounded State Mutation for Reliable and Auditable LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Shuyu Zhang, Yaqi Shi, Jiarui Zhang, Yanxiao Zhao, Lu Wang
items.x: LLM multi-agent systems often coordinate through natural-language dialogue or loosely structured shared memory, making intermediate state difficult to validate, attribute, and audit. We introduce PatchBoard, a schema-grounded collaboration architecture that replaces inter-agent dialogue with validated JSON Patch mutations over a shared structured state. An Architect agent constructs a task-specific schema and workflo…
items.sm: Introduces PatchBoard, which coordinates agents through validated changes to shared structured state, reporting higher task success and lower token use than two comparison systems.

items.t: Counterfactual Graph for Multi-Agent LLM Calibration
items.a: Jiatan Huang, Mingchen Li, Ziming Li, Sunjae Kwon, Hong Yu, Chuxu Zhang
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems often treat agreement as evidence: when many agents in a panel give the same answer, that answer is assumed to be more reliable. We show that this assumption can fail after agents communicate. Communication can induce correlated failures and false consensus, so the same vote share may reflect reliable agreement in one topology but over-confidence in another. We propose CAGE-CAL, a counterfactu…
items.sm: Proposes calibrating agent team confidence by comparing communication and no-communication graphs to account for correlated failures and misleading consensus.

items.t: Unifying Temporal and Structural Credit Assignment in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Prompt Optimization
items.a: Wenwu Li, Yuran Song, Mingze Zhao, Bo Jin, Wenhao Li
items.x: While Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) empower Large Language Models to tackle complex reasoning tasks through collaborative interaction, optimizing their dynamics remains a formidable challenge due to the discrete, non-differentiable nature of the computation graph and the sparsity of global supervisory signals. Existing black-box optimizers struggle to attribute trajectory-level failure to specific local components, resul…
items.sm: Proposes improving multi-agent prompts by identifying critical interaction rounds and separating individual agent contributions to assign responsibility for failures.

items.t: MINDGAMES: A Live Arena for Evaluating Social and Strategic Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.a: Kevin Wang, Anna Thöni, Benjamin Kempinski, Bobby Cheng, Jianzhu Yao, Benjamin Finch, Leon Guertler, Viraj Nadkarni
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as interactive agents, yet their capacity for social and strategic reasoning over extended interaction remains poorly understood. Existing evaluations rely on static vignettes or single-game benchmarks that cannot capture the sustained, multi-faceted reasoning that real-world multi-agent settings demand. We introduce Mindgames, a multi-game arena and evaluation p…
items.sm: Introduces Mindgames, a four-game evaluation platform for measuring language model agents' belief inference, opponent modeling, cooperation, and sustained deception.

items.t: LLM-ALSO: LLM-Driven Adaptive Learning-Signal Optimization for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Xiaoguang Wu, Zhi Zheng, Hui Xiong
items.x: Effective training-time guidance is central to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), yet remains difficult in sparse-reward settings where weak supervision limits coordination and policy improvement, and existing methods often require substantial domain expertise or manual design effort. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising alternative for flexible learning-signal design, yet existing LLM-based metho…
items.sm: Introduces LLM-ALSO, which iteratively diagnoses coordination problems, proposes learning signals, and validates them during cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning.

items.t: Can LLM Teams Play What? Where? When?
items.a: Anastasia Kotelnikova, Viktor Byzov, Maria Dolzhenkova, Evgeny Kotelnikov
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) remain limited on tasks requiring indirect reasoning, cultural knowledge, and coordinated hypothesis testing. We investigate whether team-based interaction improves LLM performance in What? Where? When? (ChGK), a quiz game designed to reward collective reasoning. We introduce three team strategies: Voting, Silent Team (the captain observes final answers), and Talkative Team (the captain o…
items.sm: Reports that language model teams outperform individual models on a reasoning quiz dataset, with accuracy gains reaching 20 percentage points.

items.t: Learning to Choose: An Empowerment-Guided Multi-Agent System with semantic communication for Adaptive Method Selection
items.a: Geremy Loachamín-Suntaxi, Robert Lazar, Dimitrios G. Giovanis, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Eleni D. Koronaki
items.x: Automating scientific computing workflows requires more than generating executable code: autonomous systems must also select appropriate computational strategies, implement them faithfully, and ensure that the resulting outcomes remain causally attributable to the decisions that produced them. In multi-agent pipelines, this process is particularly fragile, as small inconsistencies between agent intentions and actions…
items.sm: Proposes a multi-agent scientific computing framework using contextual bandits, structured communication, and semantic checkpoints to keep executed methods consistent with selected strategies.

items.t: Formalizing Mathematics at Scale
items.a: Ahmad Rammal, Niket Patel, Fabian Gloeckle, Amaury Hayat, Julia Kempe, Remi Munos, Charles Arnal, Vivien Cabannes
items.x: We present AutoformBot, a multi-agent system for building an Autoformalized Textbook Library At Scale (Atlas) in Lean 4. AutoformBot orchestrates thousands of LLM agents, equipped with formal verification tools, dependency-aware task scheduling, and collaborative version control, to translate informal textbook prose into machine-checked definitions and proofs. We apply our methods to a corpus of 26 open-access textbo…
items.sm: Introduces AutoformBot, which coordinates thousands of agents to translate 26 mathematics textbooks into a verified Lean library containing over 45,000 declarations.

items.t: Towards Verifiable Multimodal Deep Research: A Multi-Agent Harness for Interleaved Report Generation
items.a: Chenghao Zhang, Guanting Dong, Yufan Liu, Tong Zhao, Xiaoxi Li, Zhicheng Dou
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced autonomous agents from deep search, which retrieves concise factual answers, to deep research, which synthesizes scattered evidence into long-form reports. However, verifiable multimodal deep research remains challenging due to open-ended synthesis without deterministic ground truth and the need to interleave textual arguments with visual evidence. We propose Ptah, a multi-a…
items.sm: Introduces Ptah, a multi-agent system that plans, researches, writes, and verifies web reports combining textual claims, citations, and visual evidence.

items.t: AgentCVR: Active Multi-Agent Cross-Video Reasoning via Script-Simulated Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Yilun Qiu, Jiahe Wang, Cilin Yan, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Chun Yuan
items.x: Cross-Video Reasoning (CVR) has emerged as a critical frontier in multimodal intelligence, requiring models to retrieve, align, and aggregate evidence distributed across multiple videos. Current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) often struggle with CVR, as simple single-pass strategies encode multiple videos into a shared compressed context, potentially obscuring rare but critical evidence. In this paper, we p…
items.sm: Introduces AgentCVR, which coordinates visual and audio agents to gather evidence across videos and trains its policy using simulated scripts.

items.t: DynaGraph: Lightweight Multi-Model Interaction Framework via Dynamic Topological Reconfiguration
items.a: Yanxing Guo, Zihao Zheng, Fangzhou Wu, Ling Liang, Lin Bao, Zongwei Wang, Yimao Cai
items.x: Tackling complex reasoning tasks typically relies on massive monolithic LLMs, which suffer from severe computational redundancy. While task decomposition through structured pipelines or multi-agent collaborations offers an alternative, these approaches inevitably fall into a critical dilemma: predefined static topologies are highly vulnerable to cascading errors, whereas unconstrained dynamic agents suffer from traje…
items.sm: Introduces DynaGraph, which dynamically reorganizes model interactions and shares a base model across adapters to support training and inference on one consumer GPU.

items.t: Indexing the Unreadable: LLM-Native Recursive Construction and Search of Service Taxonomies
items.a: Wei Zheng, Yang Yan, Yiyang Shao, Jinyang Li, Zeze Chang, Yukuang Jia, Qiming Mao, Chihyung Wang
items.x: The era of the Internet of Agents (IoA) is taking shape: LLM agents are expected to fulfill user goals by orchestrating fast-growing populations of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Agent-to-Agent (A2A) endpoints, reusable skills, and other LLM-callable services. Yet LLMs face a structural mismatch with this regime: effective context is a scarce resource that does not scale with the number of services. Concatenat…
items.sm: Proposes A2X, a service discovery approach that recursively organizes callable services into taxonomies and progressively reveals relevant descriptions within limited model context.
Provides a multi-agent orchestration framework advertising dynamic task graphs, structured memory, safety controls, observability, human intervention, and native MCP support.

items.t: MediHive: A Decentralized Agent Collective for Medical Reasoning
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized medical reasoning tasks, yet single-agent systems often falter on complex, interdisciplinary problems requiring robust handling of uncertainty and conflicting evidence. Multi-agent systems (MAS) leveraging LLMs enable collaborative intelligence, but prevailing centralized architectures suffer from scalability bottlenecks, single points of failure, and role confusion in…
items.sm: Introduces MediHive, a decentralized medical question-answering system whose agents assign themselves specialized roles and combine reasoning through shared memory and iterative fusion.

items.t: Defending LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems Against Cooperative Attacks with Sentence-Level Rectification
items.a: Yaoyang Luo, Zhi Zheng, Ziwei Zhao, Tong Xu, Zhao Jielun, Wenjun Xue, Yong Chen, Enhong Chen
items.x: Recent years have witnessed the rapid development of Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (MAS), which excel at collaborative decision-making and complex problem-solving. However, malicious agents in MAS may inject misinformation to mislead other agents and disrupt system performance, giving rise to a new research direction that focuses on attack mechanisms and defense strategies in MAS. Prior studies large…
items.sm: Studies coordinated misinformation attacks by malicious agents and proposes sentence-level rectification to defend multi-agent language model systems.

items.t: AutoScientists: Self-Organizing Agent Teams for Long-Running Scientific Experimentation
items.a: Shanghua Gao, Ada Fang, Marinka Zitnik
items.x: Scientific research proceeds through iterative cycles of hypothesis generation, experiment design, execution, and revision. AI agents can automate parts of this process, but existing approaches typically follow a single research trajectory or coordinate through a central planner with fixed objectives. As a result, they struggle to sustain parallel exploration, adapt as experimental evidence changes, or preserve knowl…
items.sm: Introduces AutoScientists, decentralized agents that form research teams, critique hypotheses, run experiments, and share findings and failures during extended scientific investigations.

items.t: The Best-Laid SCHEMEs: Coordinated Sabotage and Monitoring in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Nikolay Radev, Lennart Haas, Benjamin Arnav, Pablo Bernabeu-Pérez
items.x: As agentic coding systems decompose work across multiple model instances, a critical safety question is whether those instances can coordinate to achieve a hidden malicious objective while remaining aligned with user intent. We introduce SCHEME, a benchmark of 17 task instances across 7 settings and 8 real open-source libraries, each pairing a legitimate software-engineering task with a covert side task. Every settin…
items.sm: Introduces SCHEME, a benchmark testing whether coding agents can coordinate covert sabotage while completing legitimate software tasks, and reports successful coordinated sabotage.

items.sm: Examines how AI subagents and specialized skills can support software development stages for distributed systems and data analysis.

items.t: Roles with Rails: Contract-Preserving Role Evolution in Multi-Agent Structured Reasoning
items.x: Role-based LLM multi-agent systems need adaptive role pools, yet adapting such systems is not merely a matter of prompt optimization: roles often carry structural obligations, including capability coverage, message compatibility, validation, final-answer aggregation, and parser-compatible output protocols. Existing systems either fix the role inventory and lose adaptivity, or allow unconstrained generation to induce …
items.sm: Proposes a framework that adapts agent roles while preserving required capabilities, communication, validation, answer aggregation, and output formats.

items.t: Plan-Augmented Multi-Agent LLM Systems for Enterprise Workflow Automation: A Thinking Fast and Slow Decision Framework

items.t: Long Live the Librarian! A Persistent Search Sub-Agent for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Software Engineering Systems

items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) have substantially advanced autonomous software engineering (SWE), but their growing inference energy demands raise sustainability concerns. In this paper, we demonstrate that this cost is concentrated in an overlooked source: redundant output tokens generated across agents. Two empirical findings ground this claim. First, our per-token energy attribution for MAS reveals a sharp asymmetry: a…
items.sm: Proposes a persistent repository search agent that reduces repeated exploration and output tokens to lower energy use in multi-agent software engineering.

items.x: Communities can sustainably manage shared resources (commons) through self-governance and cooperative norms, a central finding of Ostrom's theory of self-governance. However, real-world commons (e.g., fisheries, forests, and irrigation systems) are often governed under asymmetric power structures, where certain individuals or institutions possess disproportionate control over resource extraction and collective outcom…
items.sm: Introduces a simulation framework for studying cooperation over shared resources when one language model agent has disproportionate governing power.

items.x: Effective multi-agent systems cannot be designed by selecting prompts or communication graphs in isolation. Agent behavior depends on the information an agent receives, while the usefulness of a communication edge depends on how the receiving agent interprets and uses that information. We propose \textbf{TCP-MCP} (Topology-Coupled Prompting for Multi-Agent Collaborative Problem-Solving), a co-evolution framework that…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that jointly optimizes agent prompts and communication networks while balancing task accuracy, token costs, and structural complexity.

items.t: Beyond Consensus: Trace-Level Synthesis in Mixture of Agents
items.a: Shreyas Fadnavis, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Felix Wyss
items.x: When multiple LLM agents solve the same problem, standard practice compresses each agent's reasoning into a majority vote or layered synthesis, treating agreement as the finish line. We show this is unnecessarily lossy: an LLM aggregator that reads complete reasoning traces recovers correct solutions even when agents unanimously agree, with beneficial corrections consistently outweighing harmful ones -- the \emph{agg…
items.sm: Finds that combining agents' full reasoning traces can recover correct answers beyond majority voting by assembling complementary intermediate steps.

items.t: Eliminating Coordination Chaos in Test-Time Scaling: Phase-Vector Geometrodynamics for Multi-Agent Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Models coordination in multi-agent reasoning as a geometric process governed by localized informational stress to address coordination problems during inference.

items.t: Adaptive Multimodal Agents-Based Framework for Automatic Workflow Execution
items.a: Susanna Cifani, Mario Luca Bernardi, Marta Cimitile
items.x: Modern information systems require autonomous agents capable of navigating complex workflows, yet current methodologies often struggle with the transition from structured metadata parsing to general environmental perception. While the integration of MLLMs has enabled agents to interact directly with GUIs, existing approaches typically treat task sequences as discrete, linear episodes. This fragmentation prevents agen…
items.sm: Proposes multimodal agents that build a knowledge base of workflow transitions from execution logs and retrieve it to guide automatic workflow execution.

items.t: TRACER: Turn-level Regret Matching with Inner Reinforcement Credit for Cooperative Multi-LLM Reasoning
items.a: Chusen Li, Zhou Liu, Shuigeng Zhou, Wentao Zhang
items.x: Large language models increasingly rely on either reinforcement learning or multi-agent prompting to improve reasoning, yet these two paradigms remain difficult to combine. Directly applying single-agent reinforcement learning to multi-turn multi-agent systems faces following dilemmas: i) Sparse rewards, role-level free-riding and excessive training overhead. ii) Agents only imitate to collaborate. iii) Fixed collabo…
items.sm: Introduces reinforcement learning that decides when agents speak and assigns separate rewards to proposing and reviewing contributions in collaborative reasoning.

items.t: Examining Agents' Bias Amplification versus Suppression in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zejian Eric Wu, Zhongyi Jiang, Yuan Zhuang, Paul Jen-Hwa Hu
items.x: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed to support various tasks where agents interact to achieve individual and collective objectives. Although these systems can enhance task performance and decision-making, fairness preservation through bias reduction remains challenging. This study examines how agent-level biases shift and impact system-wide fairness. We use prompts to expose individual agents to group-favor…
items.sm: Studies how biases introduced into individual agents affect system fairness and proposes a metric separating favored-group gains from disfavored-group losses.

items.t: Out of Sight, Not Out of Mind: Unveiling Latent Attack in Latent-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Chenxi Wang, Ruiyang Huang, Jiayan Sun, Lei Wei, Yifan Wu
items.x: Latent-based multi-agent systems replace parts of explicit inter-agent communication with hidden representations, offering a new direction for efficient and flexible agent collaboration. However, moving coordination into latent space may also move attacks beyond the reach of visible-text inspection. In this paper, we study whether latent states can carry attack-associated information that remains effective during cle…
items.sm: Shows that hidden agent representations can retain attack effects and degrade later clean executions, especially when transferred through inter-agent caches.

items.t: UnityMAS-O: A General RL Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yiqun Chen, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Shijie Wang, Qi Liu, Zechun Niu, Bin Zhang, Haitao Li
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems decompose complex tasks into interacting roles, but most remain manually orchestrated by prompts, tools, and control rules, while agents are rarely optimized through a unified reinforcement learning interface. Existing RL post-training frameworks mainly target single-policy optimization and lack abstractions for user-defined multi-agent workflows, structured interaction, role-specific cr…
items.sm: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes complete multi-agent workflows using configurable roles, interaction histories, rewards, and mappings between agents and models.

items.t: AgensFlow: A Coordination-Policy Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) require many coordination choices that are difficult to fix a priori: which skill protocol to invoke, which agent role should perform a subtask, which model to bind to each role, how roles should interact, when to use retrieval or verification, and when to omit a step entirely. These choices interact with task regime and operational constraints, so static pipe…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that learns coordination policies for agent skills, roles, models, communication, retrieval, and verification from repeated workflow executions.

items.t: Got a Secret? LLM Agents Can't Keep It: Evaluating Privacy in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Aman Priyanshu, Supriti Vijay, Esha Pahwa
items.x: LLM safety evaluations predominantly test models in isolation, yet deployed AI agents increasingly operate within persistent social environments alongside other agents. We introduce a Moltbook-style simulation platform where thousands of LLM agents interact across communities over a simulated month, and use it to evaluate privacy as a downstream safety concern under varying degrees of social pressure. We find that sh…
items.sm: Finds that extended social interactions increase agents' disclosure of sensitive information, with peer disclosures encouraging further leaks despite explicit privacy instructions.

items.t: Agents that Matter: How Subtle Choices Shape Agent Attribution in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Mingyu Lu, Yushan Huang, Chris Lin, Su-In Lee
items.x: As multi-agent systems (MAS) become increasingly complex, identifying the contributions of agents is critical for system optimization. However, existing approaches lack a unified formulation for credit assignment. In this work, we formalize agent attribution as a cooperative game, parameterized by the coalition distribution, intervention protocol, and target metric. Using this framework, we demonstrate that intervent…
items.sm: Models agent contributions using cooperative games and finds that removing agents individually can identify workflow bottlenecks at lower cost than combinatorial methods.

items.t: Detection Without Correction: A Two-Parameter Decomposition of Multi-Stage LLM Pipelines
items.a: Prashanti Nilayam, Kiran Ramanna, Prashil Tumbade
items.x: Multi-stage LLM pipelines that perform multi-agent debate, intrinsic self-correction, or retrieval-augmented verification exhibit puzzling aggregate behaviors: accuracy plateaus and reversals across rounds, non-replication of debate gains on contemporary frontier models, intrinsic self-correction degradation, and qualitative cross-provider divergence in debate dynamics. Downstream agent response can be operationalize…
items.sm: Analyzes multi-stage language model failures by separating the decision to distrust earlier content from the ability to generate a correct replacement.

items.t: HARP: Measuring Harm Amplification in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Md Hafizur Rahman, Zafaryab Haider, Tanzim Mahfuz, Prabuddha Chakraborty
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems decompose workflows across agents, tools, shared context, memory, and decision gates. This modularity improves interpretability, but creates a propagation risk: a bounded perturbation to one component can be reused by other agents and amplified into system-level harm. We introduce HARP (Harm Amplification through Role Perturbation), a trace-first methodology for studying local-to-global harm a…
items.sm: Introduces a method comparing clean and perturbed execution traces to measure how local disruptions spread into broader harm across multi-agent workflows.

items.t: Learning to Orchestrate Agents under Uncertainty
items.a: Mary Chriselda Antony Oliver, Lan Jiang, Aaron Bundi Anampiu, Elaf Almahmoud, Francesco Quinzan, Umang Bhatt
items.x: Adaptive orchestration of heterogeneous agents requires making sequential delegation decisions under uncertain and evolving agent behaviour, e.g., coordinating specialised AI models with varying reliability, cost, and response quality. While prior work on agent orchestration focuses on performance or cost, uncertainty in agent reliability and output distributions is typically not modelled explicitly at the orchestrat…
items.sm: Proposes a controller that learns which agents to delegate tasks to while accounting for uncertain reliability, costs, and differences in output distributions.

items.t: Architecting Multi-Agent Generative AI Ecosystems for Predictive Market Simulation and Strategic Foresight
items.v: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.t: You Only Align Once: Propagating Cooperative Behaviors in Multi-Agent Systems through Seed Agents
items.a: Nicole Summer Hsing, Asuka Yuxi Zheng, Yi Zhao, Haoqin Tu, Jen-tse Huang
items.x: Ensuring aligned agent behaviors in distributed open multi-agent systems remains challenging, especially as populations grow and unaligned agents may exist. We show that a single aligned agent can propagate cooperative behaviors to unmodified agents purely through natural-language interaction, a phenomenon we term Alignment Propagation. We study this in the Red-Black Game, a team-based iterated Prisoner's Dilemma in …
items.sm: Shows that one trained cooperative agent can encourage unmodified teammates to cooperate through conversation, raising cooperation rates in a repeated social dilemma.

items.t: PEAR: Permutation-Equivariant Adaptive Routing Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Yang Feng, Ziwei Xu, Xia Hu, Fengxiang He
items.x: Multi-agent debate improves the reliability of large language models (LLMs) through iterative peer critiques. items.sm: Introduces a training-free debate protocol that changes communication networks and role assignments between rounds to reduce positional bias and distribute agent influence.

items.t: SGAgent : Suggestion-Guided LLM-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Repository-Level Software Repair

items.sm: SGAgent adds a suggestion stage between locating bugs and generating fixes to guide multiple language model agents in repository-level software repair.

items.t: Voluntary Collusion with Secret Tools in Competing LLM Agents
items.x: Even when a tool is explicitly described as unfair and harmful to others, ostensibly safety-aligned LLM agents still voluntarily engage in secret collusion whenever doing so confers a strategic advantage. items.x: Recent advances in agentic systems increasingly treat code as an executable operational substrate rather than as a disposable output artifact. However, the governance, lifecycle management, and operational evol…
items.sm: Proposes governance mechanisms for managing, revising, and retaining agent-generated code as persistent capabilities within multi-agent runtimes.

items.t: Exploring Agent Interactions in MoltBook through Social Network Analysis
items.a: I-Hsien Ting, Kazunori Minetaki, Dario Liberona, Mu-En Wu
items.x: The rapid evolution of large language model based multiagent systems has transformed digital communication, with platforms like MoltBook emerging as essential agent native environments for observing autonomous social behaviors. items.a: Rui Zhang, Chaeeun Kim, Liting Hu

items.sm: Proposes a runtime layer between agent frameworks and serving engines so policies can combine agent information with engine events.

items.x: Multi-agent systems increasingly expose explicit workflow structure: agents, tools, tool-access rules, restrictions, and delegation paths. Inspired by multi-channel communication theory, we propose HyLaT, a hybrid latent-text communicat…

items.a: Qiming Ye, Peixian Zhang, Yupeng He, Zifan Peng, Gareth Tyson

items.a: Samuel Rothfarb, Megan Christina Davis, Ivana Matanović, Baikun Li, Edward F. Holby, Wilton J. M. Kort-Kamp
items.x: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific exploration, but most methods automate procedural tasks without engaging in scientific reasoning, limiting autonomy in discovery. items.t: Multi-Agent Systems are Mixtures of Experts: Who Becomes an Influencer?

items.x: Production language-model systems answer a request by partitioning it across an invisible orchestration of worker agents that recompose one integrated report. items.t: Sentinel: Embodied Cooperative Spatial Reasoning and Planning
