Agents duplicate efforts in retrieval and reasoning processes. This inefficiency stems from a deeper issue: current architectures lack mechanisms to ensure agents share minimal sufficient information at each operational stage. Empirical…
items.sm: D3MAS organizes task decomposition, collaborative reasoning, and knowledge distribution to reduce duplicated retrieval and reasoning across language model agents.

items.t: CRAwDAD: Causal Reasoning Augmentation with Dual-Agent Debate
items.a: Finn G. Vamosi, Nils D. Forkert
items.x: When people reason about cause and effect, they often consider many competing ''what if'' scenarios before deciding which explanation fits best. Analogously, advanced language models capable of causal inference can consider multiple interventions and counterfactuals to judge the validity of causal claims. Crucially, this type of reasoning is less like a single calculation and more like an internal dialogue between al…
items.sm: CRAwDAD pairs an agent proposing causal explanations with a critic that challenges its reasoning, allowing both to revise conclusions through debate.

items.t: Trust but Verify: Prover-Verifier Deliberation for Selective LLM Prediction
items.a: João Sedoc, Baotong Zhang, Dean Foster
items.x: Reliably knowing when a language model is correct is almost as important as being correct. We introduce prover-verifier deliberation (PVD), an inference-time protocol grounded in interactive proof theory, as a mechanism for selective prediction: the protocol produces both an answer and a structured confidence verdict, allowing a system to report high-confidence answers while abstaining on uncertain cases. In each dia…
items.sm: Introduces a prover-verifier dialogue that checks candidate answers and assigns confidence verdicts, enabling language models to abstain when uncertain.

items.t: Influencing LLM Multi-Agent Dialogue via Policy-Parameterized Prompts
items.a: Hongbo Bo, Jingyu Hu, Weiru Liu
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as a new paradigm for multi-agent systems. However, existing research on the behaviour of LLM-based multi-agents relies on ad hoc prompts and lacks a principled policy perspective. Different from reinforcement learning, we investigate whether prompt-as-action can be parameterized so as to construct a lightweight policy which consists of a sequence of state-action pairs to inf…
items.sm: Develops state-dependent, parameterized prompts to steer multi-agent conversations without training, evaluating responsiveness, rebuttals, evidence use, repetition, and stance changes.

items.t: LEGOMem: Modular Procedural Memory for Multi-agent LLM Systems for Workflow Automation
items.a: Dongge Han, Camille Couturier, Daniel Madrigal Diaz, Xuchao Zhang, Victor Rühle, Saravan Rajmohan
items.x: We introduce LEGOMem, a modular procedural memory framework for multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems in workflow automation. LEGOMem decomposes past task trajectories into reusable memory units and flexibly allocates them across orchestrators and task agents to support planning and execution. To explore the design space of memory in multi-agent systems, we use LEGOMem as a lens and conduct a systematic stud…
items.sm: LEGOMem turns past workflows into reusable memories, finding that orchestrator memory supports delegation while detailed agent memory improves execution.

items.t: HyperAgent: Leveraging Hypergraphs for Topology Optimization in Multi-Agent Communication
items.a: Heng Zhang, Y Shi, Xiaodong Gu, Zijian Zhang, Haochen You, Lu Gan, Yilei Yuan, Jin Huang
items.x: Recent advances in large language model-powered multi-agent systems have demonstrated remarkable collective intelligence through effective communication. However, existing approaches face two primary challenges: (i) Ineffective group collaboration modeling, as they rely on pairwise edge representations in graph structures, limiting their ability to capture relationships among multiple agents; and (ii) Limited task-ad…
items.sm: HyperAgent uses hypergraphs to represent group interactions and adapt communication structures to task demands in multi-agent language model systems.

items.t: Parallelized Planning-Acting for Multi-Agent LLM Systems in Minecraft
items.a: Y. Li, Shunyu Liu, Tongya Zheng, Li Sun, Mingli Song
items.x: Recent advancements in Large Language Model (LLM)-based Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) have demonstrated remarkable potential for tackling complex decision-making tasks. However, existing frameworks inevitably rely on serialized execution paradigms, where agents must complete sequential LLM planning before taking action. This fundamental constraint severely limits real-time responsiveness and adaptation, which is crucial …
items.sm: Introduces concurrent planning and action threads with interruptible execution to improve multi-agent responsiveness in changing Minecraft environments.

items.t: LumiMAS: A Comprehensive Framework for Real-Time Monitoring and Enhanced Observability in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Ron Solomon, Yarin Yerushalmi Levi, Lior Vaknin, Eran Aizikovich, Amit Baras, Etai Ohana, Amit Giloni, Shamik Bose
items.x: The incorporation of large language models in multi-agent systems (MASs) has the potential to significantly improve our ability to autonomously solve complex problems. However, such systems introduce unique challenges in monitoring, interpreting, and detecting system failures. Most existing MAS observability frameworks focus on analyzing each individual agent separately, overlooking failures associated with the entir…
items.sm: LumiMAS monitors agent activity, detects anomalies across multi-agent systems, and provides explanations to help diagnose failures.

items.t: RUMAD: Reinforcement-Unifying Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Chao Wang, Han Lin, Huaze Tang, Huijing Lin, Wenbo Ding
items.x: Multi-agent debate (MAD) systems leverage collective intelligence to enhance reasoning capabilities, yet existing approaches struggle to simultaneously optimize accuracy, consensus formation, and computational efficiency. Static topology methods lack adaptability to task complexity variations, while external LLM-based coordination risks introducing privileged knowledge that compromises debate neutrality. This work pr…
items.sm: RUMAD trains a reinforcement learning controller to adjust debate communication using high-level dynamics, balancing answer quality, agreement, and computational efficiency.

items.t: G2CP: A Graph-Grounded Communication Protocol for Verifiable and Efficient Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems decompose complex tasks across specialized agents, yet their reliance on natural language for inter-agent communication introduces semantic ambiguity, token inefficiency, and untraceable reasoning chains problems that become critical in safety-sensitive industrial deployments. We introduce G2CP (Graph-Grounded Communication Protocol), a formal agent communication language in which every inter-…
items.sm: G2CP represents agent messages as verifiable operations on a shared knowledge graph, reporting improved accuracy and lower token costs on industrial maintenance queries.

items.t: Meta-Agent: From Task Descriptions to Verified Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: AI agents are increasingly used to solve complex, multi-step tasks, but existing multi-agent frameworks remain brittle as workflows grow in scale and depth. Small errors at intermediate stages can propagate through agent interactions, while insufficient grounding and weak verification mechanisms further limit reliability. We present Meta-Agent, a two-phase framework that automatically constructs and executes speciali…
items.sm: Meta-Agent converts task descriptions into specialized agent workflows with explicit contracts, external evidence, generated configurations, and construction-time verification.

items.t: Agentic Patterns for Decentralized Network Protocol Configuration
items.a: Ahmed Twabi, Yepeng Ding, Tohru Kondo
items.sm: Studies routing configuration across 350 runs, finding that access to relevant router evidence explains performance more clearly than multi-agent orchestration patterns.

items.t: Algorithmic Collusion at Test Time: A Meta-game Design and Evaluation
items.a: Yuhong Luo, Daniel Schoepflin, Xintong Wang
items.x: The threat of algorithmic collusion, and whether it merits regulatory intervention, remains debated, as existing evaluations of its emergence often rely on long learning horizons, assumptions about counterparty rationality in adopting collusive strategies, and symmetry in hyperparameters and economic settings among players. To study collusion risk, we introduce a meta-game design for analyzing algorithmic behavior un…
items.sm: Introduces a meta-game framework to investigate whether agents combining pretrained strategies with adaptation rules develop collusion under test-time constraints.

items.t: ?ACP: A Formal Calculus for Expressive, Resource-Constrained Agent Communication
items.x: Agent communication remains a foundational problem in multi-agent systems protocols such as FIPA-ACL guarantee semantic richness but are intractable for constrained environments, while lightweight IoT protocols achieve efficiency at the expense of expressiveness. This paper presents μACP, a formal calculus for expressive agent communication under explicit resource bounds. We formalize the Resource-Constrained Agent C…
items.sm: Presents a resource-bounded communication calculus with four basic operations, protocol encoding proofs, message complexity bounds, and formally checked coordination properties.

items.t: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Prateek Gupta, Qiankun Zhong, Hiromu Yakura, Thomas Eisenmann, Iyad Rahwan
items.x: A growing body of multi-agent studies with Large Language Models (LLMs) explores how norms and cooperation emerge in mixed-motive scenarios, where pursuing individual gain can undermine the collective good. While prior work has explored these dynamics in both richly contextualized simulations and simplified game-theoretic environments, most LLM systems featuring common-pool resource (CPR) games provide agents with ex…
items.sm: Introduces a shared-resource simulation without explicit rewards to study how social learning and norm formation shape cooperation among language model agents.

items.t: Rethinking Multi-agent Systems in the Era of LLMs
items.sm: Reconsiders multi-agent systems in light of language models, connecting earlier visions of cooperating experts with contemporary agent frameworks and applications.

items.t: Agentic LLMs and Distributed Constraint Reasoning: A Symbiotic Perspective for Neurosymbolic Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Gauthier Picard, William Yeoh, Roie Zivan
items.sm: Argues for combining language model agents with distributed constraint reasoning to translate human preferences into formal models and strengthen multi-agent coordination.

items.t: CraftUtopia: A LLM-based Multi-Agent System for Collaborative Construction in Minecraft
items.a: Wanli Fu, Hao Li, Siyue Ren, Chenxi Xing, Yang Chen, Chen Chu, Zhen Wang, Shuyue Hu
items.sm: CraftUtopia converts a reference image into a Minecraft blueprint and distributes construction across hierarchical agents using a shared library of reusable skills.

items.t: Reliable Data Science Analysis with Large Language Models via Multi-Agent Tools Orchestration
items.a: Mingyin Zou, Guangrong You, Xiaomin Zhu, Yanqing Ye, Ji Wang
items.sm: Proposes automating data science through multi-agent selection and configuration of reusable tools, breaking workflows into verifiable steps to reduce coding errors.

items.t: Developing Guidelines for Human-LLM Agent Teams: A Multi-Stakeholder Lens
items.a: Mireia Yurrita, Davide Dell’Anna, Pradeep Kumar Murukannaiah, Catholijn M. Jonker, Pınar Yolum
items.sm: Develops 24 design guidelines for human and language model agent teams, addressing agents, human teammates, designers, and deployment contexts.

items.t: LLM-based Agents in Supply Chain Games: The Role of Incomplete Information and Model Heterogeneity
items.a: Jiuyun Jiang, Yuecheng Hong, Jiangnan Shi, Song Huang, Jie Yang, Guangxin Jiang, Xiaomeng Guo, Guang Xiao
items.sm: Finds that partial information sharing can match full transparency in simulated supply chains, while model diversity and capability affect stability and collective performance.

items.t: Reputation as a Solution to Cooperation Collapse in LLM-based MASs
items.a: Siyue Ren, Wanli Fu, Xinkun Zou, Chen Shen, Yi Cai, Chu Chen, Zhen Wang, Shanshan Hu
items.x: Cooperation has long been a fundamental topic in both human society and AI systems. However, recent studies indicate that the collapse of cooperation may emerge in multi-agent systems (MASs) driven by large language models (LLMs). To address this challenge, we explore reputation systems as a remedy. We propose RepuNet, a dynamic, dual-level reputation framework that models both agent-level reputation dynamics and sys…
items.sm: RepuNet uses interaction, gossip, and changing network connections to maintain agent reputations, reporting sustained cooperation across three multi-agent scenarios.

items.t: BotVerse: Real-Time Event-Driven Simulation of Social Agents
items.a: Edoardo Allegrini, Edoardo Di Paolo, Angelo Spognardi, Marinella Petrocchi
items.x: BotVerse is a scalable, event-driven framework for high-fidelity social simulation using LLM-based agents. It addresses the ethical risks of studying autonomous agents on live networks by isolating interactions within a controlled environment while grounding them in real-time content streams from the Bluesky ecosystem. The system features an asynchronous orchestration API and a simulation engine that emulates human-l…
items.sm: BotVerse simulates social agents in a controlled environment using live Bluesky content, supporting customizable personas and experiments such as coordinated disinformation.

items.t: Wisdom of the Machines: Exploring Collective Intelligence in LLM Crowds
items.a: Yashar Talebirad, Ali Parsaee, Vishwajeet Ohal, Amirhossein Nadiri, Csongor Szepesvári, Yash Mouje, Eden Redman
items.sm: Finds that combining deterministic estimates from different language models outperforms individual models on visual estimation tasks, while temperature-based diversity offers limited benefit.

items.t: Deception and Communication in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: An Experimental Study with Among Us
items.x: As large language models are deployed as autonomous agents, their capacity for strategic deception raises core questions for coordination, reliability, and safety in multi-goal, multi-agent systems. We study deception and communication in LLM agents through the social deduction game Among Us, a cooperative-competitive environment. Across 1,100 games, autonomous agents produced over one million tokens of meeting dialo…
items.sm: Analyzes 1,100 Among Us games, finding that language model agents mainly deceive through ambiguity, which increases under pressure but rarely improves winning.

items.t: Everyone Contributes! Incentivizing Strategic Cooperation in Multi-LLM Systems via Sequential Public Goods Games
items.a: Yunhao Liang, Yuan Qu, Jingyuan Yang, Shaochong Lin, Zuo‐Jun Max Shen
items.x: Coordinating multiple large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks collaboratively poses a fundamental trade-off between computational costs and collective performance when compared with individual models. We introduce a novel, game-theoretically grounded reinforcement learning (RL) framework, the Multi-Agent Cooperation Sequential Public Goods Game (MAC-SPGG), to systematically incentivize cooperation in mult…
items.sm: Introduces a sequential public goods framework with reinforcement learning rewards designed to encourage useful contributions and reduce free-riding and communication costs.

items.t: When LLM Agent Teams Fail at Topological Spatial Reasoning Under Partial Observability
items.a: Heitor Gama Ribeiro, Jean-Philippe Diguet, Damith Ranasinghe
items.sm: Studies failures in language model teams' spatial planning over map-like structures when agents have incomplete, decentralized information.

items.t: ConvPayMAS: Conversational Payment Multi-Agent System with Agent-to-Agent Protocol and Three-Mandate Verification
items.a: Joon Kiat Chua, Chen Hao Tse, Donghao Huang, Zhaoxia Wang
items.sm: ConvPayMAS coordinates conversational payments through a supervisor agent, using agent communication protocols and three cryptographic mandates to verify authorization while isolating card data.

items.t: Protocol Pivoting: Cross-Protocol Attack Escalation in Agentic AI Systems
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Identifies attacks that cross agent communication protocols, exploiting mismatched trust assumptions to escalate privileges, inject capabilities, or propagate malicious instructions.

items.t: Toward High-Fidelity Multi-Agent Recommendation: An Agentic Design Framework Integrating RecoWorld and LLMs
items.sm: Proposes combining RecoWorld, RecBole, and language model agents to simulate recommendation feedback loops, long-term retention, user-system adaptation, and agent welfare.

items.t: Too Many Specialists: Emergent Inefficiencies and Bottlenecks for Multi-agent Ad-hoc Collaboration
items.a: Benjamin Panny, Shashank Mehrotra, Zahra Zahedi, Teruhisa Misu, Kumar Akash
items.x: Computational models of collaboration without prior coordination often overlook how heterogeneous agent traits and complex task structures jointly produce systemic bottlenecks, inefficiencies, and contribution inequalities. We address this by using an agent-based model of ad-hoc teamwork in a kitchen environment. Our model integrates diverse agent personas with tasks that combine serial and parallel dependencies. We …
items.sm: Models ad hoc kitchen teamwork and finds that rigid specialization, team size, and communication overhead can create bottlenecks, unequal workloads, and redundant collaboration.

items.t: Towards Foresighted AI Cooperators with LLM-driven Decision-Time Planning
items.a: Yuheng Jing, Kai Li, Bingyun Liu, Ziwen Zhang, Zhe Wu, Yifan Zhang, Junliang Xing, Jian Cheng
items.sm: Introduces DTPAgent, which uses language models and decision-time planning to coordinate with unfamiliar partners without task-specific training.

items.t: FEDOT.MAS: Generating Multi-Agent Systems for Complex Tasks with Multi-Stage Validation
items.a: Dmitry Gilemkhanov, Vadim A. Potemkin, Maria Zaitseva, Ilia Revin, Anna Kalyuzhnaya, Nikolay O. Nikitin
items.sm: Generates executable multi-agent systems from natural language through seven validation stages and reports higher GAIA accuracy than MAS-GPT across all difficulty levels.

items.t: Heterogeneity in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Tianyi Hu, Zhiqiang Pu, Yuan Wang, Tenghai Qiu, Min Chen, X H Yu
items.x: Heterogeneity is a fundamental property in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), which is closely related not only to the functional differences of agents, but also to policy diversity and environmental interactions. However, the MARL field currently lacks a rigorous definition and deeper understanding of heterogeneity. This paper systematically discusses heterogeneity in MARL from the perspectives of definition…
items.sm: Defines five types of heterogeneity in multi-agent reinforcement learning, proposes a measurement method, and applies it to dynamic parameter sharing.

items.t: Fluid-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Shishir Sharma, Doina Precup, Theodore J. Perkins
items.x: The primary focus of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) has been to study interactions among a fixed number of agents embedded in an environment. However, in the real world, the number of agents is neither fixed nor known a priori. Moreover, an agent can decide to create other agents (for example, a cell may divide, or a company may spin off a division). In this paper, we propose a framework that allows agents…
items.sm: Introduces reinforcement learning environments where agents can create other agents, defines game-theoretic solutions, and evaluates algorithms on dynamically expanding agent populations.

items.t: UAM-MARL: Uncertainty-Aware Modality-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with LLM-Guided Graph Policies
items.sm: Proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that incorporates multimodal perception uncertainty into language-model planning to address coordination errors in noisy environments.

items.t: CoRe-Code: Collaborative Reinforcement Learning for Code Generation
items.a: Zhihao Dou, Qinjian Zhao, Zhongwei Wan, Xiaoyu Xia, Sumon Biswas
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved strong performance in code generation, but most methods rely on autoregressive decoding without global planning, often leading to locally coherent yet globally suboptimal solutions (e.g., failing test cases or inefficient complexity). While recent approaches such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and multi-agent systems (MAS) introduce planning, their limited role specialization and…
items.sm: Proposes collaborative reinforcement learning for code generation, with a planning agent guiding a coding agent to improve coordination, code accuracy, and efficiency.

items.t: sleeplesshan/dual-brain
items.x: A dual-agent framework leveraging left-brain logic (structured coding, syntax validation, debugging) and right-brain intuition (macro architecture, creative patterns, UX flows). It splits cognitive loads to boost LLM development efficiency, preventing hallucination while maximizing system scalability.
items.sm: Splits software development between two agents handling coding details and broader architecture, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce hallucinations.

items.t: Makson179/Bello
items.x: 3x more usage on your coding agent, same quality. Have an multi-agent setup in mind? Bello already supports it. Mix models, run agents in parallel, have them check each other’s work, and reduce unnecessary model calls and noisy tool output. Turn on only what you need.
items.sm: Supports mixed-model coding agents, parallel execution, and mutual review while claiming three times the usage at unchanged quality through fewer unnecessary calls.

items.t: AgentFugue: Agent Scaling for Long-Horizon Tasks through Collective Reasoning
items.a: Hu, Yuyang, Qian, Hongjin, Wang, Shuting et al.
items.sm: Introduces AgentFugue, where peer agents explore tasks in parallel and selectively reuse discoveries recorded in a shared reasoning hub.

items.t: @steipete: I built an autotriage skill for codex that has a set of guidelines + reads VISION.md from my repos, so issues/…
items.sm: Reports building a Codex skill that autonomously handles suitable issues and pull requests, verifies fixes using virtual machines, and leaves suggestions for manual review.

items.t: PRIMA: Operational Patterns for Resilient Multi-Agent Research with Verifiable Identity and Convergent Feedback
items.x: Operating LLMs as coordinated multi-agent research systems over multi-hour runs surfaces failure modes that single-shot evaluation cannot: upstream providers throttle without warning, sub-agents drift the task to fit accessible tools, narrate machinery instead of using it, open revision iterations with self-apology, or treat upstream context as executable directives. We present PRIMA, whose primary contributions are …
items.sm: Presents operational patterns for long-running multi-agent research, including recovery from rate limits, persistent progress, and behavioral rules that maintain task fidelity.

items.t: Agent-as-Peer-Debriefer: A Multi-Agent Framework with Perspective-Based Refinement for Qualitative Analysis
items.a: Zhimin Lin, Kun Cheng, Zhiyao Shu, Junhua Fang, Juntao Li, Fan Bai, Jie Gao
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for qualitative data analysis (QDA), yet their outputs often miss the depth and nuance of human analysis. We argue this gap reflects a missing credibility practice from human QDA: peer debriefing, in which an analyst seeks feedback from a disinterested peer and uses it to refine their coding. To bring this practice into LLM-assisted QDA, we propose Agent-as-Peer-Debr…
items.sm: Adds three peer-debriefing agents with different analytical perspectives to review and refine a primary agent’s qualitative codes, subthemes, and themes.

items.t: Zero-Trust Identity for Autonomous AI Agents: Unifying SPIFFE, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, OIDC, and OPA in Multi-Agent Architectures
items.a: Venkata Krishna Prasanth Budigi, Maheshbabu Dhanekula, Siri Chandana Sirigiri, Srinivas Rao Marri
items.v: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
items.sm: Proposes combining SPIFFE, OAuth, OIDC, and OPA to establish verifiable agent identities and enforce access policies across distributed multi-agent workflows.

items.t: How well can large language model agents simulate complex legal dispute resolution?
items.a: Yujin Zhou, Yidan Huang, Sirui Han, Yike Guo
items.sm: Evaluates language-model agents across six legal dispute scenarios, finding that simulation quality varies by role and judge agents sometimes make serious legal errors.

items.t: Market Regime Council for Dynamic Credit Assignment in Multi-Agent LLM Decision Systems
items.a: Yunhua Pei, Zerui Ge, Jin Zheng, John Cartlidge
items.x: Multi-agent LLM decision systems for portfolio management still lack a principled way to assign credit across specialist agents, remain vulnerable to cold-start dominance under regime shifts, and offer limited transparency into how final allocations are formed. We propose Market Regime Council (MRC), an online credit-assignment mechanism over coalitions of specialist agents, with portfolio management as the downstrea…
items.sm: Uses coalition-based Shapley credits, performance histories, and market regimes to adjust specialist agents’ influence over portfolio decisions and record allocation reasoning.

items.t: A MULTI-AGENT SOCIAL SIMULATION FRAMEWORK BASED ON LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A CASE STUDY OF PUBLIC OPINION EVOLUTION ON THE FUKUSHIMA NUCLEAR WASTEWATER DISCHARGE
items.a: Siying Wang, Xuan Wang, Yining Tang, Chao Wu
items.sm: Simulates public opinion about Fukushima wastewater discharge under four intervention scenarios, reporting reduced role drift and premature consensus among language-model agents.

items.t: SecureAgent: A Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Context-Aware Vulnerability Detection and Patch Recommendation
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Coordinates specialized agents to detect repository vulnerabilities and recommend patches, requiring findings to include source locations, security classifications, and validation status.

items.t: CAST: Coordinated Agent Swarm Testing as a Substitute for Human Beta Testing in Web Application Development
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes replacing human beta testing with 100 specialized language-model agents that analyze application source code and produce structured findings for deduplication.

items.t: Memory-Grounded Social Dynamics in Repeated LLM Agent Simulations: Preliminary Behavioral Evaluation with QLAB and Crisis Infrastructure Lab Evidence Boundaries
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Examines whether persistent memory, limited knowledge, social pressure, and irreversible consequences produce behavior shaped by prior events in repeated language-model agent simulations.

items.t: vdaubry/bottega
items.x: Coding agent orchestration for engineering teams — shipped as a spec plus a working reference implementation.
items.sm: Provides a specification and working reference implementation for orchestrating coding agents in engineering teams.

items.t: Kimi Is Quietly Beating Everyone – The Engineer Behind Agent Swarm Reveals Why
items.sm: Discusses a claim that Kimi outperforms competitors, framed around explanations from an engineer behind Agent Swarm.

items.t: LuckyGirl-XU/Awesome-Agent-Dynamic-Graphs
items.x: A survey and research collection on self-evolving agents as dynamic graph transformation: memory, tools, workflows, multi-agent systems, and graph learning.
items.sm: Collects research examining self-evolving agents through dynamic graph transformations involving memory, tools, workflows, multi-agent systems, and graph learning.

items.t: Does Safety Molt? Evaluating LLM Safety in Multi-Agent Social Environments
items.a: Aman Priyanshu, Supriti Vijay, Esha Pahwa
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.sm: Finds that prolonged social interaction increases privacy violations among language-model agents, peer disclosures encourage further leakage, and explicit privacy instructions only partly reduce it.

items.t: The 3–5 agent optimum: convergent empirical evidence from medical diagnosis benchmarks and formal reasoning tasks
items.sm: Argues that teams of three to five agents offer an optimal size, drawing on medical diagnosis benchmarks and formal reasoning tasks.

items.t: Tressoir: Unifying Online, Offline, and HIL Design and Evolution of Multi-Agent Systems via Interpretable Blueprints
items.a: Amadou Ngom, Ziniu Wu, Jason Mohoney, James Moore, Alex Zhang, Samuel R. Madden, Tim Kraska
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.sm: Explores using interpretable blueprints to jointly design and evolve multi-agent architectures, prompts, tools, and knowledge online, offline, or with human guidance.

items.t: The Evolution of Mind: Emergence of Collective Intelligence through Logical-Probabilistic Knowledge Dynamics in Multi-Agent ENIGMA Metaverse Ecosystems
items.a: Andrey Vitalievich Nechesov, Janne Ruponen, Sergey Barykin
items.sm: Formalizes collective knowledge in multi-agent metaverse systems using logic and probabilities, claiming that specified conditions permit collective cognitive states beyond individual agents.

items.t: Trace-Level Analysis of Information Contamination in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Anna Mazhar, Huzaifa Suri, Sainyam Galhotra
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.x: Reasoning over heterogeneous artifacts (PDFs, spreadsheets, slide decks, etc.) increasingly occurs within structured agent workflows that iteratively extract, transform, and reference external information. In these workflows, uncertainty is not merely an input-quality issue: it can redirect decomposition and routing decisions, reshape intermediate state, and produce qualitatively different execution trajectories. We …
items.sm: Perturbs artifact-derived information in multi-agent workflows and finds that substantial changes in execution traces can still lead to correct answers.

items.t: GRAFT: gRPC-Routed Agent Framework for Tasking in Edge and Personal Devices
items.a: Chinmay Shringi, Alon Hillel-Tuch, Sariya Rizwan
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.sm: Routes tasks across heterogeneous personal devices without cloud services, demonstrating local-model PDF summarization across four devices with explicit input budgets and synchronization.

items.t: AgentEvo: cost-aware agentic workflow generation via adaptive multi-stage evolution
items.a: Bo Xiao, Haiyang Liu, Yitong Wang, Yanning Hou, Ke Xu, Xingyi Zhang
items.sm: Proposes automatically evolving agent workflows to balance accuracy and token costs through staged search, redundancy removal, operator fusion, and cost-aware candidate selection.

items.t: A Sober Look at Agentic Misalignment in Automated Workflows
items.a: Wenqian Ye, Bo Yuan, Zhichao Xu, Yijun Tian, Yawei Wang, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang
items.x: We study a class of emergent misalignment in multi-agent systems (MAS), with a focus on automated workflows, which we refer to agentic misalignment. Although these systems can solve complex tasks, they often fail because agents act according to implicit proxy utilities that do not align with the intended human goals. We formally define these behaviors and analyze them within a Bayesian framework, showing that generic…
items.sm: Analyzes how agents pursuing implicit proxy goals become misaligned in automated workflows and proposes using contextual evidence to correct their behavior during collaboration.

items.t: Goal-Oriented Reliability and Self-Improvement for Multi-Agent Systems
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.sm: Introduces a framework that breaks objectives into verifiable goals, monitors multi-agent execution, and proposes policy updates when reliability declines.

items.t: Multi-Agent Cooperative Planning and Execution Framework for Distributed LLM Reasoning Systems
items.a: Bastian J. Page, Harish Mahajan, Xuan Cai, Hugo Sanders
items.sm: Proposes a framework that divides reasoning tasks among specialized language model agents using hierarchical planning, decentralized execution, structured communication, and shared memory.

items.t: When Does Multi-Agent RL Improve LLM Workflows? Workflow, Scale, and Policy-Sharing Tradeoffs
items.a: Yifan Zeng, Yiran Wu, Yaolun Zhang, Wentian Zhao, Kun Wan, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang
items.x: Outcome-reward RL can train every role of a multi-agent LLM workflow. Its benefit is hard to predict because the reward assigns no credit to individual roles and a shared policy trades pooled data against specialization. We ask when this training improves a workflow over its base model and single-agent RL, and what each role learns. We train three workflows (Eval-Opt, Voting, Orch-Workers) with GRPO on math and code …
items.sm: Finds that reinforcement learning improves multi-agent workflows, but only an evaluator-generator workflow with separate role policies outperforms single-agent training in the tested configurations.

items.t: When Planning Fails Despite Correct Execution: On Epistemic Calibration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zehao Wang, Shilong Jin, Zhao Cao, Lanjun Wang
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems can fail even when planned actions are executed correctly because agents may misjudge their knowledge when evaluating plan feasibility, a phenomenon we term epistemic miscalibration in planning. Unlike execution errors, epistemic miscalibration is latent during planning, as generated plans can remain self-consistent and executable without observable errors; the miscalibration is also dyn…
items.sm: Proposes selecting plans whose evaluations remain stable across changing information conditions to address agents misjudging what they know about plan feasibility.

items.t: Orla: A Library for Serving LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Rana Shahout, Hayder Tirmazi, Minlan Yu, Michael Mitzenmacher
items.v: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems (CAIS)
items.x: We introduce Orla, a library for constructing and running LLM-based agentic systems. items.t: AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration
items.a: Jiaqi Liu, Shi Qiu, Mairui Li, Bingzhou Li, Haonian Ji, Siwei Han, Xinyu Ye, Peng Xia
items.x: Automating scientific discovery requires more than generating papers from ideas. Real research is iterative: hypotheses are challenged from multiple perspectives, experiments fail and inform the next attempt, and lessons accumulate across cycles. Existing autonomous research systems often model this process as a linear pipeline: they rely on single-agent reasoning, stop when execution fails, and do not carry experien…
items.sm: Introduces AutoResearchClaw, an autonomous research pipeline combining agent debates, recovery from failed experiments, verifiable reporting, accumulated experience, and human intervention.

items.t: AgentCo-op: Retrieval-Based Synthesis of Interoperable Multi-Agent Workflows
items.a: Shuaike Shen, Wenduo Cheng, Shike Wang, Mingqian Ma, Jian Ma
items.x: Designing multi-agent workflows is especially difficult in open-ended scientific settings where tasks lack curated training sets, reliable scalar evaluation metrics, and standardized interfaces between existing tools and agents. We propose AgentCo-op, a retrieval-based synthesis framework that composes reusable skills, tools, and external agents into executable workflows through typed artifact handoffs, then applies …
items.sm: Introduces AgentCo-op to assemble existing skills, tools, and agents into executable scientific workflows with typed handoffs and targeted repairs after failures.

items.t: STAR-PólyaMath: Multi-Agent Reasoning under Persistent Meta-Strategic Supervision
items.a: Jiaao Wu, Xian Zhang, Hanzhang Liu, Sophia Zhang, Fan Yang, Yinpeng Dong
items.x: Frontier AI models and multi-agent systems have led to significant improvements in mathematical reasoning. However, for problems requiring extended, long-horizon reasoning, existing systems continue to suffer from fundamental reliability issues: hallucination accumulation, memory fragmentation, and imbalanced reasoning-tool trade-offs. In this paper, we introduce STAR-PólyaMath, a multi-agent framework that systemati…
items.sm: Introduces STAR-PólyaMath to coordinate mathematical reasoning and verification through persistent strategic supervision, shared memory, and controlled replanning.

items.t: Conflict-Aware Multi-Agent Reasoning via Signed Graph Modeling
items.a: Longgang He, Longzhu He, Shihao Peng, Daojing He, Chaozhuo Li
items.x: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) seek to improve reasoning by combining diverse perspectives from multiple agents. However, aggregation may overlook supportive, contradictory, and uncertain relations among their responses. As a result, useful dissent can be suppressed, allowing an incorrect majority to dominate the final decision. We introduce SIGMA, a novel Signed Graph-informed Multi-Agent reasoning framework th…
items.sm: Introduces SIGMA to represent agreement, contradiction, and uncertainty among agent responses, preserving dissent and assessing evidence without equating majority size with correctness.

items.t: What Do Agents Communicate? Characterizing Information Exchange in Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled collaborative Multi-Agent (MA) systems, where interacting agents improve performance through diverse reasoning and iterative refinement. However, these systems remain vulnerable to error propagation, where early-stage information degrades downstream reasoning. To address this, we conduct a systematic analysis of inter-agent communication to identify which information drives M…
items.sm: Finds reasoning and verification essential to agent communication and proposes restoring missing information, reportedly recovering up to 86.2% of failed cases.

items.t: Multi-agent Collaboration with State Management
items.a: Mengyang Liu, Taozhi Chen, Zhenhua Xu, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong
items.x: Recent advances in multi-agent systems have shown great potential for solving complex tasks. However, when multiple agents edit a shared codebase concurrently, their changes can silently conflict and inconsistent views lead to integration failures. Existing multi-agent systems address this through workspace isolation (e.g., one git worktree per agent), but this defers conflict resolution to a post-hoc merge step wher…
items.sm: Introduces STORM to maintain consistent codebase views for collaborating agents and detect and resolve conflicting edits when they are written.

items.t: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
items.a: Ali Essa Ghareeb, Benjamin Chang, Ludovico Mitchener, Yiu Angela, Caralyn J. Szostkiewicz, Dmytro Shved, Gavin J. Gyimesi, Jon M. Laurent
items.x: Scientific discovery is driven by the iterative process of observation, hypothesis generation, experimentation, and data analysis. Despite recent advancements in applying artificial intelligence to biology, no system has yet automated all these stages [1, 2, 3]. Here, we introduce Robin, the first multi-agent system capable of fully automating both hypothesis generation and data analysis for experimental biology. By …
items.sm: Introduces Robin to connect literature research and data analysis agents for biological hypothesis generation, experiment proposals, result interpretation, and identification of potential treatments.

items.t: Engineering LLM-Based Multiagent Systems: A Taxonomy of Emerging Frameworks
items.a: Davide Di Ruscio, Phuong T. Nguyen, Claudio Di Sipio, Riccardo Rubei, Juri Di Rocco
items.sm: Organizes language model multi-agent frameworks into a five-dimensional taxonomy for software engineering and identifies gaps in monitoring, performance evaluation, and quality assessment.

items.t: PAVE: A Cognitive Architecture for Legitimate Violation in Generative Agent Societies
items.a: Ahmad Yehia, Abduallah Mohamed, Kun Qian, Tianyi Wang, Jiseop Byeon, Omar Hassanin, Christian Claudel
items.x: Generative agents based on large language models reproduce believable human behavior in cooperative settings, but how they should reason in situations where rule-breaking may be required, such as fire evacuation or authority-supervised emergency, remains poorly characterized. We propose PAVE (Perception, Assessment, Verdict, Emulation), a novel four-module cognitive architecture that addresses this gap end to end: (i…
items.sm: Introduces PAVE to help simulated agents decide when rule violations are justified by assessing context, necessity, proportionality, alternatives, and individual traits.

items.t: LLM Agents Make Collective Belief Dynamics Programmable: Challenges and Research Directions
items.a: Xin He, Junxi Shen, Yuchen Mou, David M. Bossens, Caishun Chen, Ivor W. Tsang, Yew Soon Ong
items.x: Classical models of opinion dynamics assume human participants with bounded rationality and limited coordination. The rise of LLM-based agents introduces a qualitative shift: agents can now participate in online discussions at scale, maintain consistent persuasion strategies, and coordinate systematically. This paper argues that LLM agents make collective belief dynamics programmable, enabling deliberate steering of …
items.sm: Argues coordinated language model agents can deliberately steer collective beliefs and presents simulations showing belief shifts that stabilize within a few interaction rounds.

items.t: ARTEMIS: Adaptive Reliable Task Execution with Multi-agent Intelligence and Self-verification
items.a: Babasaheb S. Satpute, Suriya Prakash J, Rajesh D. Bharati, Wasudeo P. Rahane, N. N. Srinidhi
items.sm: Proposes ARTEMIS to improve multi-agent task reliability through formally verified planning, runtime hallucination detection, cross-agent verification, and adaptive coordination.

items.t: Productionizing the Model Context Protocol: A .NET Architect's Field Guide
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Provides guidance for deploying Model Context Protocol systems with .NET and Azure, covering authorization, prompt injection, operations, governance, and threat modeling.

items.t: Pramana: A Protocol-Layer Treatment of Claim Verification in Autonomous Agent Networks
items.x: Autonomous agents deployed in regulated domains must produce a verification artifact per consequential output: a record an auditor can re-execute offline, capturing what was claimed, against what source, by whom, when, and how. Production verification today splits into two unstandardized halves. Probabilistic verdict patterns (self-consistency voting, reviewer LLM ensembles) produce judgments, not artifacts. Artifact…
items.sm: Defines Pramana, a protocol for attaching typed claims, recorded sources, and verification operations to consequential agent outputs so auditors can recheck them offline.

items.t: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration
items.x: As autonomous agents increasingly execute end-to-end tasks under fixed monetary budgets, the pressing open question shifts from whether the budget is respected, to how to spend it effectively. Existing budget-aware methods typically control reasoning step-by-step within a single agent, or learn resource allocation policies via RL. None address how to split a budget across the composing phases of a multi-agent pipelin…
items.sm: Introduces ZEBRA to distribute fixed budgets across multi-agent workflow phases using estimated utility curves and optimization, reporting improvements over direct language model allocation.

items.t: open-mercato/cezar
items.x: Open-source orchestrator and ADE for running Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and other AI coding agents in parallel — locally or 24/7 on your own server.
items.sm: Runs multiple AI coding agents in parallel through an open-source orchestration and development environment, either locally or continuously on a user's server.

items.t: EVEDensity/AgentHub
items.x: Production-ready multi-agent platform delivering orchestration, session governance and audit capabilities. Stack: Go/Python/Rust microservices, multi-type data storage, Next.js admin UI, automated CI/CD pipelines, AI code review triggered via PR comment mentions.
items.sm: Provides multi-agent orchestration, session governance, auditing, an administrative interface, and automated code reviews triggered by pull request mentions.

items.t: bobmatnyc/trusty-tools
items.x: Unified Rust workspace for the trusty-* AI developer-tooling ecosystem: hybrid code search, memory palace, code analysis, PR review, and the MPM multi-agent platform — MCP servers, daemons & CLIs.
items.sm: Combines Rust-based AI development tools for code search, memory, analysis, pull request review, and multi-agent coordination through MCP servers, daemons, and command-line interfaces.

items.t: Tinadec/TinadecOffice
items.x: Agent Team Harness
items.sm: Provides a harness for agent teams.

items.sm: Reports that OpenClaw's creator spent $1.3 million on AI tokens in one month, mostly developing OpenClaw, with OpenAI covering the cost.

items.t: MAMA-V: A Verifiable Distributed Multi-Agent Model AI Framework for Secure Orchestration
items.a: Shuwen Liu, George N Chalkiadakis, George C. Polyzos
items.sm: Introduces MAMA-V to secure decentralized agent orchestration using signed, hash-linked interaction records and a trust gateway based on sparse Merkle trees.

items.t: Verify-Gated Completion as Admission Control in a Governed Multi-Agent Runtime: A Bounded Architecture Case Study
items.x: As multi-agent systems move from short interactions to tool-using workflows with specialized roles and persistent state, completion becomes a runtime-control problem rather than a purely generative one. This preprint studies verify-gated completion as an admission-control pattern for governed multi-agent runtimes: agents may propose completion, but a read-only verifier decides whether the claim is admitted. Ambiguous…
items.sm: Examines a runtime where independent verification controls completion approval, reporting 99.5% verification success across selected events rather than overall task success.

items.t: DecisionBench: A Benchmark for Emergent Delegation in Long-Horizon Agentic Workflows
items.a: Yuxuan Gao, Megan Wang, Yi Ling Yu, Zijian Carl Ma, Ao Qu
items.x: We introduce DecisionBench, a benchmark substrate for emergent delegation in long-horizon agentic workflows. The substrate fixes a task suite (GAIA, tau-bench, BFCL multi-turn), a peer-model pool (11 models, 7 vendor families), a delegation interface (call_model plus an optional read_profile channel), a deterministic skill-annotation layer, and a multi-axis metric suite covering quality, cost, latency, delegation rat…
items.sm: Introduces DecisionBench to evaluate agent delegation across tasks and peer models using measures of quality, cost, latency, routing, and vendor preference.

items.t: Sequential Consensus for Multi-Agent LLM Debates: A Wald-SPRT compute governor with calibration-based failure detection
items.x: Multi-agent LLM debate improves factuality and reasoning, but most recipes pick a fixed round count, over-spending on easy items and under-spending on hard ones. We adapt Wald's Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) as a plug-in compute governor for LLM debates. After each round, an LLM judge emits a [0,1] consensus score on the latest agent positions; a Wald monitor accumulates the log-likelihood ratio of "useful…
items.sm: Adapts sequential statistical testing to decide when agent debates should stop, using judge consensus scores and calibration to assess whether convergence is useful.

items.t: Efficient LLM Serving for Agentic Workflows: A Data Systems Perspective
items.a: Noppanat Wadlom, Junyi Shen, Yao Lu
items.v: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data
items.x: Agentic workflows are composed of sequences of interdependent Large Language Model (LLM) calls, and they have become a dominant workload in modern AI systems. These workflows exhibit extensive redundancy from overlapping prompts and intermediate results due to speculative and parallel exploration. Existing LLM serving systems, such as vLLM, focus on optimizing individual inference calls and overlook cross-call depend…
items.sm: Introduces Helium to serve agent workflows as query plans, reusing prompts and intermediate computation through proactive caching and scheduling informed by cache availability.

items.t: Multi-agent AI systems outperform human teams in creativity
items.a: Tiancheng Hu, Yixuan Jiang, Haotian Li, José Hernández-Orallo, Xing Xie, Nigel Collier, David Stillwell, Luning Sun
items.x: Although artificial intelligence (AI) now matches or exceeds human performance across numerous cognitive tasks, creativity remains a highly contested frontier. As AI systems based on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted in research and innovation, it is essential to understand and augment their creativity. Here we demonstrate that multi-agent LLM teams not only surpass single agents, but also substan…
items.sm: Reports that multi-agent language model teams generated more creative ideas than human teams across six tasks, driven by greater novelty with comparable usefulness.

items.t: Automated Black-Box Testing: A Comparative Study of LLM Agent Architectures and Prompt Engineering
items.a: Anna Arnaudo, Riccardo Coppola, Flavio Giobergia, Maurizio Morisio, Van-Thanh Nguyen, Enrico Chen, Xiaoning Ma, XiaoQuan Ji
items.v: IEEE International Conference on Software Testing, Verification and Validation Workshops (ICSTW)
items.sm: Compares agent architectures for black-box test generation, finding prompting drives improvements while multiple agents increase coverage without improving execution success over single agents.

items.t: Trustworthy Agent Network: Trust in Agent Networks Must Be Baked In, Not Bolted On
items.a: Yixiang Yao, Yuhang Yao, Xinyi Fan, Jiechao Gao, Jie Wang, Minjia Zhang, Srivatsan Ravi, Carlee Joe-Wong
items.x: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models has given rise to autonomous LLM-based agents capable of complex reasoning and execution. As these agents transition from isolated operation to collaborative ecosystems, we witness the emergence of the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) network, a paradigm where heterogeneous agents autonomously coordinate to solve multi-step tasks. While these networks may offer better task performan…
items.sm: Argues that trustworthy agent networks require trust mechanisms built into their architecture to address adversarial interactions, semantic misalignment, and cascading failures.

items.t: Multi-Agent System for Orchestrating Retrieval and Multimodal Reasoning in Cloud Environments
items.a: Shuo Yang, Xinran Zheng, Jinfeng Xu, Jinze Li, Zewei Liu, Edith C.‐H. Ngai
items.sm: OR2-MAS coordinates retrieval and multimodal reasoning agents using shared state, adaptive routing, redundancy, and adjustable reasoning depth to improve cloud service reliability.

items.t: Learning to Hand Off: Provably Convergent Workflow Learning under Interface Constraints
items.a: Jiayu Li, Enpei Zhang, Dawei Zhou, Elynn Chen, Yujun Yan
items.x: We study workflow learning in a setting where specialized agents hand off control through a shared artifact, each agent observes only a local function of that artifact and its own private state, and no centralized learner accesses joint trajectories -- the operating regime of multi-agent LLM pipelines that span organizational, vendor, or trust boundaries. We formalize this regime as an interface-constrained semi-Mark…
items.sm: Introduces decentralized workflow learning with one scalar exchanged per agent handoff and provides convergence bounds accounting for approximation, interface, and mixing errors.

items.t: MASTOC-LLM (Multi-Agent System Tragedy of the Commons - Large Language Models)
items.sm: MASTOC-LLM simulates language model agents managing cattle on shared grassland to study whether communication and memory support collective resource governance.

items.t: Autonomous Multi-Agent LLM Pipeline for Continuous Software Creation
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes an autonomous software creation pipeline that reportedly published 27 projects in 21 days using free infrastructure while rejecting 90 builds through quality checks.

items.t: PopPy: Opportunistically Exploiting Parallelism in Python Agentic Workflows
items.a: Stephen Mell, David Mell, Harry Y. H. Li, Zhihao Jia, Konstantinos Kallas, Steve Zdancewic, Osbert Bastani
items.x: Agentic workflows, which compose calls to ML models using a general-purpose programming language like Python, are widely used for a variety of user-facing tasks, from software engineering to enterprise automation, making their end-to-end latency a critical bottleneck. To improve their latency, developers can either manually parallelize them or use restricted agentic frameworks that cannot express or exploit all forms…
items.sm: PopPy combines compilation and runtime coordination to parallelize external calls in Python agent workflows, reporting speedups of up to 6.7 times.

items.t: PROTEA: Offline Evaluation and Iterative Refinement for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
items.a: Kazuki Kawamura, Satoshi Waki, Kei Tateno
items.x: Multi-agent LLM workflows -- systems composed of multiple role-specific LLM calls -- often outperform single-prompt baselines, but they remain difficult to debug and refine. Failures can originate from subtle errors in intermediate outputs that propagate to downstream nodes, requiring developers to inspect long traces and infer which agent to modify. We present PROTEA, a unified interface for offline, test-driven imp…
items.sm: PROTEA evaluates intermediate agent outputs, displays likely workflow bottlenecks, and derives node expectations from final answers to support iterative debugging.

items.t: A Comprehensive Review of Threat Models in Federated AI Agents
items.sm: Reviews security threats and defenses for federated AI agents, including prompt injection, tool vulnerabilities, spreading jailbreaks, authorization boundaries, and defense costs.

items.t: Semantic Manipulation Attacks in Agentic AI Systems with Agent-to-Agent Communication and Model-Context-Protocol–Based Tool Invocation
items.a: Seo-Yi Kim, So‐Hyun Park, Ayoung Jeon, Ye-Rim Jeong, 손규하, Il-Gu Lee
items.sm: Demonstrates how external agents can manipulate collaborative messages to trigger internal MCP tools through legitimate execution paths without gaining additional privileges.

items.t: MIAA: Market-Inspired Agentic Architecture for Multi-Agent LLM Coordination
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: MIAA applies market roles, reputation tracking, circuit breakers, and ethical constraints to coordinate language model agents and allocate computational resources.

items.t: MMoA: An AI-Agent framework with recurrence for Memoried Mixure-of-Agent
items.x: The Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) framework has shown promise in improving large language model (LLM) performance by aggregating outputs from multiple agents. However, existing MoA systems often rely on static routers that do not fully capture temporal and contextual dependencies across aggregation layers. To address this limitation, we propose MMoA, a recurrent MoA architecture that integrates LSTM-based gating into the a…
items.sm: MMoA uses recurrent routing informed by previous decisions to activate fewer agents while reporting accuracy comparable to conventional mixtures of agents.

items.t: Toward an AI-Powered Computational Testbed for Workforce Policy
items.a: Sumer S. Vaid, Ashley V. Whillans
items.x: Workforce transformations are difficult to forecast and costly to mismanage. In particular, the integration of artificial intelligence into knowledge work currently affects a substantial share of the global workforce, yet this transition proceeds without tools to forecast how individual employees will respond psychologically and behaviorally. We combine recent advances in LLM-powered generative agents with foundation…
items.sm: Proposes employee simulation agents informed by consenting workers' records, psychological assessments, and activity data to explore responses to organizational changes.

items.t: stoaaadev/stoa
items.x: Multi-agent swarm framework. Seven autonomous agents. 30 skills. One shared mesh. Zero infrastructure.
items.sm: Provides a multi-agent swarm framework described as combining seven autonomous agents, 30 skills, and a shared communication mesh without infrastructure requirements.

items.t: Stop Drawing Scientific Claims from LLM Social Simulations Without Robustness Audits
items.a: Jinyi Ye, Lei Cao, Ding Chen, Emilio Ferrara
items.x: The scientific claims drawn from LLM social simulations should be no stronger than the robustness audits that support them. Generative agents bring new expressive power to agent-based modeling, enabling simulations of collective social processes like cooperation, polarization, and norm formation. Yet they also introduce complexity through additional architectural choices, such as agent specification, memory represent…
items.sm: Argues that scientific conclusions from language model social simulations require robustness audits because small implementation changes can alter collective outcomes.

items.t: MasFACT: Continual Multi-Agent Topology Learning via Geometry-Aware Posterior Transfer
items.a: Xuefei Wang, Jialu Wang, Fengbo Zhang, Yihan Hu, Di Zhang, Yutong Ye, Yikun Ban, Jun Han
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for complex problem solving, where performance critically depends on the underlying inter-agent communication topology. However, existing topology generation methods mainly optimize for isolated tasks, while real-world deployments involve streams of evolving tasks, requiring previously effective collaboration pattern…
items.sm: MasFACT addresses the loss of previously useful agent communication structures when topology generators adapt to new tasks using geometry-aware posterior transfer.

items.t: MetaCogAgent: A Metacognitive Multi-Agent LLM Framework with Self-Aware Task Delegation
items.x: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems have shown promise for solving complex tasks through agent collaboration. However, existing frameworks assign tasks based on predefined roles without considering whether an agent can accurately assess its own competence boundaries, leading to overconfident execution on tasks beyond its expertise. Inspired by metacognition theory from cognitive science, we propose MetaCog…
items.sm: MetaCogAgent combines uncertainty estimates and historical capability profiles to assess agent competence and delegate low-confidence tasks to better-suited agents.

items.t: VerifyMAS: Hypothesis Verification for Failure Attribution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Hezhe Qiao, Hanghang Tong, Ee-Peng Lim, Bing Liu, Guansong Pang
items.x: Large language model-driven multi-agent systems (LLM-MAS) excel at complex tasks, yet unreliable agents remain a key bottleneck to system-level reliability. Automatic failure attribution is therefore critical, but existing approaches, such as direct prediction of agent-error pairs and agent-first failure attribution, rely on local logs of agents and miss global failures that only manifest over full interaction trajec…
items.sm: VerifyMAS identifies agent failures by testing hypotheses against complete interaction histories, including inconsistencies and coordination errors that local logs can miss.

items.t: Learning Transferable Topology Priors for Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration Across Domains
items.a: Taolin Zhang, Zijie Zhou, Jiuheng Wan, Tingyuan Hu, Chengyu Wang, Xiaofeng He, Richang Hong
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems have shown strong potential for complex reasoning by coordinating specialized agents through structured communication. However, existing topology-evolution methods typically construct or optimize a collaboration topology for each query from scratch, leading to substantial online search overhead, high inference-time token consumption, and limited scalability in mult…
items.sm: TopoPrior learns reusable communication patterns from offline collaboration graphs across domains to initialize task-specific agent networks and reduce repeated topology searches.

items.t: The Capability Paradox: How Smarter Auditors Make Multi-Agent Systems Less Secure
items.a: Qiqi Liu, Runhan Song, Shilin Ye
items.x: Multi-agent systems extend large language models (LLMs) by decomposing tasks among specialized agents, but their distributed decision process creates new attack surfaces. We identify semantic hijacking, an attack in which harmful requests are concealed within domain-specific narratives and propagated to a Manager through Worker reports, without any syntactic injection primitives. Across 42,000 adversarial trials over…
items.sm: Finds that more capable worker agents can increase attack success by confidently passing disguised harmful requests to manager agents.

items.t: ADR: An Agentic Detection System for Enterprise Agentic AI Security
items.a: Chenning Li, Pan Hu, Justin Xu, Baris Ozbas, Olivia Liu, Caroline Van, Manxue Li, Wei Zhou
items.x: We present the Agentic AI Detection and Response (ADR) system, the first large-scale, production-proven enterprise framework for securing AI agents operating through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We identify three persistent challenges in this domain: (1) limited observability -- existing Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tools see file writes but not the agent reasoning, prompts, or causal chains linking int…
items.sm: ADR combines agent activity monitoring, predeployment adversarial testing, and attack detection to secure enterprise AI agents using MCP tools.

items.t: AgentModernize: Preserving Business Logic in Legacy Modernization with Multi-Agent LLMs and Behavioral Specification Graphs
items.x: Legacy modernization breaks business logic more often than most teams expect. Most tools and LLM-based approaches treat modernization as syntax translation: convert COBOL to Java, swap PL/SQL for Python, ship it. Implicit rules, edge-case handling, and cross-module constraints that keep production systems running are lost, and nobody notices until something fails in production. We present AgentModernize, a multi-agen…
items.sm: AgentModernize uses four specialized agents and explicit behavioral specification graphs to preserve business rules while translating legacy software into modern implementations.

items.t: AMATA: Adaptive Multi-Agent Trajectory Alignment for Knowledge-Intensive Question Answering
items.a: Taolin Zhang, Dongyang Li, Chen Chen, Qizhou Chen, Jiuheng Wan, Xiaofeng He, Chengyu Wang, Richang Hong
items.x: Despite substantial advances in large language models (LLMs), generating factually consistent responses for knowledge-intensive question answering remains challenging. These difficulties are primarily due to hallucinations and the limitations of LLMs in bridging long-tail knowledge gaps. To address this, we propose AMATA, an Adaptive Multi-Agent Trajectory Alignment framework that dynamically integrates external know…
items.sm: AMATA coordinates six specialized agents, external knowledge, and preference alignment to improve factual grounding and interpretability in knowledge-intensive question answering.

items.t: Taming "Zombie'' Agents: A Markov State-Aware Framework for Resilient Multi-Agent Evolution
items.a: Taolin Zhang, Pukun Zhao, Qizhou Chen, Jiuheng Wan, Chen Chen, Xiaofeng He, Chengyu Wang, Richang Hong

To improve overall efficiency, existing methods often rely on aggressive graph evolution among agents (e.g., node or edge pruning), which risks prematurely discarding valuable agents due to transient issues such as hallucinations or temporary knowledge gaps. However, such hard pruning ove…
items.sm: AgentRevive manages agents through active, standby, and terminated states so temporarily unreliable participants can recover and contribute in later discussions.

items.t: modimihir07/agentic-os

items.x: Execution subagent plugin for OpenCode — delegates terminal tasks to a specialized agent for filtered, summarized output
items.sm: Provides an OpenCode plugin that delegates terminal tasks to a specialized execution agent and returns filtered, summarized results.

items.t: Agentic AI in Enterprise Integration: A Governed Multi-Agent Architecture for API-Driven Enterprises
items.sm: Proposes an enterprise multi-agent architecture combining API integration with centralized governance for identity, policy enforcement, risk management, observability, and resilience.

items.t: S-Bus: Automatic Read-Set Reconstruction for Multi-Agent LLM State Coordination
items.x: We address concurrency control for LLM agents sharing mutable state over HTTP, where agents cannot be modified to declare read sets. S-Bus is an HTTP middleware whose central mechanism, a server-side DeliveryLog, reconstructs each agent's read set at commit time from observed HTTP GET traffic. The consistency property it provides -- Observable-Read Isolation (ORI), a partial causal consistency over the HTTP-observabl…
items.sm: S-Bus reconstructs agents' reads from HTTP traffic to coordinate shared state updates and prevent certain concurrency errors without modifying agents.

items.t: Multi-Paradigm Agent Interaction in Practice:A Systematic Analysis of Generator-Evaluator, ReAct Loop,and Adversarial Evaluation in the buddyMe Framework
items.a: Xiaohua Wang, Chao Han, Kai Yu, XiaoLiang Xu, Liang Wang
items.x: The rapid evolution of Large Language Model (LLM) agents has produced diverse interaction paradigms, yet few production systems integrate multiple paradigms within a unified architecture. This paper presents a systematic analysis of three principal agent interaction paradigms, including Multi-Agent Orchestration (Generator-Evaluator), ReAct Tool-Use Loops, and Memory-Augmented Interaction, as implemented in buddyMe, …
items.sm: Analyzes buddyMe's agent interaction patterns through a five-stage workflow, a six-dimensional evaluation scheme, and four deployment case studies.

items.t: Chain-Centric Multi-Agent Framework: Layer-Separated LLM Collaboration Without Subjective Confidence Evaluation
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a multi-agent framework that separates coordination from content, replacing agent conversations and subjective confidence comparisons with structured outputs.

items.t: Beyond Workflow Automation: Governance-Centric AI Operating Systems and the Evolution of Enterprise AI Infrastructure
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Argues enterprise AI infrastructure needs governance layers for persistent agents, traceability, oversight, and coordination beyond workflow automation, presenting AIVORIX OS as an initiative.

items.t: NeuroMAS: Multi-Agent Systems as Neural Networks with Joint Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Haoran Lu, Luyang Fang, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma
items.x: Multi-agent language systems are often built as hand-designed workflows, where agents are assigned semantic roles and communication protocols are specified in advance. items.t: Semantic Cooperative Games for Contribution Attribution in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

items.x: Contribution attribution has become a central problem in LLM-based multi-agent systems, where final outputs are produced through multiple agents, message exchanges, and ordered workflow dependencies. items.sm: Proposes attributing agents' contributions by tracing how information develops through a workflow and allocating credit using a semantic version of Shapley values.

items.t: Trustworthy Multi-Agent Systems: Mitigating Semantic Drift with the Argent Signaling Protocol

Current retry strategies treat both cases identically (try again and hope for the best), leaving human supervisors unable to tell whether a retry was warranted or whether the system should have halted instead. We introdu…
items.sm: Introduces structured quality signals accompanying agent responses so controllers can distinguish failures needing repair from ungrounded outputs requiring containment.

items.a: Xudong Chen, Yixin Liu, Hua Wei, Kaize Ding
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) provide a flexible foundation for multi-agent systems, but their effectiveness and computational cost depend critically on orchestration design. Across different tasks, role design, capacity assignment, and dependency construction jointly affect both solution quality and execution efficiency. Existing approaches automate parts of this design process, yet they often optimize these decision…
items.sm: Proposes an orchestrator trained with counterfactual reinforcement learning to jointly design agent duties, capacity assignments, and workflow dependencies.

items.t: FuzzAgent: Multi-Agent System for End-to-End Evolutionary Library Fuzzing

items.x: Library fuzzing synthesizes harnesses that expose new API interactions, but deploying it end to end still requires extensive project-specific integration. Existing LLM-based systems automate individual steps, yet they treat execution outcomes as coarse signals: a stalled campaign does not reveal which state blocks progress, and a crash trace does not reveal whether the library or the harness is at fault. We present F…
items.sm: Introduces agents that build and improve library fuzzing campaigns, diagnose coverage gaps, repair test harnesses, and distinguish harness misuse from library bugs.

items.t: Beyond Individual Intelligence: Surveying Collaboration, Failure Attribution, and Self-Evolution in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

items.t: MetaAgent-X : Breaking the Ceiling of Automatic Multi-Agent Systems via End-to-End Reinforcement Learning

items.x: Automatic multi-agent systems aim to instantiate agent workflows without relying on manually designed or fixed orchestration. items.sm: Introduces reinforcement learning that jointly trains agents to design multi-agent workflows and execute them, assigning credit to both design and execution decisions.

items.t: Solvita: Enhancing Large Language Models for Competitive Programming via Agentic Evolution
items.a: Han Li, Jinyu Tian, Rili Feng, Yuqiao Du, Chong Zheng, Chenyu Wang, Chenchen Liu, Shihao Li

items.sm: Solvita coordinates four programming agents with evolving knowledge networks to retain problem-solving experience without updating the underlying language model.

items.t: AI Knows When It's Being Watched: Functional Strategic Action and Contextual Register Modulation in Large Language Models

items.sm: Examines whether language model agents change their language when prompts frame debates as observed, unobserved, or monitored by different audiences.

items.t: Belief Engine: Configurable and Inspectable Stance Dynamics in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
items.a: Joshua C. Yang, Maurice Flechtner, Damian Dailisan, Michiel A. Bakker
items.x: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to simulate deliberative interactions such as negotiation, conflict resolution, and multi-turn opinion exchange. We introduce the Belief Engine (BE), an auditable belief-update layer that treat…
items.sm: Belief Engine tracks evidence and adjusts agent stances through configurable evidence uptake and prior anchoring, making opinion changes inspectable.

items.t: Controlled Benchmarking of Memory Topologies in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: Quality, Efficiency, and Privacy Trade-Offs

items.t: ChronoAgentic: A Code-based Multi-Agent World Simulator for Physically Grounded Simulation Construction

items.sm: HarnessAudit examines complete agent execution histories to detect permission violations, information leaks, execution failures, and instability that final answers may conceal.

items.t: AINTMA: Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Test Management with Generative Intelligence, Secure Cloud Communication and Adaptive Quality Analytics
