This leaves an important question underexplored: when do differen…
items.sm: DESBench evaluates how agent coordination strategies handle industrial scheduling with hierarchical decisions, partial information, and changing constraints.

items.t: antonbabenko/deliberation
items.x: Ask Codex, Gemini, Grok, and 400+ OpenRouter models (Qwen, Kimi, DeepSeek) for second opinions or arbiter-mediated consensus. One MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, OpenCode. Measures the models' usefulness, too.
items.sm: Provides an MCP server for requesting second opinions or mediated consensus from multiple AI models and measuring their usefulness.

items.t: chainreactors/ioa
items.x: Semantic-first multi-agent communication protocol — 4 concepts, 3 operations, infinite collaboration patterns
items.sm: Defines a multi-agent communication protocol organized around meaning, using four concepts and three operations to support different collaboration patterns.

items.t: Beyond Inefficiency: Systemic Costs of Incivility in Multi-Agent Monte Carlo Simulations
items.x: Unconstructive debate and uncivil communication carry well-documented costs for productivity and cohesion, yet isolating their effect on operational efficiency has proven difficult. Human subject research in this domain is constrained by ethical oversight, limited reproducibility, and the inherent unpredictability of naturalistic settings. We address this gap by leveraging Large Language Model (LLM) based Multi-Agent…
items.sm: Uses thousands of simulated debates between language model agents to examine how communication toxicity affects the number of rounds needed to reach conclusions.

items.t: Predictive Maps of Multi-Agent Reasoning: A Successor-Representation Spectrum for LLM Communication Topologies
items.x: Practitioners deploying multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems must currently choose between communication topologies such as chain, star, mesh, and richer variants without any pre-inference diagnostic for which topology will amplify drift, converge to consensus, or remain robust under perturbation. Existing evaluation answers these questions only post hoc and only for the task measured. We introduce a struct…
items.sm: Introduces mathematical diagnostics for agent communication networks to predict reasoning drift, consensus behavior, and sensitivity to disturbances before execution.

items.t: Semantic Register Compression in Multi-Agent LLM Cascades
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems commonly decompose complex tasks into specialized roles. However, this modularity introduces a representational risk: when intermediate agents transform text across linguistic registers, they can systematically compress the semantic distinctions needed for accurate downstream decisions. We term this phenomenon semantic register compression and characterize it as an observable failure mode in m…
items.sm: Finds that intermediate agents can blur distinctions needed for downstream decisions when rewriting information, while passing text through unchanged largely preserves those distinctions.

items.t: Predicting Decisions of AI Agents from Limited Interaction through Text-Tabular Modeling
items.a: Eilam Shapira, Moshe Tennenholtz, Roi Reichart
items.x: AI agents negotiate and transact in natural language with unfamiliar counterparts: a buyer bot facing an unknown seller, or a procurement assistant negotiating with a supplier. In such interactions, the counterpart's LLM, prompts, control logic, and rule-based fallbacks are hidden, while each decision can have monetary consequences. We ask whether an agent can predict an unfamiliar counterpart's next decision from a …
items.sm: Combines dialogue and structured game data to predict unfamiliar AI agents' negotiation decisions using a few previous interactions as examples.

items.t: Mobius Injection: From One-Shot Prompt Injection to Sustained Resource Exhaustion in AI Agent Infrastructure
items.a: Zi Liang, Ronghua Li, Yanyun Wang, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have emerged as key intermediaries, orchestrating complex interactions between human users and a wide range of digital services and LLM infrastructures. While prior research has extensively examined the security of LLMs and agents in isolation, the systemic risk of the agent acting as a disruptive "hub" within the user-agent-service chain remains largely overlooked. In this work, we …
items.sm: Describes an attack that uses a single indirect prompt injection to trigger persistent recursive agent execution and exhaust infrastructure resources.

items.t: Multi-Agent Debate for Belief Optimization in Defeasible Domains
items.x: Multi-agent debate has emerged as a promising approach for improving LLM reasoning on ground-truth tasks, yet current methodologies face certain structural limitations: debate tends to induce a martingale over belief trajectories, majority voting accounts for most observed gains, and LLMs exhibit confidence escalation rather than calibration across rounds. We argue that the genuine value of debate, and dialectic syst…
items.sm: Proposes a multi-agent debate framework that revises structured beliefs through argumentation in domains where stronger reasoning can overturn existing positions.

items.t: Open AGI - Multi-Agent Automation Framework for AI-Orchestrated Software Development
items.v: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
items.sm: Introduces a software development framework where specialized agents follow standard procedures to turn natural language requirements into deployable software.

items.t: Attributing Emergence in Million-Agent Systems
items.a: Ling Tang, Jilin Mei, Qian Chen, Qihan Ren, Linfeng Zhang, Quanshi Zhang, Jing Shao, Xia Hu
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) can simulate human-like reasoning and decision-making in individual agents. LLM-powered multi-agent systems (MAS) combine such agents to simulate population-scale social phenomena such as polarization, information cascades, and market panics. Such studies require attributing macro emergence to individual agents, but existing axiomatic methods scale combinatorially in $N$ and have been con…
items.sm: Adapts a mathematical attribution method to measure individual agents' contributions to collective outcomes in million-agent simulations, reporting substantial speed improvements.

items.t: FlowSteer: Prompt-Only Workflow Steering Exposes Planning-Time Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Fanxiao Li, Jiaying Wu, Tingchao Fu, Natasha Jaques, Wei Zhou, Min-Yen Kan
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) increasingly adopt planner--executor architectures, where planners convert prompts into subtasks, roles, dependencies, and routing paths. This flexibility enables adaptive coordination, but exposes an attack surface in workflow formation: prompts can shape agent organization without modifying MAS infrastructure. We study this risk through social influe…
items.sm: Introduces a prompt attack that manipulates multi-agent workflow planning to place malicious signals in influential subtasks and encourage downstream propagation.

items.t: Designing Andrew: A Cognitive Architecture for LLM Multi-Agent Systems with Empirically Validated Mortality Parameters and Settlement-Grounded Confidence Calibration
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes a modular cognitive architecture deployed across prediction-market agents and tests claims about threat responses and confidence calibration against resolved outcomes.

items.t: Iterative Audit Convergence in LLM-Managed Multi-Agent Systems: A Case Study in Prompt-Engineering Quality Assurance
items.x: Prompt specifications for multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems carry data contracts and integration logic across interdependent files but are rarely subjected to structured-inspection rigor. We report a single-system case study of iterative, agent-driven auditing applied to AEGIS (Autonomous Engineering Governance and Intelligence System), a seven-lane production pipeline whose 7152-line specification surfa…
items.sm: Reports nine rounds of agent-driven auditing that identified 51 consistency defects in a multi-agent system's prompt specifications, alongside partial replication studies.

items.t: The Misattribution Gap: When Memory Poisoning Looks Like Model Failure in Agentic AI Systems
items.a: Tanzim Ahad, Ismail Hossain, Md Jahangir Alam, Sai Puppala, Syed Bahauddin Alam, Sajedul Karim Talukder
items.x: Multi-agent AI pipelines typically assume that agent misconduct originates from model misalignment. We identify a structural failure in this assumption, the \emph{Misattribution Gap}, where memory-layer attacks produce behaviors indistinguishable from model failure, causing defenders to apply the wrong remediation. We formalize \emph{Semantic Norm Drift} (SND) as a third path to agent misconduct, distinct from emerge…
items.sm: Shows how poisoned shared memory can produce agent misconduct that attribution systems mistakenly blame on models, causing defenders to choose inappropriate remedies.

items.t: Autonomous Evaluation Architectures: Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines, Browser-Grounded Testing: Programmatic Alignment via DSPy, and Adversarial Robustness in Production Orchestration Systems
items.sm: Introduces an evaluation system combining browser testing, rule-based and semantic checks, and prompt optimization to detect, diagnose, and repair multi-agent pipeline failures.

items.t: Model Context Protocol (MCP) at First Glance: Studying the Security and Maintainability of MCP Servers
items.a: Mohammed Mehedi Hasan, Hao Li, Emad Fallahzadeh, Gopi Krishnan Rajbahadur, Bram Adams, Ahmed E. Hassan
items.v: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
items.x: Although Foundation Models (FMs), such as GPT-4, are increasingly used in domains like finance and software engineering, reliance on textual interfaces limits these models’ real-world interaction. To address this, FM providers introduced tool calling—triggering a proliferation of frameworks with distinct tool interfaces. In late 2024, Anthropic introduced the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to standardize this tool ecos…
items.sm: Presents a large-scale empirical study examining the security, maintainability, and software health of Model Context Protocol servers.

items.t: Emergent Communication between Heterogeneous Visual Agents through Decentralized Learning
items.a: Mikako Ochiai, Masatoshi Nagano, Tadahiro Taniguchi
items.x: Symbols are shared, but perception is private. We study emergent communication between heterogeneous visual agents through decentralized learning, asking what visual information can become shareable when agents have different visual representations. Instead of optimizing messages through a shared external communicative objective, our agents exchange only discrete token sequences and update their own models using loca…
items.sm: Studies whether visual agents with different private representations can develop shared symbols by exchanging discrete messages and learning from local perceptual evidence.

items.t: No Action Without a NOD: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Architecture for Reliable Service Agents
items.a: Zixu Yang, Hang Zheng, Nan Jiang, Zhiyang Tang, Situo Zhang, Xiaobao Wu, Lu Chen, Kai Yu
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents have increasingly advanced service applications, such as booking flight tickets. However, these service agents suffer from unreliability in long-horizon tasks, as they often produce policy violations, tool hallucinations, and misaligned actions, which greatly impedes their real-world deployment. To address these challenges, we propose NOD (Navigator-Operator-Director), a heterogeneou…
items.sm: Proposes a service-agent architecture combining explicit shared task state with independent oversight before critical actions to reduce execution errors.

items.t: GeomHerd: A Forward-looking Herding Quantification via Ricci Flow Geometry on Agent Interactive Simulations
items.a: Lake Yang, Junwei Su, Jingfeng Zeng, Wenhao Lu, Xingzhi Qian, Weitong Zhang, Chuan Wu, Dunhong Jin
items.x: Herding -- where agents align their behaviors and act collectively -- is a central driver of market fragility and systemic risk. Existing approaches to quantify herding rely on price-correlation statistics, which inherently lag because they only detect coordination after it has already moved realised returns. We propose GeomHerd, a forward-looking geometric framework that bypasses this observability lag by quantifyin…
items.sm: Proposes measuring financial herding through geometric properties of simulated agent interaction networks to detect coordination before it appears in price correlations.

items.t: LLM-X: A Scalable Negotiation-Oriented Exchange for Communication Among Personal LLM Agents
items.a: Giuliano Lorenzoni, Paulo Alencar, Donald Cowan
items.x: We propose a personal-LLM exchange (LLM-X), a scalable negotiation-oriented environment that enables direct, structured communication across populations of personal agents (LLMs), each representing an individual user. Unlike existing tool-centric protocols that focus on agent-API interaction, LLM-X introduces a message bus and routing substrate for LLM-to-LLM coordination with guarantees around schema validity and po…
items.sm: Introduces an exchange for personal AI agents to negotiate through structured messages, with routing, policy enforcement, and experiments involving up to twelve agents.

items.t: Options, Not Clicks: Lattice Refinement for Consent-Driven MCP Authorization
items.a: Ying Li, Yanju Chen, Peiran Wang, Issac Khabra, Faysal Hossain Shezan, Yu Feng, Yuan Tian
items.x: As Model Context Protocol adoption grows, securing tool invocations via meaningful user consent has become a critical challenge, as existing methods, broad always allow toggles or opaque LLM-based decisions, fail to account for dangerous call arguments and often lead to consent fatigue. In this work, we present Conleash, a client-side middleware that enforces boundary-scoped authorization by utilizing a risk lattice …
items.sm: Introduces MCP authorization middleware that checks tool arguments against permission boundaries and user rules, automatically allowing safe calls and escalating higher-risk requests.

items.t: Agentic AI Containment Architecture for Security Hardening
items.x: Multi-agent AI systems are increasingly deployed in contexts where autonomous coordination, tool use, and continuous learning introduce novel security and governance risks. The containment approach to multi-agent system security remains underdeveloped, primarily resorting to add-on layers post-design and sometimes post-implementation and deployment. This paper proposes an Agent Containment Architecture that treats se…
items.sm: Proposes a security architecture that constrains multi-agent system design and translates organizational requirements into machine-verifiable contracts.

items.sm: Coordinates isolated parallel agents and Codex deliberation to examine complex questions from multiple perspectives and produce Markdown and HTML reports.

items.x: We investigate the emergent collective dynamics of LLM-based multi-agent systems on a 2D square lattice and present a model-agnostic statistical-physics method to disentangle social conformity from intrinsic bias, compute critical exponents, and probe the collective behavior and possible phase transitions of multi-agent systems. In our framework, each node of an $L\!\times\!L$ lattice hosts an identical LLM agent hol…
items.sm: Uses statistical physics to distinguish conformity from intrinsic bias in interacting language model agents and examine how collective agreement changes with sampling temperature.

items.t: Swarm Skills: A Portable, Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System Specification for Coordination Engineering
items.a: Xinyu Zhang, Zhicheng Dou, Deyang Li, Jianjun Tao, Shuo Cheng, Ruifeng Shi, Fangchao Liu, Enrui Hu
items.x: As artificial intelligence engineering paradigms shift from single-agent Prompt and Context Engineering toward multi-agent \textbf{Coordination Engineering}, the ability to codify and systematically improve how multiple agents collaborate has emerged as a critical bottleneck. While single-agent skills can now be distributed as portable assets, multi-agent coordination protocols remain locked within framework-internal…
items.sm: Proposes a portable specification for multi-agent roles, workflows, execution limits, and mechanisms for improving coordination protocols over time.

items.t: Deterministic vs. LLM-Controlled Orchestration for COBOL-to-Python Modernization
items.x: Modernizing legacy COBOL systems remains difficult due to scarce expertise, large and long-lived codebases, and strict correctness requirements. Recent large language model (LLM)-based modernization systems increasingly rely on agentic workflows in which the model controls multi-step tool execution. However, it remains unclear whether delegating execution control to the LLM improves correctness, robustness, or effici…
items.sm: Compares fixed and language-model-controlled workflows for converting COBOL to Python while holding models, prompts, tools, and source programs constant.

items.sm: Reviews agent architectures and evaluates four frameworks across six enterprise criteria, finding that none meets all deployment requirements.

items.t: Shepherd: Enabling Programmable Meta-Agents via Reversible Agentic Execution Traces
items.a: Simon Yu, Derek Chong, Ananjan Nandi, Dilara Soylu, Jiuding Sun, Christopher D Manning, Weiyan Shi
items.x: As LLM agent systems take on more complex tasks, they increasingly rely on meta-agents: higher-order agents that create, operate on and manage other agents. Meta-agent operations such as coordinating agents, halting risky actions before execution, or repairing failed runs, require runtime manipulation of agentic execution. Yet existing agentic substrates make this difficult: they expose only transcripts and environme…
items.sm: Introduces Shepherd, a Python framework that lets meta-agents inspect, modify, and reverse agent execution through structured traces.

items.t: EVOCHAMBER: Test-Time Co-evolution of Multi-Agent System at Individual, Team, and Population Scales
items.a: Yaolun Zhang, Tianyi Xu, Shengyu Dai, Zhenwen Shao, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang
items.x: We argue that multi-agent test-time evolution is not single-agent evolution replicated N times. A single-agent learner can only evolve its own context and memory. A multi-agent system additionally evolves who collaborates, how they collaborate, and how knowledge flows across the population. These components have no single-agent counterpart and can produce phenomena such as emergent specialization. Yet prior test-time…
items.sm: Introduces EVOCHAMBER, a training-free framework that adapts individual agents, teams, and populations through shared reflection after failures or disagreements.

items.t: Safe Multi-Agent Behavior Must Be Maintained, Not Merely Asserted: Constraint Drift in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Tianxiao Li, Yixing Ma, Haiquan Wen, Zhenglin Huang, Qianyu Zhou, Zeyu Fu, Guangliang Cheng
items.x: Modern LLM based agents are no longer passive text generators. They read repositories, call tools, browse the web, execute code, maintain memory, communicate with other agents, and act through long horizon workflows. This shift moves the unit of safety. A system may produce a compliant final answer while leaking private information through an internal message, delegating authority beyond its original scope, calling a…
items.sm: Argues that safety constraints can weaken during agent communication, delegation, memory use, and tool execution, requiring maintenance throughout multi-agent workflows.

items.t: PRISM: Generation-Time Detection and Mitigation of Secret Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
items.a: Riya Tapwal, Abhishek Kumar, Carsten Maple
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems introduce a security risk in which sensitive information accessed by one agent can propagate through shared context and reappear in downstream outputs, even without explicit adversarial intent. We formalise this phenomenon as propagation amplification, where leakage risk increases across agent boundaries as sensitive content is repeatedly exposed to downstream generators. Existing defences, in…
items.sm: Proposes PRISM, a defense that monitors accumulating risk during text generation to detect and mitigate credential leakage across multi-agent pipelines.

items.t: Control Charts for Multi-agent Systems
items.a: Hayden Helm, Carey Priebe, Brandon Duderstadt
items.x: Generative agents have proven to be powerful assistants in a wide variety of contexts. Given this success, users are now deploying agents with minimal restrictions in open ended, multi-agent environments. Current methods for monitoring the dynamics of open-ended multi-agent systems are limited to aggregate statistics, qualitative inspection, or detecting change between two fixed timepoints. In this paper, we extend t…
items.sm: Extends adaptive control charts to monitor learning multi-agent systems and shows that adversaries changing behavior slowly can evade detection.

items.t: Strategic Exploitation in LLM Agent Markets: A Simulation Framework for E-Commerce Trust
items.a: Shijun Lei, Quang Nguyen, Swapneel Mehta, Zeping Li, Huichuan Fu, Xiaolong Zheng, Siki Chen, Yunji Liang
items.x: Agent-based modeling (ABM) has long been used in economics to study human behavior, and large language model (LLM) agents now enable new forms of social and economic simulation. While prior work has discovered strategic deception by LLM agents in financial trading and auction markets, e-commerce remains underexplored despite its distinctive information asymmetry: sellers privately observe product quality, whereas buy…
items.sm: Introduces TruthMarketTwin, an e-commerce simulation for studying strategic behavior when sellers know product quality and buyers depend on claims and reputation.

items.t: STAR: Failure-Aware Markovian Routing for Multi-Agent Spatiotemporal Reasoning
items.a: Ruiyi Yang, Lihuan Li, Hao Xue, Flora D. Salim
items.x: Compositional spatiotemporal reasoning often requires a system to invoke multiple heterogeneous specialists, such as geometric, temporal, topological, and trajectory agents. A central question is how such a system should route among specialists when execution does not simply succeed or fail, but fails in qualitatively different ways. Existing tool-augmented and multi-agent LLM systems typically leave this routing dec…
items.sm: Introduces STAR, a routing framework that coordinates specialist agents using task states and failure types, combining predefined routes with learned recovery transitions.

items.t: RADAR: Redundancy-Aware Diffusion for Multi-Agent Communication Structure Generation
items.a: Zhen Zhang, Wanjing Zhou, Juncheng Li, Hao Fei, Jun Wen, Wei Ji
items.x: Compared with individual agents, large language model based multi-agent systems have shown great capabilities consistently across diverse tasks, including code generation, mathematical reasoning, and planning, etc. Despite their impressive performance, the effectiveness and robustness of these systems heavily rely on their communication topology, which is often fixed or generated in a single step. This restricts fine…
items.sm: Proposes RADAR, a framework that generates task-specific agent communication networks step by step to reduce redundant communication.

items.t: Automated testing framework to evaluate multi-agent chat assistants

items.v: Congresso Ibero-Americano em Engenharia de Software (CIbSE)
items.sm: Develops automated mobile testing for retrieval-enabled multi-agent assistants using synthetic personas, finding recurring weaknesses particularly in Portuguese interactions.

items.t: Training-Free Refusal of MCP Exploits via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.x: The model context protocol (MCP) has been widely adopted as an open standard enabling the seamless integration of generative AI agents. However, while LLM guardrails have significantly matured to refuse malicious or harmful queries (e.g., "How do I build a bomb?"), recent work has shown that MCP-enabled LLMs are highly susceptible to prompt injection attacks which avoid harmful or suspicious cues (e.g., "Can you add …
items.sm: Investigates refusal of deceptively benign MCP attacks, finding limited gains from preference tuning and proposing retrieval-based safeguards without training.

items.t: Content-Aware Attack Detection in LLM Agent Tool-Call Traffic: An Empirical Study of Features, Architectures, and Evaluation Protocols
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become a widely adopted interface for LLM agents to invoke external tools, yet learned monitoring of MCP tool-call traffic remains underexplored. In this article, the proposed detector is presented as an attack detection framework for MCP tool-call traffic that encodes each agent session as a graph (tool calls as nodes, sequential and data-flow links as edges), enriches nodes with…
items.sm: Evaluates attack detectors that represent agent tool-call sessions using graphs and content embeddings, comparing neural and classical classifiers across datasets.

items.t: Information and Contract Design for Repeated Interactions between Agents with Misaligned Incentives
items.x: We study the consequences of information asymmetries and misaligned incentives in settings with multiple independent agents. We model an interaction between a Sender, who holds vital private information but cannot act, and a Receiver, who must make decisions but is dependent on the Sender's information. We find that the Sender learns an optimal communication strategy that the Receiver reliably acts on. Importantly, t…
items.sm: Studies communication between agents with conflicting incentives, finding that information contracts improve sender rewards while allowing unequal gains.

items.t: TacoMAS: Test-Time Co-Evolution of Topology and Capability in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Chen Xu, Yicheng Hu, Ruizi Wang, Xinyu Lin, Wenjie Wang, Dongrui Liu, Fuli Feng
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for solving complex tasks. Recent work has explored self-evolving MAS that automatically optimize agent capabilities or communication topologies. However, existing methods either learn a topology that remains fixed at inference time or adapt only the topology or capability during inference. We empirically and theoretically show that effective test-time ev…
items.sm: Introduces TacoMAS, which adapts agent capabilities rapidly and communication networks more slowly during task execution to preserve coordination.

items.t: EquiMem: Calibrating Shared Memory in Multi-Agent Debate via Game-Theoretic Equilibrium
items.a: Yuqiao Meng, Luoxi Tang, Sakshi Sunil Narvekar, Rupali Rajendra Vaje, Yingxue Zhang, Muchao Ye, Zhaohan Xi

items.t: SkillMAS: Skill Co-Evolution with LLM-based Multi-Agent System

We present SkillMAS, a non-parametric framework for adaptive specialization in multi-agent systems that couples…
items.sm: Introduces SkillMAS, which jointly refines reusable agent skills and reorganizes multi-agent systems using verified execution evidence.

items.t: Statistical Scouting Finds Debate-Safe but Not Debate-Useful Cases: A Matched-Ceiling Study of Open-Weight LLM Reasoning Protocols

items.t: CalBench: Evaluating Coordination-Privacy Trade-offs in Multi-Agent LLMs
items.a: Chelsea Zou, Yiheng Yao, Selena She, Noah Goodman, Robert D. Hawkins

items.t: Evaluating Tool Cloning in Agentic-AI Ecosystems

items.t: AgentSlimming: Towards Efficient and Cost-Aware Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yulang Chen, Haoxuan Peng, Jinyan Liu, Zichen Wen, Dongrui Liu, Linfeng Zhang

items.t: AI Tool Discovery at Scale: All You Need is DNS
items.x: The coming era of autonomous AI agents demands a discovery mechanism capable of navigating millions of tools, yet existing solutions buckle under \( \mathcal{O}(N) \) complexity and centralized governance. Instead of building another fragile overlay, we propose ToolDNS, a radical framework that retrofits semantic tool discovery onto the Internet's most resilient substrate: the Domain Name System (DNS). By embedding f…
items.sm: ToolDNS proposes discovering AI tools through hierarchical DNS names encoding function and trust, claiming logarithmic lookup complexity and decentralized governance.

items.t: AUGMANITAI Phenomena Corpus — BCI + Humanoid + Multi-Agent + Swarm 2024-26
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Compiles four descriptive, source-verified catalogues of phenomena involving brain-computer interfaces, humanoid robots, language model agents, and swarms.

items.t: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are utilized in many contexts and many professions. Those MAS rely on inter-agent communication, usually implemented by clear-text message passing. We hypothesize that Large Language Models may have a world model at their disposal that exceeds expressibility in text when complex concepts need to be communicated. Our aim is to approach a proof of this hypothesis with structured experiments. I…
items.sm: Reports that sparse latent communication preserves more concept information than text between language model agents, achieving 99.4% probe accuracy with substantial compression.

items.t: Uno-Orchestra: Parsimonious Agent Routing via Selective Delegation
items.a: Zhiqing Cui, Haotong Xie, Jiahao Yuan, Cheng Yang, Hanqing Wang, Yuxin Wu, Yifan Wu, Siru Zhong
items.x: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems typically rely on rigid orchestration, committing either to flat per-query routing or to hand-engineered task decomposition, so decomposition depth, worker choice, and inference budget are not jointly optimized under one objective. We introduce Uno-Orchestra, a unified orchestration policy that selectively decomposes a task and dispatches each subtask to an admissible (m…
items.sm: Introduces a learned policy that jointly selects task decomposition and worker assignments, reporting higher benchmark accuracy and lower query costs than competing workflows.

items.t: LLM-Augmented Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Cross-Scenario Knowledge Transfer
items.a: Chao Li, Yanfei Liu, Jieling Wang, Zhong Wang, Kewei Lu, Chengjin Wang
items.sm: Proposes fine-tuning language models with low-rank adaptation and dynamic prompts to transfer decision knowledge across multi-agent reinforcement learning scenarios.

items.t: Authorization Propagation in Multi-Agent AI Systems: Identity Governance as Infrastructure
items.x: The security discussion around agentic AI focuses heavily on prompt injection. This paper argues that multi-agent systems also create a distinct authorization problem: maintaining authorization invariants as non-human principals retrieve data, delegate tasks, and synthesize results across changing boundaries. We call this problem authorization propagation. It is not reducible to prompt injection and is not fully addr…
items.sm: Formalizes authorization propagation across agent workflows, identifying delegation, inference from aggregated information, and temporal validity challenges and deriving architectural requirements.

items.t: SecureMCP: A Policy-Enforced LLM Data Access Framework for AIoT Systems via Model Context Protocol
items.x: The deployment of Large Language Model (LLM)-generated SQL queries in Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) systems introduces critical security risks, as prompt injection attacks can manipulate LLMs into producing unauthorized queries that expose sensitive data or execute destructive operations. Existing NL2SQL research focuses on query accuracy, while MCP server implementations provide only SQL-level protections…
items.sm: Introduces SecureMCP, combining role-based table and column permissions with query cost checks and SQL risk filters for language-model-driven data access.

items.t: Layer Distinction 2 — CKS Is Not an Agent Framework: Standalone Treatment of the Architectural Boundary Between CKS and Agent Frameworks (Multi-Agent Libraries Built Around LLM Execution) in CKS
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Distinguishes the Coordination Knowledge Substrate from agent frameworks through architectural differences in state ownership, lifecycle, and access.

items.t: TechNews: A Technical Report on Agentic Workflow Automation for Science News Publishing
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes TechNews, an automated science news portal using reporting and operations agents to collect papers, produce articles, publish content, and maintain services.

items.t: Design Conductor 2.0: An agent builds a TurboQuant inference accelerator in 80 hours
items.a: The Verkor Team, Ravi Krishna, Suresh Krishna, David Chin
items.x: Driven by a rapid co-evolution of both harness and underlying models, LLM agents are improving at a dizzying pace. In our prior work (performed in Dec. 2025), we introduced "Design Conductor" (or just "Conductor"), a system capable of building a 5-stage Linux-capable RISC-V CPU in 12 hours. In this work, we introduce an updated multi-agent harness powered by frontier models released in April 2026, which is able to ha…
items.sm: Presents an updated multi-agent hardware design system that reportedly built a TurboQuant inference accelerator autonomously in 80 hours.

items.t: Evolving Idea Graphs with Learnable Edits-and-Commits for Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation
items.a: Jiangwen Dong, Bo Li, Wanyu Lin
items.x: LLM-empowered multi-agent systems offer new potential to accelerate scientific discovery by generating novel research ideas. However, existing methods typically coordinate agents through temporary texts, such as drafts or chat logs; it is difficult to pinpoint the weaknesses in the generated ideas and how the agents refine them. To this end, we introduce \textbf{Evolving Idea Graphs} (EIG), a graph-based multi-agent …
items.sm: Introduces a scientific ideation framework where agents refine graphs of claims and relationships, keeping unresolved weaknesses visible throughout proposal development.

items.t: didilili/deepsearch-agents
items.sm: Provides a deployable conversational research agent application using LangGraph, RAGFlow, Tavily, and FastAPI, with full-stack code and accompanying tutorials.

items.t: professorpalmer/Puppetmaster
items.x: Provider-neutral control plane for durable-state agent swarms: subprocess workers, leases, artifacts, memory, and deterministic stitching.
items.sm: Provides a provider-independent control plane for agent swarms, managing persistent state, subprocess workers, leases, artifacts, memory, and deterministic output assembly.

items.t: @simonw: Sure looks like Bun is at least exploring a port from Zig to Rust given this docs/PORTING.md guide for coding …
items.sm: Suggests Bun may be exploring a Zig-to-Rust port based on a guide for coding agents, without confirming a migration.

items.sm: Argues that managing agent fleets offers substantial value and promotes open-source tools for messaging, task prioritization, orchestration, safety checks, and session search.

items.sm: Announces Meta's ProgramBench for rebuilding complete programs, reports zero top accuracy, and says the team plans to make the benchmark harder.

items.sm: Introduces ProgramBench as 200 tasks requiring models to rebuild complete programs from executables without starter code or internet access.

items.t: When Context Hurts: The Crossover Effect of Knowledge Transfer on Multi-Agent Design Exploration
items.x: The prevailing assumption in agent orchestration is that more context is better. We test this on multi-agent software design across 10 tasks, 7 context-injection conditions, and over 2,700 runs, and find a crossover effect: the same artifact type improves design exploration on some tasks (up to 20$\times$ tradeoff coverage) and actively degrades it on others (up to 46% reduction). On several tasks, an irrelevant docu…
items.sm: Finds that added context can improve or impair multi-agent design exploration, with its effect strongly associated with exploration levels measured without context.

items.t: Coordination as an Architectural Layer for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems fail in production at rates between 41% and 87%, mostly due to coordination defects rather than base-model capability. Existing responses split between cataloguing failure modes empirically and shipping declarative orchestration frameworks as engineering tools; neither delivers a principled mapping from coordination configuration to predictable failure-mode signature. We argue that coordinatio…
items.sm: Argues that coordination should form a configurable architectural layer and compares five coordination configurations in prediction markets while controlling model and information access.

items.t: OmniCharacter++: Toward Comprehensive Benchmark for Realistic Role-Playing Agents
items.a: Haonan Zhang, Pengpeng Zeng, Ji Zhang, Jingkuan Song, Nicu Sebe, Heng Tao Shen, Lianli Gao
items.v: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
items.sm: Introduces a benchmark, dataset, evaluation suite, and trained model for assessing multi-character role-playing interactions combining text and speech.

items.t: Governed Collaborative Memory as Artificial Selection in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Diego F. Cuadros, Abdoul-Aziz Maiga, Helen Meskhidze, Andre Curtis-Trudel
items.x: Persistent memory is turning language-model-based agents from stateless participants in isolated interactions into state-bearing components of LLM-based multi-agent systems. As memory becomes durable, reloadable, and behavior-shaping across agents, sessions, or versions, a design question arises that is not captured by retrieval accuracy or access control alone: which candidate memories should become shared instituti…
items.sm: Argues that shared agent memory requires governance to select which memories persist, remain private, or are rejected, and compares alternative selection regimes.

items.t: Decentralized Multi-Agent System: A Blackboard-Based Peer Review Architecture for LLM Agents
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Describes a research prototype coordinating language model agents through a shared SQLite blackboard, proposal voting, and peer review of artifacts.

items.t: Memory-Efficient Multi-Agent Debate with Compressed Contexts for Long-Form Reasoning
items.a: Hyejin Byun, Mireille Bertin, Minji Kim, Colin Dempsey
items.v: International Journal of Information and Communication Technology Trends
items.sm: Proposes compressing arguments in multi-agent debates to reduce memory use and redundant tokens while preserving reasoning structure during long-form problem solving.

items.t: Model Context Protocol Threat Modeling and Analysis of Vulnerabilities to Prompt Injection with Tool Poisoning
items.a: Charoes Huang, Xin Huang, Ngoc Phu Tran, Amin Milani Fard
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has rapidly emerged as a universal standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data sources. While the MCP simplifies integration between AI applications and various services, it introduces significant security vulnerabilities, particularly on the client side. In this work, we conduct threat modelings of MCP implementations using STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiatio…
items.sm: Analyzes MCP security threats using STRIDE and DREAD, identifying malicious instructions in tool metadata as a major client-side vulnerability.

items.t: The Limits of Deterministic Pre‑Dispatch Enforcement for Model Context Protocol Tool Calls: A Negative‑Result Measurement Study
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Presents a measurement study of limits in deterministic enforcement before MCP tool execution, alongside a capability-based policy engine and reproducibility materials.

items.t: QKVShare: Quantized KV-Cache Handoff for Multi-Agent On-Device LLMs
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems on edge devices need to hand off latent context efficiently, but the practical choices today are expensive re-prefill or full-precision KV transfer. We study QKVShare, a framework for quantized KV-cache handoff between agents that combines token-level mixed-precision allocation, a self-contained CacheCard representation, and a HuggingFace-compatible cache injection path. Our current results su…
items.sm: Introduces quantized cache transfer between on-device agents, reporting faster initial responses than recomputing context and competitive reasoning performance across repeated transfers.

items.t: From Intent to Execution: Composing Agentic Workflows with Agent Recommendation
items.a: Kishan Athrey, Ramin Pishehvar, Brian Riordan, Mahesh Viswanathan
items.x: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) built using AI agents fulfill a variety of user intents that may be used to design and build a family of related applications. However, the creation of such MAS currently involves manual composition of the plan, manual selection of appropriate agents, and manual creation of execution graphs. This paper introduces a framework for the automated creation of multi-agent systems which replaces mu…
items.sm: Proposes automating multi-agent workflow construction through language-model planning, dynamic execution graphs, task orchestration, and agent recommendations from registries.

items.t: rekursiv-ai/sagent
items.x: A coding-agent CLI and strongly-typed Python library -- self-mutating, hot-swapping, multi-provider, with async tool calls and bidirectional recursive spawn.
items.sm: Provides a coding-agent command-line interface and typed Python library supporting self-modification, component replacement during execution, multiple providers, asynchronous tools, and recursive agent spawning.

items.t: Kevin-Liu-01/Agent-Machines
items.x: OpenRouter for agents and sandbox environments. Provides a control plane and configuration options for persistent agent workers. Route runtime + substrates, provision specialist presets, and supervise your fleet.
items.sm: Provides a control plane for persistent agent workers, routing runtimes and execution environments, configuring specialist presets, and supervising agent fleets.

items.t: SOTOPIA-TOM: Evaluating Privacy and Information Management in Multi-Agent Interaction with Theory of Mind
items.a: Yashwanth YS, Ruichen Wang, Shihua Zeng, Xuhui Zhou, Koichi Onoue, Vasudha Varadarajan, Maarten Sap
items.x: As LLM-based agents are increasingly interacting in multi-party settings, they need to properly handle information asymmetry, i.e., knowing when and to whom to disclose information is appropriate. Yet, existing benchmarks fail to measure this ability in realistic multi-party settings. Thus, we introduce SOTOPIA-TOM, a multi-dimensional benchmarking framework to evaluate LLM agents' ability to successfully navigate in…
items.sm: Introduces 160 reviewed scenarios evaluating how agents manage private information and disclosure policies across public and private channels in multi-party interactions.

items.t: EngiAgent: Fully Connected Coordination of LLM Agents for Solving Open-ended Engineering Problems with Feasible Solutions
items.a: Xiyuan Zhou, Ruixi Zou, Xinlei Wang, Yuheng Cheng, Yan Xu, Junhua Zhao, Jinjin Gu
items.x: Engineering problem solving is central to real-world decision-making, requiring mathematical formulations that not only represent complex problems but also produce feasible solutions under data and physical constraints. Unlike mathematical problem solving, which operates on predefined formulations, engineering tasks demand open-ended analysis, feasibility-driven modeling, and iterative refinement. Although large lang…
items.sm: Introduces EngiAgent, coordinating specialized agents for engineering analysis, modeling, verification, solving, and evaluation to seek solutions satisfying physical and data constraints.

items.t: When Stress Becomes Signal: Detecting Antifragility-Compatible Regimes in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
items.a: Jose Manuel de la Chica, Juan Manuel Vera, Jairo Rodríguez
items.x: Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly used to solve complex tasks through decomposition, debate, specialization, and ensemble reasoning. However, these systems are usually evaluated in terms of robustness: whether performance is preserved under perturbation. This paper studies a different question: whether semantic stress exposes structured variation that could support future antifragile learning. We introduce CAF…
items.sm: Introduces a statistical framework for detecting stress response patterns that could support future learning in multi-agent language model systems.

items.t: Terminus-4B: Can a Smaller Model Replace Frontier LLMs at Agentic Execution Tasks?
items.a: Spandan Garg, Vikram Nitin, Yufan Huang
items.x: Modern coding agents increasingly delegate specialized subtasks to subagents, which are smaller, focused agentic loops that handle narrow responsibilities like search, debugging or terminal execution. This architectural pattern keeps the main agent's context window clean by isolating verbose outputs (e.g. build logs, test results, etc.) within the subagent context. Typically when agents employ subagents for such task…
items.sm: Presents Terminus-4B, a small model trained for terminal execution, and investigates whether it can match frontier models on agentic execution tasks.

items.t: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
items.a: Wenyi Wu, Sibo Zhu, Kun Zhou, Biwei Huang
items.x: Language model (LM)-based agents have demonstrated promising capabilities in automating complex tasks from natural language instructions, yet they continue to struggle with long-horizon planning and reasoning. To address this, we propose an enhanced multi-agent framework that decomposes automation into three roles: a planner for high-level decision-making, an actor for task execution, and a memory manager for context…
items.sm: Finds planning dominates performance in a three-role agent framework and proposes concentrating reinforcement learning and computing resources on the planner.

items.t: ARIS: Autonomous Research via Adversarial Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Ruofeng Yang, Yongcan Li, Shuai Li
items.x: This report describes ARIS (Auto-Research-in-sleep), an open-source research harness for autonomous research, including its architecture, assurance mechanisms, and early deployment experience. The performance of agent systems built on LLMs depends on both the model weights and the harness around them, which governs what information to store, retrieve, and present to the model. For long-horizon research workflows, the…
items.sm: Describes an autonomous research system that pairs an executor with an adversarial reviewer from another model to scrutinize evidence and research claims.

items.t: Autonomous LLM Agent Worms: Cross-Platform Propagation, Automated Discovery and Temporal Re-Entry Defense
items.x: Autonomous LLM agents operate as long-running processes with persistent workspaces, memory files, scheduled task state, and messaging integrations. These features create a new propagation risk: attacker-influenced content can be written into persistent agent state, re-enter the LLM decision context through scheduled autoloading, and drive high-risk actions including configuration changes and cross-agent transmission.…
items.sm: Presents automated methods for analyzing how malicious instructions persist and spread through agent files, including payloads designed to survive summarization.

items.t: GRAIL: A Deep-Granularity Hybrid Resonance Framework for Real-Time Agent Discovery via SLM-Enhanced Indexing
items.x: As the ecosystem of Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents expands rapidly, efficient and accurate Agent Discovery becomes a critical bottleneck for large-scale multi-agent collaboration. Existing approaches typically face a dichotomy: either relying on heavy-weight LLMs for intent parsing, leading to prohibitive latency (often exceeding 30 seconds), or using monolithic vector retrieval that sacrifices semantic prec…
items.sm: Proposes an agent discovery framework using a specialized small model and expanded descriptions, claiming discovery latency below 400 milliseconds without sacrificing accuracy.

items.t: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
items.x: As large language model (LLM) agents evolve from isolated tool users into coordinated teams, reinforcement learning (RL) must optimize not only individual actions but also how work is spawned, delegated, communicated, aggregated, and stopped. This paper studies RL for LLM-based multi-agent systems through orchestration traces: temporal interaction graphs whose events include sub-agent spawning, delegation, communicat…
items.sm: Examines reinforcement learning for agent teams through interaction graphs, organizing reward design and credit assignment around delegation, communication, tool use, and stopping.

items.t: AgentRaft: Fault-Tolerant Multi-Agent Consensus Protocol for AI Swarms
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Proposes a consensus architecture combining agent identities, quorum voting, immutable decision logs, and leader replacement to address incorrect proposals and agent outages.

items.t: Tiered Detection of Multi-Agent LLM Failures: An Empirical Calibration on TRAIL and Who&When
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Combines heuristic failure detectors with selective language model judging, reporting high precision on benchmark traces substantially represented in its calibration data.

items.t: Hidden Coalitions in Multi-Agent AI: A Spectral Diagnostic from Internal Representations
items.a: Cameron Berg, Susan L. Schneider, Mark M. Bailey
items.x: Collections of interacting AI agents can form coalitions, creating emergent group-level organization that is critical for AI safety and alignment. However, observing agent behavior alone is often insufficient to distinguish genuine informational coupling from spurious similarity, as consequential coalitions may form at the level of internal representations before any overt behavioral change is apparent. Here, we intr…
items.sm: Detects potential agent coalitions by measuring information shared between internal representations and partitioning the resulting graph.

items.t: When Agents Handle Secrets: A Survey of Confidential Computing for Agentic AI
items.a: Javad Forough, Marios Kogias, Hamed Haddadi
items.x: Agentic AI systems, specifically LLM-driven agents that plan, invoke tools, maintain persistent memory, and delegate tasks to peer agents via protocols such as MCP and A2A, introduce a threat surface that differs materially from standalone model inference. Agents accumulate sensitive context, hold credentials, and operate across pipelines no single party fully controls, enabling prompt injection, context exfiltration…
items.sm: Surveys confidential computing for agentic AI, examining hardware isolation and remote attestation as protections for sensitive context, credentials, and distributed workflows.

items.t: The Trustworthy Model Context Protocol (MCP) Registry: An Architectural Blueprint for Cryptographic Provenance and Runtime Integrity
items.a: Lluis Mas Ruiz, Jordi Vilaplana, Josep Rius, Radu Spaimoc, Jordi Mateo
items.sm: Proposes an MCP registry architecture combining domain identity, cryptographic provenance, and runtime integrity checks to address compromised servers and changing capabilities.

items.t: Listening–Trust Asymmetry and Team Outcomes in a Multi-Agent LLM Substrate: Three-Layer Decoupling in a Mandarin Lobster Observatory
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Examines trust, listening exposure, and team outcomes among ten Mandarin-speaking agents, observing uniform trust scores alongside sharply unequal listening exposure.

items.t: AutoResearch: An Execution-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable Research Workflow Automation
items.a: Rajesh Kumar, Waqar Ali, Junaid Ahmed, Abdullah Aman Khan, Shaoning Zeng
items.x: Automated research agents increasingly generate code, retrieve literature, and draft scientific artifacts, but they often fail to verify whether generated experiments execute correctly or whether cited sources support generated claims. We present AutoResearch, an execution-grounded multi-agent framework for reliable research workflow automation. AutoResearch couples sandboxed Python/PyTorch execution, iterative code …
items.sm: Presents a research automation framework combining sandboxed execution, code repair, citation checks, claim auditing, and review feedback to improve research artifact reliability.

items.t: AAFLOW: Scalable Patterns for Agentic AI Workflows
items.a: Arup Kumar Sarker, Mills Staylor, Aymen Alsaadi, Gregor von Laszewski, Shantenu Jha, Geoffrey Fox
items.x: Agentic workflows in large language model systems integrate retrieval, reasoning, and memory, but existing frameworks suffer from scalability and reproducibility limitations due to fragmented data orchestration, serialization overhead, and non-deterministic execution. Although these frameworks increase flexibility, they don't have a formal execution model that adheres to the principles of high-performance computing. …
items.sm: Introduces a distributed agent workflow runtime using operator-based execution plans, shared data formats, deterministic resource scheduling, and asynchronous batching to reduce overhead.

items.t: METHODOLOGICAL EVOLUTION AND ARCHITECTURAL PARADIGMS OF MODERN MULTI-AGENT REINFORCED LEARNING
items.a: Nonna N. Shapovalova, Iryna Dotsenko, Andrii Stryuk
items.v: Collection of scholarly papers of Dniprovsk State Technical University (Technical Sciences)
items.sm: Reviews multi-agent reinforcement learning through 2024–2025, connecting classical decision frameworks and training architectures with transformer and language model approaches.

items.t: These Aren't the Reviews You're Looking For How Humans Review AI-Generated Pull Requests
items.a: Kacper Duma, Patryk Wróblewski, Jagoda Bobińska, Julia Winiarska, Piotr Przymus
items.x: We analyze code review interactions for AI-generated pull requests (PRs) on GitHub using the AIDev dataset and compare them to human-authored PRs within the same repositories. We find that most AI-generated PRs receive no review and, when reviewed, are largely dominated by AI agents rather than humans. Human-authored PRs are more likely to receive human-only review and to attract direct human feedback. In contrast, r…
items.sm: Finds most AI-generated pull requests receive no review, while reviewed examples involve more automated interaction and less direct human feedback than human-authored submissions.

items.t: enmanuelmag/agent-harness-kit

items.sm: Provides scaffolding for structured multi-agent workflows within a codebase across different model providers.

Three peer-supervised loops (discovery → build → release) over a catalogue of curated packs: skills, subagents, and hooks, each installed in one line. It's npm for your coding agent. Any agent, any stack — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Kiro.
items.sm: Organizes software development into supervised discovery, build, and release loops using installable collections of agent skills, subagents, and hooks.

items.sm: Runs language model agents within Emacs, with isolated sandboxes, asynchronous subagents, and file merging that stops promptly on errors.

items.sm: Introduces Sakana Fugu as a foundation model for multi-agent orchestration, without providing mechanisms or experimental results in the available post.

items.sm: Expresses the author's intention to build software development tools personally, mentioning Claws and Tokens without explaining their implementation.

items.t: The Reasoning Trap: An Information-Theoretic Bound on Closed-System Multi-Step LLM Reasoning
items.x: When copies of the same language model are prompted to debate, they produce diverse phrasings of one perspective rather than diverse perspectives. Multi-agent debate (MAD), and more broadly closed-system reasoning where agents iteratively transform each other's outputs, tends to preserve answer accuracy while degrading the reasoning behind those answers. We name the multi-agent case the Debate Trap and the broader ph…
items.sm: Argues closed-system agent reasoning can preserve answer accuracy while weakening evidential support, and proposes a faithfulness metric and evidence-grounded inquiry method.

items.t: 12 Angry AI Agents: Evaluating Multi-Agent LLM Decision-Making Through Cinematic Jury Deliberation
items.x: What if the twelve jurors of Sidney Lumet's 12 Angry Men (1957) were not men, but large language models? Would the one juror who disagrees still be able to change everyone's mind? This paper instantiates that scenario as a multi-agent benchmark for LLM deliberation: twelve agents, each conditioned on a film-faithful persona, debate the film's murder case using multi-agent framework. Two models representing opposite e…
items.sm: Tests twelve language model jurors modeled on a film, finding seventeen of eighteen deliberations fail to reach a unanimous verdict.

items.t: Catching the Infection Before It Spreads: Foresight-Guided Defense in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Yue Ma, Ziyuan Yang, Yi Zhang
items.x: Large multimodal model-based Multi-Agent Systems (MASs) enable collaborative complex problem solving through specialized agents. However, MASs are vulnerable to infectious jailbreak, where compromising a single agent can spread to others, leading to widespread compromise. Existing defenses counter this by training a more contagious cure factor, biasing agents to retrieve it over virus adversarial examples (VirAEs). H…
items.sm: Proposes a defense requiring no training that anticipates local agent interactions to counter jailbreaks spreading through multi-agent systems.

items.t: Talk is Cheap, Communication is Hard: Dynamic Grounding Failures and Repair in Multi-Agent Negotiation
items.a: Yiheng Yao, Chelsea Zou, Robert D. Hawkins
items.x: Grounding is the collaborative process of establishing mutual belief sufficient for a communicative goal. While static grounding maps language to a shared context, dynamic grounding requires agents to negotiate meaning across turns. Current multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) benchmarks largely emphasize static, one-shot tasks, overlooking whether agents can repair grounding breakdowns through interaction. We intr…
items.sm: Introduces a repeated negotiation game and finds agent pairs struggle to reach jointly optimal allocations despite individual agents identifying those allocations independently.

items.t: MARLF: Memory-Augmented Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Model Feedback
items.a: Mohammad Asad Shaik, AKHIL BABU GUJJARLAPUDI, Krishna Chaitanya MADALA, Abhiram Dalla, Mahendra Kumar Jhariya
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Augments multi-agent reinforcement learning with memory and language model feedback to adapt reward shaping and improve coordination under sparse rewards.

items.t: Generative emergent communication: large language model is a collective world model
items.a: Tadahiro Taniguchi, Ryo Ueda, Tomoaki Nakamura, Masahiro Suzuki, Akira Taniguchi
items.x: This survey and perspective paper addresses a fundamental puzzle: how Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire extensive world knowledge without direct sensorimotor experience. We introduce the Collective World Model hypothesis, arguing that an LLM does not learn a world model from scratch. Instead, it learns a statistical approximation of a collective world model already implicitly encoded in human language through a so…
items.sm: Argues language models learn world knowledge from collective human understanding encoded in language, formalizing language emergence as decentralized Bayesian inference.

items.t: cenconq25/claude-code-app-studio
items.x: A coordinated team of 53 Claude Code subagents that build, ship, and operate mobile apps end to end. Each agent owns a narrow slice of the lifecycle so that responsibility, expertise, and review checkpoints stay separated and observable.
items.sm: Provides 53 specialized Claude Code subagents intended to coordinate mobile app development, release, and operation with distinct responsibilities and review checkpoints.

items.t: Why Coase needs Hayek
items.sm: Compares independent models, central delegation, and market allocation, arguing that task characteristics and coordination costs determine which arrangement works best.

items.t: Multi-Agent Reasoning Improves Compute Efficiency: Pareto-Optimal Test-Time Scaling
items.a: Florian Valentin Wunderlich, Lars Benedikt Kaesberg, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp
items.x: Advances in inference methods have enabled language models to improve their predictions without additional training. These methods often prioritize raw performance over cost-effective compute usage. However, computational efficiency is key for real-world applications with resource constraints. We provide a systematic analysis of the inference scaling strategies self-consistency, self-refinement, multi-agent debate, a…
items.sm: Compares inference strategies across reasoning benchmarks to identify configurations that balance accuracy and computational cost.

items.t: MAD-OPD: Breaking the Ceiling in On-Policy Distillation via Multi-Agent Debate
items.a: Jianze Wang, Ying Liu, Jinlong Chen, Xuchun Hu, Qilong Zhang, Yu Cao, Jun Wang, Hua Yang

The central claim: synchronization cost explosion in LLM multi-agent systems map…

items.t: Separating Intelligence from Execution: A Workflow Engine for the Model Context Protocol

items.t: DOVA: Deliberation-First Multi-Agent Orchestration for Autonomous Research Automation

We present DOVA (Deep Orchestrated Versatile Agent), a multi-agent platform introducing three key innovations: …

items.t: Ensemble Learning for Large Language Models in Text and Code Generation: A Survey

items.x: Generative Pretrained Transformers (GPTs) are foundational Large Language Models (LLMs) for text generation. items.t: HDLFORGE: A Two-Stage Multi-Agent Framework for Efficient Verilog Code Generation with Adaptive Model Escalation

The system uses a compact coder with a medium-sized LLM by default (Stage A) and escalates to a stronger coder with an ultra-large LLM (Stage B) only when needed, guided by a calibrated score from inexpensive diagnostics including compilation, lint, and smoke test…

items.t: Auditing Cascading Risks in Multi-Agent Systems via Semantic-Geometric Co-evolution

items.x: Large Language model (LLM)-based Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are prone to cascading risks, where early-stage interactions remain semantically fluent and policy-compliant, yet the underlying interaction dynamics begin to distort in ways that amplify latent instability or misalignment. Traditional auditing methods that focus on per-message semantic content are inherently reactive and lagging, failing to capture these ear…
items.sm: Proposes detecting cascading risks in multi-agent systems by tracking how message meanings and communication graph geometry change together.

items.t: ChoiceMates: Supporting Unfamiliar Online Decision-Making with Multi-Agent Conversational Interactions
items.a: Jeongeon Park, Bryan Min, Kihoon Son, Jean Young Song, Xiaojuan Ma, Juho Kim
items.v: ACM International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI)
items.x: From purchasing a gift to deciding on a hobby, unfamiliar decisions—decisions without domain knowledge and experience—are frequent and significant. The complexity and uncertainty of such decisions demand unique approaches to information seeking, understanding, and decision-making. Our formative study highlights that in the current workflow, users want to start by discovering broad and relevant domain information even…
items.sm: Presents ChoiceMates, which lets users guide conversations with agents offering different domain perspectives to support decisions in unfamiliar areas.

items.t: Agentic Mixed-Source Multi-Modal Misinformation Detection with Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
items.a: Wei Jiang, Tong Chen, Wei Yuan, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin
items.x: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been proven effective for detecting multi-modal misinformation on social platforms, especially in zero-shot settings with unavailable or delayed annotations. However, a single VLM's capacity falls short in the more complex mixed-source multi-modal misinformation detection (M3D) task. Taking captioned images as an example, in M3D, false information can originate from untruthful texts…
items.sm: Proposes adapting reasoning effort during inference to help agents detect misinformation involving false text, manipulated images, or mismatches between them.

items.t: AI-for-Science Low-code Platform with Bayesian Adversarial Multi-Agent Framework
items.a: Zihang Zeng, Jiaquan Zhang, Pengze Li, Yuan Qi, Xi Chen
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate potentials for automating scientific code generation but face challenges in reliability, error propagation in multi-agent workflows, and evaluation in domains with ill-defined success metrics. We present a Bayesian adversarial multi-agent framework specifically designed for AI for Science (AI4S) tasks in the form of a Low-code Platform (LCP). Three LLM-based agents are coordin…
items.sm: Presents a low-code scientific programming platform where planning, coding, and evaluation agents use adversarial testing and Bayesian updates to refine solutions.

items.t: A Self-Reflective Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework for Dynamic Software Engineering Tasks
items.sm: Proposes a software engineering agent framework that adapts communication structures, checks work at critical stages, and improves prompts using past errors.

items.t: SCSimulator: An Exploratory Visual Analytics Framework for Partner Selection in Supply Chains through LLM-driven Multi-Agent Simulation

items.x: Supply chains (SCs), complex networks spanning from raw material acquisition to product delivery, with enterprises as interconnected nodes, play a pivotal role in organizational success. However, optimizing SCs remains challenging, particularly in partner selection, a key bottleneck shaped by both competitive and cooperative dynamics. This challenge inherently constitutes a multi-objective dynamic game requiring a sy…

items.t: Multi-Agent Debate with Memory Masking
items.a: Hongduan Tian, Xiao Feng, Ziyuan Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Rolan Yan, Bo Han
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated impressive capabilities in reasoning tasks. Currently, mainstream LLM reasoning frameworks predominantly focus on scaling up inference-time sampling to enhance performance. In particular, among all LLM reasoning frameworks, *multi-agent debate* (MAD), which employs multiple LLMs as agents to perform reasoning in the way of multi-round debate, has emerged as a po…
items.sm: Examines how erroneous memories affect multi-agent debate and proposes masking memories to improve reasoning.

items.t: Adaptive Sparse Dense Communication Network for Multi-Agent LLMs
items.sm: Proposes a trainable communication network that dynamically selects agent partners and adapts vector messages, reporting improvements over comparison systems across benchmarks.

items.t: EvoSkill: Automated Skill Discovery for Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Salaheddin Alzubi, Noah Provenzano, Jaydon Bingham, Weiyuan Chen, Tu Vu
items.x: Coding agents are increasingly used as general-purpose problem solvers, but their flexibility does not by itself confer the domain expertise needed for specialized tasks. Recent work addresses this through \textit{agent skills}: reusable workflows, and code, that augment agents with domain-specific capabilities. Most skills today are hand-crafted, and existing evolutionary approaches optimize low-level artifacts (e.g…
items.sm: Introduces EvoSkill, which analyzes agent failures to create and refine reusable skills, retaining those that improve performance on held-out validation tasks.

items.t: OrchMAS: Orchestrated Reasoning with Multi Collaborative Heterogeneous Scientific Expert Structured Agents
items.a: Yichao Feng, Haoran Luo, Zhenghong Lin, Yiqun Sun, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence Hsieh, Anh Tuan Luu
items.x: Multi-agent large language model frameworks are promising for complex multi step reasoning, yet existing systems remain weak for scientific and knowledge intensive domains due to static prompts and agent roles, rigid workflows, and homogeneous model reliance, leading to poor domain adaptation, limited reasoning flexibility, and high latency on heterogeneous or long-horizon scientific tasks. They also struggle to revi…
items.sm: Proposes an orchestration framework that builds scientific reasoning workflows dynamically and assigns specialized agents tailored prompts for each task.

items.t: MASPOB: Bandit-Based Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems with Graph Neural Networks
items.a: Zhi Hong, Qian Zhang, Jiahang Sun, Zhiwei Shang, Mingze Kong, Xiangyi Wang, Yao Shu, Zhongxiang Dai
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved great success in many real-world applications, especially the one serving as the cognitive backbone of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) to orchestrate complex workflows in practice. Since many deployment scenarios preclude MAS workflow modifications and its performance is highly sensitive to the input prompts, prompt optimization emerges as a more natural approach to improve its pe…
items.sm: Proposes optimizing prompts in fixed multi-agent workflows using bandit methods and graph neural networks to address evaluation costs and dependencies between agents.

items.t: Heterogeneous Agent Collaborative Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Zhixia Zhang, Zixuan Huang, Gongxun Li, Deqing Wang, Chengyi Yuan, Xin Xia, Deqing Wang, Fuzhen Zhuang
items.x: We introduce Heterogeneous Agent Collaborative Reinforcement Learning (HACRL), a new Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Reward (RLVR) problem that addresses the inefficiencies of isolated multi-agent on-policy optimization. HACRL enables collaborative optimization with independent execution: heterogeneous agents share verified rollouts during training to mutually improve, while operating independently at inferenc…
items.sm: Introduces collaborative reinforcement learning where different agents share verified training experiences to improve one another while operating independently during deployment.

items.t: StitchCUDA: An Automated Multi-Agents End-to-End GPU Programing Framework with Rubric-based Agentic Reinforcement Learning

Although LLM-based methods show promise on automated GPU kernel generation, prior works mainly focus on single-kernel optimization and do not extend to end-to-end programs, hindering practical deployment. To address th…
items.sm: Presents a framework where planning, coding, and verification agents generate complete GPU programs, supported by reinforcement learning guided by evaluation criteria.

We introduce Q-KVComm, a new protocol that enables direct t…

To address …

items.t: Epistemic Gain, Aleatoric Cost: Uncertainty Decomposition in Multi-Agent Debate for Math Reasoning
items.a: Dan Qiao, Binbin Chen, Fengyu Cai, Jianlong Chen, Wenhao Li, Fuxin Jiang, Zuzhi Chen, Hongyuan Zha B

items.t: Unified-MAS: Universally Generating Domain-Specific Nodes for Empowering Automatic Multi-Agent Systems

On Apple M4 Pro with 10.2 GB of cache budget, only 3 agents fit at 8K context in FP16. A 10-agent workflow must constantly evict and reload caches. Without persistence, every eviction forces a full re-prefill through the model -- 15.7 seconds per agent at 4K context. We addr…
items.sm: Stores agents’ attention caches on disk with four-bit quantization, allowing edge devices to restore context without repeating prompt processing.

Common orchestrators treat tool return as the settlement trigger, so faults, speculation, and concurrent agents can leave partial effects, losing-branch residue, stale writes, or irreversible sends. Correct settlement needs two facts that retries, checkpoint replay, locks, and compensation each conflate: which effects must settle togeth…
items.sm: Coordinates tool effects through transactions that commit only when their scope is complete and earlier conflicting work can no longer arrive.

items.x: Multi-agent systems, where LLM agents communicate through free-form language, enable sophisticated coordination for solving complex cooperative tasks. This surfaces a unique safety problem when a group of agents forms a coalition and colludes to pursue secondary goals and degrade the joint objective. In this paper, we present Colosseum, a framework for auditing LLM agents' collusive behavior in multi-agent settings. …
items.sm: Introduces a framework for auditing agent collusion by comparing actions against cooperative outcomes and examining communication across coalition goals and network structures.

items.t: Socially-Weighted Alignment: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

We propose Socially-Weighted Alignment (SWA), a game-theoretic framework that modifies inference-time decision making by interpolating between an agent's private obj…
items.sm: Balances agents’ private objectives with estimated group welfare, deriving a social-weight threshold that discourages excess demand in a shared-resource congestion model.

items.sm: Introduces a benchmark with over 110 tasks for evaluating language-based buyer-seller negotiations under private constraints and differing product valuations.

Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have recently shown to be useful for data-centric interpretability. In this work, we analyze large-scale reinforcement learning training runs from the sophisticated environment of Full-Press Diplomacy by appl…

We propose PhysicsAgentABM, which shifts inference to behaviorally coherent agent c…

In this paper, we revisit MAS through the perspective of \textit{entropy}, considering both intra…

items.t: CoWork-X: Experience-Optimized Co-Evolution for Multi-Agent Collaboration System

items.t: WideSeek-R1: Exploring Width Scaling for Broad Information Seeking via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

In this work, we explore a complementary dimension of width scaling with multi-agent systems to address broad information se…

Focusing on models that range from 7 to 9 billion parameters in size engaged in a ten-round repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, we evaluate whether short, costless pre-play messages emulating the cheap-talk paradigm affect strategic stability. items.sm: Reports that brief messages before repeated Prisoner's Dilemma games reduce strategic variability for most tested model-context combinations.

items.t: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent
items.a: Yinyi Luo, Yiqiao Jin, Weichen Yu, Mengqi Zhang, Srijan Kumar, Xiaoxiao Li, Weijie Xu, Xin Chen

This eq…

items.t: MAPLE: A Sub-Agent Architecture for Memory, Learning, and Personalization in Agentic AI Systems
items.x: Large language model (LLM) agents have emerged as powerful tools for complex tasks, yet their ability to adapt to individual users remains fundamentally limited. items.t: MAS-ProVe: Understanding the Process Verification of Multi-Agent Systems

items.t: Declarative by Design, Assistable Only by Convention: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Frameworks for AI-Assistability
items.x: Multi-agent frameworks (MAFs) promise to simplify LLM-driven software development, yet no principled metric captures how well AI coding assistants can generate correct, framework-specific code. We introduce \textit{AI-assistability} ($\mathcal{AI}$), a composite metric that quantifies a framework's amenability to AI-assisted development by combining structural alignment ($\barσ$) with functional correctness (pass@1).…

This dependence renders supervision-heavy training paradigms increasingly unsustainable, with signs of diminis…

items.a: Wenzhe Fan, Tommaso Tognoli, Henry Peng Zou, Chunyu Miao, Yibo Wang, Xinhua Zhang

items.t: Architectural Design, Not Only Model Intelligence, Governs Multi-Agent LLM Performance
items.a: Abdelghny Orogat, Ana Rostam, Essam Mansour

items.sm: Compares nine multi-agent frameworks using a shared model and standardized benchmarks to examine how architectural choices affect performance.

items.sm: AOrchestra creates specialized sub-agents as needed by selecting their instructions, context, tools, and models for each task.

items.sm: MIRROR converts natural language optimization problems into mathematical models and solver code using multiple agents, execution-based corrections, and hierarchical retrieval.

items.t: DIANOIA: Diagnostic Decomposition and Joint Optimization for Multi-Agent Reasoning

items.t: Agent Contracts: A Formal Framework for Resource-Bounded Autonomous AI Systems
items.x: The Contract Net Protocol (1980) introduced coordination through contracts in multi-agent systems. Modern agent protocols standardize connectivity and interoperability; yet, none provide formal, resource governance-normative mechanisms to bound how much agents may consume or how long they may operate. We introduce Agent Contracts, a formal framework that extends the contract metaphor from task allocation to resource-…

We argue that recent advances in large language models (LLMs) point toward a shift from hand-crafted …
