items.t: Tool-RoCo: An Agent-as-Tool Self-organization Large Language Model Benchmark in Multi-robot Cooperation
items.a: Ke Zhang, Xiaoning Zhao, Ce Zheng, Jiahong Ning, Dandan Zhu, Wenqi Zhang, Sun, Chen, Toshiharu Sugawara
items.x: This study proposes Tool-RoCo, a novel benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in long-term multi-agent cooperation based on RoCo, a multi-robot cooperative benchmark. Recent research on LLM-based multi-agent systems has relied on predefined orchestration, while ignoring agent autonomy. Tool-RoCo treats other agents as tools and introduces cooperative tools, leveraging tool usage to evaluate multi-agent…
items.sm: Introduces a robot cooperation benchmark that treats agents as tools to evaluate language models across different levels of autonomy and self-organization.

items.t: Matrix: Peer-to-Peer Multi-Agent Synthetic Data Generation Framework
items.a: Dong Wang, Yang Li, Ansong Ni, Yeh, Ching-Feng, Youssef Emad, Lei, Xinjie, Robbins, Liam, Karthik Padthe
items.x: Synthetic data has become increasingly important for training large language models, especially when real data is scarce, expensive, or privacy-sensitive. Many such generation tasks require coordinated multi-agent workflows, where specialized agents collaborate to produce data that is higher quality, more diverse, and structurally richer. However, existing frameworks for multi-agent synthesis often depend on a centra…
items.sm: Generates synthetic data through decentralized agents that exchange messages through distributed queues, removing the need for a central coordinator.

items.t: Breaking Algorithmic Collusion in Human-AI Ecosystems
items.a: Natalie Collina, Eshwar Ram Arunachaleswaran, Meena Jagadeesan
items.x: AI agents are increasingly deployed in ecosystems where they repeatedly interact not only with each other but also with humans. In this work, we study these human-AI ecosystems from a theoretical perspective, focusing on the classical framework of repeated pricing games. In our stylized model, the AI agents play equilibrium strategies, and one or more humans manually perform the pricing task instead of adopting an AI…
items.sm: Shows theoretically that humans using strategies that minimize regret can disrupt AI pricing collusion, with additional human participation pushing prices closer to competitive levels.

items.t: Multi-Agent Systems for Dataset Adaptation in Software Engineering: Capabilities, Limitations, and Future Directions
items.a: Jingyi Chen, Xiaoyan Guo, Songqiang Chen, Shing-Chi Cheung, Jiasi Shen
items.x: Automating the adaptation of software engineering (SE) research artifacts across datasets is essential for scalability and reproducibility, yet it remains largely unstudied. Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems, such as GitHub Copilot's agent mode, promise to automate complex development workflows through coordinated reasoning, code generation, and tool interaction. This paper prese…
items.sm: Evaluates Copilot agents adapting software engineering research artifacts to different datasets, measuring success and failures across comprehension, editing, command generation, validation, and execution.

items.t: NetworkGames: Simulating Cooperation in Network Games with Personality-driven LLM Agents
items.x: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have been extensively tested in dyadic game-theoretic scenarios, their collective behavior within complex network games remains surprisingly unexplored. To bridge this gap, we present NetworkGames, a framework connecting Generative Agents and Geometric Deep Learning. By formalizing social simulation as a message-passing process governed by LLM policies, we investigate how node heter…
items.sm: Simulates repeated cooperation games with language model agents assigned personality types to study how individual differences and network structure affect collective welfare.

items.t: Tacit Bidder-Side Collusion: Artificial Intelligence in Dynamic Auctions
items.x: We study whether large language models acting as autonomous bidders can tacitly collude by coordinating when to accept platform posted payouts in repeated Dutch auctions, without any communication. We present a minimal repeated auction model that yields a simple incentive compatibility condition and a closed form threshold for sustainable collusion for subgame-perfect Nash equilibria. In controlled simulations with m…
items.sm: Finds tacit coordination among language model bidders in small repeated auctions, with prices becoming more competitive as bidder numbers increase.

items.t: METHODS OF PREVENTING INFORMATION LEAKS CAUSED BY THE USAGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AGENT SYSTEMS
items.sm: Examines information leakage in cooperating AI agents and proposes layered defenses to control data flows and risks from tool access.

items.t: Aragog: Just-in-Time Model Routing for Scalable Serving of Agentic Workflows
items.a: Yinwei Dai, Zhuofu Chen, Anand Padmanabha Iyer, Ravi Netravali
items.x: Agentic workflows have emerged as a powerful paradigm for solving complex, multi-stage tasks, but serving them at scale is computationally expensive given the many LLM inferences that each request must pass through. Configuration selection, or the cost-aware assignment of workflow agents to specific LLMs, can reduce these costs, but existing approaches bind configuration decisions before request execution, making the…
items.sm: Adjusts language model assignments during agent workflow execution to respond to changing system loads and reduce serving costs.

items.t: zijus/zijus-chat-ui
items.x: A free, plug-and-play chat UI that works with any agentic framework—including Autogen, LangGraph, ADK, and more.
items.sm: Provides a free chat interface designed to connect with various agent frameworks, including Autogen, LangGraph, and ADK.

items.t: Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Zou, Jiaru, Qiu, Ruizhong, Li, Gaotang, Yang, Xiyuan, Tieu, Katherine, Lu, Pan, Shen, Ke, Tong, Hanghang
items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) extend large language models (LLMs) from independent single-model reasoning to coordinative system-level intelligence. While existing LLM agents depend on text-based mediation for reasoning and communication, we take a step forward by enabling models to collaborate directly within the continuous latent space. We introduce LatentMAS, an end-to-end training-free framework that enables pure lat…
items.sm: Enables language model agents to collaborate through hidden representations and shared latent memory without additional training or text-based communication.

items.t: Evaluating Multi-Agent Defences Against Jailbreaking Attacks on Large Language Models
items.a: Maria Carolina, Cornelia Wit, Jun Pang
items.v: International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)
items.x: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have raised concerns about jailbreaking attacks, i.e., prompts that bypass safety mechanisms. This paper investigates the use of multi-agent LLM systems as a defence against such attacks. We evaluate three jailbreaking strategies, including the original AutoDefence attack and two from Deepleaps: BetterDan and JB. Reproducing the AutoDefence framework, we compare single-…
items.sm: Finds that multi-agent defenses improve resistance to tested jailbreak attacks but vary by attack and increase false alarms and computational costs.

items.t: A Hybrid, Multi-Layered Memory Architecture for Collaborative Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems
items.v: International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)
items.sm: Proposes four memory layers for collaborating agents, with automated processes that promote significant information and consolidate experiences into lasting knowledge.

items.t: Emergent Deception and Governance in Common-Pool Resource Multi-Agent Simulations
items.v: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.sm: Examines cooperation, deception, resource extraction, and monitoring in simulations where language model agents share a renewable resource and vote on auditing policies.

items.t: Tractable Asymmetric Verification for Large Language Models via Deterministic Replicability
items.a: Zan‐Kai Chong, Hiroyuki Ohsaki, Bryan Ng Cheng Kuan
items.v: IEEE Student Conference on Research and Development (SCOReD)
items.x: The landscape of Large Language Models (LLMs) shifts rapidly towards dynamic, multi-agent systems. This introduces a fundamental challenge in establishing computational trust, specifically how one agent can verify that another’s output was genuinely produced by a claimed LLM, and not falsified or generated by a cheaper or inferior model. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a verification framework that ach…
items.sm: Proposes probabilistic checks of claimed language model computations using deterministic replication, requiring identical hardware and software environments to make verification cheaper than generation.

items.t: Securing the Model Context Protocol (MCP): Risks, Controls, and Governance
items.a: Herman Errico, Jiquan Ngiam, Shanita Sojan
items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) replaces static, developer-controlled API integrations with more dynamic, user-driven agent systems, which also introduces new security risks. As MCP adoption grows across community servers and major platforms, organizations encounter threats that existing AI governance frameworks (such as NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001) do not yet cover in detail. We focus on three types of adversarie…
items.sm: Analyzes Model Context Protocol security threats involving injected instructions, compromised servers, and agents exceeding their roles, alongside controls and governance considerations.

items.t: Do LLMs Benefit from Self-Ensembles? A Study of Self-Mixture-of-Agents
items.v: International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models (FLLM)
items.sm: Evaluates whether combining multiple responses from a single language model improves performance across models and datasets.

items.t: M$^3$Prune: Hierarchical Communication Graph Pruning for Efficient Multi-Modal Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.a: Shao, Weizi, Taolin Zhang, Zijie Zhou, Chen Chen, Chengyu Wang, Xiaofeng He
items.x: Recent advancements in multi-modal retrieval-augmented generation (mRAG), which enhance multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) with external knowledge, have demonstrated that the collective intelligence of multiple agents can significantly outperform a single model through effective communication. Despite impressive performance, existing multi-agent systems inherently incur substantial token overhead and increased…
items.sm: Prunes redundant communication links among text and vision agents to reduce token costs in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation while preserving task performance.

items.t: ThibautMelen/agentic-ai-systems
items.x: Agentic AI explained with chickens 🐔 every pattern a runnable, CI-checked file.

items.t: Be My Eyes: Extending Large Language Models to New Modalities Through Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Huang, James Y., Zhang, Sheng, Liu, Qianchu, Qin, Guanghui, Zhu, Tinghui, Tristan Naumann, Chen, Muhao, Hoifung Poon
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in challenging, knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks. However, extending LLMs to perceive and reason over a new modality (e.g., vision), often requires costly development of large-scale vision language models (VLMs) with LLMs as backbones. Smaller VLMs are more efficient and adaptable but often lack the broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities of…
items.sm: Pairs smaller vision models with language model reasoners through conversation and trains the vision agents to communicate useful perceptual information.

items.t: Value-based large language model agent simulation for mutual evaluation of trust and interpersonal closeness
items.a: Yuki Sakamoto, Takahisa Uchida, Hiroshi Ishiguro
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for simulating complex social phenomena using human-like agents with specific traits. In human societies, value similarity is important for building trust and close relationships; however, it remains unexplored whether this principle holds true in artificial societies comprising LLM agents. Therefore, this study investigates the influence of value similarity…
items.sm: Investigates whether shared values influence trust and interpersonal closeness between language model agents after dialogue, following experiments on controlling agent values.

items.x: As agentic AI becomes more widespread, agents with distinct and possibly conflicting goals will interact in complex ways. While reinforcement learning (RL) has been effective for aligning large language models (LLMs) in the single-agent regime, prior small…

items.t: A Layered Protocol Architecture for the Internet of Agents
items.a: Fleming, Charles, Luca Muscariello, Pandey, Vijoy, Ramana Kompella

items.t: Trust-Based Social Learning for Communication (TSLEC) Protocol Evolution in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: Emergent communication in multi-agent systems typically occurs through independent learning, resulting in slow convergence and potentially suboptimal protocols. We introduce TSLEC (Trust-Based Social Learning with Emergent Communication), a framework where agents explicitly teach successful strategies to peers, with knowledge transfer modulated by learned trust relationships. Through experiments with 100 episodes acr…

items.t: VideoChat-M1: Collaborative Policy Planning for Video Understanding via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

items.x: Multi-agent systems perform well on general reasoning tasks. However, the lack of training in specialized areas hinders their accuracy. Current training methods train a unified large language model (LLM) for all agents in the system. This may limit the performances due to different distributions underlying for different agents. Therefore, training multi-agent systems with distinct LLMs should be the next step to solv…
items.sm: Introduces M-GRPO, a hierarchical training method for multi-agent systems with distinct language models serving as planners and tool-executing subagents.

items.t: MoMoE: A Mixture of Expert Agent Model for Financial Sentiment Analysis

items.x: We present a novel approach called Mixture of Mixture of Expert (MoMoE) that combines the strengths of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures with collaborative multi-agent frameworks. By modifying the LLaMA 3.1 8B architecture to incorporate MoE layers in each agent of a layered collaborative structure, we create an ensemble of specialized expert agents that iteratively refine their outputs. Each agent leverages an …
items.sm: Combines mixture-of-experts layers with collaborating language model agents and reports improvements across language understanding and generation benchmarks.

items.t: LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Intelligent Industrial On-Call Automation
items.a: Ruowei Fu, Yang Zhang, Zeyu Che, Xin Wu, Zhenyu Zhong, Zhiqiang Ren, Shenglin Zhang, Feng Wang

items.sm: Introduces OncallX, which uses knowledge bases, dialogue, and expert agents collaborating through tree search to automate industrial incident management.

items.a: Yi Li, Congcong Zhu, Minghao Wang, Mengyang Wu, MingLu Zhu, Xin Hu

items.t: Traceability and Accountability in Role-Specialized Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
items.v: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering Workshops (ASEW)
items.x: Sequential multi-agent systems built with large language models (LLMs) can automate complex software tasks, but they are hard to trust because errors quietly pass from one stage to the next. We study a traceable and accountable pipeline, meaning a system with clear roles, structured handoffs, and saved records that let us trace who did what at each step and assign blame when things go wrong. Our setting is a Planner …
items.sm: Evaluates planner, executor, and critic pipelines, finding that structured handoffs improve accuracy while saved records help trace errors and assign responsibility.

items.t: Requirements Development and Formalization for Reliable Code Generation: A Multi-Agent Vision
items.a: Xu Lu, Weisong Sun, Yiran Zhang, Ming Hu, Cong Tian, Zhi Gang Jin, Yang Liu
items.v: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
items.x: Automated code generation has long been considered the holy grail of software engineering. The emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) has catalyzed a revolutionary breakthrough in this area. However, existing methods that only rely on LLMs remain inadequate in the quality of generated code, offering no guarantees of satisfying practical requirements. They lack a systematic strategy for requirements development and…
items.sm: Envisions ReDeFo, a three-agent framework that integrates formal methods into requirements development and modeling to improve code generation reliability.

items.t: Bridging the Prototype-Production Gap: A Multi-Agent System for Notebooks Transformation
items.a: Hanya Elhashemy, Youssef Lotfy, Yongjian Tang
items.v: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering Workshops (ASEW)
items.x: The increasing adoption of Jupyter notebooks in data science and machine learning workflows has created a gap between exploratory code development and production-ready software systems. While notebooks excel at iterative development and visualization, they often lack proper software engineering principles, making their transition to production environments challenging. This paper presents Codelevate1, a novel multiag…
items.sm: Introduces Codelevate, which coordinates architect, developer, and structure agents through a shared dependency tree to transform Jupyter notebooks into maintainable Python repositories.

items.t: ALMAS: an Autonomous LLM-based Multi-Agent Software Engineering Framework
items.a: Vali Tawosi, Keshav Ramani, Salwa Alamir, Xiaomo Liu
items.v: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering Workshops (ASEW)
items.x: Multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems have been leading the way in applied LLM research across a number of fields. One notable area is software development, where researchers have advanced the automation of code implementation, code testing, code maintenance, inter alia, using LLM agents. However, software development is a multifaceted environment that extends beyond just code. As such, a successful LLM syst…
items.sm: Envisions ALMAS, a modular framework aligning language model agents with agile roles to collaborate with human developers across the software development lifecycle.

items.t: Envisioning Intelligent Requirements Engineering via Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Jiangping Huang, Dongmin Jin, Weisong Sun, Yang Liu, Zhi Gang Jin

items.sm: Proposes KGMAF, a framework with six knowledge-equipped agents and shared artifacts to help requirements engineers turn client ideas into software requirements specifications.

items.t: A Large-Scale Evolvable Dataset for Model Context Protocol Ecosystem and Security Analysis

items.x: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has recently emerged as a standardized interface for connecting language models with external tools and data. items.sm: Introduces MCPCORPUS, a dataset of approximately 14,000 MCP servers and 300 clients, with normalized metadata and tools for updating and inspecting ecosystem records.

items.sm: Provides a Mastra-based multi-agent framework with enterprise tools, specialized agents, and A2A/MCP orchestration for financial analysis, retrieval pipelines, monitoring, and governance.

items.sm: Routes agent requests to cheaper models and tool paths, claiming to reduce operating costs without reducing performance.

items.t: TrustOrch: A Dynamic Trust-Aware Orchestration Framework for Adversarially Robust Multi-Agent Collaboration

items.t: UFO3: Weaving the Digital Agent Galaxy
items.a: Chaoyun Zhang, Liqun Li, He Huang, Chiming Ni, Qiao, Bo, Qin, Si, Yu Kang, Minghua Ma
items.x: Large language model (LLM)-powered agents are transforming digital devices from passive tools into proactive intelligent collaborators. However, most existing frameworks remain confined to a single OS or device, making cross-device workflows brittle and largely manual. We present UFO$^3$, a system that unifies heterogeneous endpoints, desktops, servers, mobile devices, and edge, into a single orchestration fabric. UF…
items.sm: Introduces UFO3, which coordinates agents across devices using evolving task dependency graphs to support asynchronous execution, recovery, and workflow optimization.

items.t: MALBO: Optimizing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Teams via Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
items.x: The optimal assignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) to specialized roles in multi-agent systems is a significant challenge, defined by a vast combinatorial search space, expensive black-box evaluations, and an inherent trade-off between performance and cost. Current optimization methods focus on single-agent settings and lack a principled framework for this multi-agent, multi-objective problem. This thesis introdu…
items.sm: Introduces MALBO, which uses multi-objective Bayesian optimization to assign language models to agent roles while balancing task accuracy and inference cost.

items.t: TwinFlow: A Conceptual Framework for Digital Twin Personas in Agile Software Development
items.a: Toyese Oloyede, Olatunji Sikiru, Fatimat Okeleye, Eboesomi Esther Bunmi, Oke Oviemuno Anthony, Olusegun Akinfenwa, Arinzechukwu Hipolite Madukasi, Christian Chimezie

items.sm: TwinFlow proposes digital replicas of Agile team members using language model agents and development tool data to simulate collaboration and anticipate workflow problems.

items.t: Exposing Weak Links in Multi-Agent Systems under Adversarial Prompting
items.a: Nitu Arora, Sathvik Joel, Ishan Kavathekar, Palak, Rohan Gandhi, Yash Pandya, Tanuja Ganu, Aditya Kanade
items.x: LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems (MAS). As these systems move toward real-world applications, their security becomes paramount. Existing research largely evaluates single-agent security, leaving a critical gap in understanding the vulnerabilities introduced by multi-agent design. However, existing systems fall short due to lack of unified frameworks and metrics focusing on unique reje…
items.sm: SafeAgents assesses multi-agent security under adversarial prompts, while its Dharma measure identifies vulnerabilities associated with planning, shared context, and fallback behavior.

items.t: iMAD: Intelligent Multi-Agent Debate for Efficient and Accurate LLM Inference
items.a: Weiguo Fan, JinYi Yoon, Bo Ji
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM) agent systems have advanced rapidly, driven by their strong generalization in zero-shot settings. To further enhance reasoning and accuracy on complex tasks, Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) has emerged as a promising framework that engages multiple LLM agents in structured debates to encourage diverse reasoning. However, triggering MAD for every query is inefficient, as it incurs substantial compu…
items.sm: iMAD learns when multi-agent debate is likely to correct a single agent’s answer, aiming to reduce unnecessary computation and avoid harmful revisions.

items.t: Multi-agent Undercover Gaming: Hallucination Removal via Counterfactual Test for Multimodal Reasoning

items.a: Shulin Liu, Du, Dong, Tao Yang, Li, Yang, Boyu Qiu

items.sm: MarsRL jointly trains solver, verifier, and corrector agents through reinforcement learning, using agent-specific rewards and pipeline parallelism to improve training efficiency.

Conventional solutions, such as fine-tuni…

items.t: Homophily-induced emergence of biased structures in LLM-based multi-agent AI systems
items.x: Abstract This study examines how interactions among artificially intelligent (AI) agents, guided by large language models (LLMs), drive the evolution of collective network structures. We ask LLM-driven agents to grow a network by informing them about current link constellations. Our observations confirm that agents consistently apply a preferential attachment mechanism, favoring connections to nodes with higher degre…
items.sm: Finds that language model agents favor well-connected nodes when building networks and form more socially segregated communities when given demographic and political attributes.

items.t: Evaluating Software Process Models for Multi-Agent Class-Level Code Generation
items.a: Wasique Islam Shafin, Md Nakhla Rafi, Zhenhao Li, Tse-Hsun Peter Chen
items.x: Modern software systems require code that is not only functional but also maintainable and well-structured. This work examines how process structure and role specialization shape multi-agent LLM workflows for class-level code generation. We simulate a Wa…
items.sm: Evaluates multi-agent Waterfall workflows on Python class generation, finding cleaner, more maintainable code alongside reduced functional correctness for some models.

items.t: Evolution of AI Agent Registry Solutions: Centralized, Enterprise, and Distributed Approaches
items.a: Aditi Singh, Abul Ehtesham, Mahesh Lambe, Jared Grogan, Abhishek Singh, Saket Kumar, Luca Muscariello, Vijoy Pandey

We propose TeleMCP, the Telecom Model Context Protocol, to enable str…
items.sm: Tele-LLM-Hub provides low-code tools for building telecom-focused multi-agent systems, using TeleMCP to share structured network context among agents.

items.t: Upgrade or Switch: Do We Need a Next-Gen Trusted Architecture for the Internet of AI Agents?

In real-life settings, it is impractical to rely on users to detect these errors and request a new response. One way to address this problem is to refine the response before returning…
items.sm: Proposes refining conversational responses before delivery through specialized agents that review factual accuracy, personalization, and coherence.

items.t: Who Gets the Reward & Who Gets the Blame? Evaluation-Aligned Training Signals for Multi-LLM Agents

We propose a theoretical framework that unifies cooperative game-theoretic attribution with process reward modeling to transform system evaluation to agent credit to response-level signals. Unlike pr…
items.sm: Proposes translating system-level evaluations into agent credit and message-level training signals, rewarding cooperation and corrections while penalizing harmful contributions.

items.t: Designing LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems for Software Engineering Tasks: Quality Attributes, Design Patterns and Rationale
items.a: Yangxiao Cai, Ruiyin Li, Peng Liang, Mojtaba Shahin, Zengyang Li
items.x: As the complexity of Software Engineering (SE) tasks continues to escalate, Multi-Agent Systems (MASs) have emerged as a focal point of research and practice due to their autonomy and scalability. Furthermore, through leveraging the reasoning and planning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), the application of LLM-based MASs in the field of SE is garnering increasing attention. However, there is no dedicated…
items.sm: Studies 94 papers to identify quality priorities, design patterns, and design rationales for language model multi-agent systems used in software engineering.

items.t: Convergence dynamics of Agent-to-Agent Interactions with Misaligned objectives
items.a: Romain Cosentino, Sarath Shekkizhar, Adam Christopher Earle

We then study the coupled dynamics when two such LSA agents alternatel…

items.t: SciAgent: A Unified Multi-Agent System for Generalistic Scientific Reasoning

SciAgent organizes problem solving as a hierarchic…
items.sm: SciAgent coordinates specialized reasoning agents for scientific problems, adapting workflows by domain and difficulty and reporting performance matching or exceeding human gold medal standards.

items.t: Automatic Paper Reviewing with Heterogeneous Graph Reasoning over LLM-Simulated Reviewer-Author Debates

items.t: From Conversation to Orchestration: HCI Challenges and Opportunities in Interactive Multi-Agentic Systems

items.t: Agentic Services Computing
items.a: Shuiguang Deng, Hailiang Zhao, Ziqi Wang, Guanjie Cheng, Chen, Peng, Wenzhuo Qian, Ling, Zhiwei, Jianwei Yin
items.x: Services computing has evolved from Web services and microservices to cloud-native and serverless paradigms. These approaches established mature principles for describing, composing, deploying, operating, and governing reusable software functions. LLM-based agents now introduce a fundamentally different service form. Service value in this paradigm emerges not only from invoking predefined functions but also from dele…
items.sm: Outlines a research agenda for engineering and managing autonomous agents as services that pursue goals, maintain state, use tools, and collaborate.

items.t: ATLAS: Constraints-Aware Multi-Agent Collaboration for Real-World Travel Planning
items.a: Choi, Jihye, Jinsung Yoon, J.-C. CHEN, Somesh Jha, Tomas Pfister
items.x: While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable advancements in reasoning and tool use, they often fail to generate optimal, grounded solutions under complex constraints. Real-world travel planning exemplifies these challenges, evaluating agents' abilities to handle constraints that are explicit, implicit, and even evolving based on interactions with dynamic environments and user needs. In this paper, we pre…
items.sm: Introduces a travel planning framework that coordinates agents through changing constraint management, repeated plan review, and adaptive search.

items.t: Demystifying the Lifecycle of Failures in Platform-Orchestrated Agentic Workflows
items.a: Ma, Xuyan, Xiaofei Xie, Yawen Wang, Junjie Wang, Boyu Wu, Mingyang Li, Qing Wang
items.x: Agentic workflows built on low-code orchestration platforms enable rapid development of multi-agent systems, but they also introduce new and poorly understood failure modes that hinder reliability and maintainability. Unlike traditional software systems, failures in agentic workflows often propagate across heterogeneous nodes through natural-language interactions, tool invocations, and dynamic control logic, making f…
items.sm: Analyzes how failures arise, spread, and get repaired in agent workflows using a dataset of 307 cases from two orchestration platforms.

items.t: MedLA: A Logic-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Complex Medical Reasoning with Large Language Models
items.a: Ma, Siqi, Jiajie Huang, Fan Zhang, Shen, Yue, Jinlin Wu, Fan, Guohui, Zhu Zhang, Zelin Zang
items.x: Answering complex medical questions requires not only domain expertise and patient-specific information, but also structured and multi-perspective reasoning. Existing multi-agent approaches often rely on fixed roles or shallow interaction prompts, limiting their ability to detect and resolve fine-grained logical inconsistencies. To address this, we propose \textsc{MedLA}, a logic-driven multi-agent framework built on…

items.t: CORRECT: COndensed eRror RECognition via knowledge Transfer in multi-agent systems

items.x: Multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly capable of tackling complex real-world tasks, yet their reliance on inter-agent coordination, tool use, and long-horizon reasoning makes error recognition particularly challenging. Minor errors can propagate across agents, escalating into task failures while producing long, intertwined execution trajectories that impose significant costs for both human developers and automat…
items.sm: Introduces a framework that caches condensed error patterns and reuses them to locate failures in new multi-agent execution logs without training.

items.t: Beyond the Strongest LLM: Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Orchestration vs. Single LLMs on Benchmarks
items.a: Tian, Aaron Xuxiang, Zhang, Ruofan, Tang, Jiayao, Cho, Young Min, Xueqian Li, Yi Qiang, Wang, Ji, Zhunping Zhang
items.x: We study multi-turn multi-agent orchestration, where multiple large language model (LLM) agents interact over multiple turns by iteratively proposing answers or casting votes until reaching consensus. items.t: moazbuilds/CodeMachine-CLI
items.x: CodeMachine is an open-source tool that orchestrates AI coding agents into repeatable, long-running workflows. ⚡️
items.sm: Provides an open-source tool for coordinating AI coding agents through repeatable workflows that can run for extended periods.

items.t: Deceive, Detect, and Disclose: Large Language Models Play Mini-Mafia
items.x: Large language models are increasingly deployed in multi-agent settings whose outcomes hinge on social intelligence, motivating evaluations of their interactive capabilities; yet existing studies remain overwhelmingly empirical, leaving us without a theoretical understanding of how agent interactions determine collective outcomes. To address this, we introduce \textit{Mini-Mafia}, a four-player simplification of the …

items.t: isekOS/awesome-a2a-agents
items.x: Awesome A2A Agents is a curated list of tools, frameworks, and projects built on the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communication protocol. It aims to showcase interoperable agent systems, share best practices, and help developers explore the emerging A2A ecosystem.
items.sm: Curates tools, frameworks, and projects using the A2A communication protocol to help developers explore interoperable agent systems and development practices.

items.sm: RobustFlow trains workflow generators to produce consistent agent workflows across differently worded equivalent instructions and introduces a benchmark for measuring that consistency.

items.x: Agentic workflows -- where multiple large language model (LLM) instances interact to solve tasks -- are increasingly built on feedback mechanisms, where one model evaluates and critiques another. Despite the promise of feedback-driven improvement, the stability of agentic workflows rests on the reliability of the judge. However, judges may hallucinate information, exhibit bias, or act adversarially -- introducing cri…
items.sm: Analyzes agent workflows receiving misleading judge feedback and introduces a judge taxonomy and WAFER-QA benchmark for studying these vulnerabilities.

items.t: Towards Orchestrating Agentic Applications as FaaS Workflows
items.a: Shiva Sai Krishna Anand Tokal, Vaibhav Jha, Anand Eswaran, Praveen Jayachandran, Yogesh L. Simmhan

items.sm: Proposes composing planner, executor, evaluator, and judge agents from simple prompts and deploying their workflows through cloud Function as a Service infrastructure.

items.t: To trust or not to trust: Attention-based Trust Management for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: He, Pengfei, Zhenwei Dai, Xianfeng Tang, Xing, Yue, Hui Liu, Jingying Zeng, Qiankun Peng, Shrivats Agrawal
items.x: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MAS) have demonstrated strong capabilities in solving complex tasks but remain vulnerable when agents receive unreliable messages. This vulnerability stems from a fundamental gap: LLM agents treat all incoming messages equally without evaluating their trustworthiness. While some existing studies approach trustworthiness, they focus on a single type of harmfulness ra…
items.sm: Defines six dimensions of message trustworthiness and introduces an attention-based score to help language model agents assess incoming messages.

items.t: Why do AI agents communicate in human language?
items.a: Pengcheng Zhou, Feng, Yinglun, Halimulati Julaiti, Zhongliang Yang
items.x: Large Language Models (LLMs) have become foundational to modern AI agent systems, enabling autonomous agents to reason and plan. In most existing systems, inter-agent communication relies primarily on natural language. While this design supports interpretability and human oversight, we argue that it introduces fundamental limitations in agent-to-agent coordination. The semantic space of natural language is structural…
items.sm: Argues that natural language communication loses information between AI agents and that current language model training inadequately supports coordination and persistent roles.

These systems, which consist of multiple LLM-powered agents working collaboratively, are increasingly deployed in high-stakes applications but face novel security threats due to their complex structures. While single-agent vulnerabilities are well-stud…
items.sm: Proposes a systematic framework for analyzing multi-agent language model vulnerabilities, including threats involving communication, trust relationships, and tool integration.

items.t: Distinguishing Autonomous AI Agents from Collaborative Agentic Systems: A Comprehensive Framework for Understanding Modern Intelligent Architectures
items.x: The emergence of large language models has catalyzed two distinct yet interconnected paradigms in artificial intelligence: standalone AI Agents and collaborative Agentic AI ecosystems. This comprehensive study establishes a definitive framework for distinguishing these architectures through systematic analysis of their operational principles, structural compositions, and deployment methodologies. We characterize AI A…
items.sm: Develops a framework distinguishing individual tool-using AI agents from collaborative systems of agents through their structures, operating principles, and deployment methods.

items.t: A Study on the MCP x A2A Framework for Enhancing Interoperability of LLM-based Autonomous Agents
items.x: This paper provides an in-depth technical analysis and implementation methodology of the open-source Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol developed by Google and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) introduced by Anthropic. While the evolution of LLM-based autonomous agents is rapidly accelerating, efficient interactions among these agents and their integration with external systems remain significant challenges. In modern AI s…
items.sm: Analyzes how A2A and MCP can support communication between autonomous agents and connections to external tools, with guidance for implementation.

items.t: Agentic AI and Multiagentic: Are We Reinventing the Wheel?
items.x: The terms Agentic AI and Multiagentic AI have recently gained popularity in discussions on generative artificial intelligence, often used to describe autonomous software agents and systems composed of such agents. However, the use of these terms confuses these buzzwords with well-established concepts in AI literature: intelligent agents and multi-agent systems. This article offers a critical analysis of this conceptu…
items.sm: Argues that agentic AI terminology often repackages established concepts from intelligent agents and multi-agent systems, reviewing their theoretical origins and architectures.

items.t: Show HN: Agno – A full-stack framework for building Multi-Agent Systems
items.sm: Introduces Agno as a full-stack framework for building multi-agent systems.

items.t: A Survey of Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Task Scenarios
items.a: Jiajun Chai, Zijie Zhao, Yuanheng Zhu, Dongbin Zhao
items.sm: Surveys cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning for multiple tasks, organizing challenges around differing rewards, environments, and numbers of agents.

items.t: EvoGit: Decentralized Code Evolution via Git-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.a: Beichen Huang, Ran Cheng, Kay Chen Tan
items.x: We introduce EvoGit, a decentralized multi-agent framework for collaborative software development driven by autonomous code evolution. EvoGit deploys a population of independent coding agents, each proposing edits to a shared codebase without centralized coordination, explicit message passing, or shared memory. Instead, all coordination emerges through a Git-based phylogenetic graph that tracks the full version linea…
items.sm: Introduces EvoGit, where independent coding agents coordinate software changes through Git version histories, with users setting goals and providing occasional feedback.

items.t: HASHIRU: Hierarchical Agent System for Hybrid Intelligent Resource Utilization
items.a: Kunal Pai, Shah, Parth, Patel, Harshil
items.x: Rapid Large Language Model (LLM) advancements are fueling autonomous Multi-Agent System (MAS) development. However, current frameworks often lack flexibility, resource awareness, model diversity, and autonomous tool creation. This paper introduces HASHIRU (Hierarchical Agent System for Hybrid Intelligent Resource Utilization), a novel MAS framework enhancing flexibility, resource efficiency, and adaptability. HASHIRU…
items.sm: Introduces HASHIRU, a hierarchical agent framework that allocates specialized agents and models according to task needs, resource constraints, and team management costs.

items.t: Data management for LLM-based multi-agent systems
items.v: Repository of the University of Namur

items.t: Language-Driven Coordination and Learning in Multi-Agent Simulation Environments

items.sm: Introduces LLM-MARL, combining language-based coordination, messaging, and memory with reinforcement learning, and reports improved cooperation and generalization in simulated games.

items.t: Review of Autonomous and Collaborative Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Systems for Enterprise Applications

items.sm: Reviews enterprise uses of autonomous agents and multi-agent systems, discussing automation opportunities, limitations, governance needs, and human collaboration.

items.t: The Coming Crisis of Multi-Agent Misalignment: AI Alignment Must Be a Dynamic and Social Process

While AI alignment with human values and preferences remains a core challenge, the growing prevalence of MAS in real-world applications introduces a new dyn…
items.sm: Argues that AI alignment in multi-agent systems depends on changing social interactions, which can shift agents away from human values and preferences.

items.t: TRiSM for Agentic AI: A review of Trust, Risk, and Security Management in LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems

items.x: Agentic AI systems, built upon large language models (LLMs) and deployed in multi-agent configurations, are redefining intelligence, autonomy, collaboration, and decision-making across enterprise and societal domains. items.sm: Reviews trust, risk, and security management for language model multi-agent systems, adapting governance principles and classifying threats such as coordination failures and adversarial prompts.

items.t: STRATUS: A Multi-agent System for Autonomous Reliability Engineering of Modern Clouds
items.a: Yinfang Chen, Jiaqi Pan, Jackson Clark, Yiming Su, Noah Zheutlin, Bhavya Bhavya, Rohan Arora, Yu Deng

Yet current simulations remain grounded in a behaviorist "demographics in, behavi…
items.sm: Argues that credible social simulations require traceable, revisable reasoning and introduces GenMinds, a cognitive science-inspired approach to representing agents' beliefs.

items.t: CitySim: Modeling Urban Behaviors and City Dynamics with Large-Scale LLM-Driven Agent Simulation
items.v: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)

items.a: S. S. Zhu, Jiao Jiao Sun, Nian Yi, Tobin South, Alex Pentland, Jiaxin Pei
items.x: AI agents are increasingly used in consumer-facing applications to assist with tasks such as product search, negotiation, and transaction execution. In this paper, we explore a future scenario where both consumers and merchants authorize AI agents to fully automate negotiations and transactions. We aim to answer two key questions: (1) Do different LLM agents vary in their ability to secure favorable deals for users? …
items.sm: Benchmarks automated negotiations and transactions between consumer and merchant agents, finding unequal outcomes across models and risks from anomalous agent behavior.

items.t: LLM Agents Should Employ Security Principles
items.a: Kaiyuan Zhang, Zian Su, Pin‐Yu Chen, Elisa Bertino, Zhang, Xiangyu, Ninghui Li
items.x: Large Language Model (LLM) agents show considerable promise for automating complex tasks using contextual reasoning; however, interactions involving multiple agents and the system's susceptibility to prompt injection and other forms of context manipulation introduce new vulnerabilities related to privacy leakage and system exploitation. items.sm: Argues that deploying language model agents should incorporate established security principles, including least privilege, layered defenses, and checks on every access.

items.t: LLM Agents for Bargaining with Utility-based Feedback
items.x: Bargaining, a critical aspect of real-world interactions, presents challenges for large language models (LLMs) due to limitations in strategic depth and adaptation to complex human factors. items.sm: Introduces BargainArena, utility-based evaluation metrics, and iterative feedback to assess and improve language model bargaining strategies across complex negotiation scenarios.

items.t: MermaidFlow: Redefining Agentic Workflow Generation via Safety-Constrained Evolutionary Programming
items.a: Zheng, Chengqi, Chen, Jianda, Yueming Lyu, Ng, Wen Zheng Terence, Haopeng Zhang, Yew-Soon Ong, Ivor Wai-Hung Tsang, Yin, Haiyan
items.x: Despite the promise of autonomous agentic reasoning, existing workflow generation methods frequently produce fragile, unexecutable plans due to unconstrained LLM-driven construction. At its core, MermaidFlow represent workflows as a verifiable intermediate representation using Mermaid, a structure…
items.sm: MermaidFlow evolves agent workflows represented as Mermaid graphs using constrained edits, reporting higher success rates and faster convergence to executable plans.

Although Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) alleviate some of these limitations through collaborative mechanisms like task de…
items.sm: Co-Saving uses accumulated experience to coordinate software development agents with attention to token consumption, execution time, and solution quality.

items.t: Topological Structure Learning Should Be A Research Priority for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Jiaxi Yang, Mengqi Zhang, Yiqiao Jin, Hao Chen, Qingsong Wen, Lu Lin, Yi He, Srijan Kumar
items.x: Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Systems (MASs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for tackling complex tasks through collaborative intelligence. However, the topology of these systems--how agents in MASs should be configured, connected, and coordinated--remains largely unexplored. In this position paper, we call for a paradigm shift toward \emph{topology-aware MASs} that explicitly model and dynamically optim…
items.sm: Argues for prioritizing research on multi-agent interaction structures and proposes a framework covering agent selection, structure profiling, and topology synthesis.

items.t: On the Limits of Agency in Agent-based Models
items.a: Ayush Chopra, Shashank Kumar, Nurullah Giray Kuru, Ramesh Raskar, Arnau Quera-Bofarull
items.x: Agent-based modeling (ABM) offers powerful insights into complex systems, but its practical utility has been limited by computational constraints and simplistic agent behaviors, especially when simulating large populations. items.sm: Introduces shared language model archetypes to simulate millions of adaptive agents while examining tradeoffs between population size and individual behavioral complexity.

items.t: AgentDNS: A Root Domain Naming System for LLM Agents
items.a: Enfang Cui, Yujun Cheng, Rui She, Dan Liu, Zhiyuan Liang, Minxin Guo, Tianzheng Li, Wei Qian
items.x: The rapid evolution of Large Language Model (LLM) agents has highlighted critical challenges in cross-vendor service discovery, interoperability, and communication. Existing protocols like model context protocol and agent-to-agent protocol have made significant strides in standardizing interoperability between agents and tools, as well as communication among multi-agents. However, there remains a lack of standardized…
items.sm: Proposes AgentDNS, a naming and discovery system that lets language model agents locate and securely invoke services across vendors and organizations.

items.t: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
items.x: Large language models (LLMs) provide a compelling foundation for building generally-capable AI agents. These agents may soon be deployed at scale in the real world, representing the interests of individual humans (e.g., AI assistants) or groups of humans (e.g., AI-accelerated corporations). At present, relatively little is known about the dynamics of multiple LLM agents interacting over many generations of iterative …
items.sm: Investigates whether generations of language model agents develop cooperative social norms while playing a donor game with incentives to defect.

items.a: Dattatray Vishnu Kute, Zihao Xu, Yuekang Li, Fethi Rabhi

items.a: Yingxuan Yang, Qiuying Peng, Jun Wang, Ying Wen, Weinan Zhang

items.t: Training Language Models for Social Deduction with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Bidipta Sarkar, Warren Xia, C. Karen Liu, Dorsa Sadigh
items.x: Communicating in natural language is a powerful tool in multi-agent settings, as it enables independent agents to share information in partially observable settings and allows zero-shot coordination with humans. However, most prior works are limited as they either rely on training with large amounts of human demonstrations or lack the ability to generate natural and useful communication strategies. In this work, we t…
items.sm: Trains language models for social deduction without human demonstrations, using predictions about the environment to reward useful listening and communication.

items.t: Will Systems of LLM Agents Lead to Cooperation: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
items.a: Richard Willis, Yali Du, Joel Z. Leibo
items.sm: Finds that behavioral instructions and prompt format influence biases and the relative success of cooperative and aggressive strategies generated for repeated Prisoner's Dilemma games.

items.t: Implicit Repair with Reinforcement Learning in Emergent Communication
items.a: Fábio Vital, Alberto Sardinha, Francisco S. Melo
items.x: Conversational repair is a mechanism used to detect and resolve miscommunication and misinformation problems when two or more agents interact. This work explores how redundanc…
items.sm: Studies communication under noisy conditions and finds that reinforcement learning agents develop redundant messages to preserve information needed for their task.

items.t: Azorus: Commitments over Protocols for BDI Agents
items.a: Amit K. Chopra, Matteo Baldoni, Samuel H. Christie V, Munindar Paul Singh

items.sm: Proposes doctoral research on evaluating emergent agent languages and studying how experimental settings shape communication resembling human language use.

items.t: Market-based Architectures in RL and Beyond
items.x: Market-based agents refer to reinforcement learning agents which determine their actions based on an internal market of sub-agents. Furthermore, we argue that market-based algorithms have the potential…
items.sm: Introduces a reinforcement learning architecture where internal markets coordinate specialized subagents over components of the state, and discusses broader applications.

items.t: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Selective State-Space Models
items.a: Jemma Daniel, Ruan John de Kock, Louay Ben Nessir, Sasha Abramowitz, Omayma Mahjoub, Wiem Khlifi, Juan Claude Formanek, Arnu Pretorius
items.x: Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). items.sm: Introduces Multi-Agent Mamba, which replaces transformer attention with state-space components and reportedly matches performance while improving computational efficiency in cooperative reinforcement learning.

items.t: Herd Behavior: Investigating Peer Influence in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Youngmin Cho, Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Lyle Ungar
items.x: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled the emergence of multi-agent systems where LLMs interact, collaborate, and make decisions in shared environments. In this paper, we investigate herd behavior, the tendency of agents to align their outputs with those of their…

items.t: GGBond: Growing Graph-Based AI-Agent Society for Socially-Aware Recommender Simulation
items.a: Zhong, Hailin, Hanlin Wang, Ye, Yujun, Zhang, Meiyi, Shengxin Zhu

items.sm: Proposes GGBond, a social simulation platform using cognitive agents and evolving relationships to model changes in user preferences under recommendation systems.

items.t: Silence is Not Consensus: Disrupting Agreement Bias in Multi-Agent LLMs via Catfish Agent for Clinical Decision Making

items.sm: Introduces a dissenting agent that challenges premature diagnostic agreement in medical language model teams, adjusting interventions according to case complexity and tone.

items.t: MedSentry: Understanding and Mitigating Safety Risks in Medical LLM Multi-Agent Systems

items.t: MA-RAG: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Collaborative Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

items.t: Multi-agent systems powered by large language models: applications in swarm intelligence

items.t: Epidemic Modeling with Generative Agents
items.a: Williams, Ross, Niyousha Hosseinichimeh, Aritra Majumdar, Navid Ghaffarzadegan
items.x: This study offers a new paradigm of individual-level modeling to address the grand challenge of incorporating human behavior in epidemic models. Using generative artificial intelligence in an agent-based epidemic model, each agent is empowered to make its own reasonings and decisions via connecting to a large language model such as ChatGPT. Through various simulation experiments, we present compelling evidence that g…
items.sm: Models epidemics using language model agents that make behavioral decisions, reporting simulated isolation, infection waves, and reduced epidemic peaks.

items.t: Wireless Multi-Agent Generative AI: From Connected Intelligence to Collective Intelligence
items.a: Hang Zou, Qiyang Zhao, Lina Bariah, Mehdi Bennis, Merouane Abdelkader Debbah

This article puts the stepping-stone for incorporating multi-agent gen…

items.t: Building Cooperative Embodied Agents Modularly with Large Language Models

items.t: Emergent Resource Exchange and Tolerated Theft Behavior Using Multiagent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: For decades, the evolution of cooperation has piqued interest in numerous academic disciplines, such as game theory, economics, biology, and computer science. This form of cooperation is made possible by the introduction of a campfire, which adds an exte…
items.sm: Shows that reinforcement learning agents develop resource exchange and tolerate some theft in a foraging environment where a campfire encourages gathering.

Communication with discrete messages is considered a desired characteristic, for scientific and applied reasons. However, training a multi-agent system with discrete communication is not straightforward, requiring either reinforcement learnin…
items.sm: Proposes quantizing messages to train agents with discrete communication end to end, reporting better performance across multiple experimental setups.

items.t: Inductive Bias for Emergent Communication in a Continuous Setting
items.a: John Isak Fjellvang Villanger, Troels Arnfred Bojesen

The communication channel may consist of either discrete symbols or continuous variables. We introduce an inductive bias to aid with the emergence of good communication protocols for continuous messages, and we look at the effect this type of inductive b…
items.sm: Introduces a learning bias that improves communication protocols among cooperating agents in two simplified environments, examining both continuous and discrete messages.

items.t: Multi-Agent Collaboration: Harnessing the Power of Intelligent LLM Agents
items.x: In this paper, we present a novel framework for enhancing the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by leveraging the power of multi-agent systems. We demonstrate the practicality and versatility of …

items.t: Chaos persists in large-scale multi-agent learning despite adaptive learning rates
items.a: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Konstantinos Metaxas, Lampros Flokas, Georgios Piliouras

We find our system predicts the decisions of the real-world Supreme Court with better-than-random accuracy. We fu…
