items.t: Model-free conventions in multi-agent reinforcement learning with heterogeneous preferences
items.a: Raphaël Koster, Kevin R. McKee, Everett, Richard, Laura Weidinger, William Samuel Isaac, Edward Hughes, Edgar A. Duéñez‐Guzmán, Thore Graepel
items.x: Game theoretic views of convention generally rest on notions of common knowledge and hyper-rational models of individual behavior. However, decades of work in behavioral economics have questioned the validity of both foundations. Meanwhile, computational neuroscience has contributed a modernized 'dual process' account of decision-making where model-free (MF) reinforcement learning trades off with model-based (MB) rei…
items.sm: Investigates how model-free reinforcement learning can produce complex social conventions among agents with differing preferences.

items.t: cool-RR/marley
items.x: A framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning.
items.sm: Marley provides a framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning.

items.t: PettingZoo: Gym for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Justin K. Terry, Benjamin Black, Nathaniel Grammel, Mario Jayakumar, Ananth Hari, Sullivan, Ryan, Luís Santos, Rodrigo Perez
items.x: This paper introduces the PettingZoo library and the accompanying Agent Environment Cycle ("AEC") games model. PettingZoo is a library of diverse sets of multi-agent environments with a universal, elegant Python API. PettingZoo was developed with the goal of accelerating research in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning ("MARL"), by making work more interchangeable, accessible and reproducible akin to what OpenAI's Gym …
items.sm: Introduces PettingZoo, a library of multi-agent environments with a shared Python interface and a game model designed to reduce modeling errors.

items.t: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
items.a: Emilio Calvano, Giacomo Calzolari, Vincenzo Denicolò, Sergio Pastorello
items.sm: Finds that pricing algorithms learn to sustain prices above competitive levels without communicating, using punishment and subsequent cooperation in simulated repeated competition.

items.t: Persistent And Scalable JADE: A Cloud based InMemory Multi-agent Framework
items.a: Khalid, Nauman, Ghalib Ahmed Tahir, Peter Charles Bloodsworth
items.x: Multi-agent systems are often limited in terms of persistenceand scalability. This issue is more prevalent for applications inwhich agent states changes frequently. This makes the existingmethods less usable as they increase the agent's complexityand are less scalable. This research study has presented anovel in-memory agent persistence framework. Two prototypeshave been implemented, one using the proposed solution a…
items.sm: Proposes an in-memory framework for preserving agent states in cloud systems and reports greater scalability than an established alternative with similar persistence.

items.t: The Emergence of Adversarial Communication in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: Many real-world problems require the coordination of multiple autonomous agents. Recent work has shown the promise of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to learn explicit communication strategies that enable complex multi-agent coordination. These works use models of cooperative multi-agent systems whereby agents strive to achieve a shared global goal. When considering agents with self-interested local objectives, the stan…
items.sm: Presents a learning model that lets agents with individual rewards learn communication strategies through a shared differentiable channel.

items.t: QPLEX: Duplex Dueling Multi-Agent Q-Learning
items.a: Jianhao Wang, Zhizhou Ren, Terry Z. Liu, Yang Yu, Chongjie Zhang
items.x: We explore value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) in the popular paradigm of centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE). CTDE has an important concept, Individual-Global-Max (IGM) principle, which requires the consistency between joint and local action selections to support efficient local decision-making. However, in order to achieve scalability, existing MARL methods either limit repres…
items.sm: Introduces QPLEX, a network architecture that combines agents' value estimates while keeping individual action choices consistent with the team's preferred joint action.

items.t: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Cooperative Tasks
items.a: Georgios Papoudakis, Filippos Christianos, Lukas Schäfer, Stefano V. Albrecht
items.x: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) suffers from a lack of commonly-used evaluation tasks and criteria, making comparisons between approaches difficult. In this work, we provide a systematic evaluation and comparison of three different classes of MARL algorithms (independent learning, centralised multi-agent policy gradient, value decomposition) in a diverse range of cooperative multi-agent learning tasks.…
items.sm: Compares three classes of multi-agent learning algorithms across cooperative tasks and releases EPyMARL and two research environments to support evaluation.

items.t: Incorporating Pragmatic Reasoning Communication into Emergent Language
items.a: Yipeng Kang, Tonghan Wang, Gerard de Melo
items.x: Emergentism and pragmatics are two research fields that study the dynamics of linguistic communication along substantially different timescales and intelligence levels. From the perspective of multi-agent reinforcement learning, they correspond to stochastic games with reinforcement training and stage games with opponent awareness. Given that their combination has been explored in linguistics, we propose computationa…
items.sm: Combines reasoning about communication partners with learned communication, evaluating models in reference games and StarCraft II through experiments and theoretical analysis.

items.t: ANALYTICAL REVIEW OF MULTI-AGENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING PROBLEMS
items.v: Vestnik komp iuternykh i informatsionnykh tekhnologii
items.sm: Reviews reinforcement learning methods and coordination challenges in multi-agent systems, including hierarchical learning and group actions.

items.t: Obedience-based Multi-Agent Cooperation for Sequential Social Dilemmas
items.sm: Proposes rewarding agents for following others' commands and issuing successful commands, reporting improved coordination and communication in sequential social dilemmas.

items.t: NovaStelo: Block-style programming for multi-agent systems, based on MIT Scratch
items.sm: The post introduces NovaStelo as a Scratch-based tool for programming multi-agent systems with blocks.

items.t: On Emergent Communication in Competitive Multi-Agent Teams
items.a: Paul Pu Liang, Jeffrey W. Chen, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Louis‐Philippe Morency, Satwik Kottur
items.x: Several recent works have found the emergence of grounded compositional language in the communication protocols developed by mostly cooperative multi-agent systems when learned end-to-end to maximize performance on a downstream task. However, human populations learn to solve complex tasks involving communicative behaviors not only in fully cooperative settings but also in scenarios where competition acts as an additi…
items.sm: Investigates whether competition between cooperative agent teams encourages communication protocols with better task performance, compositional structure, and faster learning.

items.t: Networked Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Emergent Communication
items.a: Shubham Gupta, Rishi Hazra, Ambedkar Dukkipati
items.x: We develop a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) method that finds approximately optimal policies for cooperative agents that co-exist in an environment. Central to achieving this is how the agents learn to communicate with each other. Can they together develop a language while learning to perform a common task? We formulate and study a MARL problem where cooperative agents are connected via a fixed underlying …
items.sm: Trains cooperative agents connected by a fixed network to communicate using learned discrete symbols and reports improved traffic control performance against comparison methods.

items.t: A Practical Guide to Studying Emergent Communication through Grounded Language Games
items.a: Jens Nevens, Paul Van Eecke, Katrien Beuls
items.x: The question of how an effective and efficient communication system can emerge in a population of agents that need to solve a particular task attracts more and more attention from researchers in many fields, including artificial intelligence, linguistics and statistical physics. A common methodology for studying this question consists of carrying out multi-agent experiments in which a population of agents takes part …
items.sm: Provides practical guidance for studying how agent populations develop shared communication systems through repeated task-based language games.

items.t: Re-conceptualising the Language Game Paradigm in the Framework of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: In this paper, we formulate the challenge of re-conceptualising the language game experimental paradigm in the framework of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). If successful, future language game experiments will benefit from the rapid and promising methodological advances in the MARL community, while future MARL experiments on learning emergent communication will benefit from the insights and results gained f…
items.sm: Proposes reframing language game experiments within multi-agent reinforcement learning so both research communities can share methods and insights about emergent communication.

items.t: nirholas/agenti
items.x: Give any AI agent a crypto wallet. Agents deserve access to money.  Pay x402 APIs, receive USDC, check balances — autonomously. Works with Claude, LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, and any MCP client. EVM + Solana.
items.sm: Agenti gives AI agents cryptocurrency wallets to pay APIs, receive USDC, and check balances across EVM and Solana networks.

items.t: Emergence of Writing Systems through Multi-Agent Cooperation (Student Abstract)
items.v: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
items.x: Learning to communicate is considered an essential task to develop a general AI. While recent literature in language evolution has studied emergent language through discrete or continuous message symbols, there has been little work in the emergence of writing systems in artificial agents. In this paper, we present a referential game setup with two agents, where the mode of communication is a written language system t…
items.sm: Shows that two agents can develop written communication to coordinate in a reference game and examines how game rules shape the resulting writing system.

items.t: Learning to cooperate: Emergent communication in multi-agent navigation
items.a: Ivana Kajić, Eser Aygün, Doina Precup
items.x: Emergent communication in artificial agents has been studied to understand language evolution, as well as to develop artificial systems that learn to communicate with humans. We show that agents performing a cooperative navigation task in various gridworld environments learn an interpretable communication protocol that enables them to efficiently, and in many cases, optimally, solve the task. An analysis of the agent…
items.sm: Shows that agents learn interpretable spatial communication for cooperative gridworld navigation, with population experiments revealing basic compositional structure.

items.t: TonghanWang/ROMA
items.x: Codes accompanying the paper "ROMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Emergent Roles" (ICML 2020 https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.08039)
items.sm: Provides code accompanying ROMA, a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that learns agent roles.

items.t: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Tabish Rashid, Mikayel Samvelyan, Christian Schröder de Witt, Gregory Farquhar, Jakob Foerster, Shimon Whiteson
items.x: In many real-world settings, a team of agents must coordinate its behaviour while acting in a decentralised fashion. At the same time, it is often possible to train the agents in a centralised fashion where global state information is available and communication constraints are lifted. Learning joint action-values conditioned on extra state information is an attractive way to exploit centralised learning, but the bes…
items.sm: Introduces QMIX, which combines individual agent values monotonically to train coordinated policies centrally while allowing agents to choose actions independently.

items.t: ROMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Emergent Roles
items.a: Tonghan Wang, Heng Dong, Victor Lesser, Chongjie Zhang
items.x: The role concept provides a useful tool to design and understand complex multi-agent systems, which allows agents with a similar role to share similar behaviors. However, existing role-based methods use prior domain knowledge and predefine role structures and behaviors. In contrast, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides flexibility and adaptability, but less efficiency in complex tasks. In this paper, we…
items.sm: Introduces ROMA, which learns changing agent roles that encourage shared learning and specialization in subtasks without predefined role structures.

items.t: FACMAC: Factored Multi-Agent Centralised Policy Gradients
items.a: Peng, Bei, Tabish Rashid, Christian A. Schroeder de Witt, Pierre-Alexandre Kamienny, Philip H. S. Torr, Wendelin Böhmer, Shimon Whiteson
items.x: We propose FACtored Multi-Agent Centralised policy gradients (FACMAC), a new method for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning in both discrete and continuous action spaces. Like MADDPG, a popular multi-agent actor-critic method, our approach uses deep deterministic policy gradients to learn policies. However, FACMAC learns a centralised but factored critic, which combines per-agent utilities into the joint a…
items.sm: Introduces FACMAC, a cooperative learning method using a centralized critic composed of agent utilities, with experiments showing benefits from allowing nonmonotonic combinations.

items.t: Multi-Agent Systems and Complex Networks: Review and Applications in Systems Engineering
items.a: Manuel Herrera, Marco Pérez Hernández, Ajith Kumar Parlikad, Joaquín Izquierdo
items.sm: Reviews how multi-agent systems and complex network theory combine to address engineering and management problems, including infrastructure, manufacturing, and supply chains.

items.t: Language Support for Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Tony Clark, Balbir S. Barn, Vinay Kulkarni, Souvik Barat
items.sm: Proposes and implements an ESL language extension for building systems with learning agents, illustrating its features through examples and a supply chain application.

items.t: Emergent Communication with World Models
items.x: We introduce Language World Models, a class of language-conditional generative model which interpret natural language messages by predicting latent codes of future observations. This provides a visual grounding of the message, similar to an enhanced observation of the world, which may include objects outside of the listening agent's field-of-view. We incorporate this "observation" into a persistent memory state, and …
items.sm: Introduces models that interpret messages by predicting future observations and incorporating them into memory, improving communication and navigation success in gridworld tasks.

items.t: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning as a Computational Tool for Language Evolution Research: Historical Context and Future Challenges
items.x: Computational models of emergent communication in agent populations are currently gaining interest in the machine learning community due to recent advances in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). Current contributions are however still relatively disconnected from the earlier theoretical and computational literature aiming at understanding how language might have emerged from a prelinguistic substance. The goal…
items.sm: Places recent multi-agent reinforcement learning research on emergent communication within the history of language evolution research and identifies future challenges.

items.t: Language Evolution in Swarm Robotics: A Perspective
items.a: Nicolas Cambier, Roman Miletitch, Vincent Frémont, Marco Dorigo, Eliseo Ferrante, Vito Trianni
items.sm: Discusses language evolution in robot swarms, arguing that richer communication could improve autonomy while examining limitations of existing evolutionary approaches.

items.t: On the interaction between supervision and self-play in emergent communication
items.a: Ryan Lowe, Abhinav Gupta, Jakob Foerster, Douwe Kiela, Joëlle Pineau
items.x: A promising approach for teaching artificial agents to use natural language involves using human-in-the-loop training. However, recent work suggests that current machine learning methods are too data inefficient to be trained in this way from scratch. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between two categories of learning signals with the ultimate goal of improving sample efficiency: imitating human languag…
items.sm: Studies how supervised language learning and self-play interact, finding that training on human language before self-play performs better than reversing that order.

items.t: Structural Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
items.a: Agnieszka Słowik, Abhinav Gupta, William L. Hamilton, Mateja Jamnik, Sean B. Holden, Christopher Pal
items.x: In order to communicate, humans flatten a complex representation of ideas and their attributes into a single word or a sentence. We investigate the impact of representation learning in artificial agents by developing graph referential games. We empirically show that agents parametrized by graph neural networks develop a more compositional language compared to bag-of-words and sequence models, which allows them to sys…
items.sm: Finds that graph neural network agents develop more compositional communication than bag-of-words or sequence models and generalize to new combinations of familiar features.

items.t: Towards Graph Representation Learning in Emergent Communication
items.a: Agnieszka Słowik, Abhinav Gupta, William L. Hamilton, Mateja Jamnik, Sean B. Holden
items.x: Recent findings in neuroscience suggest that the human brain represents information in a geometric structure (for instance, through conceptual spaces). In order to communicate, we flatten the complex representation of entities and their attributes into a single word or a sentence. In this paper we use graph convolutional networks to support the evolution of language and cooperation in multi-agent systems. Motivated b…
items.sm: Uses graph convolutional networks in reference games, reporting learned communication that captures underlying factors, supports cooperation, and generalizes beyond training examples.

items.t: Emergence of Pragmatics from Referential Game between Theory of Mind Agents
items.a: Luyao Yuan, Zipeng Fu, Jingyue Shen, Xu, Lu, Jun-Hong Shen, Song Chun Zhu
items.x: Pragmatics studies how context can contribute to language meanings. In human communication, language is never interpreted out of context, and sentences can usually convey more information than their literal meanings. However, this mechanism is missing in most multi-agent systems, restricting the communication efficiency and the capability of human-agent interaction. In this paper, we propose an algorithm, using which…
items.sm: Proposes a reinforcement learning algorithm that lets cooperating agents develop context-sensitive communication by reasoning about each other's mental states.

items.t: Generalizing Emergent Communication
items.x: We converted the recently developed BabyAI grid world platform to a sender/receiver setup in order to test the hypothesis that established deep reinforcement learning techniques are sufficient to incentivize the emergence of a grounded discrete communication protocol between generalized agents. This is in contrast to previous experiments that employed straight-through estimation or specialized inductive biases. Our r…
items.sm: Shows that environmental incentives can produce grounded communication using standard reinforcement learning, with longer communication intervals encouraging more abstract meanings.

items.t: Co-evolution of language and agents in referential games
items.a: Gautier Dagan, Dieuwke Hupkes, Elia Bruni
items.v: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
items.x: Referential games offer a grounded learning environment for neural agents which accounts for the fact that language is functionally used to communicate.However, they do not take into account a second constraint considered to be fundamental for the shape of human language: that it must be learnable by new language learners.Cogswell et al. (2019) introduced cultural transmission within referential games through a chang…
items.sm: Introduces a simulator that jointly evolves agent architectures and communication protocols to study how learner biases shape language transmission.

items.t: Algorithmic Pricing and Market Coordination – Toward a Notion of ‘Collusive Risk’
items.sm: Proposes a notion of collusive risk for assessing algorithmic pricing coordination while preserving competition law's emphasis on independent market conduct.

items.t: Dota 2 with Large Scale Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.sm: Describes training five Dota 2 agents with shared policy parameters through PPO and self-play, examining scaling, data freshness, and adaptation to system changes.

items.t: Biases for Emergent Communication in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Tom Eccles, Yoram Bachrach, Guy Lever, Angeliki Lazaridou, Thore Graepel
items.x: We study the problem of emergent communication, in which language arises because speakers and listeners must communicate information in order to solve tasks. In temporally extended reinforcement learning domains, it has proved hard to learn such communication without centralized training of agents, due in part to a difficult joint exploration problem. We introduce inductive biases for positive signalling and positive…
items.sm: Introduces biases encouraging agents to send useful signals and respond to messages, improving communication learning and task performance in reinforcement learning environments.

items.t: Learning to Request Guidance in Emergent Communication
items.a: Benjamin Kolb, Leon Lang, Henning Bartsch, Arwin Gansekoele, Raymond Koopmanschap, Leonardo Romor, Speck, David, Mathijs Mul
items.x: Previous research into agent communication has shown that a pre-trained guide can speed up the learning process of an imitation learning agent. The guide achieves this by providing the agent with discrete messages in an emerged language about how to solve the task. We extend this one-directional communication by a one-bit communication channel from the learner back to the guide: It is able to ask the guide for help, …
items.sm: Trains learners to request costly guidance through a binary channel, finding that requests decline during training and concentrate in uncertain situations.

items.t: Simplified Action Decoder for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: In recent years we have seen fast progress on a number of benchmark problems in AI, with modern methods achieving near or super human performance in Go, Poker and Dota. One common aspect of all of these challenges is that they are by design adversarial or, technically speaking, zero-sum. In contrast to these settings, success in the real world commonly requires humans to collaborate and communicate with others, in se…
items.sm: Proposes a simplified action decoder for deep multi-agent reinforcement learning in the cooperative card game Hanabi.

items.t: Biology and Compositionality: Empirical Considerations for Emergent-Communication Protocols
items.x: Significant advances have been made in artificial systems by using biological systems as a guide. However, there is often little interaction between computational models for emergent communication and biological models of the emergence of language. Many researchers in language origins and emergent communication take compositionality as their primary target for explaining how simple communication systems can become mo…
items.sm: Questions whether compositionality should be the primary target of emergent communication research, drawing on biological perspectives on language origins.

items.t: The Good, the Bad, and the Ethical Implications of Bridging Blockchain and Multi-Agent Systems
items.a: Davide Calvaresi, Jean-Paul Calbimonte, Alevtina Dubovitskaya, Valerio Mattioli, Jean-Gabriel Piguet, Michael Schumacher
items.sm: Examines the benefits and ethical implications of combining blockchain with multi-agent systems to distribute trust and improve accountability and transparency.

items.t: Learning Efficient Multi-agent Communication: An Information Bottleneck Approach
items.a: Rundong Wang, Xu Dong He, Runsheng Yu, Wei Qiu, Bo An, Zinovi Rabinovich
items.x: We consider the problem of the limited-bandwidth communication for multi-agent reinforcement learning, where agents cooperate with the assistance of a communication protocol and a scheduler. The protocol and scheduler jointly determine which agent is communicating what message and to whom. Under the limited bandwidth constraint, a communication protocol is required to generate informative messages. Meanwhile, an unne…
items.sm: Introduces an information bottleneck approach for learning informative messages and communication schedules among cooperating agents under bandwidth constraints.

items.t: deepset-ai/haystack
items.x: Open-source AI orchestration framework for building context-engineered, production-ready LLM applications. Design modular pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation. Built for scalable agents, RAG, multimodal applications, semantic search, and conversational systems.
items.sm: Provides an open-source framework for building language model applications with modular pipelines and agent workflows controlling retrieval, routing, memory, and generation.

items.t: Avoiding hashing and encouraging visual semantics in referential emergent language games
items.x: There has been an increasing interest in the area of emergent communication between agents which learn to play referential signalling games with realistic images. In this work, we consider the signalling game setting of Havrylov and Titov and investigate the effect of the feature extractor's weights and of the task being solved on the visual semantics learned or captured by the models. We impose various augmentation …
items.sm: Shows that image augmentations and carefully chosen signaling tasks can help agents learn communication grounded in visual concepts without external supervision.

items.t: Learning to Communicate in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning : A Review
items.x: We consider the issue of multiple agents learning to communicate through reinforcement learning within partially observable environments, with a focus on information asymmetry in the second part of our work. We provide a review of the recent algorithms developed to improve the agents' policy by allowing the sharing of information between agents and the learning of communication strategies, with a focus on Deep Recurr…
items.sm: Reviews communication learning in multi-agent reinforcement learning, examines evaluation methods, and proposes an entropy-based metric for assessing learned communication.

items.t: To Populate is To Regulate
items.x: We examine the effects of instantiating Lewis signaling games within a population of speaker and listener agents with the aim of producing a set of general and robust representations of unstructured pixel data. Preliminary experiments suggest that the set of representations associated with languages generated within a population outperform those generated between a single speaker-listener pair on this objective, maki…
items.sm: Reports preliminary evidence that training populations of communicating agents produces more general and robust visual representations than training a single speaker-listener pair.

items.t: Emergence of Numeric Concepts in Multi-Agent Autonomous Communication
items.x: With the rapid development of deep learning, most of current state-of-the-art techniques in natural langauge processing are based on deep learning models trained with argescaled static textual corpora. However, we human beings learn and understand in a different way. Thus, grounded language learning argues that models need to learn and understand language by the experience and perceptions obtained by interacting with…
items.sm: Investigates how numeric concepts can emerge through autonomous communication among agents learning from interactions with their environment.

items.t: Grandmaster level in StarCraft II using multi-agent reinforcement learning
items.sm: Describes achieving Grandmaster-level StarCraft II play using multi-agent reinforcement learning.

items.t: MAVEN: Multi-Agent Variational Exploration
items.a: Anuj Mahajan, Tabish Rashid, Mikayel Samvelyan, Shimon Whiteson
items.x: Centralised training with decentralised execution is an important setting for cooperative deep multi-agent reinforcement learning due to communication constraints during execution and computational tractability in training. In this paper, we analyse value-based methods that are known to have superior performance in complex environments [43]. We specifically focus on QMIX [40], the current state-of-the-art in this dom…
items.sm: Identifies exploration limitations in QMIX and proposes MAVEN, which uses a shared latent variable and hierarchical policy to coordinate agent exploration.

items.t: Developmentally motivated emergence of compositional communication via template transfer
items.a: Tomasz Korbak, Julian Zubek, Łukasz Kuciński, Piotr Miłoś, Joanna Rączaszek‐Leonardi
items.x: This paper explores a novel approach to achieving emergent compositional communication in multi-agent systems. We propose a training regime implementing template transfer, the idea of carrying over learned biases across contexts. In our method, a sender-receiver pair is first trained with disentangled loss functions and then the receiver is transferred to train a new sender with a standard loss. Unlike other methods …
items.sm: Shows that transferring a receiver trained with disentangled losses to a new sender can encourage compositional communication without specialized agent architectures.

items.t: Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula
items.a: Bowen Baker, Ingmar Kanitscheider, Todor Markov, Wu, Yi, Glenn Powell, Bob McGrew, Igor Mordatch
items.x: Through multi-agent competition, the simple objective of hide-and-seek, and standard reinforcement learning algorithms at scale, we find that agents create a self-supervised autocurriculum inducing multiple distinct rounds of emergent strategy, many of which require sophisticated tool use and coordination. We find clear evidence of six emergent phases in agent strategy in our environment, each of which creates a new …
items.sm: Reports that competing hide-and-seek agents develop successive strategies involving coordinated tool use, including building shelters with boxes and overcoming obstacles with ramps.

items.t: Emergent Tool Use from Multi-Agent Interaction
items.sm: Discusses tool use emerging from interactions among multiple agents.

items.t: AI and SWARM
items.sm: Presents AI and swarm intelligence methods combining evolutionary algorithms and other optimization techniques, with applications to complex adaptive systems and practical problems.

items.t: openai/multi-agent-emergence-environments
items.x: Environment generation code for the paper "Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula"
items.sm: Provides environment generation code for research on tool use emerging through multi-agent competition.

items.t: Arena: a toolkit for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Qing Wang, Jiechao Xiong, Lei Han, Meng Fang, Xinghai Sun, Zhuobin Zheng, Peng Sun, Zhengyou Zhang
items.x: We introduce Arena, a toolkit for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) research. In MARL, it usually requires customizing observations, rewards and actions for each agent, changing cooperative-competitive agent-interaction, and playing with/against a third-party agent, etc. We provide a novel modular design, called Interface, for manipulating such routines in essentially two ways: 1) Different interfaces can be …
items.sm: Introduces Arena, a multi-agent reinforcement learning toolkit with composable interfaces for customizing observations, actions, rewards, and cooperative or competitive interactions.

items.t: Evolving recurrent neural networks for emergent communication
items.a: Joshua Sirota, Vadim V. Bulitko, Matthew Robert Graham Brown, Sergio Poo Hernandez
items.v: Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference Companion (GECCO Companion)
items.sm: Uses neuroevolution to jointly discover neural network architectures and weights that enable agents to develop shared communication protocols.

items.t: Dealing with Non-Stationarity in Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Georgios Papoudakis, Filippos Christianos, Arrasy Rahman, Stefano V. Albrecht
items.x: Recent developments in deep reinforcement learning are concerned with creating decision-making agents which can perform well in various complex domains. A particular approach which has received increasing attention is multi-agent reinforcement learning, in which multiple agents learn concurrently to coordinate their actions. In such multi-agent environments, additional learning problems arise due to the continually c…
items.sm: Surveys methods for handling changing agent policies in multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, including centralized training, opponent modeling, meta-learning, and communication.

items.t: Ease-of-Teaching and Language Structure from Emergent Communication
items.x: Artificial agents have been shown to learn to communicate when needed to complete a cooperative task. Some level of language structure (e.g., compositionality) has been found in the learned communication protocols. This observed structure is often the result of specific environmental pressures during training. By introducing new agents periodically to replace old ones, sequentially and within a population, we explore…
items.sm: Examines how periodically replacing agents creates pressure for easier teaching and changes the structure of learned communication protocols.

items.t: Escaping the State of Nature: A Hobbesian Approach to Cooperation in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
items.x: Cooperation is a phenomenon that has been widely studied across many different disciplines. In the field of computer science, the modularity and robustness of multi-agent systems offer significant practical advantages over individual machines. At the same time, agents using standard reinforcement learning algorithms often fail to achieve long-term, cooperative strategies in unstable environments when there are short-…
items.sm: Explores Hobbes's account of political authority as an approach to fostering cooperation among reinforcement learning agents facing incentives to defect.

items.t: Anti-efficient encoding in emergent communication
items.a: Rahma Chaabouni, Eugene Kharitonov, Emmanuel Dupoux A, Marco Baroni
items.x: Despite renewed interest in emergent language simulations with neural networks, little is known about the basic properties of the induced code, and how they compare to human language. One fundamental characteristic of the latter, known as Zipf's Law of Abbreviation (ZLA), is that more frequent words are efficiently associated to shorter strings. We study whether the same pattern emerges when two neural networks, a "s…
items.sm: Finds that neural signaling agents assign longer messages to more frequent inputs, reversing the abbreviation pattern observed in human language.

items.t: QTRAN: Learning to Factorize with Transformation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.a: Son, Kyunghwan, Kim, Daewoo, Wan Ju Kang, David Earl Hostallero, Yung Yi
items.x: We explore value-based solutions for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) tasks in the centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) regime popularized recently. However, VDN and QMIX are representative examples that use the idea of factorization of the joint action-value function into individual ones for decentralized execution. VDN and QMIX address only a fraction of factorizable MARL tasks due to t…
items.sm: Introduces QTRAN, which transforms joint action values into a factorizable form while preserving optimal actions and relaxing constraints imposed by earlier methods.

items.t: Malthusian Reinforcement Learning
